Joel, “Yahweh is God”; Jehu, see 2:38; Joshibiah, “Yahweh causes to dwell”; Seraiah, see verse 13; Asiel, “God has made.”

Elioenai, see 3:23; Jaakobah, a form of Jacob, “heel-holder” or “may he protect”; Jeshohaiah, uncertain; Asaiah, “Yahweh has made”; Adiel, “ornament of God”; Jesimiel, “God establishes”; Benaiah, “Yahweh has built.”
Ziza, uncertain; Shiphi, “abundance”; Allon, “oak”; Jedaiah, “Yahweh knows”; Shimri, “my guard”; Shemaiah, see 3:22.
The Septuagint reads “Gerara,” that is, Gerar.
Hebrew Me‘inim (Qere), a people perhaps related to Maon; the written text could be read “dwellings.” The Septuagint reads “Minaeans.”
Pelatiah and Rephaiah, see 3:21; Neariah, see 3:22; Uzziel, “God is my strength”; Ishi, see 2:31.

verses.text: The sons of Reuben, Israel’s firstborn (he was the firstborn, but because he dishonored his father’s bed, his birthright was given to the sons of Joseph son of Israel, so that he is not recorded in the family records as the firstborn;{a}
for Judah prevailed above his brothers, and from him came a prince,{b} yet the right of the firstborn was Joseph’s):
the sons of Reuben the firstborn of Israel: Hanoch, Pallu, Hezron, and Carmi.{c}
The sons of Joel: Shemaiah his son, Gog his son, Shimei his son,{d}
Micah his son, Reaiah his son, Baal his son,{e}
Beerah his son, whom Tilgath-pilneser king of Assyria took away captive; he was prince of the Reubenites.{f}
His brothers by their families, when the genealogy of their generations was reckoned: the chief, Jeiel, and Zechariah,{g}
and Bela son of Azaz, son of Shema, son of Joel. They settled in Aroer and extended to Nebo and Baal-meon.{h}
To the east they also settled up to the edge of the desert, which borders the Euphrates River, since their herds had grown large in Gilead.
During Saul’s reign they fought the Hagrites and defeated them, and then they settled in the tents of the Hagrites across the whole eastern side of Gilead.{i}
The sons of Gad lived over against them, in the land of Bashan to Salecah:{j}
Joel the chief, Shapham the second, Janai, and Shaphat in Bashan.{k}
Their relatives, by family: Michael, Meshullam, Sheba, Jorai, Jacan, Zia, and Eber, seven in all.{l}
These were the sons of Abihail the son of Huri, son of Jaroah, son of Gilead, son of Michael, son of Jeshishai, son of Jahdo, son of Buz.{m}
Ahi the son of Abdiel, son of Guni, was chief of their fathers’ house.{n}
They lived in Gilead, in Bashan and its towns, and in all the pasture lands of Sharon to their limits.{o}
All of these were entered in the family records during the reigns of Jotham king of Judah and Jeroboam king of Israel.{p}
Among the Reubenites, the Gadites, and the half-tribe of Manasseh were 44,760 brave soldiers, trained for war, who carried shields and swords, could shoot the bow, and were ready to go to battle.
They fought with the Hagrites, with Jetur, Naphish, and Nodab.{q}

They were helped in fighting them, and the Hagrites and all their allies were handed over to them, because during the battle they called out to God, and he granted their request since they put their trust in him.
They took away their animals: of camels fifty thousand, of sheep two hundred and fifty thousand, of donkeys two thousand, and of people a hundred thousand.{r}
For many fell slain, because the war was of God. And they lived in their place until the exile.
The half-tribe of Manasseh settled in the land, and they grew very numerous, from Bashan to Baal-hermon, Senir, and Mount Hermon.{s}
These were the heads of their family groups: Epher, Ishi, Eliel, Azriel, Jeremiah, Hodaviah, and Jahdiel. They were brave warriors and well-known men, each the head of his family.{t}
But they broke faith with the God of their fathers, and prostituted themselves after the gods of the peoples of the land, whom God had destroyed before them.

So the God of Israel roused the spirit of Pul king of Assyria, who is also called Tilgath-pilneser king of Assyria, and Tilgath-pilneser took the Reubenites, the Gadites, and the half-tribe of Manasseh into exile. He brought them to Halah, Habor, Hara, and the River Gozan, and they are there today.{u}

notes.text: See Genesis 35:22; 49:3–4; 48:5. Reuben, see 2:1.
Or “a leader.” Hebrew nagid.
Hanoch, see 1:33; Pallu, “distinguished”; Hezron, see 2:5; Carmi, see 2:7.
Joel, see 4:35; Shemaiah, see 3:22; Gog, uncertain; Shimei, see 3:19. Joel’s link to Reuben is not stated.
Micah, “who is like Yahweh?”; Reaiah, see 4:2; Baal, see 4:33.
Tilgath-pilneser is the Chronicler’s spelling of Tiglath-pileser (2 Kings 15:29), Assyrian Tukulti-apil-Esharra, “my trust is in the son of Esharra.” Beerah, “well.” He reigned about 745–727 B.C.
Jeiel, perhaps “God sweeps away” or “God lives”; Zechariah, “Yahweh remembers.”
Bela, see 1:43; Azaz, “strong”; Shema, see 2:43; Aroer, perhaps “juniper”; Nebo, a god’s name (Nabu); Baal-meon, “lord of the dwelling.”

The Hagrites (Hebrew Hagri’im) were a people east of the Jordan, perhaps named after Hagar (Genesis 16); the Septuagint reads “sojourners” here (taking the word as “stranger”), and “Agarenes” in verse 19. Saul, see 1:48 (Shaul); Gilead, see 2:21.
Gad, see 2:2; Bashan, perhaps “fertile plain”; Salecah, uncertain.
Shapham, perhaps “bold”; Janai, “he answers”; Shaphat, see 3:22.
Michael, “who is like God?”; Meshullam, see 3:19; Sheba, see 1:9; Jorai, perhaps “Yahweh teaches”; Jacan, perhaps “trouble”; Zia, “motion”; Eber, see 1:18.
Abihail, see 2:29; Huri, “linen worker”; Jaroah, perhaps “moon”; Jeshishai, “aged”; Jahdo, “his union”; Buz, “contempt.”
Ahi, “my brother”; Abdiel, “servant of God”; Guni, perhaps “painted.”
This Sharon, “plain,” is east of the Jordan, not the coastal plain.
Jotham reigned in Judah about 750–735 B.C., and Jeroboam II in Israel about 793–753 B.C. Jeroboam means “the people contend” or “may the people multiply.”
Jetur and Naphish, see 1:31; Nodab, “nobility.”
Hebrew “souls of men.” The Septuagint (B text) reads “five thousand camels.”
Manasseh, see 3:13; Baal-hermon, “lord of Hermon”; Senir, the Amorite name for Hermon (Deuteronomy 3:9); Hermon, “sacred mountain.”
Epher, see 1:33; Ishi, see 2:31; Eliel, “my God is God”; Azriel, “my help is God”; Jeremiah, “Yahweh lifts up” or “Yahweh founds”; Hodaviah, see 3:24; Jahdiel, “God makes glad.”

Or “Pul king of Assyria, and the spirit of Tilgath-pilneser.” Pul (Assyrian Pulu) was the Babylonian throne name of Tiglath-pileser III (compare 2 Kings 15:19, 29). Halah, Habor, and Gozan were in northern Mesopotamia (2 Kings 17:6); Hara, uncertain, is not in Kings.

verses.text: The sons of Levi: Gershon, Kohath, and Merari.{a}
The sons of Kohath: Amram, Izhar, Hebron, and Uzziel.{b}
The children of Amram: Aaron, Moses, and Miriam. The sons of Aaron: Nadab, Abihu, Eleazar, and Ithamar.{c}
Eleazar became the father of Phinehas, Phinehas became the father of Abishua,{d}
Abishua became the father of Bukki, Bukki became the father of Uzzi,{e}
Uzzi became the father of Zerahiah, Zerahiah became the father of Meraioth,{f}
Meraioth became the father of Amariah, Amariah became the father of Ahitub,{g}
Ahitub became the father of Zadok, Zadok became the father of Ahimaaz,{h}
Ahimaaz became the father of Azariah, Azariah became the father of Johanan,
and Johanan became the father of Azariah, who performed the priest’s office in the temple that Solomon built in Jerusalem.{i}
Azariah became the father of Amariah, Amariah became the father of Ahitub,
Ahitub became the father of Zadok, Zadok became the father of Shallum,
Shallum became the father of Hilkiah, Hilkiah became the father of Azariah,{j}
Azariah fathered Seraiah, and Seraiah fathered Jehozadak;{k}
and Jehozadak went into captivity when Yahweh carried Judah and Jerusalem away by the hand of Nebuchadnezzar.{l}
The sons of Levi: Gershom, Kohath, and Merari.{m}
These are the names of the sons of Gershom: Libni and Shimei.{n}
The sons of Kohath: Amram, Izhar, Hebron, and Uzziel.
The sons of Merari: Mahli and Mushi. These are the clans of the Levites according to their fathers.{o}
Of Gershom: Libni his son, Jahath his son, Zimmah his son,{p}
Joah his son, Iddo his son, Zerah his son, Jeatherai his son.{q}
The sons of Kohath: Amminadab his son, Korah his son, Assir his son,{r}
Elkanah his son, Ebiasaph his son, Assir his son,{s}
Tahath his son, Uriel his son, Uzziah his son, and Shaul his son.{t}
The sons of Elkanah: Amasai and Ahimoth.{u}
Elkanah: the sons of Elkanah:{v} Zophai his son, Nahath his son,{w}
Eliab his son, Jeroham his son, Elkanah his son.{x}
The sons of Samuel: the firstborn Joel,{y} and the second Abijah.{z}
The sons of Merari: Mahli, Libni his son, Shimei his son, Uzzah his son,{aa}
Shimea his son, Haggiah his son, Asaiah his son.{ab}
These are those whom David set over the service of song in the house of Yahweh, after the ark had a resting place.{ac}
They served with singing in front of the tent of meeting, the tabernacle, until Solomon built Yahweh’s house in Jerusalem, and they carried out their duties following their assigned order.
These are the men who served, with their sons. Of the sons of the Kohathites: Heman the singer, the son of Joel, son of Samuel,{ad}
son of Elkanah, son of Jeroham, son of Eliel, son of Toah,{ae}
son of Zuph, son of Elkanah, son of Mahath, son of Amasai,{af}
son of Elkanah, son of Joel, son of Azariah, son of Zephaniah,{ag}
son of Tahath, son of Assir, son of Ebiasaph, son of Korah,
son of Izhar, son of Kohath, son of Levi, son of Israel.
And his kinsman Asaph, who stood at his right hand: Asaph the son of Berechiah, son of Shimea,{ah}
son of Michael, son of Baaseiah, son of Malchijah,{ai}
son of Ethni, son of Zerah, son of Adaiah,{aj}
son of Ethan, son of Zimmah, son of Shimei,
son of Jahath, son of Gershom, son of Levi.
On the left hand were their kinsmen the sons of Merari: Ethan the son of Kishi, son of Abdi, son of Malluch,{ak}
son of Hashabiah, son of Amaziah, son of Hilkiah,{al}
son of Amzi, son of Bani, son of Shemer,{am}
son of Mahli, son of Mushi, son of Merari, son of Levi.
Their kinsmen the Levites were appointed for all the service of the tabernacle of the house of God.

Aaron and his descendants made offerings on the altar for burnt offerings and on the incense altar, handling all the work in the Most Holy Place and making atonement for Israel, exactly as Moses the servant of God had ordered.
These are the sons of Aaron: Eleazar his son, Phinehas his son, Abishua his son,
Bukki his son, Uzzi his son, Zerahiah his son,
Meraioth his son, Amariah his son, Ahitub his son,
Zadok his son, Ahimaaz his son.
These are their dwelling places according to their encampments within their borders: to the sons of Aaron of the clans of the Kohathites, for theirs was the first lot,{an}
to them they gave Hebron in the land of Judah and its pasture lands around it,
but the fields of the city and its villages they gave to Caleb the son of Jephunneh.
To the sons of Aaron they gave the cities of refuge: Hebron, Libnah with its pasture lands, Jattir, Eshtemoa with its pasture lands,{ao}
Hilen with its pasture lands, Debir with its pasture lands,{ap}
Ashan with its pasture lands, and Beth-shemesh with its pasture lands;{aq}
and from the tribe of Benjamin: Geba with its pasturelands, Alemeth and its pasturelands, and also Anathoth together with its pasturelands. Altogether their clans received thirteen towns.{ar}
The rest of the Kohathites received ten towns by lot from the clans of the half-tribe of Manasseh.{as}
To the sons of Gershom, by their families, thirteen cities were given from the tribe of Issachar, from the tribe of Asher, from the tribe of Naphtali, and from the tribe of Manasseh in Bashan.
To the sons of Merari, by their families, twelve cities were given by lot from the tribe of Reuben, from the tribe of Gad, and from the tribe of Zebulun.
So the Israelites gave the Levites the cities with their pasture lands.
They assigned these towns, which are listed by name, by lot from the tribes of Judah, Simeon, and Benjamin.
Some of the families of the sons of Kohath had cities of their borders from the tribe of Ephraim.
They gave to them the cities of refuge, Shechem in the hill country of Ephraim with its pasture lands, and Gezer with its pasture lands,{at}
Jokmeam with its pasture lands, Beth-horon with its pasture lands,{au}
Aijalon with its pasture lands, and Gath-rimmon with its pasture lands;{av}
and from the half-tribe of Manasseh: Aner with its pasturelands, and also Bileam with its pasturelands. These went to the remaining families of the Kohathites.{aw}
The Gershomites received from the clan of the half-tribe of Manasseh: Golan in Bashan with its pasturelands, and also Ashtaroth with its pasturelands;{ax}
and out of the tribe of Issachar: Kedesh with its pasture lands, Daberath with its pasture lands,{ay}
Ramoth with its pasture lands, and Anem with its pasture lands;{az}
out of the tribe of Asher: Mashal with its pasture lands, Abdon with its pasture lands,{ba}
Hukok with its pasture lands, and Rehob with its pasture lands;{bb}
and out of the tribe of Naphtali: Kedesh in Galilee with its pasture lands, Hammon with its pasture lands, and Kiriathaim with its pasture lands.{bc}
To the rest of the Merarites were given out of the tribe of Zebulun: Rimmono with its pasture lands and Tabor with its pasture lands;{bd}
and across the Jordan from Jericho, east of the Jordan, from the tribe of Reuben: Bezer in the desert and its pasturelands, and Jahzah and its pasturelands,{be}
Kedemoth with its pasture lands, and Mephaath with its pasture lands;{bf}
and out of the tribe of Gad: Ramoth in Gilead with its pasture lands, Mahanaim with its pasture lands,{bg}
Heshbon with its pasture lands, and Jazer with its pasture lands.{bh}

notes.text: Verses 1–15 are 5:27–41 in Hebrew, and verses 16–81 are 6:1–66. Gershon (also Gershom, verse 16), perhaps “a stranger there” (Exodus 2:22); Kohath, perhaps “assembly”; Merari, “bitter.”
Amram, “exalted people”; Izhar, “shining oil”; Hebron, see 2:42; Uzziel, see 4:42.

Aaron, uncertain; Moses, “drawn out” (Exodus 2:10), probably also an Egyptian word for “son”; Miriam, see 4:17; Nadab, see 2:28; Abihu, “he is my father”; Eleazar, “God has helped”; Ithamar, perhaps “island of palms.”
Phinehas, an Egyptian name, “the Nubian”; Abishua, “my father is salvation.”
Bukki, perhaps “proved” or a short form of Bukkiah; Uzzi, “my strength.”
Zerahiah, “Yahweh has dawned”; Meraioth, “rebellious.”
Amariah, “Yahweh has said”; Ahitub, “my brother is good.”
Zadok, “righteous”; Ahimaaz, perhaps “my brother is anger” or “brother of counsel.”
This note may belong to the Azariah of verse 9, who was Solomon’s priest (1 Kings 4:2). The list here also omits several known priests, such as Jehoiada (2 Kings 11) and Uriah (2 Kings 16:10).
Hilkiah, “my portion is Yahweh” (2 Kings 22).
Jehozadak, “Yahweh is righteous”; Seraiah, see 4:13 (2 Kings 25:18).
Nebuchadnezzar, Babylonian Nabu-kudurri-usur, “O Nabu, protect the heir.” The exile was in 586 B.C.
Verse 16 is 6:1 in Hebrew. Gershom, see verse 1.
Libni, “white”; Shimei, see 3:19.
Mahli, “sick” or “shrewd”; Mushi, perhaps “yielding.”
Jahath, see 4:2; Zimmah, “plan, purpose.”
Joah, “Yahweh is brother”; Iddo, perhaps “his witness” or “timely”; Zerah, see 1:37; Jeatherai, uncertain.
Amminadab, see 2:10; here apparently another name for Izhar (verses 2, 38). Korah, see 1:35; Assir, “prisoner.” Compare Exodus 6:21–24, where Assir, Elkanah, and Abiasaph are sons of Korah.
Elkanah, “God has created”; Ebiasaph (Exodus 6:24 Abiasaph), “my father has gathered.”
Tahath, “beneath” or “substitute”; Uriel, “God is my light”; Uzziah, “Yahweh is my strength”; Shaul, see 1:48.
Amasai, “burden-bearer”; Ahimoth, “my brother is death” (compare Mahath, verse 35).
The Hebrew of the opening of this verse is difficult; compare verses 34–35.
Zophai (verse 35 Zuph), “honeycomb”; Nahath (verse 34 Toah), see 1:37.
Eliab (verse 34 Eliel), see 2:13; Jeroham, “he is shown compassion.” The text may have lost “Samuel his son” (compare verse 28 and 1 Samuel 1:1, 20).

“Joel” is supplied from verse 33 and 1 Samuel 8:2, as in some ancient versions. Hebrew “the firstborn Vashni,” a word that may be read as “and the second.” Samuel, perhaps “name of God” or “heard by God” (1 Samuel 1:20).
The Septuagint (B text) reads “Sani the firstborn, and Abia.” Abijah, see 2:24.
Uzzah, “strength.”
Shimea, see 2:13; Haggiah, “feast of Yahweh”; Asaiah, see 4:36.
Ark, see 13:3. Second Samuel 6:17.
Verse 33 is 6:18 in Hebrew. Heman, see 2:6 (a different man); Joel, see 4:35.
Eliel, see 5:24; Toah, “lowly.” Compare verses 26–27.
Zuph, see verse 26; Mahath, “snatching.”
Azariah, see 2:8; Zephaniah, “Yahweh has hidden.”
Asaph, “he gathers”; Berechiah, see 3:20; Shimea, see 2:13.
Michael, see 5:13; Baaseiah, perhaps “work of Yahweh”; Malchijah, “my king is Yahweh.”
Ethni, “gift”; Adaiah, “Yahweh has adorned.”
Ethan, see 2:6 (also called Jeduthun, 16:41; 25:1); Kishi, “snarer” (15:17 Kushaiah); Abdi, “my servant”; Malluch, “counselor” or “king.”
Hashabiah, “Yahweh has reckoned”; Amaziah, see 3:12; Hilkiah, see verse 13.
Amzi, “my strength”; Bani, “built”; Shemer, “guard.”
Verses 54–81 parallel Joshua 21:10–39, with many differences in the names. The Hebrew word for “encampments” can also mean “settlements.”
Libnah, “whiteness”; Jattir, “abundance”; Eshtemoa, see 4:17. In Joshua 21:13 only Hebron among these is a city of refuge; the plural here may be general.
Hilen (Joshua 21:15 Holon), “sand”; Debir, “back part” or “sanctuary.”
Ashan (Joshua 21:16 Ain), see 4:32; Beth-shemesh, “house of the sun.” Joshua 21:16 also lists Juttah.

Joshua 21:17–18 includes Gibeon and names Almon for Alemeth. Geba, “hill”; Alemeth, “covering”; Anathoth, plural of the goddess name Anath, “answers.” The thirteen count implies two cities missing from this list.
Joshua 21:5 reads “out of the clans of the tribe of Ephraim, from the tribe of Dan, and the half-tribe of Manasseh”; the Hebrew here seems to lack the first part.
Joshua 21:21 names only Shechem as a city of refuge. Shechem, “shoulder”; Ephraim, “doubly fruitful”; Gezer, “portion.”
Jokmeam (Joshua 21:22 Kibzaim), “the people will be raised up”; Beth-horon, “house of the hollow.”
Joshua 21:23–24 adds Eltekeh and Gibbethon from Dan. Aijalon, “place of deer”; Gath-rimmon, “winepress of the pomegranate.”
Aner (Joshua 21:25 Taanach), uncertain; Bileam (Joshua Gath-rimmon), perhaps a form of Ibleam.
Golan, perhaps “circuit”; Ashtaroth (Joshua 21:27 Be-eshterah), named after the goddess Astarte.
Kedesh (Joshua 21:28 Kishion), “holy place”; Daberath, “pasture.”
Ramoth (Joshua 21:29 Jarmuth), “heights”; Anem (Joshua En-gannim), “two springs.”
Mashal (Joshua 21:30 Mishal), “entreaty”; Abdon, “servile.”
Hukok (Joshua 21:31 Helkath), “cut, engraved”; Rehob, “broad place.”
Galilee, “circle, district”; Hammon (Joshua 21:32 Hammoth-dor), “warm”; Kiriathaim (Joshua Kartan), “two cities.”
Joshua 21:34–35 lists Jokneam, Kartah, Dimnah, and Nahalal. Rimmono (Joshua 19:13 Rimmon), see 4:32; Tabor, “height.”
Some Hebrew manuscripts of Joshua lack the parallel (Joshua 21:36–37). Jericho, perhaps “moon city”; Jordan, “descender”; Bezer, “fortress”; Jahzah, perhaps “trampled place.”
Kedemoth, “eastern places”; Mephaath, “splendor.”
Ramoth, see verse 73; Mahanaim, “two camps” (Genesis 32:2).
Heshbon, “reckoning”; Jazer, “he helps.”

verses.text: The sons of Issachar: Tola, Puah, Jashub, and Shimron, four.{a}
Tola’s sons were Uzzi, Rephaiah, Jeriel, Jahmai, Ibsam, and Shemuel. They were heads of the families of Tola and brave warriors of their generations. In David’s time their number was 22,600.{b}
The son{c} of Uzzi: Izrahiah. And the sons of Izrahiah: Michael, Obadiah, Joel, and Isshiah, five, all of them chiefs.{d}
With them, by their generations, after their fathers’ houses, were bands of the host for battle, thirty-six thousand, because they had many wives and sons.
Their kinsmen among all the clans of Issachar were mighty warriors, eighty-seven thousand, all enrolled by genealogy.
The sons of Benjamin: Bela, Becher, and Jediael, three.{e}
Bela’s sons were Ezbon, Uzzi, Uzziel, Jerimoth, and Iri, a total of five. These were family heads and brave warriors, and their family records list 22,034.{f}
The sons of Becher: Zemirah, Joash, Eliezer, Elioenai, Omri, Jeremoth, Abijah, Anathoth, and Alemeth. All these were the sons of Becher.{g}
Their family records, listed by generation as family heads and brave warriors, show 20,200.
The son{h} of Jediael: Bilhan. And the sons of Bilhan: Jeush, Benjamin, Ehud, Chenaanah, Zethan, Tarshish, and Ahishahar.{i}
All these were the sons of Jediael according to the heads of their fathers’ houses, mighty warriors, seventeen thousand two hundred, able to go out to war.
Shuppim also and Huppim were sons of Ir, and Hushim was son{j} of Aher.{k}
The sons of Naphtali: Jahziel, Guni, Jezer, and Shallum, sons of Bilhah.{l}
Manasseh’s descendants: Asriel, whom his Aramean concubine bore, and she also bore Machir, the father of Gilead.{m}
Machir found wives for Huppim and Shuppim. His sister’s name was Maacah. Another descendant was named Zelophehad, who had only daughters.{n}
And Maacah the wife of Machir bore a son, and she called his name Peresh; and the name of his brother was Sheresh, and his sons were Ulam and Rakem.{o}
The son{p} of Ulam: Bedan. These were the sons of Gilead the son of Machir, son of Manasseh.{q}
And his sister Hammolecheth bore Ishhod, Abiezer, and Mahlah.{r}
The sons of Shemida were Ahian, Shechem, Likhi, and Aniam.{s}
The sons of Ephraim: Shuthelah, and Bered his son, Tahath his son, Eleadah his son, Tahath his son,{t}
Zabad his son, Shuthelah his son, and Ezer and Elead, whom the men of Gath who were born in the land killed, because they came down to take their livestock.{u}
And Ephraim their father mourned many days, and his brothers came to comfort him.
And he went in to his wife, and she conceived and bore a son, and he called his name Beriah, because disaster had come upon his house.{v}
His daughter Sheerah built Beth-horon, the lower and the upper, and also Uzzen-sheerah.{w}
Rephah was his son, and Resheph his son, Telah his son, Tahan his son,{x}
Ladan his son, Ammihud his son, Elishama his son,{y}
Nun{z} his son, Joshua his son.{aa}
Their lands and settlements included Bethel and its villages, Naaran to the east, Gezer and its villages to the west, Shechem and its villages, and Ayyah{ab} and its villages;{ac}
and along the borders of Manasseh’s descendants, Beth-shean, Taanach, Megiddo, and Dor, each with its villages. The descendants of Joseph son of Israel lived in these towns.{ad}
The sons of Asher: Imnah, Ishvah, Ishvi, and Beriah, and Serah their sister.{ae}
The sons of Beriah: Heber and Malchiel, who was the father of Birzaith.{af}
Heber became the father of Japhlet, Shomer, Hotham, and Shua their sister.{ag}
The sons of Japhlet: Pasach, Bimhal, and Ashvath. These are the sons of Japhlet.{ah}
The sons of Shemer:{ai} Ahi, Rohgah, Jehubbah,{aj} and Aram.{ak}
The sons of Helem his brother: Zophah, Imna, Shelesh, and Amal.{al}
The sons of Zophah: Suah, Harnepher, Shual, Beri, Imrah,{am}
Bezer, Hod, Shamma, Shilshah, Ithran, and Beera.{an}
The sons of Jether: Jephunneh, Pispa, and Ara.{ao}
The sons of Ulla: Arah, Hanniel, and Rizia.{ap}
All these were descendants of Asher, heads of fathers’ houses, choice mighty warriors, chiefs of the princes. Their number enrolled by genealogy for service in war was twenty-six thousand men.

notes.text: Issachar, see 2:1; Tola, “worm” (crimson dye); Puah, perhaps “madder” (a red dye); Jashub, “he returns” (Hebrew written text Jashib); Shimron, “watch.”
Rephaiah, see 3:21; Jeriel, “founded by God”; Jahmai, perhaps “protector”; Ibsam, “fragrant”; Shemuel, the same name as Samuel (6:28).
Hebrew “sons.”
Izrahiah, “Yahweh shines”; Michael, see 5:13; Obadiah, see 3:21; Isshiah, “Yahweh lends.” Five includes Izrahiah.
The lists of Benjamin’s sons differ: compare Genesis 46:21, Numbers 26:38–41, and 8:1–5. Bela, see 1:43; Becher, “young camel”; Jediael, “known by God.”
Ezbon, uncertain; Uzziel, see 4:42; Jerimoth, “heights”; Iri, “my city” or “watchful.”
Zemirah, “song”; Joash, see 3:11; Eliezer, “my God is help”; Omri, perhaps “servant of Yahweh” or “life”; Jeremoth, “heights”; Anathoth and Alemeth, see 6:60.
Hebrew “sons.”
Bilhan, see 1:42; Jeush, see 1:35; Ehud, perhaps “united”; Chenaanah, “toward Canaan”; Zethan, “olive tree”; Tarshish, see 1:7; Ahishahar, “brother of the dawn.”
Hebrew “sons.”

Shuppim and Huppim (compare Genesis 46:21, Muppim and Huppim), “serpents” and “coverings”; Ir, “city” (perhaps Iri, verse 7); Hushim, “hasty ones”; Aher, “another.” The text may be damaged; some scholars think a list for Dan stood here (compare Genesis 46:23, “the son of Dan: Hushim”).
Genesis 46:24 and Numbers 26:48 read Jahzeel and Shillem. Jahziel, “God apportions”; Guni, see 5:15; Jezer, “form, purpose”; Shallum, see 2:40; Bilhah, “faltering” (Genesis 30:3–8).
The Hebrew of verses 14–15 is difficult. Asriel, “God has bound”; Aramean, of Aram (Syria). Machir and Gilead, see 2:21.
Numbers 26:33 and 27:1 make Zelophehad, “shadow of dread” (meaning uncertain), a great-grandson of Machir. Here “his sister” and “the second” have no clear antecedent. Maacah, see 2:48.
Peresh, “dung” or “separation”; Sheresh, “root”; Ulam, “porch” or “first”; Rakem, see Rekem, 2:43.
Hebrew “sons.”
Bedan, perhaps “son of judgment” (compare 1 Samuel 12:11, where some read Abdon or Barak).
Hammolecheth, “the queen”; Ishhod, “man of majesty”; Abiezer, “my father is help”; Mahlah, “sickness” or “dancer.”
Shemida, “the name knows”; Ahian, “brotherly”; Shechem, see 6:67; Likhi, “learned”; Aniam, “I am a people.”
Shuthelah, uncertain; Bered, “hail”; Tahath, see 6:24; Eleadah, “God has adorned.”

Gath, “winepress,” a Philistine city. Zabad, see 2:36; Ezer, see 1:38; Elead, “God has testified.” The raid seems to come from Ephraim’s own lifetime (verse 22), though the list of descendants is long.
Beriah sounds like Hebrew bera‘ah, “in disaster.”
Sheerah, “kinswoman”; Beth-horon, see 6:68; Uzzen-sheerah, “ear (point of land) of Sheerah.”
Rephah, “riches”; Resheph, “flame” (also a god’s name); Telah, “fracture”; Tahan, “camp.”
Ladan, uncertain; Ammihud, “my kinsman is majesty”; Elishama, see 2:41.
Hebrew “Non.”
Nun, “fish” (or “continuance”); Joshua, “Yahweh is salvation.”
So the Leningrad Codex; other Hebrew manuscripts read “Azzah,” that is, Gaza, which is unlikely here.
Bethel, “house of God”; Naaran, “youthful”; Gezer, see 6:67; Ayyah, “ruin” (perhaps Ai).
Beth-shean, “house of quiet”; Taanach, perhaps “sandy soil”; Megiddo, perhaps “place of troops”; Dor, “dwelling.” Joseph, see 2:2.
Compare Genesis 46:17 and Numbers 26:44–46. Asher, see 2:2; Imnah, “good fortune” or “right hand”; Ishvah and Ishvi, “level”; Beriah, see verse 23; Serah, “abundance.”
Heber, see 4:18; Malchiel, “my king is God”; Birzaith, perhaps “well of olives.”
Japhlet, “he delivers”; Shomer (verse 34 Shemer), “guard”; Hotham (verse 35 Helem), “seal”; Shua, see 2:3 (Bath-shua).
Pasach, “divider”; Bimhal, “son of circumcision”; Ashvath, uncertain.
Hebrew Shamer; see Shomer, verse 32.
So the Hebrew margin (Qere); the written text reads “and Hubbah.”
Ahi, see 5:15 (or “his brother”); Rohgah, “outcry”; Jehubbah, “hidden”; Aram, see 1:17.
Helem, “strength” or “hammer”; Zophah, perhaps “jug”; Imna, “he holds back”; Shelesh, “triad”; Amal, “toil.”
Suah, “sweeping”; Harnepher, an Egyptian name, perhaps “Horus is good”; Shual, “fox”; Beri, “my well”; Imrah, perhaps “he rebels.”
Bezer, see 6:78; Hod, “majesty”; Shamma, “desolation”; Shilshah, “triad”; Ithran, see 1:41 (perhaps Jether, verse 38); Beera, “well.”
Jether, see 2:17; Jephunneh, see 4:15; Pispa and Ara, uncertain.
Ulla, “yoke”; Arah, “wayfarer”; Hanniel, “grace of God”; Rizia, “delight.”

verses.text: Benjamin became the father of Bela his firstborn, of Ashbel the second, of Aharah the third,{a}
Nohah the fourth, and Rapha the fifth.{b}
And Bela had sons: Addar, Gera, Abihud,{c}
Abishua, Naaman, Ahoah,{d}
Gera, Shephuphan, and Huram.{e}
These are the sons of Ehud; these are heads of fathers’ houses of those who lived in Geba, and they were carried away captive to Manahath:{f}
and Naaman, Ahijah, and Gera; he carried them away,{g} and he became the father of Uzza and Ahihud.{h}
And Shaharaim became the father of sons in the country of Moab after he had sent away Hushim and Baara his wives.{i}
By Hodesh his wife he became the father of Jobab, Zibia, Mesha, Malcam,{j}
Jeuz, Sachia, and Mirmah. These were his sons, heads of fathers’ houses.{k}
By Hushim he had became the father of Abitub and Elpaal.{l}
The sons of Elpaal: Eber, Misham, and Shemed, who built Ono and Lod with its towns,{m}
and Beriah and Shema, who were heads of families among the people of Aijalon and who drove out the people of Gath;{n}
and Ahio, Shashak, and Jeremoth.{o}
Zebadiah, Arad, Eder,{p}
Michael, Ishpah, and Joha were sons of Beriah.{q}
Zebadiah, Meshullam, Hizki, Heber,{r}
Ishmerai, Izliah, and Jobab were sons of Elpaal.{s}
Jakim, Zichri, Zabdi,{t}
Elienai, Zillethai, Eliel,{u}
Adaiah, Beraiah, and Shimrath were sons of Shimei.{v}
Ishpan, Eber, and Eliel;{w}
Abdon, Zichri, and Hanan;{x}
Hananiah, Elam, and Anthothijah;{y}
and Iphdeiah and Penuel{z} were the sons of Shashak.{aa}
Shamsherai, Shehariah, Athaliah,{ab}
Jaareshiah, Elijah, and Zichri were sons of Jeroham.{ac}
These were heads of fathers’ houses through their generations, chief men; these lived at Jerusalem.
In Gibeon lived the father of Gibeon,{ad} and the name of his wife was Maacah.{ae}
and his firstborn son Abdon, and Zur, Kish, Baal,{af} Nadab,{ag}
Gedor, Ahio, and Zecher.{ah}
Mikloth became the father of Shimeah. They also lived with their brothers in Jerusalem, over against their brothers.{ai}
Ner was the father of Kish. Kish was the father of Saul, and Saul had sons named Jonathan, Malchi-shua, Abinadab, and Esh-baal.{aj}
The son of Jonathan was Merib-baal; and Merib-baal became the father of Micah.{ak}
The sons of Micah: Pithon, Melech, Tarea, and Ahaz.{al}
Ahaz became the father of Jehoaddah, and Jehoaddah of Alemeth, Azmaveth, and Zimri; and Zimri of Moza.{am}
Moza became the father of Binea; Raphah was his son, Eleasah his son, Azel his son.{an}
Azel had six sons named Azrikam, Bocheru, Ishmael, Sheariah, Obadiah, and Hanan. These were all the sons of Azel.{ao}
The sons of Eshek his brother: Ulam his firstborn, Jeush the second, and Eliphelet the third.{ap}
The sons of Ulam were mighty warriors, archers, and had many sons and grandsons, one hundred and fifty. All these were of the descendants of Benjamin.

notes.text: Compare 7:6–12. Benjamin, see 2:2; Bela, see 1:43; Ashbel, perhaps “man of Baal”; Aharah, perhaps “after a brother” (Genesis 46:21 Ehi; Numbers 26:38 Ahiram).
Nohah, “rest”; Rapha, “he has healed” or “giant.”
Addar, “threshing floor” or “glorious” (Numbers 26:40 Ard); Gera, “grain”; Abihud, “my father is majesty.” Or “Gera the father of Ehud” (compare verse 6 and Judges 3:15).
Abishua, see 6:4; Naaman, “pleasantness”; Ahoah, “brotherly.”
Shephuphan, “serpent”; Huram, “noble.”
Ehud, see 7:10; Geba, see 6:60; Manahath, see 1:40.
Or “Gera, that is, Heglam.” The Hebrew word heglam can be read as “he exiled them” or as a name.
Ahijah, see 2:25; Uzza, “strength”; Ahihud, “brother of majesty.”
Shaharaim, “double dawn”; Moab, perhaps “from father” (Genesis 19:37); Hushim, see 7:12; Baara, perhaps “burning.”
Hodesh, “new moon”; Jobab, see 1:23; Zibia, “gazelle”; Mesha, see 2:42; Malcam, “their king.”
Jeuz, “counselor”; Sachia, uncertain; Mirmah, “deceit.”
Abitub, “my father is good”; Elpaal, “God is maker.”
Eber, see 1:18; Misham, “their cleansing”; Shemed, “destruction”; Ono, “strength”; Lod, later Lydda.
Beriah, see 7:23; Shema, see 2:43; Aijalon, see 6:69; Gath, see 7:21.
Or “and their brothers were Shashak and Jeremoth” (so the Septuagint, “and his brothers”). Ahio, “brotherly”; Shashak, uncertain; Jeremoth, see 7:8.
Zebadiah, “Yahweh has given”; Arad, “wild donkey”; Eder, “flock.”
Michael, see 5:13; Ishpah, “bald”; Joha, perhaps “Yahweh is living.”
Meshullam, see 3:19; Hizki, a short form of Hezekiah; Heber, see 4:18.
Ishmerai, “Yahweh keeps”; Izliah, “Yahweh draws out”; Jobab, see 1:23.
Jakim, “he raises up”; Zichri, “my remembrance”; Zabdi, “my gift.”
Elienai, short for Elioenai (3:23); Zillethai, “shadow”; Eliel, see 5:24.
Adaiah, see 6:41; Beraiah, “Yahweh has created”; Shimrath, “guarding”; Shimei, see 3:19.
Ishpan, “he hides”; Eliel, see 5:24.
Abdon, see 6:74; Hanan, “gracious.”
Hananiah, see 3:19; Elam, see 1:17; Anthothijah, “of Anathoth” (6:60).
Hebrew Penuel; some read “Peniel.” See 4:4.
Iphdeiah, “Yahweh redeems.”
Shamsherai, uncertain; Shehariah, “Yahweh is dawn”; Athaliah, “Yahweh is exalted.”
Jaareshiah, uncertain; Elijah, “my God is Yahweh”; Jeroham, see 6:27.
Verses 29–38 are repeated in 9:35–44, which names this father of Gibeon as Jeiel. Gibeon, “hill city.”
Maacah, see 2:48.
The Septuagint (after Nadab) and 9:36 add “Ner.”
Zur, “rock”; Kish, perhaps “bow” or “gift”; Baal, see 4:33; Nadab, see 2:28.
Gedor, see 4:4; Ahio, see verse 14; Zecher, “memorial” (9:37 Zechariah).
Mikloth, “staffs”; Shimeah (9:38 Shimeam), see Shimea, 2:13.

First Samuel 14:49 lists Saul’s sons as Jonathan, Ishvi, and Malchi-shua; 31:2 adds Abinadab. Esh-baal, “man of Baal” (Baal meaning “lord”), is called Ish-bosheth, “man of shame,” in 2 Samuel 2:8; later scribes replaced “Baal” with bosheth, “shame.” Ner, “lamp”; Saul, see 5:10; Jonathan, see 2:32; Malchi-shua, “my king is salvation”; Abinadab, see 2:13. The Septuagint (B text) reads “Asabal.”
Merib-baal, perhaps “Baal contends” or “hero of Baal,” is called Mephibosheth, “from the mouth of shame,” in 2 Samuel 4:4 and 9:6. Micah, see 5:5 (2 Samuel 9:12, Mica).
Pithon, uncertain; Melech, “king”; Tarea (9:41 Tahrea), uncertain; Ahaz, see 3:13.
Jehoaddah (9:42 Jarah), “Yahweh has adorned”; Alemeth, see 6:60; Azmaveth, “death is strong”; Zimri, see 2:6; Moza, see 2:46.
Binea, uncertain; Raphah (9:43 Rephaiah), see Rapha, verse 2; Eleasah, see 2:39; Azel, “noble.”
Azrikam, see 3:23; Bocheru, “firstborn” (or read “his firstborn”); Ishmael, see 1:28; Sheariah, “Yahweh has esteemed”; Obadiah, see 3:21; Hanan, see verse 23.
Eshek, “oppression”; Ulam, see 7:16; Jeush, see 1:35; Eliphelet, see 3:6.

verses.text: So all Israel was reckoned by genealogies, and see, they are written in the Book of the Kings of Israel. Judah was carried away captive to Babylon for their unfaithfulness.{a}
Now the first inhabitants who lived again in their possessions in their cities were Israel, the priests, the Levites, and the temple servants.{b}
Some of the people of Judah, of Benjamin, and of Ephraim and Manasseh lived in Jerusalem:{c}
Uthai son of Ammihud, son of Omri, son of Imri, son of Bani, a descendant of Perez son of Judah.{d}
Of the Shilonites: Asaiah the firstborn, and his sons.{e}
From the descendants of Zerah: Jeuel and his relatives, 690 in all.{f}
Of the sons of Benjamin: Sallu the son of Meshullam, son of Hodaviah, son of Hassenuah,{g}
Ibneiah the son of Jeroham, Elah the son of Uzzi, son of Michri, and Meshullam the son of Shephatiah, son of Reuel, son of Ibnijah;{h}
and their kinsmen according to their generations, nine hundred and fifty-six. All these men were heads of fathers’ houses according to their fathers’ houses.
Of the priests: Jedaiah, Jehoiarib, Jachin,{i}
and Azariah son of Hilkiah, son of Meshullam, son of Zadok, son of Meraioth, son of Ahitub, the official in charge of God’s house;{j}
and Adaiah the son of Jeroham, son of Pashhur, son of Malchijah, and Maasai the son of Adiel, son of Jahzerah, son of Meshullam, son of Meshillemith, son of Immer;{k}
and their relatives, family heads, 1,760 in all, who were very capable men for the work of serving in God’s house.
Of the Levites: Shemaiah the son of Hasshub, son of Azrikam, son of Hashabiah, of the sons of Merari;{l}
and Bakbakkar, Heresh, Galal, and Mattaniah the son of Mica, son of Zichri, son of Asaph;{m}
and Obadiah the son of Shemaiah, son of Galal, son of Jeduthun, and Berechiah the son of Asa, son of Elkanah, who lived in the villages of the Netophathites.{n}
The gatekeepers: Shallum, Akkub, Talmon, Ahiman, and their brothers; Shallum was the chief,{o}
who until then had waited in the king’s gate eastward. They were gatekeepers for the camp of the sons of Levi.

Shallum the son of Kore, son of Ebiasaph, son of Korah, and his brothers of his father’s house, the Korahites, were over the work of the service, keepers of the thresholds of the tent; and their fathers had been over the camp of Yahweh, keepers of the entry.{p}
And Phinehas the son of Eleazar was chief over them in time past; Yahweh was with him.
Zechariah son of Meshelemiah was the gatekeeper at the entrance of the tent of meeting.{q}
The total number chosen to be gatekeepers at the thresholds was 212. They were listed by family records in their villages. David and Samuel the seer had appointed them to their trusted positions.
So they and their children had the oversight of the gates of the house of Yahweh, the house of the tent, by watches.
On the four sides were the gatekeepers, toward the east, west, north, and south.
And their kinsmen in their villages were to come in every seven days, from time to time, to be with them;
for the four chief gatekeepers, who were Levites, were in an office of trust, and they were in charge of the chambers and the treasuries of the house of God.
They stayed the night around God’s house, since guarding it was their responsibility, and they had to open it each morning.
Some of them had charge of the vessels of service; for by count they were brought in, and by count they were taken out.
Others were appointed over the furnishings and over all the holy vessels, and over the fine flour, the wine, the oil, the frankincense, and the spices.
And some of the sons of the priests mixed the ointment of the spices.
Mattithiah, one of the Levites, the firstborn of Shallum the Korahite, was in charge by trust of making the flat cakes.{r}
And some of their kinsmen of the Kohathites were in charge of the showbread, to prepare it every Sabbath.{s}
These were the singers, family heads of the Levites. They stayed in rooms of the temple and had no other duties, because they were on duty both day and night.
These were heads of fathers’ houses of the Levites, according to their generations, chief men. These lived in Jerusalem.
Jeiel{t} the father of Gibeon settled in Gibeon; the name of his wife was Maacah.
His firstborn son was Abdon, then Zur, Kish, Baal, Ner, Nadab,
Gedor, Ahio, Zechariah, and Mikloth.
Mikloth became the father of Shimeam. They also lived with their brothers in Jerusalem, over against their brothers.
Ner was the father of Kish. Kish was the father of Saul, and Saul had sons named Jonathan, Malchi-shua, Abinadab, and Esh-baal.
The son of Jonathan was Merib-baal; and Merib-baal{u} became the father of Micah.
The sons of Micah: Pithon, Melech, Tahrea, and Ahaz.{v}
Ahaz fathered Jarah, and Jarah fathered Alemeth, Azmaveth, and Zimri, and Zimri fathered Moza.{w}
Moza became the father of Binea; Rephaiah was his son, Eleasah his son, Azel his son.
Azel had six sons named Azrikam, Bocheru, Ishmael, Sheariah, Obadiah, and Hanan. These were Azel’s sons.{x}

notes.text: Or “written in the Book of the Kings of Israel and Judah, and they were carried into exile.” The Septuagint reads “the book of the kings of Israel and Judah.” Babylon, Hebrew Babel (compare Genesis 11:9).
Hebrew Nethinim, “those given.” Verses 2–17 have a close parallel in Nehemiah 11:3–19.
Ephraim, see 6:67; Manasseh, see 3:13; Jerusalem, perhaps “foundation of Shalem (peace).”
Uthai, perhaps “Yahweh has helped”; Ammihud, see 7:26; Omri, see 7:8; Imri, “eloquent”; Bani, see 6:46; Perez, see 2:4.
Shilonites, probably of Shelah (2:3; Numbers 26:20), rather than of the town of Shiloh. Asaiah, see 4:36.
Jeuel, perhaps “God sweeps away” (a form of Jeiel). Zerah, see 2:4.
Sallu, perhaps “weighed”; Meshullam, see 3:19; Hodaviah, see 3:24; Hassenuah, “the hated one.”
Ibneiah, “Yahweh builds”; Jeroham, see 6:27; Elah, see 1:52; Uzzi, see 6:5; Michri, perhaps “purchase price”; Shephatiah, see 3:3; Reuel, see 1:35; Ibnijah, “Yahweh builds.”
Jedaiah, see 4:37; Jehoiarib, “Yahweh contends”; Jachin, “he establishes.” Compare 24:7, 17.
Nehemiah 11:11 reads Seraiah. Hilkiah, Zadok, Meraioth, Ahitub, see 6:4–13.
Adaiah, see 6:41; Pashhur, uncertain, perhaps Egyptian; Malchijah, see 6:40; Maasai, “work of Yahweh”; Adiel, see 4:36; Jahzerah, uncertain; Meshillemith, “recompense”; Immer, “lamb.”
Shemaiah, see 3:22; Hasshub, “considerate”; Azrikam, see 3:23; Hashabiah, see 6:45.
Bakbakkar, uncertain; Heresh, “craftsman”; Galal, “rolling”; Mattaniah, “gift of Yahweh”; Mica, see Micah, 5:5; Zichri, see 8:19; Asaph, see 6:39.
Jeduthun, perhaps “praising” (see 16:41); Berechiah, see 3:20; Asa, see 3:10; Elkanah, see 6:23; Netophathites, see 2:54.
Shallum, see 2:40; Akkub, see 3:24; Talmon, “oppressor” or “brightness”; Ahiman, “my brother is a gift.”
Kore, “partridge” or “caller”; Ebiasaph, see 6:23; Korah, see 1:35.
Zechariah, see 5:7; Meshelemiah, “Yahweh repays.”
Mattithiah, “gift of Yahweh.” The flat cakes were baked on a griddle (Leviticus 2:5).
Hebrew “bread of the rows,” the bread laid out before Yahweh (Leviticus 24:5–9). Sabbath, “rest.”
So the Hebrew margin (Qere); the written text reads “Jeuel.” Verses 35–44 repeat 8:29–38.
The second time the Hebrew reads “Meri-baal.”
“And Ahaz” is supplied from 8:35; it is not in the Hebrew or the Septuagint (B text) here. Tahrea, see Tarea, 8:35.
Jarah, “honeycomb” (8:36 Jehoaddah); for the others see 8:36.
Compare 8:38. Shimeam (verse 38), see Shimeah, 8:32; Rephaiah, see 3:21.

verses.text: Now the Philistines fought against Israel, and the men of Israel fled before the Philistines and fell slain on Mount Gilboa.{a}
The Philistines closed in on Saul and his sons, and they killed Saul’s sons Jonathan, Abinadab, and Malchi-shua.
The fighting went sore against Saul; the archers overtook him, and he was wounded by them.

Then Saul said to his armor-bearer, “Draw your sword and thrust me through with it, lest these uncircumcised men come and make sport of me.” But his armor-bearer would not, for he was greatly afraid. So Saul took the sword and fell on it.
When his armor-bearer saw that Saul was dead, he likewise fell on the sword and died.
So Saul died, and his three sons, and all his house died together.{b}
When all the men of Israel who were in the valley saw that they had fled, and that Saul and his sons were dead, they abandoned their cities and fled; and the Philistines came and lived in them.
The next day, when the Philistines came to strip the slain, they found Saul and his sons fallen on Mount Gilboa.
They stripped him and took his head and his armor, and sent into the land of the Philistines all around, to carry the tidings to their idols and to the people.
They put his armor in the house of their gods, and fastened his skull in the house of Dagon.{c}
When all Jabesh-gilead heard all that the Philistines had done to Saul,{d}
all the valiant men arose and took away the body of Saul and the bodies of his sons, and brought them to Jabesh. They buried their bones under the oak{e} in Jabesh, and fasted seven days.
So Saul died for his unfaithfulness that he committed against Yahweh, because he did not keep the word of Yahweh, and also because he consulted a medium, seeking guidance,{f}
and did not seek guidance from Yahweh. Therefore he put him to death and turned the kingdom over to David the son of Jesse.{g}

notes.text: Verses 1–12 parallel 1 Samuel 31:1–13. Philistines, a people of the coast, perhaps “wanderers”; Gilboa, perhaps “bubbling spring.”

First Samuel 31:6 reads “his armor-bearer and all his men died together that day.” Chronicles makes the end of Saul’s dynasty explicit, though a son, Esh-baal (Ish-bosheth), survived (8:33; 2 Samuel 2:8).
According to 1 Samuel 31:10, the Philistines placed his armor in the temple of the Ashtaroth and nailed his body to the wall of Beth-shan. Dagon was a Philistine god of grain or of fish.
Jabesh-gilead, “dry place of Gilead.”
First Samuel 31:13 reads “under the tamarisk tree.” Chronicles also omits the burning of the bodies (1 Samuel 31:12).
See 1 Samuel 13:13–14; 15:22–23; 28:6–19. Verses 13–14 have no parallel in Samuel. Saul is said not to have sought Yahweh, though 1 Samuel 28:6 says Yahweh did not answer him.
David, see 2:15; Jesse, see 2:12.

verses.text: Then all Israel gathered to David at Hebron, saying, “Look, we are your bone and your flesh.{a}

In times past, even when Saul was king, it was you who led Israel out and brought them in. And Yahweh your God said to you, ‘You shall shepherd my people Israel, and you shall be prince over my people Israel.’”

So all the elders of Israel came to the king at Hebron, and David made a covenant with them at Hebron before Yahweh. And they anointed David king over Israel, according to the word of Yahweh by Samuel.{b}
David and all Israel went to Jerusalem, that is, Jebus, where the Jebusites, the inhabitants of the land, were.{c}
The inhabitants of Jebus said to David, “You will not come in here.” Nevertheless David took the stronghold of Zion, that is, the city of David.{d}
David had said, “Whoever is first to attack the Jebusites will be made chief and commander.” Joab son of Zeruiah went up first, and so he became the chief.{e}
David dwelt in the stronghold; for this reason they called it the city of David.
He built up the city around it, from the Millo to the surrounding wall, and Joab restored the rest of the city.{f}
And David became greater and greater, for Yahweh of Armies was with him.{g}
These were the leaders among David’s warriors, who stood firmly with him in his kingdom, along with all Israel, to make him king, as Yahweh had promised concerning Israel.{h}
This is the list of David’s mighty men: Jashobeam, a Hachmonite, chief of the thirty;{i} he lifted up his spear against three hundred whom he killed at one time.{j}
After him was Eleazar the son of Dodo, the Ahohite; he was one of the three mighty men.{k}
He was with David at Pas-dammim, and there the Philistines were gathered together to battle, where was a plot of ground full of barley; and the people fled from before the Philistines.{l}
But they took their stand in the middle of the plot and defended it, and struck down the Philistines; and Yahweh saved them by a great victory.
Three of the thirty chiefs went down to the rock to David, to the cave of Adullam, while the army of the Philistines was encamped in the Valley of Rephaim.{m}
David was then in the stronghold, and the garrison of the Philistines was then at Bethlehem.
David was thirsty and said, “If only someone would bring me a drink of water from the well by the gate of Bethlehem!”

So the three broke through the Philistine camp and drew water from Bethlehem’s well, the one by the gate. They carried it back to David, but he would not drink it. He poured it out before Yahweh as an offering

and said, “May my God keep me from doing this! Can I drink the blood of these men who risked their lives? They risked their lives to bring it.” So he would not drink it. Such were the deeds of the three warriors.
Abishai, Joab’s brother, was the leader of the three.{n} He swung his spear against three hundred men and killed them, and he earned a reputation among the three.
Of the three he was more honored than the two,{o} and he was made their captain; however, he did not attain to the first three.
Benaiah son of Jehoiada from Kabzeel was a brave man who did great deeds. He killed two sons of Ariel{p} of Moab, and he went down into a pit and killed a lion on a snowy day.{q}

He also struck down an Egyptian of great height, seven and a half feet tall.{r} The Egyptian held a spear as thick as a weaver’s beam, but Benaiah approached him with a club, tore the spear out of the Egyptian’s grip, and killed him with it.
Such were the deeds of Benaiah son of Jehoiada, who earned a name along with the three warriors.
He was honored among the thirty, but he did not attain to the three. And David set him over his bodyguard.
The mighty men of the armies were Asahel the brother of Joab, Elhanan the son of Dodo of Bethlehem,{s}
Shammoth the Harorite, Helez the Pelonite,{t}
Ira the son of Ikkesh the Tekoite, Abiezer the Anathothite,{u}
Sibbecai the Hushathite, Ilai the Ahohite,{v}
Maharai from Netophah, and Heled son of Baanah from Netophah,{w}
Ithai son of Ribai from Gibeah of the Benjaminites, and Benaiah from Pirathon,{x}
Hurai of the brooks of Gaash, Abiel the Arbathite,{y}
Azmaveth the Baharumite, Eliahba the Shaalbonite,{z}
the sons of Hashem the Gizonite, Jonathan the son of Shagee the Hararite,{aa}
Ahiam son of Sachar the Hararite, Eliphal son of Ur,{ab}
Hepher the Mecherathite, Ahijah the Pelonite,{ac}
Hezro from Carmel, and Naarai son of Ezbai,{ad}
Joel, Nathan’s brother, and Mibhar son of Hagri,{ae}
Zelek from Ammon, and Naharai from Beeroth, who carried the armor of Joab son of Zeruiah,{af}
Ira from the Ithrites, and Gareb from the Ithrites,{ag}
Uriah from the Hittites, and Zabad son of Ahlai,{ah}
Adina son of Shiza, a Reubenite who led the Reubenites, along with thirty men who were with him,{ai}
Hanan the son of Maacah, and Joshaphat the Mithnite,{aj}
Uzzia the Ashterathite, Shama and Jeiel the sons of Hotham the Aroerite,{ak}
Jediael the son of Shimri, and Joha his brother, the Tizite,{al}
Eliel the Mahavite, and Jeribai and Joshaviah the sons of Elnaam, and Ithmah the Moabite,{am}
Eliel, Obed, and Jaasiel the Mezobaite.{an}

notes.text: Verses 1–9 parallel 2 Samuel 5:1–10. Chronicles omits David’s seven years as king over Judah alone (2 Samuel 2–4).
See 1 Samuel 16:1–13.
Jebus, perhaps “trodden down”; compare 1:14. Second Samuel 5:6 says “the king and his men.”
Zion, perhaps “fortress” or “dry place.” Chronicles omits the saying about the blind and the lame (2 Samuel 5:6, 8).
Second Samuel 5:8 does not name Joab here. Joab, see 2:16.
Millo means “filling,” probably a terrace or earthwork.
Hebrew Yahweh Tseba’oth, often rendered “Yahweh of hosts”: Yahweh as commander of the armies of heaven and of Israel. This is its first appearance in this book.
Verses 10–41 parallel 2 Samuel 23:8–39; verses 41b–47 are found only in Chronicles.

So the written Hebrew text (Ketiv) and the Septuagint; the Hebrew margin (Qere) reads “the officers.” Second Samuel 23:8 calls him Josheb-basshebeth (perhaps a scribal change of Ish-baal) and “chief of the three.” Jashobeam, “the people will return”; Hachmonite, “wise.”
Second Samuel 23:8 reads “eight hundred.” The Septuagint (B text) here also reads “three hundred.”
Eleazar, see 6:3; Dodo, “his beloved”; Ahohite, of Ahoah (8:4).

Pas-dammim (1 Samuel 17:1 Ephes-dammim), “boundary of blood.” Here Chronicles passes from Eleazar’s deed to that of Shammah (2 Samuel 23:11–12), apparently because a line dropped out; in Samuel the field was full of lentils.
Or “Three of the thirty, the chiefs”; 2 Samuel 23:13. Adullam, perhaps “refuge”; Rephaim, “ghosts” or “giants.”
So the Hebrew; the Syriac reads “the thirty” (also in verse 21 and 2 Samuel 23:18). Abishai, see 2:16.
Or “Of the three he was doubly honored.”
Ariel, “lion of God”; Hebrew “two Ariel of Moab,” perhaps meaning “two champions.”
Benaiah, see 4:36; Jehoiada, “Yahweh knows”; Kabzeel, “God gathers.”
Hebrew “five cubits” (about 2.3 meters). Second Samuel 23:21 does not give his height.
Elhanan, “God is gracious”; Asahel, see 2:16.

Second Samuel 23:25 reads “Shammah the Harodite” and adds “Elika the Harodite.” Shammoth, “desolations”; Harorite, perhaps from Harod (“trembling”); Helez, see 2:39; Pelonite, uncertain (2 Samuel 23:26 Paltite).
Ira, “watchful”; Ikkesh, “perverse”; Tekoite, of Tekoa (2:24); Abiezer, see 7:18; Anathothite, of Anathoth (6:60).
Sibbecai (2 Samuel 23:27 Mebunnai), perhaps “Yahweh has interwoven”; Hushathite, of Hushah (4:4); Ilai (2 Samuel 23:28 Zalmon), uncertain.
Maharai, “hasty”; Heled (2 Samuel 23:29 Heleb), “duration”; Baanah, perhaps “son of affliction.”
Ithai (2 Samuel 23:29 Ittai), uncertain; Ribai, “Yahweh contends”; Gibeah, “hill”; Pirathonite, of Pirathon (Judges 12:15).
Hurai (2 Samuel 23:30 Hiddai), uncertain; Gaash, “quaking”; Abiel, “God is father”; Arbathite, of Beth-arabah (2 Samuel 23:31 Abi-albon).
Azmaveth, see 8:36; Baharumite, of Bahurim; Eliahba, “God hides”; Shaalbonite, of Shaalbim (“foxes”).
Second Samuel 23:32 reads “the sons of Jashen.” Hashem, “name”; Gizonite, uncertain; Shagee (2 Samuel 23:33 Shammah), uncertain; Hararite, perhaps “mountaineer.”
Ahiam, “mother’s brother”; Sachar (2 Samuel 23:33 Sharar), “reward”; Eliphal (2 Samuel 23:34 Eliphelet), “God judges”; Ur, “flame.”
Hepher, see 4:6; Mecherathite, uncertain; Ahijah, see 2:25. Second Samuel 23:34 reads here “Eliphelet the son of Ahasbai the Maacathite, Eliam the son of Ahithophel the Gilonite.”
Hezro, “enclosure”; Naarai (2 Samuel 23:35 Paarai the Arbite), “youthful”; Ezbai, uncertain.
Joel (2 Samuel 23:36 Igal), see 4:35; Nathan, see 2:36; Mibhar, “choice”; Hagri, “wanderer” (2 Samuel 23:36 “Bani the Gadite”).
Zelek, “cleft”; Ammonite, of Ammon (“people”); Naharai, “snorer”; Berothite, of Beeroth (“wells”).
Ira, see verse 28; Ithrite, of Jether’s clan (2:53); Gareb, “scabby.”
Second Samuel 23:39 ends the list with Uriah, adding “thirty-seven in all.” Uriah, “Yahweh is my light”; Hittite, see 1:13; Zabad, see 2:36; Ahlai, see 2:31.
Verses 42–47 are not in 2 Samuel. Adina, “delicate”; Shiza, uncertain. “And thirty with him” may mean “and over him were thirty.”
Hanan, see 8:23; Maacah, see 2:48; Joshaphat, “Yahweh has judged”; Mithnite, uncertain.
Uzzia, “Yahweh is my strength”; Ashterathite, of Ashtaroth (6:71); Shama, “he heard”; Jeiel, see 5:7 (Hebrew written text Jeuel); Hotham, see 7:32; Aroerite, of Aroer (5:8).
Jediael, see 7:6; Shimri, see 4:37; Joha, see 8:16; Tizite, uncertain.
Eliel, see 5:24; Mahavite, uncertain; Jeribai, “Yahweh contends”; Joshaviah, “Yahweh lets dwell”; Elnaam, “God is pleasantness”; Ithmah, “bereavement”; Moabite, of Moab (8:8).
Obed, see 2:12; Jaasiel, “God makes”; Mezobaite, perhaps of Zobah.

verses.text: Now these are they who came to David to Ziklag, while he yet kept himself close because of Saul the son of Kish.{a} They were among the mighty men, his helpers in war.
They were armed with bows and could use both the right hand and the left in slinging stones and shooting arrows from the bow; they were of Saul’s kinsmen, of Benjamin.{b}
The chief was Ahiezer, then Joash, the sons of Shemaah the Gibeathite; and Jeziel and Pelet the sons of Azmaveth; and Beracah, and Jehu the Anathothite;{c}
and Ishmaiah the Gibeonite, a mighty man among the thirty and over the thirty; and Jeremiah, Jahaziel, Johanan, and Jozabad the Gederathite;{d}
Eluzai, Jerimoth, Bealiah, Shemariah, and Shephatiah the Haruphite;{e}
Elkanah, Isshiah, Azarel, Joezer, and Jashobeam, the Korahites;{f}
and Joelah and Zebadiah, the sons of Jeroham of Gedor.{g}

From the Gadites some separated themselves to David in the stronghold in the wilderness, mighty men of valor, men of war fit for battle, who could handle shield and spear, whose faces were like the faces of lions, and who were as swift as gazelles on the mountains:{h}
Ezer the chief, Obadiah second, Eliab third,{i}
Mishmannah fourth, Jeremiah fifth,{j}
Attai sixth, Eliel seventh,{k}
Johanan eighth, Elzabad ninth,{l}
Jeremiah tenth, Machbannai eleventh.{m}
These of the sons of Gad were captains of the army; the least was equal to a hundred, and the greatest to a thousand.{n}

These are they who went over the Jordan in the first month (in March–April), when it had overflowed all its banks;{o} and they chased away all of the valleys, both toward the east and toward the west.
Some of the sons of Benjamin and Judah came to the stronghold to David.

David went out to meet them and said, “If you have come to me peacefully, to help me, I am ready to unite with you. But if you have come to hand me over to my enemies though I have done no wrong, may the God of our ancestors see this and pass judgment.”

Then the Spirit took hold of Amasai, the leader of the Thirty,{p} who said, “We are yours, David! We are with you, son of Jesse! Peace, peace to you, and peace to your helpers, because your God helps you.” So David received them and put them in charge of his raiding bands.

Some men of Manasseh also went over to David when he marched with the Philistines to fight against Saul. But David did not assist the Philistines, because after consulting together their rulers sent him away, saying, “He will change sides to his master Saul, and it will cost us our heads.”{q}
As he went to Ziklag, there deserted to him from Manasseh Adnah, and Jozabad, and Jediael, and Michael, and Jozabad, and Elihu, and Zillethai, captains of thousands who belonged to Manasseh.{r}
They supported David against the raiding party,{s} for all of them were brave warriors and became commanders in his army.
Day after day men came to David to help him, until his camp was large, like a camp of God.{t}
These are the numbers of the armed troops who reached David at Hebron to transfer Saul’s kingdom to him, as Yahweh had said:{u}
The sons of Judah who bore shield and spear were six thousand eight hundred, armed for war.
Of the sons of Simeon, mighty men of valor for war, seven thousand one hundred.
Of the sons of Levi, four thousand six hundred.
Jehoiada was the leader of the house of Aaron, and with him were three thousand seven hundred;{v}
and Zadok, a young man, a mighty man of valor, and twenty-two captains of his father’s house.{w}
Of the sons of Benjamin, the kinsmen of Saul, three thousand, for until then the greater part of them had kept their allegiance to the house of Saul.
Of the sons of Ephraim, twenty thousand eight hundred, mighty men of valor, famous men in their fathers’ houses.
From the half-tribe of Manasseh, 18,000 men, who were named individually to go and make David king.
From the descendants of Issachar, 200 leaders, who understood the times and knew what Israel should do, together with all their relatives who were under their command.{x}
Of Zebulun, such as were able to go out in the host, who could set the battle in array with all manner of instruments of war, fifty thousand, to help David{y} with an undivided heart.
Of Naphtali, a thousand captains, and with them, with shield and spear, thirty-seven thousand.
Of the Danites, twenty-eight thousand six hundred ready for battle.
Of Asher, forty thousand who could go out in the army, ready for battle.
From beyond the Jordan, of the Reubenites, the Gadites, and the half-tribe of Manasseh, one hundred and twenty thousand with all kinds of weapons of war.{z}

All these were men of war who could order the battle line; they came with a perfect heart to Hebron to make David king over all Israel; and all the rest of Israel too were of one heart to make David king.
They were there with David three days, eating and drinking, for their kinsmen had made provision for them.

Moreover those who were near to them, as far as Issachar, Zebulun, and Naphtali, brought food on donkeys, on camels, on mules, and on oxen: provisions of flour, cakes of figs, clusters of raisins, wine, oil, oxen, and sheep in abundance; for there was joy in Israel.

notes.text: Ziklag, perhaps “winding”; Kish, see 8:30. See 1 Samuel 27:6. This chapter has no parallel in Samuel.
Benjamin, “son of the right hand,” makes the skill with the left hand notable (compare Judges 20:16).

So the Hebrew margin (Qere); the written text (Ketiv) reads Jezuel. Ahiezer, “my brother is help”; Joash, “Yahweh has given”; Shemaah, “report”; Gibeathite, of Gibeah (“hill”); Jeziel, perhaps “God sprinkles”; Pelet, see 2:47; Beracah, “blessing”; Jehu, “Yahweh is he”; Anathothite, see 11:28.

English verse 4 is Hebrew verses 4–5, so the Hebrew numbering of this chapter is one higher from here to the end (English 12:40 = Hebrew 12:41). Ishmaiah, “Yahweh hears”; Gibeonite, of Gibeon (“hill”); Jeremiah, “Yahweh exalts”; Jahaziel, “God sees”; Johanan, see 3:15; Jozabad, “Yahweh has given”; Gederathite, of Gederah (“sheepfold,” 4:23).
So the Hebrew margin (Qere); the written text (Ketiv) reads Hariphite. Eluzai, “God is my strength”; Jerimoth, see 7:7; Bealiah, “Yahweh is lord”; Shemariah, “Yahweh guards”; Shephatiah, see 3:3.

Elkanah, see 6:23; Isshiah, “Yahweh lends”; Azarel, “God helps”; Joezer, “Yahweh is help”; Jashobeam, see 11:11; Korahites, descendants of Korah (2:43), possibly a Benjaminite family of that name rather than the Levites.
Joelah, perhaps “may he avail”; Zebadiah, “Yahweh has given”; Jeroham, see 6:27; Gedor, “wall” (4:4).
Gadites, of Gad (“fortune”).
Ezer, “help”; Obadiah, “servant of Yahweh”; Eliab, see 2:13.
Mishmannah, “fatness”; Jeremiah, see verse 4.
Attai, see 2:35; Eliel, see 5:24.
Johanan, see 3:15; Elzabad, “God has given.”
Machbannai, perhaps “clad with a mantle.”
Or “one was over a hundred, and the greatest over a thousand.”
Hebrew “the first month” (Nisan, from the spring new year), the season of the barley harvest, when the Jordan floods (Joshua 3:15). “Banks”: so the Hebrew margin (Qere).
So the written Hebrew text (Ketiv); the Hebrew margin (Qere) reads “the officers.” Amasai, “burden-bearer” (6:25); some identify him with Amasa (2 Samuel 17:25).
See 1 Samuel 29:1–11. Manasseh, “causing to forget.”
Adnah, “pleasure”; Jozabad, see verse 4; Jediael, see 7:6; Michael, see 5:13; Elihu, “he is my God”; Zillethai, “shade.”
Probably the Amalekite raiders of 1 Samuel 30.
Or “a very great army.”
Verses 23–37 are a tribal muster list found only in Chronicles; some take the Hebrew ’eleph here as “unit” rather than “thousand.”
Jehoiada, see 11:22; Aaron, see 6:3.
Zadok, see 6:8.
Issachar, perhaps “there is reward.”
So the Septuagint; Hebrew lacks “David.” Zebulun, “dwelling.”
Reubenites, of Reuben (“see, a son”).

verses.text: David consulted with the captains of thousands and of hundreds, with every leader.

David told the whole assembly of Israel, “If you approve, and if this is from Yahweh our God, let us send messages in every direction to the rest of our relatives throughout the land of Israel, and to the priests and Levites in the towns with pasturelands, inviting them to join us.
Let us bring the ark of our God back to us, since we did not consult it during the reign of Saul.”{a}
All the assembly said that they would do so, for the thing was right in the eyes of all the people.
So David assembled all Israel, from the Shihor of Egypt even to the entrance of Hamath, to bring the ark of God from Kiriath-jearim.{b}

And David and all Israel went up to Baalah, that is, to Kiriath-jearim, which belongs to Judah, to bring up from there the ark of God, Yahweh, who sits enthroned above the cherubim, where his name is called.{c}
They carried the ark of God on a new cart from the house of Abinadab, and Uzza and Ahio drove the cart.{d}
David and all Israel played before God with all their might, even with songs, and with lyres, and with harps, and with tambourines, and with cymbals, and with trumpets.
When they reached the threshing floor of Chidon, Uzza reached out to steady the ark, because the oxen had stumbled.{e}
The anger of Yahweh burned against Uzza, and he struck him because he put his hand to the ark; and there he died before God.
David was angry because Yahweh had broken out against Uzza; and that place is called Perez-uzza to this day.{f}
David was afraid of God that day, saying, “How can I bring the ark of God home to me?”
So David did not take the ark home to himself in the city of David, but turned it aside into the house of Obed-edom the Gittite.{g}
The ark of God stayed three months in Obed-edom’s house, with his family. Yahweh blessed Obed-edom’s household and everything he owned.

notes.text: Verses 5–14 parallel 2 Samuel 6:1–11. Verses 1–4 are found only in Chronicles.
Shihor, “black” or “turbid,” probably a branch of the Nile or the Wadi of Egypt; Hamath, “fortress.” Lebo-hamath may be a place name. Kiriath-jearim, “city of forests.”
Baalah, “mistress.” Second Samuel 6:2 reads “Baale-judah.” Cherubim, winged guardian figures.
Abinadab, see 2:13 (a different man); Uzza, “strength”; Ahio, “his brother” (the Septuagint takes it as “his brothers”).
Second Samuel 6:6 reads “Nacon.” Chidon may mean “javelin.”
Perez-uzza means “outburst against Uzza.”
Obed-edom, “servant of Edom”; Gittite, of Gath (“winepress”).

verses.text: Hiram king of Tyre sent messengers to David, with cedar trees, masons, and carpenters, to build him a house.{a}
And David knew that Yahweh had established him as king over Israel, for his kingdom was highly exalted for the sake of his people Israel.
David took more wives at Jerusalem, and David became the father of more sons and daughters.
These are the names of the children born to him in Jerusalem: Shammua, Shobab, Nathan, and Solomon;{b}
and Ibhar, Elishua, and Elpelet;{c}
and Nogah, Nepheg, and Japhia;
and Elishama, Beeliada, and Eliphelet.{d}
When the Philistines heard that David had been anointed king over all Israel, all the Philistines went up to seek David. David heard of it and went out against them.
Now the Philistines had come and made a raid in the Valley of Rephaim.
David asked God, “Should I go to war against the Philistines? Will you deliver them to me?” Yahweh answered him, “Go to war, and I will deliver them to you.”
So the Philistines went up to Baal-perazim, and David defeated them there. He said, “By my hand God has burst through my enemies like a flood.” That is why the place was named Baal-perazim.{e}
The Philistines abandoned their gods there, and David ordered that they be burned in a fire.{f}
Yet again the Philistines made a raid in the valley.
And when David inquired again of God, God said to him, “You shall not go up after them. Turn away from them and come against them opposite the balsam trees.{g}
When you hear the sound of marching in the tops of the balsam trees, then go out to battle, for God has gone out before you to strike the army of the Philistines.”
David did as God commanded him, and they struck down the army of the Philistines from Gibeon to Gezer.{h}
And the fame of David went out into all lands, and Yahweh brought the fear of him upon all nations.

notes.text: Verses 1–16 parallel 2 Samuel 5:11–25. Hiram, perhaps “my brother is exalted”; Tyre, “rock.” The Hebrew margin (Qere) reads Hiram; the written text (Ketiv) reads Huram.
Compare the list at 3:5–8. Shammua (3:5 Shimea), “heard”; Shobab, see 2:18; Nathan, see 2:36; Solomon, see 3:5.
Elpelet corresponds to Eliphelet in 3:6. Ibhar, see 3:6; Elishua, “God is salvation.”
Beeliada, “the Lord knows” (3:8 Eliada, “God knows,” perhaps a later change avoiding the name Baal). Second Samuel 5:14–16 omits Nogah and Elpelet.
Baal-perazim means “lord of breakings through.”
Second Samuel 5:21 says that David and his men carried the idols away. Chronicles says they were burned, as Deuteronomy 7:5, 25 commands.
Or “baca trees”; the exact kind of tree is uncertain.
Second Samuel 5:25 reads “from Geba.” Gezer, “portion.”

verses.text: David made houses for himself in the city of David, and he prepared a place for the ark of God and pitched a tent for it.
Then David said, “Only the Levites may carry the ark of God, because Yahweh chose them to carry Yahweh’s ark and to serve him always.”{a}
And David assembled all Israel at Jerusalem to bring up the ark of Yahweh to its place, which he had prepared for it.
David gathered together the sons of Aaron and the Levites:
of the sons of Kohath, Uriel the chief, and his brothers, a hundred and twenty;{b}
of the sons of Merari, Asaiah the chief, and his brothers, two hundred and twenty;{c}
of the sons of Gershom, Joel the chief, and his brothers, a hundred and thirty;{d}
of the sons of Elizaphan, Shemaiah the chief, and his brothers, two hundred;{e}
of the sons of Hebron, Eliel the chief, and his brothers, eighty;{f}
of the sons of Uzziel, Amminadab the chief, and his brothers, a hundred and twelve.{g}
David called for Zadok and Abiathar the priests, and for the Levites, for Uriel, Asaiah, Joel, Shemaiah, Eliel, and Amminadab,{h}

and said to them, “You are the heads of the fathers’ houses of the Levites. Sanctify yourselves, both you and your brothers, that you may bring up the ark of Yahweh, the God of Israel, to the place that I have prepared for it.
For because you did not bear it at the first, Yahweh our God made a breach upon us, for we did not seek him after the ordinance.”
So the priests and the Levites sanctified themselves to bring up the ark of Yahweh, the God of Israel.
The sons of the Levites bore the ark of God upon their shoulders with its poles, just as Moses commanded by the word of Yahweh.{i}
David also told the chiefs of the Levites to appoint their brothers as the singers, with instruments of music, harps and lyres and cymbals, sounding aloud, to lift up the voice with joy.
So the Levites appointed Heman the son of Joel; and of his brothers, Asaph the son of Berechiah; and of the sons of Merari their brothers, Ethan the son of Kushaiah;{j}

and with them their second-rank relatives: Zechariah, Ben,{k} Jaaziel, Shemiramoth, Jehiel, Unni, Eliab, Benaiah, Maaseiah, Mattithiah, Eliphelehu, and Mikneiah, along with the gatekeepers Obed-edom and Jeiel.{l}
The singers, Heman, Asaph, and Ethan, were to sound aloud with cymbals of bronze;
Zechariah, Aziel, Shemiramoth, Jehiel, Unni, Eliab, Maaseiah, and Benaiah, with harps set to Alamoth;{m}
and Mattithiah, Eliphelehu, Mikneiah, Obed-edom, Jeiel, and Azaziah, with lyres set to the Sheminith, to lead.{n}
Chenaniah, chief of the Levites in carrying, was in charge of the carrying; he gave instruction about it, because he was skillful.{o}
Berechiah and Elkanah were doorkeepers for the ark.{p}
Shebaniah, Joshaphat, Nethanel, Amasai, Zechariah, Benaiah, and Eliezer, the priests, were to blow the trumpets before the ark of God. Obed-edom and Jehiah were doorkeepers for the ark.{q}
So David and the elders of Israel and the captains of thousands went to bring up the ark of the covenant of Yahweh from the house of Obed-edom with joy.{r}
Because God was helping the Levites who carried Yahweh’s covenant ark, seven bulls and seven rams were offered.{s}
David wore a robe of fine linen, as did all the Levites carrying the ark, the singers, and Chenaniah, who directed the music of the singers;{t} David also wore a linen ephod.
So all Israel brought up the ark of the covenant of Yahweh with shouting, with the sound of the horn, with trumpets, and with cymbals, sounding aloud with harps and lyres.
As Yahweh’s covenant ark entered the city of David, Michal daughter of Saul watched from a window. She saw King David leaping and celebrating, and she despised him in her heart.{u}

notes.text: See Numbers 4:15; Deuteronomy 10:8. Levites, of Levi (“joined”).
Kohath, see 6:1; Uriel, see 6:24.
Merari, see 6:1; Asaiah, see 4:36.
Gershom (Gershon), see 6:1; Joel, see 4:35.
Elizaphan, “God has hidden,” a Kohathite (Numbers 3:30); Shemaiah, see 3:22.
Hebron, see 6:2; Eliel, see 5:24.
Uzziel, see 6:2; Amminadab, see 6:22.
Zadok, see 6:8; Abiathar, “the father is abundant.”
See Exodus 25:14; Numbers 7:9. Moses, see 6:3.
Heman, see 6:33; Asaph, see 6:39; Berechiah, see 3:20; Ethan, see 6:42; Kushaiah (6:44 Kishi), perhaps “bow of Yahweh.”
Ben (“son”) is probably a copying error; it is lacking in the Septuagint and in verse 20.

Zechariah, see 5:7; Jaaziel (verse 20 Aziel), “God strengthens”; Shemiramoth, perhaps “name of heights”; Jehiel, “God lives”; Unni, perhaps “afflicted”; Eliab, see 2:13; Benaiah, see 4:36; Maaseiah, “work of Yahweh”; Mattithiah, “gift of Yahweh”; Eliphelehu, “God distinguishes him”; Mikneiah, “possession of Yahweh”; Obed-edom, see 13:13; Jeiel, see 5:7.
Alamoth, “young women,” probably a musical term for a higher register (compare Psalm 46 heading).
Sheminith, “the eighth,” probably a musical term for a lower register or an eight-stringed instrument (compare Psalms 6, 12 headings). Azaziah, “Yahweh is strong.”
Or “in charge of the music … he instructed in music”; the Hebrew massa’ can mean “carrying” or “lifting up the voice.” Chenaniah, “Yahweh establishes.”
Elkanah, see 6:23.
Shebaniah, “Yahweh has brought back”; Joshaphat, see 11:43; Nethanel, see 2:14; Amasai, see 6:25; Eliezer, “God is help”; Jehiah, “Yahweh lives.”
Verses 25–29 parallel 2 Samuel 6:12–16.
Second Samuel 6:13 says that when the bearers had gone six paces he sacrificed an ox and a fatling.
Second Samuel 6:14 says only that David danced with all his might, wearing a linen ephod. “Of the singers” is perhaps a copying addition. An ephod was a linen garment worn by priests.
Michal, “who is like God?”

verses.text: They brought in the ark of God and set it inside the tent that David had pitched for it, and they offered burnt offerings and peace offerings before God.{a}
When David had finished offering the burnt offerings and the peace offerings, he blessed the people in the name of Yahweh,
and he distributed to everyone of Israel, both man and woman, to each a loaf of bread, a portion of meat,{b} and a cake of raisins.
He appointed some of the Levites to minister before the ark of Yahweh, to commemorate, to thank, and to praise Yahweh, the God of Israel:
Asaph the chief, and second to him Zechariah, then Jeiel, Shemiramoth, Jehiel, Mattithiah, Eliab, Benaiah, Obed-edom, and Jeiel, with harps and with lyres; and Asaph was to sound the cymbals;{c}
and the priests Benaiah and Jahaziel were to sound the trumpets continually before the covenant ark of God.{d}
Then on that day David for the first time committed to Asaph and his brothers the giving of thanks to Yahweh:
Give thanks to Yahweh; call on his name. Make his deeds known among the peoples.{e}
Sing to him; sing praises to him. Tell of all his marvelous works.
Glory in his holy name. Let the heart of those who seek Yahweh rejoice.
Seek Yahweh and his strength. Seek his face continually.
Remember his wonderful works that he has done, his wonders, and the judgments of his mouth,
you offspring of Israel his servant, you children of Jacob, his chosen ones.{f}
He is Yahweh our God. His judgments are in all the earth.
Remember his covenant forever,{g} the word which he commanded to a thousand generations,
the covenant which he made with Abraham, his oath to Isaac.
He confirmed it to Jacob for a statute, to Israel for an everlasting covenant,
saying, “To you I will give the land of Canaan, the portion of your inheritance,”
when you were but few in number,{h} very few, and sojourners in it.
They went about from nation to nation, from one kingdom to another people.
He allowed no man to do them wrong. Yes, he reproved kings for their sakes:
“Do not touch my anointed ones! Do my prophets no harm!”
Sing to Yahweh, all the earth!{i} Proclaim his salvation from day to day.
Declare his glory among the nations, his marvelous works among all the peoples.
For great is Yahweh, and greatly to be praised. He is to be feared above all gods.
For all the gods of the peoples are idols,{j} but Yahweh made the heavens.
Honor and majesty are before him. Strength and joy are in his place.{k}
Ascribe to Yahweh, you families of the peoples, ascribe to Yahweh glory and strength.
Ascribe to Yahweh the glory due to his name. Bring an offering, and come before him. Worship Yahweh in holy array.{l}
Tremble before him, all the earth. The world also is established, so that it cannot be moved.
Let the heavens be glad, and let the earth rejoice! Let them say among the nations, “Yahweh reigns!”
Let the sea roar, and its fullness! Let the field rejoice, and all that is therein!
Then the trees of the forest will sing for joy before Yahweh, for he comes to judge the earth.
O give thanks to Yahweh, for he is good;{m} for his steadfast love endures forever.
Say, “Save us, God of our salvation! Gather us together and deliver us from the nations, that we may give thanks to your holy name, and glory in your praise.”
Blessed be Yahweh, the God of Israel, from everlasting even to everlasting. And all the people said, “Amen,” and praised Yahweh.{n}
David left Asaph and his relatives there in front of Yahweh’s covenant ark, to serve before the ark continually according to each day’s needs,
and Obed-edom with his brothers, sixty-eight; and Obed-edom the son of Jeduthun and Hosah to be gatekeepers.{o}
And he left Zadok the priest and his brothers the priests before the tabernacle of Yahweh in the high place that was at Gibeon,{p}
to offer burnt offerings to Yahweh on the altar of burnt offering continually morning and evening, according to all that is written in the Law of Yahweh, which he commanded Israel.
With them were Heman and Jeduthun, and the rest who were chosen, who were mentioned by name, to give thanks to Yahweh, because his steadfast love endures forever.{q}
Heman and Jeduthun had trumpets and cymbals for those who should sound aloud, and instruments for the songs of God. The sons of Jeduthun were to be at the gate.
Then all the people went home, and David went back to bless his own household.{r}

notes.text: Verses 1–3 parallel 2 Samuel 6:17–19.
The meaning of the Hebrew ’eshpar is uncertain; others suggest “a date cake.”
Jeiel (second): some read Jaaziel or Aziel, as in 15:18, 20.
Jahaziel, see 12:4.
Verses 8–22 parallel Psalm 105:1–15.
Psalm 105:6 reads “offspring of Abraham.”
Psalm 105:8 reads “He has remembered his covenant forever.”
Psalm 105:12 reads “when they were.”
Verses 23–33 parallel Psalm 96:1–13, with differences.
Hebrew ’elilim, “worthless things,” a play on ’elohim, “gods.”
Psalm 96:6 reads “Strength and beauty are in his sanctuary.”
Or “in the splendor of holiness.”
Verses 34–36 parallel Psalm 106:1, 47–48. Psalm 106:47 reads “Save us, Yahweh our God.”
Psalm 106:48 ends “Let all the people say, ‘Amen!’ Praise Yah!”
Jeduthun, “praising”; Hosah, “refuge.” Obed-edom, see 13:13.
Gibeon, “hill”; compare 21:29; 2 Chronicles 1:3.
See 2 Chronicles 5:13; 7:3; Psalms 106:1; 136:1.
Second Samuel 6:19–20 parallels this verse; Chronicles omits Michal’s rebuke of David (2 Samuel 6:20–23).

verses.text: When David was living in his house, David said to Nathan the prophet, “Look, I live in a house of cedar, but the ark of the covenant of Yahweh is under curtains.”{a}
Nathan said to David, “Do all that is in your heart, for God is with you.”
But that same night the word of God came to Nathan, saying,
“Go and tell my servant David, ‘This is what Yahweh says: You are not the one to build a house for me to live in.{b}
For I have not lived in a house since the day that I brought up Israel to this day, but have gone from tent to tent and from tabernacle to tabernacle.{c}

In all places where I have walked with all Israel, did I speak a word with any of the judges of Israel, whom I commanded to shepherd my people, saying, “Why have you not built me a house of cedar?”’{d}
Now therefore you shall say to my servant David, ‘Thus says Yahweh of Armies: I took you from the pasture, from following the sheep, to be prince over my people Israel.
I have been with you wherever you have gone, and have cut off all your enemies from before you. And I will make you a name, like the name of the great ones who are in the earth.

I will appoint a place for my people Israel and will plant them, that they may dwell in their own place and be disturbed no more. The children of wickedness shall not waste them any more, as at the first,
and from the days that I commanded judges to be over my people Israel. And I will subdue all your enemies. Moreover I tell you that Yahweh will build you a house.{e}
