which I laid upon your fathers on the day I brought them out of Egypt, out of the iron-smelting furnace, saying: Listen to my voice and carry out all that I command you. So you will be my people, and I will be your God,
that I may keep the oath I swore to your fathers, to give them a land flowing with milk and honey, as it is at this day.’” Then I answered, “Amen,{a} Yahweh.”
And Yahweh told me, “Proclaim all these words in Judah’s towns and Jerusalem’s streets: ‘Hear the terms of this covenant and carry them out.
For I solemnly warned your fathers from the day I brought them up out of Egypt down to this day, warning them early and late, saying, Listen to my voice.{b}

Yet they would not listen or turn their ear, but each walked in the obstinacy of his evil heart. So I brought upon them all the terms of this covenant, which I had charged them to keep, and which they did not keep.’”
Then Yahweh said to me, “A conspiracy has been uncovered among Judah’s men and Jerusalem’s residents.

They have gone back to the guilt of their forefathers, who would not hear my words; they too have gone after other gods to serve them. Israel’s house and Judah’s house have broken my covenant that I cut with their fathers.
Therefore this is what Yahweh says: Look, I am bringing on them a calamity they cannot escape; they will cry to me, but I will not listen.
Then Judah’s towns and Jerusalem’s residents will go and cry to the gods to whom they burn offerings, but those gods will give them no rescue whatever in the hour of their calamity.
Indeed, O Judah, your gods number as many as your towns, and the altars you have erected to the Shame{c} number as many as Jerusalem’s streets—altars for sending up smoke to Baal.
“And you—intercede not for this people; raise no plea or entreaty for them, for I will refuse to listen at the time they call on me in their calamity.

What right has my beloved in my house,
when she has worked out her many schemes?
Can vows{d} and holy flesh
take your calamity from you?
Then you could exult.

Yahweh once called you a green olive tree,
beautiful and full of fine fruit.
But with a loud storm roar
he has set it on fire,
and its branches are broken.{e}
Yahweh of Armies, who planted you, has pronounced calamity against you, because of the evil that Israel’s house and Judah’s house have done, provoking me by burning offerings to Baal.”

Yahweh disclosed it to me, and so I learned of it;
then you let me see what they were doing.

But you, Yahweh of Armies, who judge rightly,
who test the inmost parts{g} and the heart,
let me see your vengeance upon them,
for to you I have laid bare my cause.
Therefore this is what Yahweh says about the people of Anathoth who are trying to kill you and tell you, “Do not prophesy in Yahweh’s name, or we will kill you”—
therefore this is what Yahweh of Armies says: “See, I will call them to account. Their young men will die by the sword; their sons and daughters will die by famine.
None of them will survive, for I will bring disaster on the people of Anathoth in the year when I punish them.”

notes.text: Hebrew ʾamen, “surely, so be it,” the response to the covenant curses (Deuteronomy 27:15–26).
The Septuagint lacks verse 7 and most of verse 8, reading only “But they did them not” (Brenton).
Hebrew bosheth, a contemptuous substitute for Baal.
Following the Septuagint, which has “prayers and holy offerings” (Brenton); the Hebrew reads “the many,” which is difficult.
The Hebrew of verses 15–16 is uncertain in places.
Hebrew “with its bread”; the translation follows a slight change of the text, or else read “its fruit.”
Hebrew “kidneys,” regarded as the seat of the emotions.

verses.text:
Righteous are you, Yahweh,
when I bring a case before you;
yet I would argue my cause with you:
Why does the path of the wicked prosper?
Why do all the treacherous live at ease?

You plant them, and they take root;
they grow and bear fruit.
Near are you in their mouth,
but far from their inmost parts.

But you, Yahweh, know me;
you see me and test my heart toward you.
Drag them off like sheep for slaughter,
and set them apart for the day of killing.

Till when shall the earth lie mourning,
the herbage of the countryside dried up?
For the wickedness of its dwellers
beast and bird have perished,
for they said, “He will not see what becomes of us.”

For even your brothers and your father’s house,
even they have dealt treacherously with you;
even they shout loudly after you.
Do not trust them,
though they speak fair words to you.

It has been turned into a wasteland;
waste and mourning, it lies before me.
All the land is made a waste,
since no one takes it to heart.

Across the barren hills in the wilderness
raiders have arrived,
for Yahweh’s sword is devouring
from one end of the land to the other;
no one is safe.

Wheat they sowed, but thorns they reaped;
they have worn themselves out to no profit.
Be ashamed{d} of your harvests
because of the fierce anger of Yahweh.”

This is what Yahweh says concerning all my evil neighbors who touch the heritage I gave my people Israel to possess: “See, I am uprooting them from their land, and the house of Judah I will uproot from among them.
But after I have pulled them out, I will have compassion on them again and bring each of them back to his own inheritance and his own land.
And if they will diligently learn the ways of my people, to swear by my name, ‘As Yahweh lives,’ even as they taught my people to swear by Baal, then they shall be built up in the midst of my people.
But if any nation will not listen, then I will pluck up that nation, plucking it up and destroying it,” declares Yahweh.

notes.text: Or “if only in a peaceful land you feel secure.”
Hebrew “the pride of the Jordan,” the dense growth along the river, home of lions (49:19).
The Hebrew is uncertain; the Septuagint reads, “Is not my inheritance to me a hyena’s cave?” (Brenton, modernized).
Or, with a change of vowels, “They shall be ashamed.”

verses.text: This is what Yahweh said to me: “Go and buy yourself a linen waistcloth{a} and wrap it about your loins, but do not let it get into water.”
So I bought a waistcloth as Yahweh directed and wrapped it about my loins.
Then Yahweh’s word came to me a second time:
“Take the waistcloth you bought, the one about your loins, and set out for Perath;{b} hide it there in a cleft of the rock.”
So I went and hid it at Perath, as Yahweh had ordered me.
After many days Yahweh said to me, “Set out for Perath, and retrieve from there the waistcloth I ordered you to hide there.”
So I went to Perath, dug, and took the waistcloth from the place where I had hidden it. And look—the waistcloth was rotted, fit for nothing at all.
Then Yahweh’s word came to me:
“This is what Yahweh says: Just so will I rot the pride of Judah and the great pride of Jerusalem.
This evil people, who refuse to hear my words, who walk in their own obstinate hearts and go after other gods to serve them and bow to them, shall be like this waistcloth, fit for nothing at all.

For just as a waistcloth hugs a man’s waist, so I bound to myself all Israel’s house and all Judah’s house,” declares Yahweh, “to be my people, my renown, my praise, and my honor; yet they refused to listen.

“Speak to them also this word: ‘This is what Yahweh, Israel’s God, says: Every jar is to be filled with wine.’ And when they answer you, ‘Do we not know perfectly well that every jar is to be filled with wine?’
then say to them, ‘This is what Yahweh says: I am about to make everyone living in this land drunk—the kings who sit on David’s throne, the priests, the prophets and all the people of Jerusalem.
And I will smash them one against another, fathers and sons alike,’ declares Yahweh. ‘I will show no pity, nor spare, nor have compassion, so as not to destroy them.’”

Listen and give ear; be not proud,
for Yahweh has spoken.

Honor Yahweh your God
before he brings darkness,
before your feet trip
on the dusky mountains,
and while you hope for light

But if you will not hear,
my soul will weep in secret for your pride;
my eye will weep bitterly and run down with tears,
because Yahweh’s flock has been taken captive.

Say to the king and to the queen mother:{c}
“Sit down low,
for your splendid crown
has come down from your heads.”

The towns of the Negev{d} are shut up,
with none to open them;
all Judah is carried into exile,
wholly carried into exile.

Lift up your eyes and see
those coming from the north.
Where is the flock that was given you,
your beautiful flock?

What will you say when he puts over you as ruler
the very people you trained
to be your close allies?{e}
Will pain not grip you
like a woman in labor?

And if you wonder,
“Why did this happen to me?”—
it is the size of your guilt
that has stripped off your skirts
and left you violated.{f}

Can a Cushite{g} alter his skin
or a leopard remove its spots?
Then you could also do good,
you who have learned only evil.

I will scatter them like chaff
driven by the wind of the desert.

This is your lot,
the portion I have measured out to you, declares Yahweh,
because you have forgotten me
and trusted in falsehood.

I myself will pull your skirts up over your face,
so that your shame is exposed.

Your adultery and your lustful cries,
your shameless prostitution
on the hills and in the fields—
I have seen your detestable acts.
Woe to you, Jerusalem!
How long will you stay unclean?

notes.text: Hebrew ʾezor, a garment worn next to the body, perhaps a loincloth or sash.

Hebrew Perath is the usual name of the Euphrates, about 350 miles (560 kilometers) away, and the Septuagint reads “the Euphrates” (Brenton). Some interpreters think of Parah (Joshua 18:23), a village about 4 miles (6 kilometers) from Anathoth.
Hebrew gevirah, “great lady,” the king’s mother, who held an official position; probably Nehushta, mother of Jehoiachin (2 Kings 24:8).
Negev, “dry land,” the arid south of Judah.
The Hebrew of this verse is uncertain.
A euphemism for sexual violation.
Cushite, a man from Cush (the upper Nile region, modern Sudan), known for dark skin.

verses.text: The word of Yahweh that came to Jeremiah concerning the drought:{a}

“Judah mourns,
and her gates languish;
her people lie in black upon the ground,
and the cry of Jerusalem goes up.

Since the soil is shattered,
since no rain has fallen on the land,
the farmers are dismayed;
they muffle their heads.

Even the doe in the field
gives birth and forsakes her fawn,
because there is no grass.

O Hope of Israel,
its Savior in time of trouble,
why should you be like a sojourner in the land,
like a traveler who turns aside to lodge for a night?

Why are you like someone bewildered,
like a warrior unable to rescue?
But you are here among us, Yahweh,
and we bear your name;
do not abandon us.”
Yahweh said to me, “Do not pray for this people’s welfare.
When they fast, I will not listen to their cry; when they present burnt offerings and grain offerings, I will not accept them; instead I will finish them off with sword, famine and plague.”
Then I said, “Ah, Lord Yahweh! Look, the prophets keep telling them, ‘You shall not see the sword, nor shall famine come upon you; I will give you lasting peace in this place.’”

Yahweh told me, “These prophets are prophesying lies in my name. I did not send them or order them or speak to them. They are prophesying to you a false vision, worthless fortune-telling and the deceit of their own minds.{b}

So this is what Yahweh says about the prophets who prophesy in my name though I never sent them, and who keep saying, ‘No sword or famine will touch this land’: By sword and by famine those very prophets will be finished off.

The people they prophesy to will lie in Jerusalem’s streets, thrown out and dying from famine and the sword, and no one will bury them—not they, nor their wives, sons or daughters. I will pour their own wickedness back on them.

“Tell them this message:
‘May my eyes overflow with tears
night and day without stopping,
for my people’s virgin daughter has suffered a crushing blow,
a terribly severe wound.

If I go out into the field,
look—those slain by the sword!
And if I enter the city,
look—the diseases of famine!
For both prophet and priest roam about in a land they know not.’”{c}

Have you cast Judah off completely?
Is Zion abhorrent to your soul?
Why have you smitten us
past all mending?
We hoped for peace, and nothing good arrived;
for a season of healing, and see—panic.

We acknowledge, O Yahweh, our wickedness,
the iniquity of our fathers,
for we have sinned against you.

Is there anyone among the worthless gods of the nations who can send rain?
Or do the skies pour showers on their own?
Isn’t it you, Yahweh our God?
We wait for you,
because you alone make all these things happen.

notes.text: Hebrew batstsaroth, “the times of dearth” or “the droughts.”
Hebrew “heart.”
Or “go off trading in a land they do not know”; the Hebrew is uncertain.

verses.text: Then Yahweh said to me, “Even if Moses and Samuel stood before me, my soul would not turn toward this people. Send them from my presence; let them be gone!
I will appoint over them four kinds of destroyers,” declares Yahweh: “the sword to slay, the dogs to drag away, and the birds of the sky and the beasts of the earth to devour and to destroy.
I will turn them into an object of dread for every realm on earth, on account of what Manasseh{a} son of Hezekiah, Judah’s king, committed in Jerusalem.

“For who will take pity on you, Jerusalem?
Who will lament over you?
Who will step aside
to inquire how you fare?

How miserable I am, mother, that you gave birth to me,
a man who brings quarrels and conflict to the whole country!
I have neither loaned money nor borrowed it,
yet everyone curses me.

Can one break iron,
iron from the north, and bronze?{c}

Your riches and your stores I will hand over as spoil, at no cost,
for all your sins, in every part of your land.

I will make you slaves to your foes{d}
in a country unknown to you,
for my anger has lit a fire
that will blaze against you.”

When your words came, I devoured them;
they became my joy
and my heart’s delight,
because I bear your name,
Yahweh, God of Armies.

Never did I sit among the revelers
or make merry with them;
under your hand I sat by myself,
for you had filled me with fury.

Why has my agony no end,
my wound no cure, past all healing?
Will you indeed prove to me a treacherous wadi,
a stream whose waters cannot be relied on?

So Yahweh answered:
“If you come back, I will restore you
and you will serve me.
If you speak what is valuable and not what is worthless,
you will be my spokesman.
They may turn to you,
but you must not turn to them.

I will turn you into a fortified wall of bronze
for this people;
they will fight you,
but they will not defeat you,
for I am with you
to save and rescue you, declares Yahweh.

I will rescue you out of the power of evildoers,
and ransom you from the clutch of tyrants.”

notes.text: Manasseh reigned about 697–642 B.C.; his sins are recounted in 2 Kings 21:1–18 and 23:26–27.
The Hebrew of verses 11–12 is difficult; the Septuagint differs considerably, reading, “So be it, Lord, in their prosperity” (Brenton). Some ancient witnesses read the verse as Jeremiah’s words.
Or “Can iron and bronze break iron from the north?”
So many Hebrew manuscripts, the Septuagint, and Syriac (compare 17:4); the standard Hebrew text reads “I will make them pass over with your enemies.”

verses.text: Yahweh’s word came to me once more:
“Take no wife for yourself, and father no sons or daughters in this place.
For here is Yahweh’s word concerning the boys and girls born in this place, and concerning the women who give them birth and the men who father them in this land:

They will perish of deadly diseases. None will mourn them, none will bury them; they will lie like manure on the face of the soil. By sword and by famine they will be finished off, and their carcasses will feed the birds of the sky and the beasts of the earth.

“For so says Yahweh: Enter no house of the mourning banquet;{a} go not in to lament or to show sympathy, for from this people I have taken away my peace,” declares Yahweh, “my steadfast love and my tender mercies.{b}
Great and small alike will perish in this land. They will go unburied; no one will mourn for them, nor gash himself, nor shave his head on their account.
No one will break bread for the mourner to console him for the dead, nor will anyone hand him the cup of consolation for his father or his mother.
Into a house of feasting likewise you must not go, to sit down with them to eat and drink.

For this is what Yahweh of Armies, Israel’s God, says: Look, before your eyes and in your days I am silencing in this place the sound of merriment and the sound of joy, the voice of bridegroom and the voice of bride.

“And when you report all these words to this people and they ask you, ‘On what grounds has Yahweh decreed all this great calamity against us? What is our guilt? What sin have we committed against Yahweh our God?’
then answer them, ‘It is because your fathers abandoned me,’ declares Yahweh, ‘and went after other gods, serving them and bowing down to them. Me they abandoned, and my law they did not keep.
And you have done worse than your fathers, for look, each of you walks in the obstinacy of his evil heart, refusing to listen to me.
So I will hurl you out of this land into a land that neither you nor your fathers have known, and there you will serve other gods day and night, for I will show you no favor.’
“However, look, the time is coming,” declares Yahweh, “when people will no longer say, ‘As surely as Yahweh lives, who brought the Israelites out of Egypt,’

but instead, ‘By the life of Yahweh, who led Israel’s sons up out of the north country and out of every land to which he had scattered them.’ For back to their own soil I will restore them, the soil I bestowed on their ancestors.

“Look, I am sending for many fishermen,” declares Yahweh, “and they will fish them out. Afterward I will send for many hunters, and they will hunt them down on every mountain and every hill and out of the clefts of the rocks.
For my eyes are on all their ways; they are not concealed from my face, nor is their guilt hidden from my eyes.
First{c} I will repay double for their guilt and their sin, because they have polluted my land with the carcasses of their detestable idols and filled my heritage with their abominations.”

Yahweh, my might and my fortress,
my shelter when trouble comes,
from earth’s farthest reaches
the nations will come to you, saying:
“Our fathers owned nothing but a lie,
a puff of air, useless through and through.

Can a man make gods for himself?
Such are no gods!”

“So look, I will teach them—
this one time I will teach them
my power and my strength,
and they will know that my name is Yahweh.”

notes.text: Hebrew marzeaḥ, a ritual banquet, here held for mourning.
The Septuagint lacks “my steadfast love and my compassion” and the first half of verse 6 (Brenton).
The Septuagint lacks “First” (Brenton).

verses.text:
while their sons remember their altars
and their Asherah poles{c}
beside every leafy tree
on the high hills,

O my mountain set in the countryside!
Your riches and every treasure of yours I will hand over as spoil,
your shrines too, for the sin in every part of your land.

Through your own fault you will lose hold
of the inheritance I bestowed on you,
and I will make you slaves to your foes
in a country strange to you,
for you have lit a fire in my nostrils
that will blaze for all time.”

This is what Yahweh says:
“Cursed is the man who relies on mortal man
and makes flesh the arm he leans on,
while his heart veers away from Yahweh.

He will be like a juniper{d} in the Arabah;
he will not see when good arrives,
but will settle in the scorched places of the wilderness,
a salt land where no one lives.

“Blessed is the man who relies on Yahweh,
whose confidence Yahweh is.

“I, Yahweh, probe the heart
and examine the inmost parts,
to repay each man according to his ways,
according to the fruit of his deeds.”

Like a partridge that hatches eggs it did not lay
is the man who gets riches unjustly;
in the middle of his days they will abandon him,
and at his end he will prove a fool.

A throne of glory, set on high from the beginning,
is the place of our sanctuary.

Look, they keep saying to me,
“Where is Yahweh’s word?
Let it come, then!”

Do not become a terror to me;
you are my refuge in the day of calamity.
This is what Yahweh said to me: “Go and stand in the People’s Gate,{h} by which Judah’s kings come in and go out, and in all the gates of Jerusalem,
and say to them, ‘Hear the word of Yahweh, you kings of Judah, and all Judah, and all Jerusalem’s residents who come in by these gates.
This is what Yahweh says: Guard yourselves, as you value your lives, and carry no load on the Sabbath day, nor bring it in through Jerusalem’s gates.
Carry no load out of your houses on the Sabbath day, and do no work at all, but keep the Sabbath day holy, as I commanded your fathers.
Yet they would not listen or turn their ear, but stiffened their necks so as not to hear or take correction.
But if you diligently heed me, declares Yahweh, and carry no burden in by this city’s gates on the Sabbath, but treat the Sabbath as holy by doing no labor on it,

then through the gates of this city will enter kings and princes who sit on David’s throne, riding in chariots and on horses, they and their princes, Judah’s men and Jerusalem’s residents; and this city will be inhabited forever.

And people will come from the towns of Judah and the places around Jerusalem, from the land of Benjamin, from the Shephelah,{i} from the hill country, and from the Negev, bringing burnt offerings and sacrifices, grain offerings and frankincense, and bringing thank offerings to Yahweh’s house.

But if you will not listen to me, to keep the Sabbath day holy and not to carry a load as you enter Jerusalem’s gates on the Sabbath day, then I will kindle a fire in its gates, and it will consume the palaces of Jerusalem and will not be quenched.’”

notes.text: Hebrew shamir, a very hard stone, perhaps emery or diamond.
The Septuagint lacks verses 1–4 (Brenton). Verses 3–4 partly repeat 15:13–14.
Asherah, a Canaanite goddess; her symbol was a wooden pole or stylized tree.
Hebrew ʿarʿar, a desert shrub, perhaps the juniper or a dwarf tamarisk; the Septuagint has “wild tamarisk” (Brenton).

Hebrew ʿaqov, “crooked, deceitful,” recalling the name Jacob. The Septuagint reads, “The heart is deep beyond all things, and it is the man” (Brenton), reflecting Hebrew ʿamoq, “deep,” and ʾenosh, “man,” for ʾanush, “sick.”
Hebrew “from me.”
Or, with a slight change, “I have not run away from being a shepherd after you”; the Hebrew is uncertain.
Or “the Gate of the Sons of the People”; its location is unknown.
Shephelah, “lowland,” the foothills between Judah’s hill country and the coastal plain.

verses.text: The word that came to Jeremiah from Yahweh:
“Get up and go down to the potter’s workshop, and there I will tell you what I have to say.”
So I went down to the potter’s workshop, and look—he was at work on the double wheel.{a}
Whenever the vessel he was shaping from the clay was spoiled in the potter’s hand, he would rework it into another vessel, as seemed right to the potter to make.
Then Yahweh’s word came to me:
“House of Israel, can I not deal with you as this potter does?” declares Yahweh. “Look, as clay in the potter’s hand, so are you in my hand, O house of Israel.
At one moment I may speak of a nation or a kingdom, to uproot and pull down and destroy it;
but if that nation I spoke of turns from its evil, I relent of the calamity I planned to bring on it.
At another moment I may speak of a nation or a kingdom, to build and to plant it;
yet should it do what is evil before me, refusing to heed my voice, I will think better of the good I had said I would do for it.

Now speak to the people of Judah and the residents of Jerusalem: ‘This is what Yahweh says: Look, I am preparing disaster for you and making plans against you. Each of you must turn from your evil way and change your ways and actions.’
But they will answer, ‘No use! Our own schemes we will pursue; each of us will do as his stubborn, evil heart dictates.’

“Therefore this is what Yahweh says:
Ask among the nations:
who ever heard the like of this?
A thing most horrible
has the virgin Israel done.

to turn their country into an appalling waste,
an object of perpetual whistling;
all who travel past it shudder
and wag their heads.

Like the east wind I will scatter them
before the enemy;
my back, not my face,{d} I will show them
in the day of their calamity.”

Then they said, “Come on, let us make plans against Jeremiah, because teaching will not disappear from the priests, advice from the wise or messages from the prophets. Come on, let us attack him with words, and pay no attention to anything he says.”

Give heed to me, O Yahweh,
and listen to the voice of my adversaries.

Should evil be the payment for good?
Yet they have dug a pit to trap me.
Remember that I stood in front of you
and spoke well of them,
to turn your anger away from them.

Let a cry be heard from their houses,
when you bring raiders on them suddenly,
for they have dug a pit to seize me
and hidden snares for my feet.

Yet you, Yahweh, know
all their plotting against me to kill me.
Do not cover over their iniquity,
nor blot out their sin from before you.
Let them be overthrown before you;
deal with them in the time of your anger.

notes.text: Hebrew “the two stones,” the upper and lower wheels of the potter’s wheel, turned by the feet.
The Hebrew of this line is uncertain; perhaps “the rock of Sirion,” another name for Hermon.
Or “Are the foreign, cold, flowing waters ever plucked up?”; the Hebrew is difficult.
So the Hebrew consonants, read with different vowels; some ancient witnesses read “I will look on their back, not their face.”

verses.text: This is what Yahweh said: “Go and buy a potter’s earthenware jar,{a} and take with you some of the elders of the people and of the senior priests,
and go out to the Valley of Ben-hinnom at the entry of the Potsherd Gate,{b} and proclaim there the words I tell you.

Declare, ‘Listen to Yahweh’s word, O kings of Judah and you who live in Jerusalem. So says Yahweh of Armies, God of Israel: I am about to bring on this place a disaster so great that whoever hears of it, both his ears will ring.

For they have abandoned me and made this place alien, burning offerings in it to other gods whom neither they nor their fathers nor Judah’s kings had known; and they have filled this place with the blood of innocents,
and have built the high places of Baal to burn their sons in the fire as burnt offerings to Baal—a thing I never commanded or spoke of, nor did it enter my mind.
So, mark it, the days are approaching, declares Yahweh, when no longer will this place be named Topheth or Ben-hinnom’s Valley, but Slaughter Valley.

Here in this place I will drain away{c} the counsel of Judah and Jerusalem; I will cause them to fall by the sword before their foes, by the hand of those hunting for their lives, and I will hand over their corpses to be eaten by the birds of the sky and the wild animals of the earth.
I will make this city a horror and a thing to hiss at; everyone who passes by it will be appalled and hiss because of all its wounds.
I will make them eat the flesh of their sons and daughters, and they will eat one another’s flesh during the siege and the hardship their enemies and those seeking their lives will inflict on them.’
“Then you shall break the jar before the eyes of the men who go with you,

and tell them, ‘This is what Yahweh of Armies says: In the same way I will smash this people and this city, as someone smashes a clay pot so that it cannot be repaired. They will bury the dead in Topheth until there is no more room.
This is what I will do to this place, declares Yahweh, and to its inhabitants, making this city like Topheth.

The houses of Jerusalem and the houses of Judah’s kings shall be defiled like the place of Topheth—all the houses on whose roofs they burned offerings to all the host of the heavens and poured out drink offerings to other gods.’”
Then Jeremiah came from Topheth, where Yahweh had sent him to prophesy, and he stood in the court of Yahweh’s house and said to all the people:

“So says Yahweh of Armies, God of Israel: Mark this—upon this city and all its villages I am bringing every disaster I have decreed against it, because they made their necks rigid and would not hear my words.”

notes.text: Hebrew baqbuq, a narrow-necked flask; the name imitates the gurgling sound of pouring. Its sound anticipates the verb baqqothi, “I will empty out,” in verse 7.
Hebrew Harsith, perhaps the gate where broken pottery was discarded.
Hebrew baqqothi, a play on baqbuq, “jar” (verse 1).

verses.text: Now Pashhur son of Immer, the priest, who was chief officer in Yahweh’s house, heard Jeremiah prophesying these things.
Then Pashhur struck Jeremiah the prophet and put him in the stocks{a} at the Upper Gate of Benjamin, in Yahweh’s house.
On the following day Pashhur let Jeremiah out of the stocks, and Jeremiah told him, “Yahweh’s name for you is not Pashhur, but Magor-missabib.{b}

For this is what Yahweh says: Look, I will make you a terror to yourself and to all your friends. They will fall by the sword of their enemies while your eyes look on. And all Judah I will give into the hand of the king of Babylon; he will carry them captive to Babylon and strike them down with the sword.
All this city’s riches, all its earnings, all its valuables, and every treasure of Judah’s kings I will hand over to their foes, who will loot them, carry them off, and take them away to Babylon.
As for you, Pashhur, you and all your household will go away as captives. To Babylon you will come; there you will die and there be buried, you and every friend of yours to whom you prophesied lies.”

For whenever I speak, I cry out;
“Violence and ruin!” I shout.
For the word of Yahweh has become for me
a reproach and derision all day long.

Yet if I resolve, “I will not bring him to mind
or speak again in his name,”
it turns within my heart into a blazing fire
locked up in my bones;
I am worn out trying to contain it,
and I am not able.

For I hear many muttering,
“Terror all around!
Report him! Yes, let us report him!”
All who were at peace with me
wait for me to trip:
“Maybe he can be lured;
then we will get the better of him
and have our revenge.”

O Yahweh of Armies, who test the righteous,
who see the inmost parts and the heart,
let me see your vengeance upon them,
for to you I have laid bare my cause.

Sing to Yahweh;
praise Yahweh!
For he has rescued the life of the needy
from the hand of evildoers.

A curse on the day
I came to birth!
The day my mother brought me forth—
may no blessing rest on it!

A curse on the man who carried word to my father,
“You have a son, a boy!”
and filled him with gladness.

Let that man be like the cities
that Yahweh overthrew without relenting;
let him hear a cry in the morning
and an alarm at noon,

because he did not slay me before birth,
that my mother might have been my tomb,
her womb pregnant for all time.

Why ever did I leave the womb
to look on trouble and grief,
and finish my days in disgrace?

notes.text: Hebrew mahpeketh, perhaps a device that held the body in a twisted posture.
Magor-missabib, “terror on every side.” The Septuagint reads “Exile” (Brenton) in place of the Hebrew name.
Or “You deceived me, and I was deceived”; the verb pathah is used of seducing (Exodus 22:16).

verses.text: The word that came to Jeremiah from Yahweh when King Zedekiah{a} sent to him Pashhur son of Malchiah and the priest Zephaniah son of Maaseiah, with this request:

“Inquire of Yahweh on our behalf, we beg you, for Nebuchadrezzar{b} king of Babylon is waging war on us. Perhaps Yahweh will deal with us in keeping with all his wonders, and make him withdraw from us.”
Jeremiah answered them, “Say this to Zedekiah:

‘So says Yahweh, God of Israel: Look, I will turn back the weapons of war in your hands, with which you are fighting the king of Babylon and the Chaldeans{c} who are besieging you outside the walls, and I will gather them into the heart of this city.
And it is I who will wage war on you, with hand stretched out and arm strong, in rage and fury and towering wrath.
I will strike down those who live in this city, man and beast alike; of a great plague they will die.

After that, declares Yahweh, I will deliver Zedekiah, Judah’s king, with his officials and the populace—whoever in this city is left over from plague, sword, and famine—over to Nebuchadrezzar, Babylon’s king, over to their foes and those who hunt their lives. He will cut them down with the edge of the sword, sparing none, pitying none, showing no compassion.’
“And to this people you shall say, ‘So says Yahweh: Look, I am setting before you the way of life and the way of death.

Anyone who remains inside this city will perish by sword, hunger, or plague; but anyone who walks out and gives himself up to the Chaldeans now besieging you will survive, and come away with his life as booty.{d}
For I have set my face against this city for harm and not for good, declares Yahweh; it will be handed over to Babylon’s king, and he will burn it with fire.’
“And to the royal house of Judah say, ‘Hear Yahweh’s word,

O house of David! So says Yahweh:
Dispense justice every morning,
and rescue the robbed from the oppressor’s hand,
lest my fury break out like fire
and burn with none to put it out,
because of your evil deeds.

Look, I am against you, O dweller in the valley,
O rock of the plain, declares Yahweh—
you who say, “Who can swoop down on us?
Who can break into our lairs?”

notes.text: Zedekiah (“Yahweh is righteousness”), the last king of Judah (597–586 B.C.), a son of Josiah, installed by Nebuchadnezzar (2 Kings 24:17). This Pashhur is not the Pashhur of 20:1.
Nebuchadrezzar is a variant spelling of Nebuchadnezzar, closer to the Babylonian Nabû-kudurri-uṣur, “O Nabu, protect the heir”; he reigned 605–562 B.C. Jeremiah uses both spellings.
The Chaldeans (Hebrew Kasdim) were the people of southern Babylonia whose dynasty ruled the Neo-Babylonian empire.
That is, he will escape with nothing but his life.

verses.text: So says Yahweh: “Go down to the palace of Judah’s king and speak this word there:
‘Hear Yahweh’s word, O king of Judah who sits on David’s throne—you, your servants, and your people who enter by these gates.

So says Yahweh: Practice justice and righteousness; rescue the robbed from the hand of the oppressor. Do no wrong or violence to the sojourner, the orphan, or the widow, and shed no innocent blood in this place.
For if you indeed carry out this word, then kings who sit for David on his throne will enter by the gates of this palace, riding in chariots and on horses, they and their servants and their people.
But if you refuse to obey these words, I swear by myself, declares Yahweh, that this palace will be turned into a ruin.’

For so says Yahweh concerning the palace of Judah’s king:
“You are to me like Gilead,
like the summit of Lebanon;
yet I will surely turn you into a wasteland,
towns left uninhabited.

I will send destroyers against you,
each with his weapons;
they will chop down your finest cedars
and throw them on the fire.
“Many nations will pass by this city, and each will ask his neighbor, ‘Why has Yahweh treated this great city so?’
And they will answer, ‘Because they abandoned the covenant of Yahweh their God and bowed to other gods and served them.’”

Weep not for the dead man,{a} nor mourn for him;
weep rather for the one going away,
for he will never return
to see the land of his birth.
For so says Yahweh concerning Shallum{b} son of Josiah, king of Judah, who reigned in place of Josiah his father and has gone away from this place: “He will never return here;
in the place where they carried him captive, there he will die, and he will see this land no more.”

“Woe to him who builds his house without righteousness,
his upper rooms without justice,
who works his neighbor for nothing
and pays him no wage for his toil,

who says, ‘I will build myself a large palace
with spacious upper rooms,’
so he cuts windows in it,
lines it with cedar
and paints it bright red.

Are you a king because you vie in cedar?{c}
Did not your father eat and drink
and do justice and righteousness?
Then it went well with him.

He defended the cause of the poor and needy;
then it went well.
Is not this what it means to know me?
declares Yahweh.

But your eyes and your heart
are set only on your unjust gain,
on shedding innocent blood,
on oppression and extortion.”

Therefore this is what Yahweh says about Jehoiakim{d} son of Josiah, king of Judah:
“Nobody will mourn for him by saying,
‘Oh, my brother!’ or ‘Oh, my sister!’
Nobody will mourn for him by saying,
‘Oh, master!’ or ‘Oh, his majesty!’

I spoke to you in your ease,
but you said, ‘I will not listen.’
This has been your way from your youth,
that you have not obeyed my voice.

The wind will shepherd all your shepherds,
and your lovers will go into captivity;
then you will be ashamed and disgraced
for all your wickedness.

You who make your home in Lebanon,
who nest high in the cedars,
what groaning{g} will be yours when the pains seize you,
throes like those of childbirth!”
“As I live, declares Yahweh, even if Coniah{h} son of Jehoiakim, king of Judah, were the signet ring on my right hand, yet I would tear you off from there,
and hand you over to those who want to kill you, to those you fear, to Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon and to the Chaldeans.
I will hurl you and the mother who bore you into another country, where you were not born, and there you will die.
But to the land to which they long to return, there they will not return.”

Is Coniah, then, a scorned and shattered jar,
a pot that pleases no one?
Why have he and his children been flung away,
tossed out into a country unknown to them?

O land, land, land,
hear the word of Yahweh!

notes.text: That is, King Josiah, killed at Megiddo in 609 B.C. (2 Kings 23:29).
Shallum (“recompense”) is the personal name of King Jehoahaz, son of Josiah, who reigned three months in 609 B.C. before Pharaoh Neco took him to Egypt (2 Kings 23:30–34).
Or “because you outdo others in cedar.”
Jehoiakim (“Yahweh raises up”), son of Josiah, reigned 609–598 B.C. (2 Kings 23:34–24:6).
2 Kings 24:6 says only that Jehoiakim “slept with his fathers”; the fulfillment of this oracle is not described.
Abarim, the mountain range east of the Dead Sea, including Mount Nebo.
So the Septuagint and other ancient witnesses; the Hebrew reads “how you will be pitied” or “how favored you will be.”

Coniah, a short form of Jeconiah or Jehoiachin (“Yahweh establishes”), who reigned three months in 598–597 B.C. before being exiled to Babylon (2 Kings 24:8–15). In verses 24–27 the Hebrew shifts between “him” and “you.”
Jehoiachin had sons (1 Chronicles 3:17–18), but none reigned as king.

verses.text: “Woe to the shepherds who ruin and scatter the sheep of my pasture!” declares Yahweh.

Therefore so says Yahweh, God of Israel, about the shepherds who tend my people: “You have dispersed my flock and driven them off, and have not attended to them. Watch: I will attend to you for the evil of your deeds,” declares Yahweh.
“And I will personally round up what is left of my sheep out of every land to which I banished them, and lead them home to their fold, where they will bear young and multiply.
Over them I will set shepherds who will tend them; no longer will they fear or be terrified, and none will be missing,” declares Yahweh.

“Look, days are coming,” declares Yahweh,
“when I will raise up for David a righteous Branch;{a}
he will reign as king and act wisely,
and he will do justice and righteousness in the land.

In his days Judah will be saved,
and Israel will dwell in safety.
And this is the name by which he will be called:
‘Yahweh Is Our Righteousness.’{b}
“Therefore, look, days are coming,” declares Yahweh, “when men will no longer say, ‘By the life of Yahweh, who brought Israel’s sons up from the land of Egypt,’

but, ‘By the life of Yahweh, who brought up and led the offspring of Israel’s house out of the northern land and out of all the lands where I had driven them.’ Then they will dwell on their own soil.”{c}

About the prophets:
Shattered is my heart inside me;
every bone of mine shakes;
I have become like one who is drunk,
like a fellow mastered by wine,
on account of Yahweh,
on account of his holy words.

“For both prophet and priest are godless;
even in my house I have found their wickedness,” declares Yahweh.

“In Samaria’s prophets
I observed something distasteful:
they spoke oracles by Baal
and misled Israel my people.

Yet in Jerusalem’s prophets
I have observed something appalling:
adultery and a life of lies;
they bolster the power of the wicked,
so that none turns back from his wickedness;
to me they are all like Sodom,
and her people like Gomorrah.”

So Yahweh of Armies pronounces this about the prophets:
“I will make them eat wormwood
and drink water laced with poison,
for out of the prophets of Jerusalem
ungodliness has spread over the whole land.”

They keep saying to those who despise me,
‘Yahweh has said, “You shall have peace”’;
and to everyone who walks in the stubbornness of his heart they say,
‘No calamity will come upon you.’”

For who has stood in the council{f} of Yahweh
to see and to hear his word?
Who has paid attention to his word and listened?

See, Yahweh’s tempest!
Fury is unleashed,
a spinning gale;
on the heads of the wicked it will crash.

Yahweh’s anger will not turn away
until he has carried out
the purposes of his mind.
In days to come
you will understand this fully.

“I never dispatched those prophets,
yet off they ran;
I never spoke to them,
yet they uttered prophecy.

But if they had attended my council,
they would have announced my words to my people
and turned them away from their evil ways
and evil deeds.

“Am I a God near at hand,” declares Yahweh,
“and not a God far off?

Can a man hide himself in secret places
so that I cannot see him?” declares Yahweh.
“Do I not fill the heavens and the earth?” declares Yahweh.
“I have heard what the prophets have said who prophesy falsehood in my name, saying, ‘I have dreamed, I have dreamed!’
How long? Is it in the heart of the prophets who prophesy falsehood, the prophets of the deceit of their own heart—
They intend to make my people forget my name through the dreams they tell each other, just as their ancestors forgot my name through Baal.
The prophet who has a dream—let him recount his dream; but the one who holds my word—let him relate my word with fidelity. What does chaff have to do with grain?” declares Yahweh.
“Is my word not like a fire,” declares Yahweh, “and like a hammer that breaks a rock apart?
“Therefore look, I am against the prophets,” declares Yahweh, “who take my words from one another.
Look, I am against the prophets,” declares Yahweh, “who use their tongues and declare, ‘He declares.’

Mark well, I am against those whose prophecies are false dreams,” declares Yahweh, “who recount them and mislead my people with their falsehoods and their wild boasting, though I never sent or commissioned them; not the slightest benefit do they bring this people,” declares Yahweh.
“Whenever this people, or a prophet, or a priest asks you, ‘What is Yahweh’s load?’{g} answer them, ‘You are the load, and I will throw you off,’ declares Yahweh.
And the prophet, priest, or commoner who says, ‘Yahweh’s load’—that man and his house I will call to account.
This is what each of you should say to his neighbor and relative: ‘What did Yahweh reply?’ or ‘What has Yahweh said?’
But never again bring up ‘Yahweh’s load,’ for each man’s own word becomes his load, and you twist the words of the living God, Yahweh of Armies, our God.
Thus you shall say to the prophet: ‘What has Yahweh answered you?’ or ‘What has Yahweh spoken?’
Yet if you persist in saying, ‘Yahweh’s load,’ then here is what Yahweh says: ‘Since you use this phrase, “Yahweh’s load,” though I sent word to you forbidding you to say, “Yahweh’s load,”
for that reason I will indeed lift you up{h} and fling you out of my sight, you along with the city I bestowed on you and your ancestors.
I will lay on you a disgrace that lasts forever, a humiliation without end, never to be forgotten.’”

notes.text: Hebrew tsemaḥ, “sprout, shoot,” a title for the coming king from David’s line (33:15; Zechariah 3:8; 6:12).
Hebrew Yahweh tsidqenu, perhaps a play on the name of King Zedekiah, tsidqiyyahu, “Yahweh is my righteousness.” The Septuagint renders the name as “Josedec” (Brenton), a personal name.
The Septuagint places verses 7–8 after verse 40 (Brenton, printed as 23:40a–b). Verses 7–8 nearly repeat 16:14–15.
Or, with some ancient witnesses, “because of these things.”
Hebrew hevel, “breath, vapor”; they fill you with empty hopes.
Hebrew sod, the council of heavenly beings around Yahweh (compare 1 Kings 22:19–22).

Hebrew massaʾ means both “load, burden” and “oracle, utterance” (literally, something “lifted” by the voice). Verses 33–40 play on the double meaning. “You are the load” follows the Septuagint (“You are the burden,” Brenton) and the Latin Vulgate; the standard Hebrew text reads “What load?” (ʾeth-mah-massaʾ), a difference only in word division.
Hebrew nashithi nasoʾ, “I will utterly forget,” is read by some Hebrew manuscripts and ancient witnesses as nasaʾthi nasoʾ, “I will surely lift up,” continuing the play on massaʾ.

verses.text: Yahweh showed me this: two baskets of figs were set in front of Yahweh’s temple. This was after Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon had deported Jeconiah{a} son of Jehoiakim, king of Judah, from Jerusalem, along with the officials of Judah, the skilled workers and the metalworkers,{b} and brought them to Babylon.
One basket held very fine figs, like first-ripe figs; the other basket held very bad figs, so bad they could not be eaten.
Then Yahweh asked me, “What do you see, Jeremiah?” I replied, “Figs—the good ones very good, and the bad ones very bad, too bad to be eaten.”
Then Yahweh’s word came to me:
“This is what Yahweh, the God of Israel, says: Like these good figs, I will treat as good the exiles of Judah, whom I sent away from this place to the land of the Chaldeans.
I will keep my eyes on them for good and bring them back to this land. I will build them and not tear them down; I will plant them and not uproot them.
I will give them a heart to know me, that I am Yahweh. They will be my people and I will be their God, for they will return to me with all their heart.

“But like the bad figs, which are too bad to be eaten—so says Yahweh—so will I treat Zedekiah king of Judah, his officials, the remnant of Jerusalem left in this land, and those who live in the land of Egypt.
I will make them a horror, a calamity{c} to all the kingdoms of the earth, a reproach, a byword, a taunt, and a curse in all the places where I drive them.
And I will send among them sword, famine, and plague, until they are wiped out from the soil I gave to them and to their fathers.”

notes.text: Jeconiah, another form of the name Jehoiachin (see the note at 22:24). The deportation took place in 597 B.C. (2 Kings 24:10–16).
Or “the smiths”; the Hebrew masger may mean “locksmith” or “fortifier.”
Hebrew “a horror for calamity.” The Septuagint reads, “I will cause them to be dispersed into all the kingdoms of the earth” (Brenton), and lacks “calamity.”

verses.text: The word that came to Jeremiah concerning all the people of Judah in the fourth year of Jehoiakim son of Josiah, king of Judah (that was the first year of Nebuchadrezzar king of Babylon),{a}
which Jeremiah the prophet spoke to all the people of Judah and all the residents of Jerusalem:

“From the thirteenth year of Josiah son of Amon, king of Judah, until this day—these twenty-three years—Yahweh’s word has come to me, and I have spoken to you, early and persistently, but you have not listened.
And Yahweh sent you all his servants the prophets, early and persistently, but you did not listen or incline your ear to hear,
when they said, ‘Turn now, each of you, from his evil way and his evil deeds, and dwell on the soil that Yahweh gave to you and your fathers from of old and forever.
Do not go after other gods to serve them and bow down to them, and do not provoke me with the work of your hands; then I will do you no harm.’
Yet you did not listen to me, declares Yahweh, so as to provoke me with the work of your hands to your own harm.{b}
“Therefore so says Yahweh of Armies: Because you have not obeyed my words,

mark this, I am summoning every northern clan, declares Yahweh, and Nebuchadrezzar, Babylon’s king, my servant,{c} and I will lead them against this land and those who live in it, and against all the surrounding nations. I will put them under the ban{d} and turn them into an object of dread, of whistling, and of perpetual ruin.
I will silence among them the noise of merriment and the noise of joy, the bridegroom’s voice and the bride’s voice, the grinding of the hand mill and the glow of the lamp.
This whole land will become a ruin and a horror, and these nations will serve the king of Babylon seventy years.{e}
Then when seventy years are completed, I will punish the king of Babylon and that nation, declares Yahweh, for their guilt—the land of the Chaldeans—and make it a desolation forever.
I will bring upon that country everything I have said about it, everything recorded in this book, which Jeremiah prophesied about all the nations.{f}
For many nations and great kings shall enslave them also, and I will repay them according to their deeds and the work of their hands.”{g}
For this is what Yahweh, Israel’s God, told me: “Accept from my hand this cup brimming with the wine of fury, and give it to every nation I send you to, that they may drink.
They shall drink and stagger and act crazed because of the sword I am sending among them.”
So I took the cup from Yahweh’s hand and gave it to all the nations Yahweh had sent me to, to drink:
Jerusalem and the towns of Judah, its kings and its officials, to make them a ruin, a horror, a thing to hiss at, and a curse, as it is this day;
Pharaoh, Egypt’s king, with his attendants, his nobles, and his whole nation;
all the mixed peoples;{h} all the kings of the land of Uz;{i} all the kings of the land of the Philistines—Ashkelon, Gaza, Ekron, and the remnant of Ashdod;
Edom, Moab, and the sons of Ammon;
all the kings of Tyre, all the kings of Sidon, and the kings of the coastland across the sea;
Dedan, Tema, Buz, and all who clip the corners of their hair;
all the kings of Arabia and all the kings of the mixed peoples who dwell in the wilderness;
all the kings of Zimri,{j} all the kings of Elam, and all the kings of Media;
and all the kings of the north, near and far, one after another—all the kingdoms on earth. After them the king of Sheshach{k} will drink.
“Then tell them, ‘This is what Yahweh of Armies, the God of Israel, says: Drink, get drunk and throw up, fall and never get up again, because of the sword I am sending among you.’
And if they refuse to take the cup from your hand to drink, say to them, ‘So says Yahweh of Armies: You must drink!

For, consider: on the very city that bears my name I am starting to bring disaster; and will you go scot-free? Not scot-free will you go, for I am calling down a sword on everyone who lives on the earth, declares Yahweh of Armies.’

“So says Yahweh of Armies:
Look, calamity goes forth
from nation to nation,
and a great storm is stirred up
from the farthest parts of the earth.
And those slain by Yahweh on that day will be from one end of the earth to the other end of the earth. They will not be mourned, gathered, or buried; they will be dung on the face of the ground.

Flight will fail the shepherds,
and escape the lords of the flock.

Listen—the cry of the shepherds,
the wail of the lords of the flock!
For Yahweh is ravaging their pasture,

and the peaceful folds are laid waste
because of the fierce anger of Yahweh.

He has quit his thicket like a lion,
for their country has turned into a wasteland
before the sword of the oppressor{m}
and before his burning anger.”

notes.text: That is, 605 B.C., the year of the battle of Carchemish (46:2). The Septuagint lacks the parenthesis (Brenton).
The Septuagint lacks most of verse 7, reading only, “But you did not listen to me” (Brenton, modernized).
The Septuagint lacks “and for Nebuchadrezzar king of Babylon, my servant” and reads “a family from the north” (Brenton). In the shorter Greek text, the foe from the north is not named here.
Hebrew ḥerem, the ban of total destruction in holy war.

The seventy years are reckoned in different ways: from 605 B.C. to the fall of Babylon in 539 B.C., or from the destruction of the temple in 586 B.C. to its rebuilding in 516 B.C. (compare 29:10; 2 Chronicles 36:21; Daniel 9:2; Zechariah 1:12). The Septuagint lacks “the king of Babylon” in verse 11 and “the king of Babylon and” in verse 12 (Brenton).

In the Septuagint, verse 13 ends at “written in this book,” and the next words introduce the oracles against the nations, beginning with Elam (Brenton: “The Prophecies of Jeremias against the Nations of Ælam”). These oracles, which stand at chapters 46–51 in the Hebrew, follow at this point in the Greek. See the introductory note.
The Septuagint lacks verse 14 (Brenton). The Greek resumes with verse 15 as chapter 32 in Brenton’s numbering.
Or “all the foreign people”; Hebrew ʿerev, perhaps foreign mercenaries or settlers.
The Septuagint lacks “all the kings of the land of Uz” (Brenton). Uz is a region east or southeast of Israel, the home of Job (Job 1:1).
Zimri is otherwise unknown; it may be a cipher like Sheshach (verse 26), or a corruption. The Septuagint lacks it (Brenton).

Sheshach is a cipher for Babel (Babylon), formed by atbash, a scribal code that replaces each Hebrew letter with its counterpart from the other end of the alphabet (aleph with taw, beth with shin, and so on): b-b-l becomes sh-sh-k. See also 51:41. The Septuagint lacks this sentence (Brenton).
Hebrew uncertain; some read “and I will shatter you.”
So some Hebrew manuscripts (compare 46:16; 50:16); the Septuagint has “the great sword” (Brenton); the standard Hebrew text reads “the oppressor’s fury,” with “fury” repeated in the next line.

verses.text: At the beginning of the reign of Jehoiakim son of Josiah, king of Judah,{a} this word came from Yahweh:

“So says Yahweh: Take your stand in the court of Yahweh’s house and speak to all the towns of Judah that come to bow down in Yahweh’s house all the words I command you to speak to them; hold back not a word.
Perhaps they will listen, and each will turn from his evil way, so that I may relent of the calamity I am planning to bring on them because of their evil deeds.
Say to them, ‘So says Yahweh: If you will not listen to me, to walk in my law that I have set before you,
and to heed the words of my servants the prophets whom I send to you early and persistently, though you have not listened,
then I will make this house like Shiloh, and I will make this city an example of a curse for all the nations on earth.’”
The priests, the prophets, and all the people heard Jeremiah speaking these words in Yahweh’s house.
When Jeremiah had said all that Yahweh ordered him to tell the people, the priests, the prophets and everyone else seized him and said, “You are going to die!
Why did you prophesy in Yahweh’s name that this house will become like Shiloh and this city will be destroyed and left uninhabited?” And all the people gathered around Jeremiah in Yahweh’s house.
When the officials of Judah heard of these things, they went up from the king’s palace to Yahweh’s house and took their seats at the entrance of the New Gate of Yahweh’s house.
Then the priests and the prophets told the officials and everyone else, “This man deserves the death penalty, since he has prophesied against this city, as you yourselves have heard.”
Jeremiah then addressed all the officials and the whole populace: “It was Yahweh who sent me to prophesy against this house and this city every word you have heard.
So now, mend your conduct and your actions, and heed the voice of Yahweh your God; then Yahweh will think better of the disaster he has decreed for you.
As for me, I am in your power; do to me whatever you think is good and right.

Only know for certain that if you put me to death, you will bring innocent blood on yourselves, on this city, and on its residents, for in truth Yahweh sent me to you to speak all these words in your hearing.”
At that the officials and all the populace told the priests and prophets, “No death sentence is due this man, since it is in the name of Yahweh our God that he has addressed us.”
And some of the elders of the land rose up and spoke to the whole assembly of the people:

“Micah of Moresheth{b} was a prophet in the time of Hezekiah king of Judah. He said to all the people of Judah, ‘This is what Yahweh of Armies says:
Zion will be plowed like a field;

Did Hezekiah king of Judah and all Judah put him to death? Did he not fear Yahweh and entreat the favor of Yahweh, and did not Yahweh relent of the calamity he had pronounced against them? But we are about to bring great calamity on ourselves.”
There was also a man who prophesied in Yahweh’s name, Uriah son of Shemaiah from Kiriath-jearim. He prophesied against this city and this land in words like all those of Jeremiah.
King Jehoiakim, along with all his fighting men and every official, heard what he said, and the king set out to have him killed. Uriah got word of it; in fear he ran off and reached Egypt.
Then King Jehoiakim sent men to Egypt—Elnathan son of Achbor{c} and others with him.
These fetched Uriah back from Egypt and delivered him to King Jehoiakim, who cut him down with a sword and flung his body among the burial plots of the common folk.
Yet Ahikam son of Shaphan{d} stood by Jeremiah and protected him, so that he was not handed over to the mob to be killed.

notes.text: That is, about 609 B.C. This chapter narrates the occasion and outcome of the temple sermon given more fully in 7:1–15.
Micah of Moresheth, the prophet whose book stands among the Twelve; the quotation is Micah 3:12. Micah means “Who is like Yahweh?”
Elnathan (“God has given”) was perhaps the father of Nehushta, Jehoiachin’s mother (2 Kings 24:8). The Septuagint lacks “Elnathan son of Achbor and others with him” (Brenton).
Ahikam son of Shaphan, an official under Josiah (2 Kings 22:12) and father of Gedaliah, later governor of Judah (40:5).

verses.text: At the beginning of the reign of Zedekiah{a} son of Josiah, king of Judah, this word came to Jeremiah from Yahweh:
This is what Yahweh told me: “Fashion for yourself thongs and wooden yoke bars, and set them upon your neck.
Then dispatch them{b} to Edom’s king, Moab’s king, the Ammonites’ king, Tyre’s king, and Sidon’s king, through the emissaries who have arrived in Jerusalem to meet Zedekiah, Judah’s king.
Give them a charge for their lords: ‘Thus speaks Yahweh of Armies, Israel’s God—tell this to your lords:
By my great power and outstretched arm I made the earth, together with the people and animals on it, and I give it to anyone I choose.
And now I have given all these lands into the hand of Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon, my servant; even the beasts of the field I have given him to serve him.
All the nations shall serve him and his son and his grandson, until the time of his own land comes; then many nations and great kings shall make him their servant.{c}

“If any nation or kingdom refuses to serve Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon and refuses to bend its neck under the yoke of the king of Babylon, I will punish that nation with sword, famine and plague, declares Yahweh, until I have finished them off through him.
So pay no heed to your prophets or your diviners, to your dreamers,{d} your fortune-tellers, or your sorcerers, who keep assuring you, “You will never be subject to Babylon’s king.”
A falsehood is what they prophesy to you, and it will only get you removed far from your homeland; I will banish you, and you will be lost.
But the nation that brings its neck under the yoke of the king of Babylon and serves him, I will leave on its own soil, declares Yahweh, to till it and dwell in it.’”
To Zedekiah king of Judah I spoke in the same way: “Bring your necks under the yoke of the king of Babylon, and serve him and his people, and live.
Why must you and your people perish by sword, starvation, and pestilence, as Yahweh has threatened against every nation that refuses to be subject to Babylon’s king?{e}
Do not listen to the words of the prophets who keep telling you, ‘You shall not serve the king of Babylon,’ for it is a lie they prophesy to you.
I never sent them, declares Yahweh; yet they prophesy lies under my name, and so I will banish you and you will be lost, both you and the prophets prophesying to you.”

Next I addressed the priests and this whole people: “So says Yahweh: Pay no heed to what your prophets prophesy to you, ‘Look, any day now the furnishings of Yahweh’s house will be returned from Babylon,’ for a falsehood is what they prophesy to you.
Do not listen to them. Serve the king of Babylon and live. Why should this city become a ruin?{f}

If they are prophets, and if Yahweh’s word is with them, let them now intercede with Yahweh of Armies, that the vessels left in Yahweh’s house, in the palace of the king of Judah, and in Jerusalem may not go to Babylon.
For Yahweh of Armies has spoken about the columns,{g} the bronze sea, the wheeled bases, and whatever other furnishings remain in this city,
which Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon did not take when he carried Jeconiah son of Jehoiakim, king of Judah, into exile from Jerusalem to Babylon, with all the nobles of Judah and Jerusalem—
so says Yahweh of Armies, God of Israel, concerning the vessels left in Yahweh’s house, in the palace of the king of Judah, and in Jerusalem:{h}
‘To Babylon they shall be carried, and there they shall remain until the day I attend to them, declares Yahweh. Then I will bring them up and restore them to this place.’”

notes.text: So a few Hebrew manuscripts and the Syriac (compare verses 3 and 12 and 28:1); the standard Hebrew text reads “Jehoiakim,” probably by copying from 26:1. The Septuagint lacks verse 1 (Brenton). The likely date is 594–593 B.C. (28:1).
Hebrew “send them.” Jeremiah’s symbolic yoke is described in 28:10–11.
The Septuagint lacks verse 7 (Brenton).
Hebrew “your dreams.”
The Septuagint lacks verse 13 (Brenton). Its text of verses 12–22 is markedly shorter throughout.
The Septuagint lacks verse 17 (Brenton).

The two bronze pillars, Jachin and Boaz, the great bronze basin called “the sea,” and the wheeled stands made for Solomon’s temple (1 Kings 7:15–39). The Septuagint lacks this list, reading only “And as for the remaining vessels” (Brenton).
The Septuagint lacks verse 21 and the last sentence of verse 22, ending, “they shall go into Babylon, says the Lord” (Brenton, modernized).

verses.text: In that same year, at the start of the reign of Zedekiah king of Judah, in the fourth year,{a} in the fifth month (in July–August),{b} the prophet Hananiah{c} son of Azzur, from Gibeon, addressed me in Yahweh’s house before the priests and all the people:
“So says Yahweh of Armies, God of Israel: I have broken the yoke of Babylon’s king.
Within two years’ time I will bring back to this place all the furnishings of Yahweh’s house that Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon removed from this place and carried to Babylon.
I will also bring back to this place Jeconiah son of Jehoiakim, king of Judah, and all the exiles of Judah who went to Babylon, declares Yahweh, for I will smash the yoke of the king of Babylon.”
Then Jeremiah the prophet answered Hananiah the prophet in the presence of the priests and of all the people standing in Yahweh’s house.
Jeremiah the prophet said, “Amen! May Yahweh do so! May Yahweh fulfill the words you have prophesied and bring back from Babylon to this place the furnishings of Yahweh’s house and all the exiles.
Nevertheless, give ear to this word that I am declaring to you and to the whole people listening:
The prophets who lived before you and me long ago prophesied war, disaster and plague against many countries and great kingdoms.
As for the prophet who prophesies peace, when that prophet’s word comes to pass, then it will be known that Yahweh truly sent him.”
Then the prophet Hananiah removed the yoke bar from the prophet Jeremiah’s neck and broke it.

And Hananiah spoke before all the people: “So says Yahweh: Just so will I break the yoke of Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon from the neck of all the nations within two years’ time.” And Jeremiah the prophet went his way.
Some time after the prophet Hananiah had broken the yoke bar that was on the prophet Jeremiah’s neck, Yahweh’s word came to Jeremiah:
“Go and tell Hananiah, ‘So says Yahweh: Yoke bars of wood you have broken, but in their place you will make{d} yoke bars of iron.

For so says Yahweh of Armies, God of Israel: A yoke of iron I have put on the neck of all these nations to serve Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon, and they shall serve him; even the beasts of the field I have given him.’”
Jeremiah the prophet then told Hananiah the prophet, “Hear me, Hananiah! Yahweh never sent you, and you have led this people to rely on falsehood.
Therefore so says Yahweh: Look, I am sending you off{e} from the face of the earth. This very year you will die, because you have spoken rebellion against Yahweh.”
And Hananiah the prophet died that same year, in the seventh month (in September–October).{f}

notes.text: That is, 594–593 B.C. The Septuagint reads simply “in the fourth year of Zedekiah king of Judah” (Brenton, modernized).
Hebrew “the fifth month,” Av.
Hananiah, “Yahweh has been gracious.” The Septuagint calls him “the false prophet” (Brenton), here and elsewhere in the chapter.
So the Hebrew; the Septuagint reads “I will make” (Brenton: “but I will make instead of them yokes of iron”).
Hebrew meshallḥakha, a play on the verb “send” (shalaḥ) in verse 15: Yahweh did not send Hananiah as a prophet, but he will send him off the earth.
Hebrew “the seventh month,” Tishri, about two months after the confrontation of verse 1. The Septuagint lacks “that same year” (Brenton).

verses.text: These are the words of the letter that Jeremiah the prophet sent from Jerusalem to the surviving elders of the exiles, to the priests, the prophets, and all the people whom Nebuchadnezzar had carried into exile from Jerusalem to Babylon.
This was after King Jeconiah had left Jerusalem, along with the queen mother, the court officials,{a} Judah’s and Jerusalem’s leaders, and the craftsmen and metalworkers.
The letter went by the hand of Elasah son of Shaphan and Gemariah son of Hilkiah, whom Zedekiah king of Judah dispatched to Babylon, to Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon. It read:
“So says Yahweh of Armies, God of Israel, to all the exiles whom I have exiled from Jerusalem to Babylon:
Build houses and settle in them; plant gardens and eat what they produce.
Take wives and father sons and daughters; take wives for your sons, and give your daughters to husbands, that they may bear sons and daughters. Multiply there; do not dwindle.
And seek the welfare{b} of the city where I have exiled you, and pray to Yahweh on its behalf, for in its welfare will be your welfare.
For so says Yahweh of Armies, God of Israel: Do not let the prophets and the diviners among you deceive you, and pay no attention to the dreams you have them dream,{c}
for it is a lie they are prophesying to you in my name. I did not send them, declares Yahweh.
“For so says Yahweh: Only when seventy years for Babylon are completed will I attend to you, and I will fulfill for you my good word, to bring you back to this place.
For I know the plans I have for you, declares Yahweh—plans for well-being and not for disaster, to give you a future with hope.{d}
Then you will cry out to me; you will come and pray to me, and I will hear you.
You will seek me and find me, when you search for me with all your heart.

Found by you I will be, declares Yahweh; I will turn your captivity around and collect you out of every nation and every place to which I banished you, declares Yahweh, and lead you home to the place from which I sent you into exile.{e}
“You have claimed, ‘Yahweh has appointed prophets for us in Babylon’—
this is what Yahweh says about the king who sits on David’s throne and about all the people who live in this city, your relatives who did not go into exile with you:{f}
So says Yahweh of Armies: Look, I am sending among them sword, famine, and plague, and I will make them like rotten figs, too bad to be eaten.

I will pursue them with sword, famine, and plague, and I will make them a horror to all the kingdoms of the earth, a curse, a desolation, a thing to hiss at, and a reproach among all the nations where I have driven them,
because they did not heed my words, declares Yahweh, which I sent to them by my servants the prophets, early and persistently; and you too would not listen, declares Yahweh.
Hear, then, Yahweh’s word, all you exiles whom I sent away from Jerusalem to Babylon:

This is what Yahweh of Armies, the God of Israel, says about Ahab son of Kolaiah and Zedekiah son of Maaseiah, who are prophesying lies to you in my name: Look, I will deliver them to Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon, and you will see him execute them.
Because of them, all the exiles from Judah in Babylon will use this curse: ‘May Yahweh make you like Zedekiah and Ahab, whom the king of Babylon roasted over a fire,’{g}
For they committed folly in Israel, sleeping with their neighbors’ wives and speaking in my name falsehoods I never charged them to speak. I know it, and I bear witness, declares Yahweh.”
To Shemaiah the Nehelamite{h} you shall say:
“So says Yahweh of Armies, God of Israel: Because you have sent letters in your own name to all the people in Jerusalem, to Zephaniah son of Maaseiah the priest, and to all the priests, saying,
‘Yahweh has appointed you priest in place of Jehoiada the priest, to be in charge in Yahweh’s house of every madman who acts like a prophet, and to put such a person in the stocks and neck irons.
Now then, why have you not rebuked Jeremiah of Anathoth, who is prophesying to you?
For he has sent to us in Babylon, saying, “It will be long; build houses and settle in them, and plant gardens and eat what they produce.”’”
Zephaniah the priest read this letter in the hearing of Jeremiah the prophet.
Then Yahweh’s word came to Jeremiah:
“Send word to all the exiles: ‘So says Yahweh about Shemaiah the Nehelamite: Since Shemaiah prophesied to you though I never sent him, and led you to rely on falsehood,

therefore so says Yahweh: Look, I will punish Shemaiah the Nehelamite and his offspring. He shall have no man dwelling among this people to see the good I will do to my people, declares Yahweh, for he has spoken rebellion against Yahweh.’”

notes.text: Hebrew sarisim, often “eunuchs,” but also a general title for court officials.
Hebrew shalom, “peace, welfare, wholeness,” three times in this verse.
Hebrew “your dreams that you cause to be dreamed”; the Septuagint reads “your dreams which you dream” (Brenton, modernized).
Hebrew “an end (aḥarith) and a hope,” that is, a hopeful future.
The Septuagint lacks most of verse 14, reading only “And I will appear to you” (Brenton).
The Septuagint lacks verses 16–20 (Brenton).
Hebrew qalam, “roasted,” a play on qelalah, “curse,” and on the name Kolaiah (verse 21).
Nehelamite, perhaps “of Nehelam,” an unknown place; it may also suggest ḥalam, “to dream.”

verses.text: The word that came to Jeremiah from Yahweh:
“So says Yahweh, God of Israel: Write down in a scroll{a} every word I have spoken to you.

For look, days are coming, declares Yahweh, when I will turn back the captivity of my people, Israel and Judah, says Yahweh, and lead them home to the land I gave their fathers, and they will take possession of it.”
These are the words Yahweh spoke concerning Israel and Judah:

So says Yahweh:
“A cry of panic we have heard,
of dread, and no peace.

Ask now and consider:
can a male give birth?
Why then do I see every man
with his hands on his loins like a woman in labor,
every face turned ashen?

Alas! For that day is great,
with none like it;
a season of distress it is for Jacob,
yet out of it he will be saved.

“On that day, declares Yahweh of Armies,
I will snap the yoke from off your{b} neck,
and your thongs I will tear apart,
and foreigners will no longer make him their slave.

Instead they will serve Yahweh their God
and David their king,
whom I will raise up for them.

Why cry out over your fracture,
your pain past cure?
Because your guilt is great,
because your sins are many,
I have done these things to you.{e}

So everyone who devours you will be devoured,
and all your enemies will be taken into exile;
those who rob you will themselves be robbed,
and all who plunder you I will give over to plunder.

For fresh skin I will grow over you,
and of your wounds I will cure you, declares Yahweh,
since “Castaway” they have named you:
“That is Zion, whom nobody seeks!”

From them will come songs of thanksgiving
and the sound of those who make merry.
I will multiply them, and they will not be few;
I will bring them honor, and they will not be small.

His sons will be as in days of old,
and his congregation will be established before me,
and I will punish all who oppress him.

Their leader will come from among them,
their ruler will arise from their own number.
I will let him come close and approach me,
for who would risk his life
to approach me? declares Yahweh.

And you will be my people,
and I will be your God.”{g}

Look, the storm of Yahweh!
Fury goes out,
a sweeping tempest;
it will whirl down on the head of the wicked.

The burning anger of Yahweh will not turn back
until he has carried out and accomplished
the purposes of his heart.
In the latter days
you will understand this.{h}

notes.text: Chapters 30–31 are often called “the Book of Consolation.”
So the Hebrew; the Septuagint reads “their neck” (Brenton).
The Septuagint lacks verses 10–11 (Brenton); they appear again at 46:27–28, where the Septuagint has them.
The Hebrew of this verse is uncertain.
The Septuagint lacks verse 15 (Brenton).
Hebrew tel, a mound of ruins built up from earlier settlements.
The Septuagint lacks verse 22 (Brenton).
Verses 23–24 nearly repeat 23:19–20.

verses.text: “In that time, declares Yahweh, I will be God to all the clans of Israel, and they shall be a people to me.”

Again I will build you, and built you shall be,
O virgin Israel!
Again you will take up your tambourines
and go forth in the dance of merrymakers.

Again you will plant vineyards
on Samaria’s hills;
the planters will plant
and enjoy the fruit.

For a day comes when watchmen will call out
on the hill country of Ephraim,
“Up, let us go to Zion,
to Yahweh our God!”’”

Look, I am bringing them from the north country
and gathering them from the far reaches of the earth,
among them the blind and the lame,
the woman with child and the one in labor together;
a great throng, they will return here.

“Nations, listen to Yahweh’s word
and tell it in the distant coastlands;
say, ‘The one who scattered Israel will gather them
and watch over them like a shepherd over his flock.’

For Yahweh has ransomed Jacob
and redeemed him from a hand too strong for him.

They will come and shout for joy on Zion’s height
and stream toward the goodness of Yahweh—
toward grain, new wine, and oil,
and the young of flock and herd;
their life will be like a well-watered garden,
and they will languish no more.

I will drench the priests’ souls with abundance,
and my people will be filled with my goodness, declares Yahweh.”

So says Yahweh:
“A voice in Ramah is heard,
lamentation, bitter weeping:
Rachel{c} weeping over her children,
refusing to be comforted over her children,
because they are no more.”

So says Yahweh:
“Hold back your voice from weeping
and your eyes from tears,
for there is a reward for your labor, declares Yahweh;
they will return from the land of the enemy.

There is hope for your future, declares Yahweh;
your children will return to their own territory.

“Clearly I have heard Ephraim rocking with grief:
‘You disciplined me, and I took the discipline,
like a calf untrained to the yoke.
Bring me back, that I may come back,
for you are Yahweh my God.

Is Ephraim a dear son to me?
A child of delight?
For as often as I speak against him,
I remember him still.
Therefore my inmost parts yearn for him;
I will surely have compassion on him, declares Yahweh.

How long will you waver,
O faithless daughter?
For Yahweh has created a new thing in the land:
a female surrounds a man.”{d}

So says Yahweh of Armies, God of Israel: “Once more they will use this saying in the land of Judah and in its cities, when I restore their fortunes:
‘Yahweh bless you, abode of righteousness,
O holy mountain!’
And Judah and all its cities will dwell in it together, the farmers and those who wander with flocks.
For the exhausted soul I will revive, and each drooping soul I will fill full.”
Upon this I woke and saw; pleasant to me my sleep had been.{e}
“Look, days are coming, declares Yahweh, when I will sow the house of Israel and the house of Judah with the seed of man and the seed of beast.
And as I watched over them to uproot and to tear down, to overthrow, to destroy, and to bring harm, so I will watch over them to build and to plant, declares Yahweh.

In those days they will no longer say,
‘The fathers ate sour grapes,
and the children’s teeth are set on edge.’
Instead, everyone will die for his own sin; whoever eats sour grapes will have his own teeth set on edge.
“Look, the days are coming, declares Yahweh, when I will make a new covenant{f} with the people of Israel and the people of Judah—

unlike the covenant I cut with their ancestors when I took hold of their hand to lead them out from Egypt’s land—that covenant of mine they shattered, even though I was master over them,{g} declares Yahweh.

For this is the covenant I will cut with the house of Israel after those days, declares Yahweh: I will set my law{h} within them, and upon their heart I will write it; and I will be their God, and they shall be my people.

And no longer will each one teach his neighbor and each his brother, saying, ‘Know Yahweh,’ for they shall all know me, from the least of them to the greatest, declares Yahweh; for I will forgive their guilt, and their sin I will remember no more.”

So says Yahweh,{i}
giver of the sun to light the daytime,
of the statutes of moon and stars to light the night,
who churns the sea till its breakers thunder—
Yahweh of Armies his name is:

“If this fixed order departs
from before me, declares Yahweh,
then also the offspring of Israel will cease
from being a nation before me for all time.”

So says Yahweh:
“If the heavens above can be measured,
and the foundations of the earth below be searched out,
then I too will reject all the offspring of Israel
for all they have done, declares Yahweh.”
“Look, the days are coming,{j} declares Yahweh, when Yahweh’s city will be rebuilt, stretching from the Tower of Hananel to the Corner Gate.
Further still the measuring cord will run, directly to Gareb’s hill, then bend around toward Goah.
