You have disgraced me among my people for the sake of a few handfuls of barley and some pieces of bread, killing those who ought not to die and letting live those who ought not to live, by deceiving my people, who listen to deceit.
“Therefore the Lord Yahweh says this: I am against your magic charms, which you use to trap people like birds. I will rip them off your arms and release the people you have been trapping like birds.
I will rip away your veils and snatch my people out of your grip; never again will they be a catch in your hands. And you will know that I am Yahweh.

Because you have disheartened the righteous with lies, when I had not caused them grief, and have strengthened the hands of the wicked so that they do not turn from their evil way and save their lives,
so your empty visions and your divining are finished. I will snatch my people out of your grip, and you will know that I am Yahweh.’”

notes.text: The meaning of the Hebrew words for “bands” and “veils” is uncertain; they were evidently objects used in magic or divination.

verses.text: Some of the elders of Israel came to me and sat down in front of me.
Then the word of Yahweh came to me:
“Son of man, these men have set up their idols in their hearts and put the stumbling block of their guilt right before their faces. Should I let them consult me at all?

So talk to them and say to them, ‘The Lord Yahweh says this: Anyone in Israel who takes his idols into his heart and puts his sinful obstacle in front of him, and then goes to the prophet—I, Yahweh, will respond to him in person, according to his many idols,
so that I may seize the house of Israel by their own hearts, since through their idols they have all become estranged from me.’
“So say to Israel’s house, ‘The Lord Yahweh says this: Come back! Turn from your idols; turn your faces from every abomination of yours.

When anyone from the Israelites, or any foreigner living among them, turns away from me, takes his idols into his heart, puts his sinful obstacle in front of him, and then goes to a prophet to ask me about something, I, Yahweh, will respond to him in person.
I will set my face against that man and make him a sign and a byword, and I will cut him off from among my people. Then you will know that I am Yahweh.
“‘If the prophet is deceived and speaks a word, I, Yahweh, have deceived that prophet, and I will stretch out my hand against him and wipe him out from among my people Israel.
They will bear their guilt; the guilt of the prophet will be the same as the guilt of the one who consults him,

so that the house of Israel will stray from me no more and no longer make themselves unclean with all their rebellions. They will be a people to me, and I will be God to them, declares the Lord Yahweh.’”
The word of Yahweh came to me:
“Son of man, if a land sins against me by acting unfaithfully, and I stretch out my hand against it, break its supply of bread, send famine on it, and cut off from it both people and animals,
if these three men were living there—Noah, Daniel,{a} and Job—their righteousness would rescue themselves alone, declares the Lord Yahweh.
“If I let wild beasts roam through the land and they leave it childless, so that it becomes a desolation that no one passes through because of the beasts,
as I live, declares the Lord Yahweh, even if these three men were in it, they could not save sons or daughters. They alone would be saved, and the land would become a desolation.
“Or suppose I bring a sword on that country and command, ‘Sword, go through the land!’ and cut away from it human and beast alike;
as I live, declares the Lord Yahweh, even if these three men were in it, they could not save sons or daughters; they alone would be saved.
“Or if I send a plague into that land and pour out my fury on it in bloodshed, to cut off from it both people and animals,
as I live, declares the Lord Yahweh, should Noah, Daniel, and Job be living there, not a son and not a daughter would they rescue. Their righteousness would rescue themselves alone.

“The Lord Yahweh says this: How much more severe it will be when I send against Jerusalem my four terrible punishments—sword, hunger, savage animals and disease—to wipe out people and livestock from it!

But look, a remnant will be left in it, a band of escapees—sons and daughters led out. They will come out to you, and when you see their ways and their doings, you will be comforted over the evil I brought on Jerusalem, over all that I brought on it.
They will console you when you see their conduct and their deeds, for you will know that it was not without cause that I did all I did in it, declares the Lord Yahweh.”

notes.text: The Hebrew spelling is Danel (as also in 28:3), the name of a righteous ancient hero known from texts found at Ugarit; Jewish tradition identifies him with the Daniel of the book of Daniel. The name means “God is my judge.”

verses.text: The word of Yahweh came to me:
“Son of man, what makes the vine’s wood any better than wood from other trees—the vine shoot that was among the forest trees?
Is wood ever taken from it to make anything useful? Do people make a peg from it to hang any utensil on?
No, it is thrown into the fire for fuel. When the fire has consumed both its ends and its middle is charred, is it good for anything?
Look, while it was still whole nothing was made from it. How much less, once fire has eaten it and it is scorched, will anything be made from it!
“Therefore the Lord Yahweh says this: Just as I made the wood of the vine, out of all the trees in the forest, into fuel for the fire, so I will treat the people living in Jerusalem.
I will set my face against them. Though they have escaped the fire, the fire will still consume them. And you will know that I am Yahweh when I set my face against them.
I will make the land a desolation, because they have acted unfaithfully, declares the Lord Yahweh.”
The word of Yahweh came to me:
“Son of man, confront Jerusalem with her abominations
and say, ‘The Lord Yahweh says this to Jerusalem: Your roots and your birthplace are in Canaan’s land. An Amorite was your father, and a Hittite your mother.{a}
On the day you were born, no one cut your umbilical cord; you were not bathed in water to make you clean, nor rubbed with salt, nor wrapped in cloth.
Nobody looked on you with enough compassion to do any one of these things for you. Instead, you were dumped in an open field, because you were hated on the day of your birth.
“‘And I passed by you and saw you thrashing in your own blood. In your blood I told you, “Live!” Yes, in your blood I told you, “Live!”{b}
I let you multiply like the sprouts of the field. You grew and grew tall and came to the fullest beauty;{c} your breasts took shape and your hair grew long, yet you were naked and exposed.

“I came by again and looked at you, and you had reached the time for love. I draped the hem of my cloak over you and hid your nakedness. I pledged myself to you with an oath and made a covenant with you, and you became mine, declares the Lord Yahweh.
I bathed you in water, rinsed your blood from you, and rubbed you with oil.
I clothed you with embroidered cloth, gave you sandals of fine leather,{d} wrapped you in fine linen, and covered you with silk.
I decked you out in ornaments: bangles for your arms, a chain for your neck,
I gave you a nose ring, earrings for your ears, and a lovely crown for your head.
So you were adorned with gold and silver, and your clothing was fine linen, silk, and embroidered cloth. You ate fine flour, honey, and oil. You became exceedingly beautiful and rose to royalty.
Among the nations word of you went out because of your beauty, flawless as it was through the splendor I had put on you, declares the Lord Yahweh.
“‘But you trusted in your beauty and used your fame to play the prostitute. You lavished your favors on anyone who passed by; your beauty became his.{e}
You took some of your clothes and made colorful shrines for yourself, and on them you acted as a prostitute—something that should never happen or take place.
You also took your beautiful jewelry of my gold and my silver, which I had given you, and made for yourself male images, and with them you played the prostitute.
You took your embroidered garments to cover them, and you set my oil and my incense before them.
My food that I gave you—the finest flour, with olive oil and honey, which I fed you—you offered before them as a pleasing fragrance. That is what happened, declares the Lord Yahweh.
“‘And you took your sons and your daughters, children you had borne to me, and slaughtered them as food for those images. Was your whoring such a small thing?
You slaughtered my children and gave them up, making them pass through the fire to the images.
In all your abominations and prostitution you did not remember the days of your youth, when you were naked and bare, kicking about in your blood.
“‘After all your wickedness—woe, woe to you, declares the Lord Yahweh—
you built yourself a mound and made yourself a lofty shrine in every square.
At the head of every street you built your lofty shrine and made your beauty an abomination. You spread your legs to everyone who passed by and multiplied your prostitution.
You prostituted yourself with the Egyptians, your lustful neighbors,{f} and multiplied your prostitution to provoke me.
So I stretched out my hand against you, cut back your allotted portion, and handed you over to the will of those who hate you, the daughters of the Philistines, who were ashamed of your lewd conduct.
You also prostituted yourself with the Assyrians, because you were not satisfied; you played the prostitute with them, and still you were not satisfied.
Then you multiplied your prostitution with the land of merchants, Chaldea,{g} and even with this you were not satisfied.
“‘How feverish{h} your heart is, declares the Lord Yahweh, when you do all these things, the deeds of a brazen prostitute!
When you built your mound at the head of every street and made your lofty shrine in every square, you were not like a prostitute, because you scorned payment.
Adulterous wife, who takes strangers instead of her husband!
Every prostitute is paid, yet you handed out payment to every lover of yours; you bribed them to come in to you from all around for your prostitution.
So you were the opposite of other women in your prostitution: no one chased after you to play the prostitute. You paid a fee instead of receiving one; you were the opposite.
“‘Therefore, prostitute, hear the word of Yahweh.

This is what the Lord Yahweh says: Since your lust{i} was spilled out and your naked body was uncovered through your prostitution with your lovers, and through all your detestable idols, and through the blood of your children that you offered to them,

that is why I am gathering every lover with whom you took pleasure, everyone you loved and everyone you hated. From all around I will gather them against you; I will uncover your nakedness before them, and they will look on all of it.
I will sentence you with the sentence for women who commit adultery and murder, and I will make you the victim of bloody rage and jealousy.

I will give you into their hands; your mound they will pull down and your lofty shrines they will break apart. They will peel off your clothing and carry away your fine jewels, and they will leave you naked and exposed.
They will bring up a mob against you, stone you, and hack you to pieces with their swords.
They will set your houses on fire and carry out sentences against you while many women look on. I will put an end to your prostitution, and you will never pay lovers again.
Then my fury against you will be spent, my jealousy will depart from you, and I will grow quiet and be angry no more.

You did not bear in mind the time of your youth; you raged at me with all of this. So now I am bringing your ways back on your head, declares the Lord Yahweh. Did you not add this lewdness to all your abominations?
“‘Look, everyone who quotes proverbs will quote this one about you: “Like mother, like daughter.”

You are the daughter of your mother, who despised her husband and her children; and you are the sister of your sisters, who despised their husbands and children. Your mother was a Hittite, and your father was an Amorite.
Your older sister is Samaria, who lives with her daughters to your north,{j} and your younger sister, who lives to your south, is Sodom with her daughters.
Not content to follow in their ways and do their abominations, you soon became, as if that were a trifle, more depraved than they in all you did.
As I live, declares the Lord Yahweh, Sodom your sister and her daughters did not do what you have done, you and your daughters.
See, this was the guilt of Sodom your sister: pride, a surplus of bread, and untroubled ease were hers and her daughters’, yet the hand of the poor and needy they did not strengthen.
They grew lofty and did abomination before me, so I took them away, as you have seen.{k}
Samaria’s sins were not half of yours. Your abominations outnumber hers, and by all you have done you have made your sisters look righteous.

You also must carry your shame, since you have pleaded your sisters’ case. Your sins were so much more abominable than theirs that they look more righteous than you. Be ashamed, then, and carry your shame, because you have made your sisters look righteous.
“‘Yet I will turn back their captivity—Sodom’s and her daughters’, Samaria’s and her daughters’—and yours too in their midst,
that you may carry your shame and blush for everything you did, becoming a comfort to them.
Your sisters Sodom and her daughters and Samaria and her daughters will return to their former condition, and you and your daughters will return to your former condition.
In your proud days you would not so much as mention your sister Sodom,

before your own evil was exposed? Now you have become like her, scorned by the daughters of Edom{l} and all the neighbors around her, and by the daughters of the Philistines—everyone around you who looks down on you.
Your lewdness and your abominations—you carry them, declares Yahweh.
“‘For this is what the Lord Yahweh says: I will deal with you as you have done, you who have despised the oath by breaking the covenant.
Yet I will remember my covenant with you in the days of your youth, and I will establish an everlasting covenant with you.
You will recall your ways and be humiliated when you take in your sisters, those older and those younger than you. I will give them to you as daughters, though not by your covenant.
I will establish my covenant with you, and you will know that I am Yahweh,
so that you remember and feel shame, and because of your humiliation never open your mouth again, when I forgive you for all you did, declares the Lord Yahweh.’”

notes.text: The Amorites and Hittites were among the peoples living in Canaan before Israel (Gen 15:19–21); the point is that Jerusalem’s origins were pagan.
The Greek lacks the repeated sentence “I said to you as you lay in your blood, ‘Live!’”
The Hebrew is uncertain; it may mean “you came to have the finest ornaments.”
Hebrew tahash, a fine leather of uncertain kind, perhaps from dolphins or sea cows.
The Hebrew phrase “your beauty became his” is uncertain.
Hebrew: “great of flesh,” a sexual euphemism.
Or “Chaldea, the land of merchants.” Hebrew: “the land of Canaan, Chaldea”; “Canaan” here means “merchants.”
Or “weak”; the meaning of the Hebrew word is uncertain.
Hebrew nechosheth, perhaps “copper” (that is, money) or “lust”; the meaning is uncertain.
Hebrew: “on your left”; the right and left referred to south and north for someone facing east.
Or “as you have seen.”
So some ancient witnesses; the main Hebrew text and the Greek have “Aram” (Syria). In Hebrew the two names differ by one similar letter.

verses.text: The word of Yahweh came to me:
“Son of man, pose a riddle and tell a parable to the house of Israel.

Say, ‘This is what the Lord Yahweh says:
A great eagle with great wings, long pinions,
and full plumage of many colors
came to Lebanon and took the top of the cedar.

It sprouted and became a spreading vine, low in height;
its branches turned toward him,
and its roots stayed beneath him.
So it became a vine, produced branches, and sent out shoots.

“‘Then came a second great eagle,
broad of wing and thick with feathers.
And see, this vine twisted its roots toward him
and sent its tendrils reaching to him,
away from the bed where it grew,
for him to water it.

It had been planted in good soil beside abundant waters,
so that it could produce branches and bear fruit
and become a magnificent vine.’

“Say, ‘The Lord Yahweh says this: Will it prosper? Will its roots not be torn out and its fruit stripped away, until every new leaf it puts forth dries up? No mighty arm, no crowd of people, will be needed to wrench it up by the roots.
Look—it is replanted; will it prosper? Once the east wind touches it, will it not dry up entirely, dry up in the very bed where it sprouted?’”
The word of Yahweh came to me:

“Say to the rebellious house: ‘Don’t you know the meaning of these things?’ Tell them: ‘Jerusalem was entered by the king of Babylon, who seized its king and its princes and brought them back with him to Babylon.{b}
He took one of royal descent{c} and cut a covenant with him, binding him by a curse-oath. The land’s men of power he carried away,
so that the kingdom would be kept low and not lift itself up, but would survive by keeping his covenant.

But that king revolted against him, sending his messengers down to Egypt for horses and a host of troops. Will he prosper? Will a man who does these things get away? He has broken the covenant—will he get away?
“‘As I live, declares the Lord Yahweh, in the place of the king who enthroned him, whose curse-oath he scorned and whose covenant he broke—with him, in the middle of Babylon, he will die.
Pharaoh, for all his great force and vast assembly, will do nothing for him in the battle, when the siege mound is heaped up and the siege tower built for cutting down many souls.
He despised the oath by breaking the covenant. He gave his hand in pledge and yet did all these things; he will not escape.
“‘So the Lord Yahweh says this: As I live, my curse-oath that he scorned and my covenant that he broke—I will lay them on his head.
I will throw my net over him, and he will be trapped in my snare. I will take him to Babylon and hold a trial there over the treachery he committed against me.
All his elite troops{d} in every unit will fall by the sword, and whoever remains will be blown to every wind. Then you will know that I, Yahweh, have spoken.’

“This is what the Lord Yahweh says:
I myself will take a sprig from the high crown of the cedar and plant it;
from the topmost of its young shoots I will break off a tender one
and plant it myself on a tall, lofty mountain.

On Israel’s lofty mountain I will plant it;
it will put out branches and bear fruit
and become a majestic cedar.
Every kind of winged creature will dwell beneath it,
sheltering in the shade of its boughs.

Then all the trees of the field will know
that I, Yahweh, bring low the high tree
and make the low tree tall,
dry up the green tree
and make the dry tree flourish.
I, Yahweh, have spoken, and I will do it.”

notes.text: The Hebrew word rendered “willow” is uncertain.
This was Nebuchadnezzar’s deportation of King Jehoiachin in 597 BC (2 Kgs 24:10–17).
That is, Zedekiah (2 Kgs 24:17).
So some ancient witnesses; the main Hebrew text has “fugitives.”

verses.text: The word of Yahweh came to me:

“What do you mean, you who keep quoting this saying concerning Israel’s land:
‘The fathers eat unripe grapes,
and it is the children’s teeth that go numb’?
As surely as I live, declares the Lord Yahweh, you will never again quote this proverb in Israel.
Look, all souls are mine. As the father’s soul is mine, so the son’s soul is mine. The soul that sins—that soul shall die.
“Take a man who is righteous, who practices justice and right.

On the mountains he does not feast at shrines; he does not raise his eyes to the idols of Israel’s house. His neighbor’s wife he does not defile, and he does not come near a woman in her time of impurity.
He wrongs no one; the pledge he took for a debt he gives back. He seizes nothing by robbery; his bread he gives to the hungry, and the naked he clothes with a garment.
He does not lend at interest or take a profit. He keeps his hand from wrongdoing and judges fairly between one person and another.
He walks in my statutes and keeps my judgments, acting faithfully. Such a man is righteous; he will surely live, declares the Lord Yahweh.
“Now let him father a son who is a robber, one who sheds blood and does any one of these things
(though the father did none of them): he eats at the mountain shrines, defiles his neighbor’s wife,
oppresses the poor and needy, commits robbery, does not return the pledge, lifts his eyes to the idols, commits abomination,
lends at interest and charges a premium. Will such a son live? No, he will not live! Since he has done all these detestable things, he will certainly die, and his death will be his own fault.
“But now let this man father a son who observes all the sins his father has done; he observes them and does nothing like them.
On the mountains he does not feast at shrines; he does not raise his eyes to the idols of Israel’s house. His neighbor’s wife he does not defile.
He wrongs no one; he holds back no pledge and seizes nothing by robbery. His bread he gives to the hungry, and the naked he clothes with a garment.
He holds back his hand from the poor,{a} takes neither interest nor increase, does my judgments, and follows my statutes. He shall not die because of his father’s guilt; he shall surely live.
His father, since he extorted and robbed a brother and did what was evil among his own people—look, he shall die in his guilt.
“Yet you ask, ‘Why does the son not bear the guilt of his father?’ When the son has done what is just and right and has kept all my statutes and carried them out, he will surely live.

The soul that sins—that soul shall die. A son shall not carry his father’s guilt, and a father shall not carry his son’s guilt. On the righteous rests his own righteousness, and on the wicked rests his own wickedness.
“But should the wicked man turn back from all the sins he did, guard all my statutes, and practice justice and right, he shall surely live; he shall not die.
None of the transgressions he has committed will be remembered against him; because of the righteousness he has practiced, he will live.
Do I take any pleasure in the death of the wicked, declares the Lord Yahweh? Would I not rather that he turn from his ways and live?

“But if a righteous man abandons his righteousness and commits injustice, doing the same detestable things that the wicked do, will he live? None of the righteous things he did will be counted. Because of the treachery he has committed and the sins he has done, he will die for them.
“Still you say, ‘The Lord’s way does not measure up.’ Hear now, house of Israel: Does my way not measure up? Is it not rather your ways that fail to measure up?
When a righteous person turns from his righteousness and does wrong, he will die for it; for the wrong he has done he will die.
And once the wicked man turns back from the wickedness he did and practices justice and right, he will keep his soul alive.
Because he considered and turned away from all the transgressions he had committed, he will surely live; he will not die.
Yet the house of Israel says, ‘The Lord’s way is not fair.’ Are my ways unfair, house of Israel? Is it not your ways that are unfair?
“Therefore I will judge you, house of Israel, each according to his ways, declares the Lord Yahweh. Repent and turn away from all your transgressions, so that guilt will not be your downfall.
Cast away from you every rebellion of yours that you have done, and make for yourselves a heart that is new and a spirit that is new. Why will you die, house of Israel?
I take no delight in anyone’s death, declares the Lord Yahweh. So repent, and live!”

notes.text: So the main Hebrew text; the Greek has “from injustice” (compare v. 8).

verses.text: “And you—raise a dirge over Israel’s princes,

and say:
‘What a lioness your mother was among the lions!
She lay down among young lions;
she reared her cubs.

“‘When she saw that her hope was lost,
that what she had waited for had come to nothing,
she took another of her cubs
and made him a young lion.

He knew their strongholds{b}
and laid waste their towns.
The land and all that filled it were appalled
at the sound of his roaring.

Then the nations set against him
the provinces on every side.
They spread their net over him;
he was caught in their pit.

They put hooks in him and locked him in a cage,
then brought him to the king of Babylon.{c}
They took him into strongholds
so his roar would never again be heard
over the mountains of Israel.

“‘Your mother was like a vine in your vineyard,{d}
planted beside the waters.
It was fruitful and full of branches
because of abundant water.

It had strong branches,
fit for rulers’ scepters.
It towered high
among the thick foliage;
it was conspicuous for its height
and its many branches.

Now it is planted in the wilderness,
in a dry and thirsty land.

Fire has gone out from its main branch
and consumed its shoots and fruit,
so that it has no strong branch left,
no scepter for ruling.’
This is a lament, and it has become a lament.”

notes.text: This was King Jehoahaz, taken to Egypt by Pharaoh Neco in 609 BC (2 Kgs 23:31–34).
Hebrew: “He knew his widows”; a slight change gives “he broke down their strongholds” or “he ravaged their widows.”
Probably King Jehoiachin (2 Kgs 24:8–15) or Zedekiah (2 Kgs 25:7).
Hebrew: “in your blood”; the text is uncertain, and many scholars emend it to “in a vineyard.”

verses.text: In the seventh year, on the tenth day of the fifth month (in July–August),{a} some of the elders of Israel came to consult Yahweh, and they sat down before me.
Then the word of Yahweh came to me:

“Son of man, speak to the elders of Israel and tell them, ‘This is what the Lord Yahweh says: Have you come to consult me? As I live, I will not let myself be consulted by you, declares the Lord Yahweh.’
“Will you judge them? Will you judge them, son of man? Then make known to them the abominations of their ancestors.

Tell them, ‘The Lord Yahweh says this: On the day I chose Israel, I lifted my hand in oath to the seed of Jacob’s house, and in Egypt’s land I made myself known to them. I lifted my hand to them, saying, “I am Yahweh your God.”
That day I lifted my hand to them, swearing to lead them out of Egypt’s land to a land I had scouted for them, one flowing with milk and honey, the jewel of every land.
And I said to them, “Each of you, throw away the detestable things your eyes feast on, and do not defile yourselves with the idols of Egypt. I am Yahweh your God.”

“‘They rebelled against me and would not hear me. Not one cast away the vile things that held his eyes, and Egypt’s idols they did not abandon. So I spoke of pouring my fury on them, of exhausting my anger on them right there in Egypt’s land.
Yet I acted for my name’s sake, to keep it from being profaned before the nations they lived among, before whose eyes I had revealed myself to them by leading them out of Egypt’s land.
So out of Egypt’s land I led them, and I brought them to the wilderness.
I gave them my statutes and made known to them my judgments, by which a person who carries them out will live.
My Sabbaths too I gave them, to be a sign between me and them, for knowing that I am Yahweh who sets them apart as holy.

“‘But the house of Israel rebelled against me in the wilderness. They did not walk in my statutes, and they rejected my judgments, by which a person who carries them out will live, and they utterly profaned my Sabbaths. So I resolved to pour out my fury on them in the wilderness to wipe them out.
Yet I acted for my name’s sake, to keep it from being profaned before the nations, in whose view I had led them out.
And I, too, lifted my hand to them in the wilderness, swearing not to bring them into the land I had given, the land flowing with milk and honey, the jewel of every land,
because they rejected my judgments, did not walk in my statutes, and profaned my Sabbaths; for their hearts went after their idols.
But my eye took pity on them, and I held back from destroying them; I did not make a full end of them in the wilderness.
“‘I told their children in the wilderness, “Do not follow the rules of your parents, or observe their laws, or make yourselves unclean with their idols.
I am Yahweh your God. Walk in my statutes, keep my judgments, and carry them out.
Keep my Sabbaths holy, so that they will be a sign between me and you, and you will know that I am Yahweh your God.”

“‘But the children defied me. They did not follow my rules or carefully observe my laws, which give life to the one who obeys them, and they desecrated my Sabbaths. So I said I would pour out my rage on them and let my anger run its course against them in the wilderness.
Yet I drew back my hand and acted for my name’s sake, to keep it from being profaned before the nations in whose view I had led them out.
In addition, I swore to them in the wilderness, with my hand raised, that I would scatter them among the nations and spread them across the lands,
because they had not carried out my judgments but had rejected my statutes and profaned my Sabbaths, and their eyes were fixed on their fathers’ idols.
So I gave them rules that were not good and laws that could not give them life.
I made them unclean by their own gifts, as they made every firstborn pass through the fire,{b} that I might appall them, and that they might know that I am Yahweh.’
“Therefore, son of man, speak to the house of Israel and tell them, ‘This is what the Lord Yahweh says: In this also your ancestors blasphemed me by acting unfaithfully toward me.

For I brought them into the land that I had lifted my hand to give them, and wherever they saw a lofty hill or a leafy tree, they slaughtered their sacrifices there, there they set their offerings that provoked me, there they laid their soothing aromas, and there they poured out their drink offerings.
So I said to them, “What is this high place you go to?” And it is called Bamah{c} to this day.’
“Therefore tell the Israelites, ‘The Lord Yahweh says this: Are you going to make yourselves unclean as your ancestors did, and chase after their vile idols?

When you present your offerings and send your sons through the fire, you make yourselves unclean with all your idols even now. Am I to answer your inquiries, Israelites? As I live, declares the Lord Yahweh, I will not answer your inquiries.
What you have in mind will never happen—when you say, “Let us be like the nations, like the clans of the countries, serving wood and stone.”
“‘As I live, declares the Lord Yahweh, with a mighty hand, an outstretched arm, and outpoured fury I will rule as king over you.
I will bring you out from the peoples and gather you from the countries where you are scattered, with a mighty hand, an outstretched arm, and outpoured fury.
I will bring you into the wilderness of the peoples, and there I will enter into judgment with you face to face.
Just as I put your ancestors on trial in the wilderness of Egypt, so I will put you on trial, declares the Lord Yahweh.
I will make you pass beneath my staff and bring you under the obligation of the covenant.{d}
I will sift out from you the rebels and those who revolt against me. From the land where they sojourn I will lead them out, but Israel’s soil they shall not enter. And you will know that I am Yahweh.

“‘And you, house of Israel, the Lord Yahweh says this: Go, every one of you, serve his idols! But afterward—surely you will listen to me, and my holy name you will profane no more with your gifts and idols.

For it is on my holy mountain, on Israel’s lofty mountain, declares the Lord Yahweh, that the entire house of Israel will serve me, all of it in the land. There I will welcome them with pleasure, and there I will ask for your contributions, the first and best of your gifts, and all your holy things.

Like a soothing aroma I will welcome you with pleasure when I lead you out of the peoples and collect you from the lands of your scattering; and through you I will show myself holy before the nations’ eyes.
Then you will know that I am Yahweh, when I bring you into the land of Israel, the land I raised my hand in an oath to give to your ancestors.
There you will remember how you lived and all the actions that made you unclean, and you will be disgusted with yourselves for all the evil you committed.
You will know that I am Yahweh when I act toward you for my name’s sake and not according to your evil ways or your corrupt actions, Israelites, declares the Lord Yahweh.’”
The word of Yahweh came to me:{e}
“Son of man, set your face toward the south. Preach against the south and prophesy against the forest of the Negev.{f}

Say to the forest of the Negev, ‘Hear Yahweh’s word. The Lord Yahweh says this: Look, I am setting a fire in you; every tree in you, green or dry, it will devour. The fierce flame will not be put out, and from the Negev to the north every face will be seared by it.
All flesh will see that I, Yahweh, have kindled it; it will not be quenched.’”
Then I said, “Ah, Lord Yahweh! They are saying of me, ‘Is he not just a maker of parables?’”

notes.text: Hebrew: “in the fifth month, on the tenth of the month,” counting from the spring new year; this was the month later called Av, in 591 BC. The Greek has only “on the fifteenth of the month.”
Or “when they offered up every firstborn”; compare 16:21.
Bamah means “high place.” Ezekiel plays on the sound of the question “What (mah) is the high place to which you go (ba’im)?”
The Greek has “and I will bring you in by number”; the meaning of the Hebrew word rendered “bond” is uncertain.
In Hebrew, 20:45–49 is numbered 21:1–5, and 21:1–32 is numbered 21:6–37.
The Negev is the dry region south of Judah; “south” here also represents Judah and Jerusalem (21:2).

verses.text: The word of Yahweh came to me:
“Son of man, set your face toward Jerusalem and preach against the sanctuaries. Prophesy against the land of Israel
and say to Israel’s land, ‘Yahweh says this: Look, I am coming at you. My sword I will draw out of its sheath, and from you I will cut away righteous and wicked alike.
Because I am going to cut off from you both righteous and wicked, my sword will go out of its sheath against all flesh from south to north.
Then all flesh will know that I, Yahweh, have drawn my sword from its sheath; it will not return to it again.’
“As for you, son of man, groan! Groan before their eyes with breaking heart{a} and bitter grief.

When they ask you, ‘Why are you groaning?’ say, ‘Because of the news that is coming. Every heart will melt, every hand go limp, every spirit grow faint, and every knee run with water. Look, it is coming, and it will happen, declares the Lord Yahweh.’”
The word of Yahweh came to me:

“Son of man, prophesy and say, ‘This is what my Lord says: Say:
A sword, a sword is sharpened
and also polished—

He has handed it over for burnishing,
for the palm to grip;
sharpened is this sword, burnished too,
to be placed in the killer’s hand.’
Shout and howl, son of man, for this sword is for my people, for every prince of Israel; they are tossed to it together with my people. So slap your thigh.{c}
For a testing has come—and what if the scepter that despises is no more? declares the Lord Yahweh.{d}

“And you, son of man, prophesy and strike your hands together.
Let the sword come down twice, even three times—
the sword of the dead,
the sword of the great slaughter,
closing in on them,

Cut hard to the right!
Turn and strike to the left,
wherever your blade is aimed.

I too will strike my hands together
and let my rage be satisfied.
I, Yahweh, have spoken.”
The word of Yahweh came to me:
“As for you, son of man, mark out two roads for the sword of the king of Babylon to take, both starting from the same land. Make a signpost and put it at the head of the road to a city.
Mark out a road for the sword to come to Rabbah of the Ammonites, and another to Judah, to fortified Jerusalem.
For Babylon’s king has halted where the road parts, where the two ways begin, to seek an omen. He rattles the arrows, inquires of the household gods,{f} and examines a liver.

In his right hand he holds the divination lot for Jerusalem, directing him to position battering rams, to give the command to kill, to shout the war cry, to place battering rams against the gates, to build an earthen ramp, and to construct siege towers.
To those who have sworn solemn oaths,{g} it will seem a false divination; but he will bring their guilt to remembrance, so that they will be captured.

“Therefore the Lord Yahweh says this: Since you have made your guilt known through your open rebellion, revealing your sins in everything you do—since you have made yourselves known, you will be seized by force.
And you, defiled and wicked one, Israel’s prince, your day has arrived, the hour when guilt reaches its end,
the Lord Yahweh says this: Take off the turban; lift away the crown! This will not stay this way. Raise up what is low; pull down what is high.
A ruin, a ruin, a ruin I will make it! This too will not happen until he comes to whom judgment belongs, and I will give it to him.{h}

“And you, son of man, prophesy and say, ‘The Lord Yahweh says this about the Ammonites and their scorn:
A sword! A sword unsheathed for the slaughter,
burnished to devour, to gleam like a lightning bolt—

while they divine emptiness for you
and see lying omens for you—
to place you on the necks of the slain, the wicked,
whose day has arrived,
the hour when guilt reaches its end.

Return it to its sheath!
In the place where you were created,
in the land of your origin, I will judge you.

I will pour out my indignation on you;
I will blow on you with the fire of my wrath.
I will hand you over to brutal men,
skilled in destruction.

You will be fuel for the fire;
your blood will be in the midst of the land.
You will not be remembered,
for I, Yahweh, have spoken.’”

notes.text: Hebrew: “with breaking of loins.”
The Hebrew of this line is very obscure, and any rendering is a guess.
A gesture of grief or alarm (Jer 31:19).
The Hebrew of v. 13 is very obscure.
The meaning of the Hebrew word rendered “slaughter” here is uncertain.
Hebrew teraphim, figurines used in divination (Gen 31:19).
The meaning of the Hebrew phrase is uncertain; it may refer to the oaths of loyalty sworn to the king of Babylon.
Or “until he comes whose right it is.” The wording echoes Gen 49:10.

verses.text: The word of Yahweh came to me:
“As for you, son of man, will you judge? Will you judge the city of bloodshed? Then confront her with all her abominations.
Say, ‘The Lord Yahweh says this: O city that sheds blood within her walls, bringing her day of doom, and that makes idols to make herself unclean!

You have become guilty by the blood you have shed and defiled by the idols you have made. You have brought your days near and arrived at the end of your years. Therefore I have made you a reproach to the nations and a mockery to all the countries.
Those near and those far from you will mock you, you of defiled name, full of turmoil.
“‘Look, the princes of Israel within you, each according to his power, have been bent on shedding blood.
In you they have treated father and mother with contempt; in your midst they have oppressed the foreigner; in you they have wronged the fatherless and the widow.
You have despised my holy things and profaned my Sabbaths.
Men who peddle slander to spill blood are in you; men who feast at mountain shrines are in you; lewdness they practice in your midst.
A father’s nakedness is uncovered{a} in you; a woman unclean in her impurity is forced in you.
With his neighbor’s wife one man does abomination; another defiles his daughter-in-law by lewdness; another in you forces his sister, his father’s daughter.
Within you people accept bribes to shed blood. You charge interest and make a profit, and you get rich by cheating your neighbors. And you have forgotten me, declares the Lord Yahweh.
“‘So look, I clap my hands over the profit you have plundered and over the blood that is shed within you.
Will your courage endure, or your hands stay strong, in the days when I deal with you? I, Yahweh, have spoken, and I will do it.
I will scatter you among the nations and spread you across the lands, and I will put an end to the filth in you.
You will be profaned{b} through your own doing in the sight of the nations. Then you will know that I am Yahweh.’”
The word of Yahweh came to me:
“Son of man, the house of Israel has become dross to me. All of them are copper, tin, iron, and lead inside a furnace; they are the dross of silver.
Therefore the Lord Yahweh says this: Because every one of you has turned into scrap metal, I will gather you together inside Jerusalem.
As people gather silver, copper, iron, lead, and tin into a furnace to blow fire on it and melt it, so I will gather you in my anger and fury, put you inside, and melt you.
I will gather you and blow on you with the fire of my wrath, and you will be melted within the city.
As silver is melted in a furnace, so you will be melted inside it. Then you will know that I, Yahweh, have poured out my fury on you.”
The word of Yahweh came to me:
“Son of man, say to her, ‘You are a land that has not been cleansed or rained upon in the day of indignation.’
There is a conspiracy of her prophets{c} within her, like a roaring lion tearing its prey. They devour lives, seize treasure and precious things, and multiply the widows within her.

Her priests wrong my teaching and treat my holy things as profane. Between sacred and common they draw no line; the difference between unclean and clean they never make known. From my Sabbaths they hide their eyes, and among them I am made profane.
Her officials within her are like wolves tearing prey, shedding blood and destroying lives to get unjust gain.
Her prophets daub whitewash over all of it, seeing empty visions and divining lies, and declaring, ‘The Lord Yahweh says this,’ though Yahweh never spoke.
The common people have extorted and robbed; the poor and the needy they have mistreated, and the foreigner they have wronged without justice.
I looked among them for one man to repair the wall, to take his stand before me in the gap for the land so that I would not wreck it—and there was none.
So I have poured out my indignation on them; I have consumed them with the fire of my wrath. I have brought their conduct down on their own heads, declares the Lord Yahweh.”

notes.text: That is, they have sexual relations with their fathers’ wives (Lev 18:8).
So the main Hebrew text. The Greek reads differently (“I will give inheritances in you”).
The Greek has “her princes,” which many scholars prefer since prophets are treated in v. 28.

verses.text: The word of Yahweh came to me:
“Son of man, there were two women, daughters of one mother.
They became prostitutes in Egypt; they played the prostitute in their youth. There their breasts were fondled, and there their virgin nipples were caressed.
The elder bore the name Oholah,{a} her sister the name Oholibah.{b} They became mine and gave birth to sons and daughters. Their names stand for this: Oholah is Samaria, and Oholibah is Jerusalem.
“Oholah went whoring though she was mine. She burned with desire for her lovers, for Assyria’s warriors{c}
clothed in blue, governors and commanders, all of them desirable young men, horsemen riding on horses.
She bestowed her prostitution on them, all of them the elite of Assyria, and she defiled herself with all the idols of everyone she lusted after.
She did not abandon the prostitution she had begun in Egypt; in her youth men had slept with her, fondled her young breasts, and spilled out their lust on her.
So I gave her over into her lovers’ hands, into the hands of the Assyrians she burned for.
They exposed her nakedness, took her sons and daughters, and killed her with the sword. She became a byword among women, and judgments were carried out on her.
“Her sister Oholibah saw this, yet in her lust she was more corrupt than her sister, and her prostitution exceeded her sister’s.
She lusted after the Assyrians—governors and commanders, warriors clothed in splendor, horsemen riding on horses, all of them desirable young men.
I saw that she too was defiled; the two of them went one road.
But she carried her prostitution further. She saw men carved on the wall, images of Chaldeans engraved in vermilion,
with belts around their waists and flowing turbans on their heads, all of them looking like officers, a portrait of Babylonians whose native land was Chaldea.
As soon as she saw them, she lusted after them and sent messengers to them in Chaldea.
Babylon’s sons came in to her, to the bed of love, and made her unclean with their whoring; and when they had defiled her, she pulled herself away from them in revulsion.
When she flaunted her prostitution and exposed her nakedness, I turned from her in disgust, just as I had turned from her sister.
Yet she multiplied her prostitution, remembering the days of her youth when she played the prostitute in the land of Egypt.
She burned for her lovers there, men with flesh like a donkey’s flesh and an issue like a stallion’s issue.
So you longed for the lewdness of your youth, when the Egyptians caressed your nipples and fondled your young breasts.{d}
“So, Oholibah, the Lord Yahweh says this: Look, I am rousing against you the lovers from whom you pulled away in revulsion; from all around I will bring them against you—

Babylon’s sons and every Chaldean, Pekod, Shoa, and Koa,{e} and with them all Assyria’s sons—handsome young men every one, governors and prefects, captains and summoned men, every one mounted on horses.

They will attack you with weapons,{f} chariots and carts, and with a huge assembly of peoples. On every side they will take their stand against you, armed with large shields, small shields and helmets. I will entrust the judgment to them, and they will sentence you by their own laws.

I will turn my jealous anger on you, and they will treat you furiously. They will slice off your nose and ears, and your survivors will die by the sword. They will carry off your sons and daughters, and your survivors will be burned up in the fire.
They will strip you of your clothes and take away your beautiful jewelry.
So I will put an end to your lewdness and the prostitution you brought from the land of Egypt. You will not lift your eyes to them or remember Egypt anymore.
“For the Lord Yahweh says this: Look, I am giving you into the hands of the ones you hate, the ones from whom you pulled away in revulsion.
They will treat you with hatred and take everything you earned, leaving you stripped and naked. Your shameful prostitution will be uncovered—your indecency and your prostitution.
These things will be done to you because you prostituted yourself with the nations and defiled yourself with their idols.
Your sister’s road you have walked, so her cup I will set in your hand.

“The Lord Yahweh says:
Your sister’s cup you will drink,
the cup that is deep and broad;
you will be laughed at and mocked,
for it holds so much.

You will drink it and drain it,
gnaw its broken pieces,
and tear your breasts.
For I have spoken, declares the Lord Yahweh.
“Therefore this is what the Lord Yahweh says: Because you have forgotten me and thrown me behind your back, you must bear the penalty of your lewdness and your prostitution.”
Yahweh said to me, “Son of man, will you judge Oholah and Oholibah? Then declare to them their abominations.

For they have committed adultery, and there is blood on their hands. They have committed adultery with their idols; they have even made the children they bore to me pass through the fire to them as food.
Moreover, they have done this to me: on that same day they defiled my sanctuary and profaned my Sabbaths.
For when they had slaughtered their children for their idols, on that same day they came into my sanctuary to profane it. That is what they did in the middle of my house.
“They even sent for men coming from far away; a messenger was sent to them, and they came. For them you bathed, painted your eyes, and adorned yourself with jewelry.
On a magnificent couch you sat, a table laid out in front of it, and on it you placed my incense and my oil.
The sound of a carefree crowd was around her, with men of the common sort brought in, drunkards{g} from the wilderness. They put bracelets on the women’s wrists and beautiful crowns on their heads.
Then I said of her who was worn out by adulteries, ‘Now they will commit prostitution with her, even her!’
And they went in to her as one goes in to a prostitute. So they went in to Oholah and to Oholibah, the lewd women.
But righteous men will judge them with the sentence for adulteresses and the sentence for women who shed blood, because they are adulteresses and there is blood on their hands.
“For this is what the Lord Yahweh says: Bring up an assembly against them, and hand them over to terror and plunder.
The assembly will pelt them with stones and hack them with swords; their sons and daughters will be killed and their houses burned down.
So I will put an end to lewdness in the land, and all women will take warning and not imitate your lewdness.
Your lewdness will be repaid on you, and you will bear the penalty for your sins with idols. Then you will know that I am the Lord Yahweh.”

notes.text: Oholah means “her tent,” perhaps alluding to Samaria’s own shrines.
Oholibah means “my tent is in her,” alluding to Yahweh’s temple in Jerusalem.
Or “neighbors”; the Hebrew word can mean “near.”
The Hebrew of this line is difficult; “the Egyptians” is implied from v. 19.
Pekod, Shoa, and Koa were peoples east of the Tigris; the names may also be wordplays on Hebrew words for “punishment” and “cry for help.” The Greek has “Phacuc, Sue, and Hychue.”
The meaning of the Hebrew word rendered “weapons” is uncertain.
Or “Sabeans,” following the written Hebrew text; the meaning is uncertain.

verses.text: In the ninth year, on the tenth day of the tenth month (in December–January),{a} the word of Yahweh came to me:
“Son of man, record for yourself the date, this very day. On this exact day Babylon’s king has closed in on Jerusalem.

For her blood remains inside her;
on bare rock she set it.
She never spilled it on the soil
where dust might hide it.

To stir up fury, to take vengeance,
I have put her blood on the bare rock,
so that it would not be covered.

“‘Therefore this is what the Lord Yahweh says:
Woe to the city of bloodshed!
I too will make the pile great.

Pile up the wood, light the fire,
boil the meat through,
stir in the spices,{e}
and let the bones burn.

Then set the empty pot on the coals,
so that it grows hot and its copper glows,
its impurity melts within it,
and its corrosion is consumed.
Your uncleanness is lewdness. I sought to make you clean, yet clean of your impurity you would not be; and clean you will not be again till I have brought my fury on you to rest.

I, Yahweh, have spoken. It will happen, and I will act. I will not hold back or show pity or change my mind. They will sentence you according to your conduct and your actions, declares the Lord Yahweh.’”
The word of Yahweh came to me:
“Son of man, I am about to take from you with a single blow the delight of your eyes. Yet you must not mourn or weep or let your tears flow.
Sigh, but silently; hold no mourning rites for the dead. Wrap your turban on and lace your sandals onto your feet. Leave your mustache uncovered, and do not eat the bread men bring to mourners.”{g}
I spoke to the people at dawn; at dusk my wife died. And at dawn I did what I had been ordered to do.
Then the people said to me, “Won’t you explain to us what these actions of yours have to do with us?”
I said to them, “The word of Yahweh came to me:

‘Say to the house of Israel, “This is what the Lord Yahweh says: I am about to profane my sanctuary, the pride of your strength, the delight of your eyes, and the longing of your soul. The sons and daughters you left behind will fall by the sword.
You will do as I have done: you will not cover your upper lip or eat the bread of mourners.
Your turbans will remain on your heads and your sandals on your feet. You will not mourn or weep, but you will waste away because of your guilt and groan to one another.
Ezekiel will be a sign to you; you will do everything he has done. When this happens, you will know that I am the Lord Yahweh.”’
“And you, son of man—on the day when I take away their fortress, their glorious joy, what delights their eyes and what their souls long for, their sons and their daughters—
on that day a fugitive will come to you to bring the news to your ears.
On that day your mouth will be opened to the fugitive; you will speak and no longer be mute. So you will be a sign to them, and they will know that I am Yahweh.”

notes.text: Hebrew: “in the tenth month, on the tenth of the month,” counting from the spring new year; this was the month later called Tevet, in January 588 BC by the usual reckoning (2 Kgs 25:1).
Or “logs”; compare v. 10.
Or “rust” or “scum”; the meaning of the Hebrew word is uncertain; also in vv. 11–12.
That is, no portion is set aside to be spared.
The meaning of the Hebrew is uncertain; others render “pour out the broth.”
The Hebrew of this line is uncertain.
Hebrew: “the bread of men”; many scholars, with a slight change, read “the bread of mourners”; also in v. 22.

verses.text: The word of Yahweh came to me:
“Son of man, turn your face toward the Ammonites{a} and prophesy against them.

Tell the Ammonites, ‘Hear the word of the Lord Yahweh. The Lord Yahweh says this: You said “Ha!” over my sanctuary when it was desecrated, over the land of Israel when it was ruined, and over the people of Judah when they went into exile.
so look, I am giving you to the sons of the east to own. They will set their camps in you and place their dwellings among you; they will be the ones to eat your fruit and drink your milk.
Rabbah I will turn into a grazing ground for camels, and Ammon’s towns into a fold for sheep. And you will know that I am Yahweh.
For this is what the Lord Yahweh says: Because you clapped your hands and stamped your feet and rejoiced with all the contempt of your heart against the land of Israel,

therefore I have stretched out my hand against you and will give you as plunder to the nations. I will cut you off from the peoples and wipe you out from the countries; I will destroy you. Then you will know that I am Yahweh.’
“This is what the Lord Yahweh says: Because Moab and Seir{b} said, ‘Look, the house of Judah is like all the other nations,’
therefore I am going to lay open the flank of Moab, stripping it of its towns, its frontier towns, the glory of the land—Beth-jeshimoth, Baal-meon, and Kiriathaim.{c}
Together with Ammon I will give it to the sons of the east to own, that Ammon may not be remembered among the nations.
And I will carry out judgments on Moab. Then they will know that I am Yahweh.
“The Lord Yahweh says this: Since Edom took vengeance on Judah’s house and became deeply guilty by avenging itself on them,

therefore this is what the Lord Yahweh says: I will stretch out my hand against Edom and cut off from it both people and animals. I will make it a ruin; from Teman to Dedan{d} they will fall by the sword.
I will take my vengeance on Edom by the hand of my people Israel, and they will deal with Edom according to my anger and my fury. Then they will know my vengeance, declares the Lord Yahweh.
“The Lord Yahweh says this: The Philistines have acted in revenge and taken vengeance with malice in their hearts, aiming to destroy with never-ending hatred.
therefore this is what the Lord Yahweh says: I am going to stretch out my hand against the Philistines. I will cut off the Cherethites{e} and destroy the rest of the seacoast.
I will take terrible vengeance on them, punishing them in fury. Then they will know that I am Yahweh, when I take my vengeance on them.”

notes.text: The Ammonites lived east of the Jordan; their capital was Rabbah (modern Amman).
Seir is the mountain region of Edom. The Greek lacks “and Seir.”
Beth-jeshimoth means “house of the wastelands”; Baal-meon, “lord of the dwelling”; Kiriathaim, “double city.”
Teman was a region of Edom; Dedan was an Arabian oasis to the southeast.
The Cherethites were a people associated with the Philistines, perhaps from Crete; the name plays on the verb “cut off” (karath).

verses.text: It was in the eleventh year, on the first of the month,{a} that Yahweh’s word came to me:
“Son of man, since Tyre{b} has said about Jerusalem, ‘Ha! She that was the door of the peoples is shattered; she has been flung open to me. Now that she is wasted, I will grow full,’
the Lord Yahweh says this: Look, I am coming at you, Tyre. Many nations I will bring up against you, as the sea heaves up its breakers.
They will demolish the walls of Tyre and knock down her towers. I will sweep the dust off her and turn her into a bare rock.
She will become a place in the middle of the sea for spreading out fishing nets, for I have spoken, declares the Lord Yahweh. She will become plunder for the nations,
and her daughters{c} on the mainland will be killed by the sword. Then they will know that I am Yahweh.
“For the Lord Yahweh says this: Look, out of the north I am bringing Nebuchadrezzar{d} of Babylon against Tyre, king of kings, with horse and chariot, cavalry and a vast mob of troops.
He will kill your daughters on the mainland with the sword. He will build a siege wall against you, heap up a ramp against you, and raise a wall of shields against you.
His battering rams he will set against your walls, and your towers he will tear down with his iron tools.
So countless are his horses that their dust will bury you. At the din of cavalry, wheels, and chariots your walls will quake, when he comes in at your gates as men come into a city broken open.
His horses’ hoofs will tread every street of yours. Your people he will slay with the sword, and your strong pillars will crash down to the earth.

Your riches will be seized and your goods carried off as plunder. Your walls will be pulled down and your pleasant houses wrecked; your stones, your timbers, and your rubble will be dumped into the sea.
I will hush the clamor of your songs; the music of your lyres will never sound again.
I will make you a bare rock; you will be a place for spreading nets. You will never be rebuilt, for I, Yahweh, have spoken, declares the Lord Yahweh.
“This is what the Lord Yahweh says to Tyre: Will not the coastlands shake at the sound of your fall, when the wounded groan and slaughter is done within you?

Then all the rulers of the coast will come down from their seats, take off their robes, and remove their embroidered clothing. They will dress themselves in terror and sit on the ground, shaking continually and horrified over you.

They will raise a dirge for you and say to you:
‘Ah, how you are lost,
you who were peopled from the seas,
the city held in honor,
strong upon the sea,
she and those who dwelt in her,
who laid their dread
on all her inhabitants!

Now the islands shake
on the day you fall;
the islands out in the sea
are terrified at your departure.’
“This is what the Lord Yahweh says: When I turn you into a ruined city, like cities where nobody lives any more, when I raise the ocean depths over you and the mighty waters cover you,

then I will bring you down with those who go down to the pit,{e} to the people of long ago. I will make you live in the land below, among ancient ruins, with those who go down to the pit, so that you will not be inhabited or take your place{f} in the land of the living.
I will make you a horror, and you will be no more. Though you are sought, you will never be found again, declares the Lord Yahweh.”

notes.text: The month is not given in the Hebrew or the Greek. The eleventh year of Jehoiachin’s exile was 587/586 BC, the year Jerusalem fell (v. 2).
Tyre means “rock.” It was the great Phoenician port, built largely on an island off the coast of modern Lebanon.
That is, its dependent settlements; also in v. 8.
Hebrew Nebuchadrezzar, a form closer to the Babylonian Nabu-kudurri-usur, “Nabu, protect my heir.” His siege of Tyre lasted thirteen years (compare 29:18).
That is, the realm of the dead.
So the Greek (“nor stand”); the Hebrew has “and I will give glory.”

verses.text: The word of Yahweh came to me:
“As for you, son of man, take up a lament over Tyre.

Say to Tyre, who sits at the gateways of the sea, merchant of the peoples to many coastlands, ‘This is what the Lord Yahweh says:
Tyre, you have said,
“I am perfect in beauty.”

Your borders were in the heart of the seas;
your builders perfected your beauty.

They fashioned all your planks
of juniper from Senir;{a}
they took a cedar from Lebanon
to make a mast for you.

The people of Sidon and Arvad{e} were your rowers;
your skilled men, Tyre, were aboard as your sailors.

Gebal’s{f} elders and its experts were in you,
mending your leaks.
Every seagoing ship and its crews
came to you to deal in your wares.
“‘Persia, Lud and Put{g} served in your army as your soldiers. They hung their shields and helmets inside you; they gave you your glory.
Men of Arvad and your army were on your walls all around, and men of Gammad{h} were in your towers. They hung their shields on your walls all around; they perfected your beauty.
“‘Tarshish{i} traded with you because of your great abundance of every kind of wealth; for your wares they gave silver, iron, tin, and lead.
Javan,{j} Tubal, and Meshech{k} were your dealers; for your wares they paid in human lives and in bronze utensils.
From Beth-togarmah{l} they gave horses, war horses, and mules for your wares.
The people of Dedan{m} traded with you; many coastlands were your markets. They paid you with ivory tusks and ebony.
Aram{n} traded with you because of your many products; for your wares they gave turquoise, purple, embroidered work, fine linen, coral, and rubies.
Judah and the land of Israel traded with you; for your merchandise they gave wheat from Minnith, millet,{o} honey, oil, and balm.
Damascus traded with you because of your many products and your great abundance of every kind of wealth, with wine from Helbon and wool from Zahar.{p}
Vedan and Javan from Uzal{q} gave wrought iron, cassia, and calamus for your wares.
Dedan traded with you in saddlecloths for riding.
Arabia and all the princes of Kedar{r} were your customers; in lambs, rams, and goats they traded with you.
The merchants of Sheba and Raamah{s} traded with you; for your wares they gave the finest of all spices, every kind of precious stone, and gold.
Haran, Canneh, Eden, the merchants of Sheba, Asshur, and Chilmad{t} traded with you.
They traded with you in choice garments, in cloaks of blue and embroidered work, and in carpets of many colors, bound with twisted cords, in your marketplace.

Ships of Tarshish transported your goods.
And so you were full and heavily laden
in the middle of the seas.

“‘Your rowers have brought you
out into the vast waters.
The east wind has shattered you
in the heart of the seas.

Your riches, your goods, your trade,
your sailors and your pilots,
your ship-menders and your merchants,
and all your soldiers within you,
together with the whole crowd in your midst,
will go down into the depths of the sea
the day you are wrecked.

At the sound of your sailors’ cry
the open lands{u} will shake.

All who handle the oar
will come down from their ships;
the seamen and all the sailors of the sea
will stand on the shore.

Over you they will shout aloud
and wail with bitter cries;
dust they will toss on their heads,
and in ashes they will wallow.

In their wailing they will take up a lament for you
and chant over you:
“Who was like Tyre,
like her now silenced{w} in the midst of the sea?”

When your goods were unloaded from the seas,
you filled many nations;
by your enormous wealth and trade
you made earth’s kings rich.

Now you are shattered by the seas,
in the depths of the waters;
your merchandise and all your company
have sunk with you.

notes.text: Senir is another name for Mount Hermon (Deut 3:9).
Hebrew bath-ashurim, traditionally “daughter of Assyrians”; with a different division of the letters, “in cypress” (bitashurim).
Kittim is Cyprus, named after the city of Kition; the term was later used of western coastlands generally.
Elishah is probably Alashiya, an ancient name for Cyprus or part of it.
Arvad was a Phoenician island city north of Tyre.
Gebal is Byblos, a Phoenician port north of Sidon.
Lud is probably Lydia in Asia Minor; Put is probably Libya.
The identity of Gammad is unknown; the Greek has “guards.”
Tarshish was a distant western port, probably in Spain (Tartessus); the Greek has “Carthaginians.”
Javan is Greece (Ionia).
Tubal and Meshech were peoples of central Asia Minor (compare 38:2).
Beth-togarmah was a region probably in eastern Asia Minor (Armenia).
So the main Hebrew text; the Greek has “Rhodians,” reflecting a reading “Rodan.”
Some ancient witnesses read “Edom”; in Hebrew the two names differ by one similar letter.
The meaning of the Hebrew word rendered “millet” (pannag) is uncertain.
Or “white wool.”
The Hebrew of v. 19 is uncertain; “from Uzal” may instead be read as part of the list of goods.
Kedar was a tribe of the Arabian desert.
Sheba and Raamah were peoples of southern Arabia.
Chilmad is unidentified; the other names are trading centers of Mesopotamia and Arabia.
Or “the pasturelands”; the meaning is uncertain.
Verse 31 is not found in the Greek.
The Hebrew word is uncertain; some read “like a ruin” or “like her destroyed one.”

verses.text: Yahweh’s word came to me:

“Son of man, tell the ruler of Tyre, ‘The Lord Yahweh says this: / Your heart has grown lofty, / and you have said, “A god am I; / in the seat of gods I sit, / in the heart of the seas.” / Yet you are a mortal, not a god, / though you have made your mind like the mind of a god.
Look, you are wiser than Danel;{a} / no secret is too dark for you.
By your wisdom and your understanding / you have gained wealth for yourself, / and gold and silver you have amassed / in your treasure houses.
By your great skill in trade / you have multiplied your wealth, / and your heart has grown lofty / because of your wealth.
“‘So the Lord Yahweh says this: / Since you have made your mind / like the mind of a god,
look, I am bringing foreigners against you, / the most ruthless of nations. / They will bare their swords against the beauty your wisdom made / and defile your splendor.
Down to the pit{b} they will send you, / and you will die the death of the slain / in the heart of the seas.

Before the one who slays you,
will you go on saying, “I am a god”?
You will be a mortal, not a god,
in the grip of those who pierce you.
You will die the death of the uncircumcised{c} / at the hand of foreigners. / For I have spoken, declares the Lord Yahweh.’”
Yahweh’s word came to me:
“Son of man, raise a dirge over the king of Tyre and say to him, ‘The Lord Yahweh says this: / You were the seal of perfection,{d} / full of wisdom and flawless in beauty.

In Eden, God’s garden, you lived;
gems of every kind adorned you:
carnelian, chrysolite, and moonstone,
beryl, onyx, and jasper,
lapis lazuli, turquoise, and emerald;{e}
and your settings and mountings were worked in gold.
On the day you were created they were made ready.
You were an anointed cherub, a guardian;{f} / I placed you there. / On God’s holy mountain you were; / among stones of fire you walked about.
Blameless you were in your ways / from the day you were created, / until wrong was discovered in you.

Through the abundance of your trade / your insides filled with violence, / and you sinned. / So I banished you as profane from God’s mountain, / and I destroyed you, guardian cherub, / from among the stones of fire.
Your heart grew lofty because of your beauty; / you ruined your wisdom for the sake of your splendor. / I hurled you to the earth; / before kings I set you out, / for them to feast their eyes on you.

By your many wrongs,
by your dishonest dealing,
you made your sanctuaries unclean.
So I brought out a fire from inside you;
it consumed you,
and I reduced you to ashes on the earth
in full view of everyone watching you.
All among the peoples who knew you / are appalled at you. / You have become a terror, / and you will be no more forever.’”
Yahweh’s word came to me:
“Son of man, set your face toward Sidon{g} and prophesy against her.

Say, ‘The Lord Yahweh says this: Look, I am coming against you, Sidon, and I will win glory in your midst. They will know that I am Yahweh when I carry out judgments on her and show myself holy in her.
I will send plague into her and blood into her streets. The slain will fall within her, by the sword that comes against her from every side. And they will know that I am Yahweh.
“‘No more will the house of Israel have a briar that pricks or a thorn that wounds from any of the neighbors around them who treat them with contempt. And they will know that I am the Lord Yahweh.

“‘The Lord Yahweh says this: When I gather Israel’s house from the peoples among whom they are scattered, and show myself holy through them before the nations’ eyes, then they will live on their own soil, which I gave to my servant Jacob.

They will live on it in security, building houses and planting vineyards; in security they will live, when I carry out judgments on all their neighbors who treat them with contempt. And they will know that I am Yahweh their God.’”

notes.text: Hebrew Danel; see the note at 14:14.
That is, the realm of the dead.
That is, a shameful death without honorable burial; the phrase is used of the Phoenicians, who practiced circumcision, as a mark of disgrace.
The Hebrew phrase is obscure; it may mean “sealer of proportion,” that is, the model of a perfect design. The Greek has “a seal of likeness.”

The identification of many of these stones is uncertain. The Hebrew lists nine stones, all found among the twelve on the high priest’s breastpiece (Exodus 28:17–20). The Greek lists all twelve of the breastpiece stones, adds silver and gold, and has a different final clause.
Or “You were with an anointed guardian cherub.” The Hebrew pronoun “you” has an unusual feminine form; the Greek reads “with the cherub” and lacks “anointed.”
Sidon, about 25 miles (40 kilometers) north of Tyre, was the other great Phoenician city.

verses.text: In the tenth year, on the twelfth day of the tenth month (in December–January),{a} Yahweh’s word came to me:
“Son of man, set your face against Pharaoh king of Egypt, and prophesy against him and against all Egypt.

Speak and say, ‘The Lord Yahweh says this: / Look, I am coming against you, / Pharaoh, king of Egypt, / the great monster{b} sprawled / in the midst of his Nile channels, / who says, “My Nile is mine; / I made it for myself.”

I will set hooks in your jaws / and cause the fish of your channels to stick to your scales. / Out of the middle of your channels I will drag you, / together with every fish of your channels / that clings to your scales.

I will fling you into the wilderness, / you and all the fish of your streams. / On the open field you will fall; / no one will gather you up or collect you. / To the beasts of the earth and the birds of the sky / I have given you as food.
Then all who live in Egypt will know / that I am Yahweh, / because they have been a staff of reed / to the house of Israel.

When they took hold of you by the hand,{c} you splintered / and tore open every shoulder of theirs; / when they leaned their weight on you, you snapped, / and made every one of their hips give way.{d}
“‘So the Lord Yahweh says this: Look, I am bringing a sword upon you, and I will cut off from you human and beast.
Egypt will become a desolate wasteland, and they will know that I am Yahweh. He claimed, “The Nile belongs to me; I created it,”
look, I am coming against you and against your streams. I will turn Egypt’s land into an utter ruin, a desolation, from Migdol to Syene{e} and as far as the border of Cush.{f}
No human foot will cross it, and no animal’s foot will cross it; for forty years it will be uninhabited.

I will make Egypt’s land a desolation among desolate lands, and its cities will lie desolate among ruined cities for forty years. I will scatter the Egyptians among the nations and disperse them through the lands.
“‘Yet the Lord Yahweh says this: At the end of forty years I will gather the Egyptians from the peoples where they were scattered.
I will turn back Egypt’s captivity and return them to Pathros,{g} their homeland, and they will be a lowly kingdom there.
It will be the lowliest of the kingdoms and will never again lift itself above the nations. I will make them so few that they will not rule over the nations.
Never again will Egypt be the trust of Israel’s house; instead it will be a reminder of their guilt in turning to them for help. And they will know that I am the Lord Yahweh.’”
In the twenty-seventh year, on the first day of the first month (in March–April),{h} Yahweh’s word came to me:

“Son of man, Nebuchadrezzar king of Babylon drove his army to hard labor against Tyre. Every head was rubbed bald and every shoulder rubbed raw. Yet from Tyre neither he nor his army got any wages for the labor he spent on it.

So the Lord Yahweh says this: Look, I am giving Egypt’s land to Nebuchadrezzar king of Babylon. He will carry off its riches,{i} take its spoil, and seize its plunder, and that will be the wages for his army.
As payment for the work he labored at, I have given him Egypt’s land, because they did it for me, declares the Lord Yahweh.
“On that day I will make a horn{j} sprout for Israel’s house, and I will give you an open mouth among them. And they will know that I am Yahweh.”

notes.text: Hebrew “in the tenth month, on the twelfth of the month.” On the spring-start calendar used in Ezekiel, the tenth month is Tevet; the date falls in January 587 BC. The Greek reads “the twelfth year ... on the first of the month.”
Hebrew tannim, a variant of tannin, “sea monster” or “dragon”; here a picture of the crocodile.
So the Hebrew margin and the Greek; the Hebrew text has “by your palm.”
Probable reading; compare the Greek “crushed the loins of them all.” The Hebrew reads “made all their hips stand.”
Migdol was in the northeast of Egypt and Syene (modern Aswan) in the far south; the phrase means “from one end of Egypt to the other.”
That is, the upper Nile region (Nubia, in modern Sudan).
That is, Upper (southern) Egypt.
Hebrew “in the first, on the first of the month.” On the spring-start calendar the first month is Nisan; the date falls in April 571 BC, the latest dated oracle in the book.
Or “its multitude.”
The horn is a symbol of strength.

verses.text: Yahweh’s word came to me:
“Son of man, prophesy and say, ‘The Lord Yahweh says this: / Howl, “Alas for the day!”
For the day is near, / the day of Yahweh is near, / a day of cloud, / a time of doom for the nations.
A sword will come against Egypt, / and anguish will seize Cush, / when the slain fall in Egypt, / when her wealth is carried away / and her foundations torn down.
Cush, Put, and Lud, all the mixed peoples,{a} Cub,{b} and the people of the allied land{c} will fall by the sword with them.

“‘Yahweh says this:
Egypt’s supporters will fall,
and her proud strength will come down.
From Migdol all the way to Syene
the sword will cut them down within her,
declares the Lord Yahweh.
They will be desolate / among desolate lands, / and its cities will lie / among ruined cities.
They will know that I am Yahweh / when I set fire to Egypt / and all her helpers are crushed.
“‘On that day messengers will go out from me in ships to terrify unsuspecting Cush. Anguish will take hold of them on Egypt’s day—for look, it is coming!
“‘The Lord Yahweh says this: / I will put an end to Egypt’s horde / by the hand of Nebuchadrezzar king of Babylon.
He and his army with him, / the cruelest of all the nations, / will be brought to devastate the country. / They will draw their swords against Egypt / and cover the land with dead bodies.

I will turn the Nile channels into dry ground / and sell the land into the hands of evil men. / By the hand of foreigners I will make desolate / the land and everything in it. / I, Yahweh, have spoken.
I will make Pathros desolate, / set fire to Zoan,{e} / and carry out judgments on Thebes.{f}
I will pour out my fury on Pelusium,{g} / Egypt’s stronghold, / and cut off the horde of Thebes.

In Tehaphnehes{l} the daylight will be blocked{m} / when I smash the yoke bars of Egypt there, / and her arrogant power ends within her. / Clouds will cover her, / and her daughters will be taken captive.
So I will carry out judgments on Egypt, / and they will know that I am Yahweh.’”
In the eleventh year, on the seventh day of the first month (in March–April),{n} Yahweh’s word came to me:
“Son of man, I have broken the arm of Pharaoh king of Egypt. Look, it has not been bound up for healing; no bandage has been put on to strengthen it so that it can grasp a sword.
So the Lord Yahweh says this: Watch out, I am against Pharaoh king of Egypt. I will break both his arms, the healthy one and the one already broken, and knock the sword out of his grasp.
I will scatter the Egyptians among the nations and disperse them through the lands.
I will strengthen the arms of Babylon’s king and put my sword into his hand, but Pharaoh’s arms I will smash, and Pharaoh will moan in front of the king like a man who is fatally wounded.

I will strengthen the arms of Babylon’s king, while Pharaoh’s arms will drop. They will know that I am Yahweh when I put my sword into the hand of Babylon’s king and he stretches it out against Egypt’s land.
I will scatter the Egyptians among the nations and disperse them through the lands. And they will know that I am Yahweh.”

notes.text: Or “all Arabia”; the Hebrew consonants can be read either way. The Greek list differs (it has “Persians, and Cretans, and Lydians, and Libyans, and all the mixed multitude”).
Cub is otherwise unknown; many scholars read Lub, “Libya.”
Hebrew “the children of the land of the covenant”; the Greek has “the children of my covenant.” The phrase may refer to allies of Egypt, or possibly to Judeans living in Egypt.
Hebrew Noph, the ancient capital of Lower Egypt, near modern Cairo; also in v. 16. Instead of “the idols,” the Greek has “the nobles.”
Zoan, called Tanis by the Greeks, was in the northeastern Nile delta.
Hebrew No, the great city of Upper Egypt, modern Luxor; also in vv. 15–16.
Hebrew Sin; also in v. 16. Pelusium was a frontier fortress in the northeastern delta. The Greek has “Sais” here and “Syene” in v. 16.
The meaning of the Hebrew is uncertain; the Greek reads “and waters will be poured out.”
Hebrew Aven (“wickedness”), a play on On, the city called Heliopolis, “city of the sun,” northeast of modern Cairo.
Pi-beseth, called Bubastis by the Greeks, was in the eastern delta.
Hebrew “they”; the pronoun is feminine and probably refers to the towns. The Greek has “the women.”
Tehaphnehes (also spelled Tahpanhes) is Daphnae, a fortress in the northeastern delta (compare Jeremiah 43:7–9).
So the Greek and some ancient witnesses; the main Hebrew text has “will hold back.”
