Hebrew “in the first, on the seventh of the month.” On the spring-start calendar the first month is Nisan; the date falls in April 587 BC.

verses.text: In the eleventh year, on the first day of the third month (in May–June),{a} Yahweh’s word came to me:
“Son of man, say to Pharaoh king of Egypt and to his horde: / ‘Whom are you like in your greatness?
Consider Assyria,{b} a cedar in Lebanon, / with lovely boughs and shade like a forest’s, / towering in height, / its crown up among the clouds.{c}
The waters made it great; / the deep made it tall, / sending its streams / all around the place it was planted / and sending its channels / to all the trees of the field.
So it grew taller / than all the trees of the field; / its boughs multiplied / and its branches grew long / from the abundant water as it spread out.
In its boughs / every bird of the sky made its nest; / under its branches / every beast of the field gave birth; / and in its shade / all the great nations lived.
It was beautiful in its greatness, / in the length of its limbs, / for its roots went down / to abundant waters.

The cedars in God’s garden / could not rival it; / the junipers were nothing like its boughs, / and the plane trees{d} were nothing / to compare with its branches. / No tree in God’s garden / matched it in beauty.
I made it beautiful / with its mass of limbs, / and all the trees of Eden, / those in God’s garden, envied it.
“‘So the Lord Yahweh says this: Because it{e} towered high and set its crown among the clouds, and its heart grew proud of its height,
I handed it over to the mightiest ruler of the nations, who will surely deal with it as its wickedness deserves. I have driven it out.

Foreigners, the most ruthless of nations, cut it down and left it lying. On the mountains and in every valley its limbs have fallen; its branches lie broken in every ravine of the land. All the peoples of the earth came out from its shade and left it.
On its fallen trunk all the birds of the sky settle, / and among its branches / all the beasts of the field take shelter.

This is so that no trees by the waters may tower to such a height or set their crowns among the clouds, and that no well-watered trees{f} may rise to equal them. For every one of them is given over to death, to the world below, among mortals, with those who descend to the pit.

“‘The Lord Yahweh says this: On the day it went down to Sheol{g} I made the deep mourn for it and covered it over;{h} I held back its streams, and the great waters were checked. For its sake I dressed Lebanon in mourning, and every tree of the field wilted over it.

At the sound of its fall I made the nations quake, when I cast it down to Sheol with those who descend to the pit. And all Eden’s trees, the choicest and best of Lebanon, all that drink water, were comforted in the world below.
They too went down with it to Sheol, to those slain by the sword—those who had been its arm,{i} who lived in its shade among the nations.

“‘Whom are you like, then, in glory and greatness among the trees of Eden? Yet you too will be brought down with the trees of Eden to the world below. Among the uncircumcised you will lie, with the sword’s slain. This is Pharaoh and all his horde, declares the Lord Yahweh.’”

notes.text: Hebrew “in the third, on the first of the month.” On the spring-start calendar the third month is Sivan; the date falls in June 587 BC.

Some scholars, reading one letter differently, find here not “Assyria” but “a cypress” (te’ashshur), so that the cedar stands for Pharaoh himself. The Greek has “the Assyrian was a cypress in Lebanon.”
So the Greek; the Hebrew word may mean “thick foliage”; also in vv. 10 and 14.
The identification of these trees is uncertain.
Hebrew “you”; the Hebrew shifts between “you” and “it.”
Hebrew “all that drink water.”
Sheol is the realm of the dead; also in vv. 16–17.
Or “I closed the deep over it.” The Hebrew is difficult; the Greek has simply “the deep mourned for him.”
The Hebrew is difficult; the Greek reads “his seed.”

verses.text: In the twelfth year, on the first day of the twelfth month (in February–March),{a} Yahweh’s word came to me:

“Son of man, raise a dirge over Pharaoh king of Egypt and say to him: / ‘Among the nations you likened yourself to a young lion, / but you are like a monster in the seas; / you burst out in your rivers, / churned the waters with your feet, / and fouled their streams.
“‘The Lord Yahweh says this: / I will cast my net over you / with a throng of many peoples, / and they will haul you up in my dragnet.
I will fling you onto the land; / on the open field I will hurl you down. / I will make every bird of the sky settle on you / and let the beasts of all the earth gorge themselves on you.
I will spread your flesh on the mountains / and fill the valleys with your carcass.{b}

I will water the land with what flows from you,
with your blood up to the mountains,
and the gullies will be full of you.

When I put out your light, I will veil the heavens
and blacken their stars;
a cloud will hide the sun,
and the moon will give no light.
Every shining light in the heavens / I will darken over you, / and I will set darkness over your land, / declares the Lord Yahweh.
“‘I will trouble the hearts of many peoples / when I bring your shattering{c} among the nations, / to lands you have not known.

I will horrify many peoples because of you, / and their kings will be shaken with dread over you / when I wave my sword in front of them. / Every one of them will shake each moment for his own life / on the day you fall.
“‘For the Lord Yahweh says this: / The sword of Babylon’s king / will come upon you.
By the swords of warriors / I will fell your horde— / the most ruthless of nations, every one. / They will ravage Egypt’s pride, / and all her horde will be wiped out.
I will destroy all her cattle / from beside the abundant waters. / No human foot will churn them again, / and no hoof of beast will churn them.
Then I will let their waters settle / and make their streams flow like oil, / declares the Lord Yahweh.

When I make Egypt’s land a desolation,
a land stripped of all that filled it,
when I strike down every one of its inhabitants,
then they will know that I am Yahweh.
This is a dirge, and they will chant it; / the daughters of the nations will chant it. / Over Egypt and over all her horde they will chant it, / declares the Lord Yahweh.’”
In the twelfth year, on the fifteenth day of the month,{d} Yahweh’s word came to me:
“Son of man, mourn for the mob of Egypt, and send her down, along with the daughters of the powerful nations, into the underworld, to join those who descend into the pit.
‘Are you lovelier than anyone? Down with you; lie among the uncircumcised!’{e}
They will fall among those slain by the sword. A sword has been handed over; drag her away with all her hordes.{f}
From inside Sheol the strongest of the mighty ones will speak to him and to his allies: ‘They have come down and lie motionless, the uncircumcised, killed by the sword.’
“Assyria is there with her whole army, her tombs surrounding him,{g} all of them killed, struck down by the sword.
Her graves are set in the remotest depths of the pit, and her company lies around her grave, all of them slain, fallen by the sword, they who once spread terror in the land of the living.

“Elam{h} is there with all her horde around her grave, all of them slain, fallen by the sword, who went down uncircumcised to the world below, they who once spread terror in the land of the living. Now they bear their disgrace with those who go down to the pit.

Among the slain they have made a bed for her with all her horde, their graves all around her, all of them uncircumcised, slain by the sword. Because terror of them was spread in the land of the living, they bear their disgrace with those who go down to the pit; she is laid among the slain.
“Meshech and Tubal{i} are there with all their multitudes; their tombs surround them. All are uncircumcised and run through with the sword, since they spread dread across the land of the living.

They do not lie beside the other fallen warriors, the uncircumcised,{j} who went down to Sheol equipped for war, with their swords laid under their heads and their shields{k} over their bones, since these heroes spread dread across the land of the living.
And you too will be broken among the uncircumcised and lie with those slain by the sword.
“Edom is there, her kings and all her chiefs, who for all their might are laid with those slain by the sword. With the uncircumcised they lie, and with those who descend to the pit.

“The rulers of the north are there, every one of them, and all the Sidonians, who went down in disgrace with the slain, though their power had inspired terror. They lie uncircumcised beside those killed by the sword and carry their shame together with those who descend to the pit.
“Pharaoh will see them and be consoled over all his horde—Pharaoh and all his army, slain by the sword, declares the Lord Yahweh.
For I spread terror of him{l} in the land of the living, yet he will be laid among the uncircumcised, with those slain by the sword—Pharaoh and all his horde, declares the Lord Yahweh.”

notes.text: Hebrew “in the twelfth month, on the first of the month.” On the spring-start calendar the twelfth month is Adar; the date falls in March 585 BC. The Greek has “the tenth month.”
Or “your heap of worms”; the Hebrew word is uncertain.
So the Hebrew; the Greek reads “your captivity.”

The Hebrew does not name the month. If the twelfth month of v. 1 is meant, the date is in March 585 BC. The Greek reads “in the first month” (Nisan, in March–April), which would place the oracle in April 586 BC.
This verse is absent from the Greek, which has a differently arranged text in vv. 19–21.
The Hebrew of this verse is difficult.
Hebrew “him”; the Hebrew shifts between masculine and feminine references to Assyria in vv. 22–23.
Elam was a kingdom east of Babylon, in what is now southwestern Iran.
On Meshech and Tubal see the note at 27:13.
The Greek has “with the giants that fell of old,” perhaps reading a slightly different Hebrew word for “of the uncircumcised.”
Probable reading; the Hebrew has “their iniquities.”
So the Hebrew text and the Greek; the Hebrew margin has “my terror.”

verses.text: Yahweh’s word came to me:
“Son of man, speak to your people’s children and tell them: Suppose I bring the sword against a land, and the people of that land pick one man from their ranks and make him their lookout.
He sees the sword coming against the land, sounds the ram’s horn,{a} and warns the people.
Then if anyone hears the horn’s blast and pays no heed, and the sword comes and takes him away, his blood will be on his own head.
He heard the horn’s blast and paid no heed; his blood is on himself. Had he heeded, he would have saved his life.

But suppose the lookout sees the sword coming and does not sound the horn, so the people are not warned, and the sword comes and takes one of them. That person is taken away in his guilt, but I will hold the lookout to account for his blood.
“As for you, son of man, I have made you a lookout for Israel’s house. Whenever you hear a word from my mouth, warn them for me.

If I tell the wicked person, ‘You wicked man, you are going to die,’ and you do not speak out to turn him from his way, then that wicked person will die for his guilt, but I will hold you accountable for his blood.
But if you do warn the wicked to turn from his course, and he does not turn from it, he will die in his guilt, but you will have rescued your own life.
“And you, son of man, say to Israel’s house: This is what you keep saying: ‘Our rebellions and our sins weigh on us, and we are wasting away under them. How then can we live?’

Tell them: ‘As I live, declares the Lord Yahweh, I take no delight in the death of the wicked, but rather in the wicked turning from his course and living. Turn back, turn back from your evil ways! Why should you die, house of Israel?’

“And you, son of man, say to your people: The righteousness of a righteous person will not save him when he rebels, and the wickedness of a wicked person will not make him stumble when he turns away from it. A righteous person cannot live on the strength of his righteousness when he sins.
If I tell the righteous that he will surely live, and he trusts in his own righteousness and does wrong, none of his righteous acts will be remembered; he will die for the wrong he has done.
And if I tell the wicked, ‘You will surely die,’ and he turns from his sin and does what is just and right—
if the wicked man returns a pledge, pays back what he stole, and walks in the statutes that give life, doing no wrong—he will surely live; he will not die.
Not one sin of his will be remembered against him. Justice and right are what he has done; he will surely live.
“Yet your people’s children say, ‘The Lord’s way is not fair,’ when it is their own way that is not fair.
When a righteous person turns from his righteousness and does wrong, he will die for it.
And if the wicked one leaves his wickedness behind and practices justice and right, by these he will live.
Yet you say, ‘The Lord’s way is not fair.’ House of Israel, I will judge each of you by your ways.”
In the twelfth year of our exile, on the fifth day of the tenth month (in December–January),{b} someone who had fled from Jerusalem reached me with the news: “The city is struck down!”
Now the evening before the fugitive arrived, Yahweh’s hand had come on me, and he opened my mouth before the man reached me at dawn. My mouth was opened, and I kept silent no longer.
Yahweh’s word came to me:

“Son of man, those living in these ruins on Israel’s soil are saying, ‘Abraham was only one man, yet he took possession of the land. But we are numerous; to us the land is surely handed over to hold.’
So tell them: ‘The Lord Yahweh says this: You eat meat with the blood in it, lift your eyes to your idols, and shed blood. Should you then possess the land?
You lean on your swords, you practice abominations, and every man of you defiles the wife of his neighbor. Should you then possess the land?’{c}

“Tell them this: ‘The Lord Yahweh says: As surely as I live, those who are among the ruins will die by the sword, anyone out in the open I will give to the wild animals as food, and those in the fortresses and caves will die of disease.
I will turn the land into a waste and a horror, and the pride of its strength will cease. Israel’s mountains will be so desolate that no one will pass through them.
Then they will know that I am Yahweh, when I turn the land into a waste and a horror for all the abominations they have done.’

“As for you, son of man, your people’s children are talking about you by the walls and in the doorways of the houses. One says to another, every man to his brother, ‘Let us go and hear what word comes from Yahweh.’

They come to you as people do, and sit before you as my people, and they hear your words, but they do not act on them. With their mouths they show much love,{d} but their hearts chase after their own gain.
To them you are like a love song, sung by one with a lovely voice who plays the instrument well. They hear your words, but they do not act on them.
Yet when this comes—and it is coming!—they will know that a prophet has been among them.”

notes.text: Hebrew shofar, also in vv. 4–6.

Hebrew “in the tenth month, on the fifth of the month.” On the spring-start calendar the tenth month is Tevet; the date falls in January 585 BC, about five months after the city fell. The Greek has “in the tenth year … in the twelfth month,” and some ancient witnesses have “the eleventh year.”
The Greek lacks most of vv. 25–26, from “You eat meat” to the end of v. 26.
Or “they act out lust”; the Hebrew is uncertain. The Greek has “falsehood is in their mouth.”

verses.text: Yahweh’s word came to me:

“Son of man, prophesy against Israel’s shepherds. Prophesy, and say to them, to the shepherds: ‘The Lord Yahweh says this: Woe to Israel’s shepherds, who have been tending only themselves! Is it not the flock that shepherds ought to tend?
You eat the fat,{a} you dress in the wool, you slaughter the fatlings, but the flock you do not tend.

The weak you have not made strong, the sick you have not healed, the injured you have not bandaged, the strays you have not brought back, the lost you have not sought; with force and harshness you have ruled them.
So they were scattered for lack of a shepherd, and once scattered they became food for every wild beast.
My sheep wandered over every mountain and every high hill; across the whole face of the earth my sheep were scattered, with no one searching or seeking for them.
“‘So, you shepherds, hear Yahweh’s word:

As I live, declares the Lord Yahweh, because my sheep have become plunder, because my sheep have become food for every wild beast for lack of a shepherd, since my shepherds did not search for my sheep but tended themselves and not my flock—
therefore, you shepherds, hear Yahweh’s word.

The Lord Yahweh says: I am against the shepherds! I will take my flock back from them and stop them from feeding the flock, so the shepherds will no longer feed themselves. I will pull my sheep out of their mouths, and the sheep will no longer be their food.
“‘For the Lord Yahweh says this: Here I am; I myself will search for my sheep and look after them.

Like a shepherd who goes looking for his flock when his sheep are scattered around him, I will go looking for my sheep. I will save them from all the places they were scattered during a day of clouds and gloom.

I will bring them out from the peoples, gather them from the lands, and bring them into their own soil. I will pasture them on Israel’s mountains, by the ravines, and in every inhabited place in the land.
In good pasture I will feed them, and on the lofty mountains of Israel their grazing ground will be. There they will lie down in a good fold and feed on rich pasture on Israel’s mountains.
I myself will be the shepherd of my sheep, and I myself will give them rest, declares the Lord Yahweh.
I will look for the lost, return the strays, bandage the wounded and give strength to the weak; but the fat and the strong I will destroy.{b} I will tend them with justice.
“As for you, my flock, the Lord Yahweh says this: I will judge between one animal and another, between the rams and the male goats.
Is it not enough for you to feed on the best pasture? Must you also tread down with your feet whatever pasture is left? Or to drink clear water, that you must muddy the rest with your feet?
Must my sheep eat the ground your hooves have trodden and drink the water your hooves have fouled?
“‘So the Lord Yahweh says this to them: Here I am; I myself will judge between the fat sheep and the lean.
Because you shove with flank and shoulder and butt all the weak ones with your horns until you have scattered them abroad,
I will save my flock; no longer will they be plunder. I will judge between one sheep and another.
Over them I will set up one shepherd, my servant David, to pasture them. He will feed them himself and be a shepherd to them.
I, Yahweh, will be their God, and my servant David will be prince among them. I, Yahweh, have spoken.
“‘With them I will cut a covenant of peace and banish the wild beasts from the land, so that in the wilderness they can dwell in safety and in the woods they can sleep.
I will make them and the places around my hill a blessing.{c} I will send down the rain in its season; there will be showers of blessing.

The trees of the field will yield their fruit and the land its produce, and they will be secure on their own soil. They will know that I am Yahweh when I break the bars of their yoke and rescue them from the hand of those who enslaved them.
No longer will they be plunder for the nations, nor will the land’s wild beasts devour them. They will live in safety, with no one to frighten them.
I will raise up for them a planting renowned for its yield,{d} and no longer will they be swept away by famine in the land or bear the scorn of the nations.
Then they will know that I, Yahweh their God, am with them, and that they, Israel’s house, are my people, declares the Lord Yahweh.
You are my sheep, the flock that I feed; you are humans,{e} and I am your God, declares the Lord Yahweh.’”

notes.text: So the Hebrew vowels; with different vowels, and the Greek, “the milk.”
So the Hebrew; the Greek has “the strong I will guard,” reading a similar Hebrew word.
Or “I will make them a blessing around my hill.” The Greek reads “I will settle them around my mountain.”
Hebrew “a planting for a name”; the Greek has “a plant of peace.”
Hebrew adam, “humankind,” the word in the title “son of man” (ben adam; see the note at 2:1). The Greek lacks “you are human.”

verses.text: Yahweh’s word came to me:
“Son of man, turn your face toward Mount Seir{a} and prophesy against it.
Say to it: ‘The Lord Yahweh says this: I am coming against you, Mount Seir; I will stretch out my hand against you and make you a desolate waste.
Your towns I will turn into ruins, and you yourself will become a desolation. Then you will know that I am Yahweh.
“‘Because you nursed an age-old hatred and handed Israel’s people over to the power of the sword at the time of their disaster, the time of their final punishment,
therefore, as I live, declares the Lord Yahweh, I will deliver you up to bloodshed, and bloodshed will hound you. Since you did not hate bloodshed, bloodshed will hound you.{b}
Mount Seir I will turn into a waste and a horror, and from it I will cut off all who pass to and fro.
I will fill your mountains with the dead; those killed by the sword will fall on your hills, in your valleys and in all your gullies.
A desolation forever I will make you, and your towns will not be inhabited.{c} Then you will know that I am Yahweh.
“‘Because you said, “These two nations and these two lands will be mine, and we will take possession of them”—though Yahweh was there—

therefore, as surely as I live, declares the Lord Yahweh, I will treat you with the same anger and jealousy that you showed in your hatred toward them. I will reveal myself among them{d} when I judge you.
Then you will know that I am Yahweh. I have heard every insult you spoke against the mountains of Israel when you said, “They are laid waste; they were given to us to devour.”
With your mouths you made yourselves great against me and piled up your words against me. I heard it.
“‘The Lord Yahweh says this: While the whole earth rejoices, I will make you a desolation.

As you rejoiced over the inheritance of Israel’s house because it was made desolate, so I will deal with you. A desolation you will be, Mount Seir, you and all Edom, every bit of it. Then they will know that I am Yahweh.’”

notes.text: See the note at 25:8.
The Hebrew of this verse is difficult; “blood” may also hint at Edom’s name (compare Hebrew dam, “blood,” and adom, “red”).
So the Hebrew margin; the Hebrew text may be read “will not return.”
The Greek has “to you.”

verses.text: “And you, son of man, prophesy to Israel’s mountains and say: ‘Mountains of Israel, hear Yahweh’s word.
The Lord Yahweh says this: Your enemy jeered over you, “Aha! Those age-old heights{a} are ours to hold now!”

So prophesy and say: The Lord Yahweh says this: Because they made you desolate and hounded you from every side, until the remaining nations owned you, and you have become the talk of gossiping tongues and the slander of the people,

therefore, mountains of Israel, listen to the word of the Lord Yahweh. To the mountains and hills, to the gullies and valleys, to the ruined wastes and abandoned cities that have been plundered and ridiculed by the other nations all around, the Lord Yahweh says this:

the Lord Yahweh says this: In the fire of my jealousy I have spoken against the rest of the nations and against all Edom, who with wholehearted glee and contempt claimed my land as their own possession, so as to drive out its pasture and plunder it.{b}

So prophesy concerning Israel’s soil and tell the mountains and the hills, the ravines and the valleys: The Lord Yahweh says this: In my jealousy and my fury I speak, because you have endured the nations’ scorn.
So the Lord Yahweh says this: I lift my hand and swear that the nations around you will themselves endure scorn.
“‘But as for you, mountains of Israel, you will grow branches and produce fruit for my people Israel, because they will return home before long.
For see, I am for you; I will turn my face to you, and plowmen and sowers will work you.
I will multiply people upon you, the whole house of Israel, all of it. The towns will be inhabited and the ruins rebuilt.

I will multiply on you both human and beast; they will increase and be fruitful. I will settle you as you were in former times and treat you better than at your beginning. Then you will know that I am Yahweh.
I will make people walk upon you, my people Israel. They will possess you, and you will be their inheritance; never again will you rob them of their children.
“‘The Lord Yahweh says this: Because people say to you, “You devour human beings and rob your nation of its children,”
therefore you will devour people no more or rob your nation{c} of its children, declares the Lord Yahweh.
I will no longer let you hear the nations’ taunts; you will bear the peoples’ scorn no more, and you will no longer make your nation stumble,{d} declares the Lord Yahweh.’”
Yahweh’s word came to me:
“Son of man, when Israel’s house lived on their own soil, they defiled it by their conduct and their deeds. In my sight their conduct was like the impurity of a woman in her monthly period.
So I emptied out my wrath upon them, because of the blood spilled on the land and the idols that had polluted it.
I scattered them among the nations, and they were dispersed through the lands. By their conduct and their deeds I judged them.
But wherever they came among the nations, they profaned my holy name, for people said of them, ‘These are Yahweh’s people, yet they had to leave his land.’
I cared, though, for my holy name, which Israel’s house profaned among the nations where they went.
“So say to Israel’s house: ‘The Lord Yahweh says this: Not for your sake am I about to act, house of Israel, but for my holy name, which you have profaned among the nations where you went.

I will demonstrate the holiness of my great name, which has been dishonored among the nations—the name you dishonored among them. Declares the Lord Yahweh: the nations will know that I am Yahweh when I show my holiness through you before their eyes.{e}
“‘I will pick you up from among the nations, collect you out of every country, and bring you to your own land.
I will sprinkle clean water on you, and you will be clean from all your impurities; from all your idols I will cleanse you.
I will give you a new heart and place a new spirit inside you. From your body I will remove the heart of stone, and I will give you a heart of flesh.
I will put my Spirit{f} within you and cause you to walk in my statutes, and you will keep my rulings and carry them out.
In the land I granted to your fathers you will dwell; you will be a people to me, and I will be God to you.
I will save you from all your impurities. I will call to the grain and make it abound, and I will lay no famine on you.
I will multiply the fruit of the tree and the produce of the field, so that among the nations you will never again bear the shame of hunger.
Then you will remember your evil ways and your deeds that were not good, and you will loathe yourselves for your iniquities and your abominations.
Not for your sake am I doing this, declares the Lord Yahweh—be sure of that. Be ashamed and humiliated for your ways, house of Israel.
“‘The Lord Yahweh says this: On the day I cleanse you from all your iniquities, I will resettle the towns, and the ruins will be rebuilt.
The desolate land will be worked, where once it lay a waste before the eyes of every passerby.
They will say, “This land that was desolate has become like the garden of Eden, and the towns that were ruined, desolate, and torn down are now fortified and inhabited.”
Then the nations left around you will know that I, Yahweh, have rebuilt what was torn down and replanted what was desolate. I, Yahweh, have spoken, and I will do it.
“‘The Lord Yahweh says this: Once more I will let Israel’s house seek this from me, and I will do it for them: I will make their people as many as a flock.
Like the flock for sacrifices, like Jerusalem’s flock at her appointed feasts, so will the ruined towns be filled with flocks of people. Then they will know that I am Yahweh.’”

notes.text: Or “the everlasting high places.”
The Hebrew of the last clause is difficult.
So the Hebrew margin and the Greek; the Hebrew text has “make your nation stumble.”
The Greek lacks this clause.

Papyrus 967, one of the earliest known Greek manuscripts of Ezekiel (about AD 200), is reported to lack the passage from here (“And the nations will know…”) through 36:38, and to place chapter 37 after chapters 38–39. Some scholars see this as evidence of an earlier edition of the book; others think the passage was lost by accident. These details are given as reported in scholarly literature.
Or “my spirit”; Hebrew ruach, also “wind” or “breath” (see 37:1–14).

verses.text: Yahweh’s hand came on me, and he carried me out by Yahweh’s Spirit{a} and set me down in the middle of the valley,{b} and it was full of bones.
He led me all around among them, and I saw a great many of them lying on the valley floor, and they were bone-dry.
He asked me, “Son of man, can these bones live again?” I replied, “Lord Yahweh, you alone know.”
Then he said to me, “Prophesy over these bones and tell them: Dry bones, hear Yahweh’s word!
The Lord Yahweh says this to these bones: I am going to bring breath{c} into you, and you will live.
I will attach tendons to you, bring flesh up over you, cover you with skin, and place breath inside you, and you will live. And you will know that I am Yahweh.”
So I prophesied as I had been commanded. While I prophesied a sound broke out, a clattering, and the bones drew together, bone joining bone.
As I watched, sinews were on them, flesh had grown, and skin covered them over, but there was no breath in them.

Then he said to me, “Prophesy to the breath; prophesy, son of man, and say to the breath: ‘The Lord Yahweh says this: From the four winds come, breath, and blow into these slain, so that they may live.’”
So I prophesied as he commanded me, and the breath entered them; they came to life and rose to their feet, an exceedingly vast army.
Then he said to me, “Son of man, these bones are the whole house of Israel. They keep saying, ‘Our bones are dried up, our hope has perished; we are cut off, every one of us.’
So prophesy and say to them: ‘The Lord Yahweh says this: My people, I am going to open your graves and raise you up out of them, and I will bring you to Israel’s soil.
You will know that I am Yahweh, my people, when I open your graves and raise you up out of them.
I will place my Spirit inside you so that you live, and I will put you in your own land. Then you will know that I, Yahweh, have spoken and have acted, declares Yahweh.’”
Yahweh’s word came to me:

“You, son of man, take a stick{d} and write on it, ‘For Judah and for the Israelites joined with him.’ Then take another stick and write on it, ‘For Joseph, the stick of Ephraim, and for all Israel’s house joined with him.’
Bring them together into one stick for yourself, so that they become one in your hand.
When your people’s children ask you, ‘Will you not explain to us what you mean by these?’

tell them, ‘The Lord Yahweh says this: Look, I am taking the stick of Joseph, which is in the hand of Ephraim, along with the tribes of Israel that are his companions, and I will add Judah’s stick to it and make them into one stick, and in my hand they will be one.’{e}
Hold the sticks you wrote on in your hand where they can see them.
Then tell them: ‘The Lord Yahweh says this: I am going to take the Israelites from among the nations where they have gone. I will gather them from every side and bring them to their own soil.
I will make them one nation in the land, on Israel’s mountains, and one king will be king over all of them. They will no longer be two nations, never again divided into two kingdoms.

They will never again make themselves unclean with their idols, their vile images or any of their crimes. I will rescue them from all the unfaithful acts by which they sinned{f} and will cleanse them. In this way they will be my people, and I will be their God.
“‘My servant David will be king over them, and there will be one shepherd for them all. They will walk in my rulings and keep my statutes and do them.

They will live in the land I gave my servant Jacob, where your fathers lived. There they will dwell forever, they and their sons and their sons’ sons, with David my servant as their prince for all time.
I will make a covenant of peace with them; an everlasting covenant it will be. I will establish them and multiply them,{g} and I will set my sanctuary among them forever.
My dwelling place will be with them; I will be their God, and they will be my people.
Then the nations will know that I, Yahweh, make Israel holy, when my sanctuary is among them forever.’”

notes.text: Or “by the spirit of Yahweh”; Hebrew ruach, which can mean “spirit,” “breath,” or “wind.” The word plays through vv. 1–14.
Or “plain”; the same word as in 3:22–23.
Hebrew ruach, also in vv. 6, 8–10; in v. 9 it is also “the four winds.”
Or “a piece of wood,” perhaps a wooden writing tablet; also in vv. 16–20.
So the Hebrew; the Greek has “one stick in the hand of Judah.”
Probable reading, following the Greek; the Hebrew has “from all their dwelling places in which they sinned.”
The Greek lacks “I will establish them and multiply them.”

verses.text: Yahweh’s word came to me:
“Son of man, turn your face toward Gog,{a} of the land of Magog,{b} the chief prince{c} of Meshech and Tubal, and prophesy against him.
Say: ‘The Lord Yahweh says this: I am coming against you, Gog, chief prince of Meshech and Tubal.

I will turn you around, put hooks in your jaws, and lead you out with your whole army, horses and horsemen, all of them splendidly equipped, a vast company with large and small shields, every one of them wielding swords.
Persia, Cush, and Put{d} are with them, all with shield and helmet,
Gomer with all its battalions, Beth-togarmah{e} from the remotest north with all its battalions—a host of peoples go with you.
“‘Be ready; make yourself ready, you and all the companies mustered around you, and be their guard.{f}

After many days you will be summoned.{g} In the latter years you will come against a land restored from the sword, whose people were gathered from many peoples onto Israel’s mountains, which had long lain in ruins. Its people were brought out from the peoples, and now all of them live securely.
You will go up, advancing like a storm; like a cloud covering the land you will be, you and all your troops and many peoples with you.
“‘The Lord Yahweh says this: On that day thoughts will rise in your mind, and you will devise an evil scheme.
You will say, “I will go up against a land of unwalled villages; I will fall on a quiet people who live in safety, all of them dwelling without walls, with neither bars nor gates,”

to seize spoil and carry off plunder, to turn your hand against ruins now resettled and against a people gathered from the nations, who are acquiring livestock and goods and live at the center{h} of the earth.

Sheba and Dedan and the merchants of Tarshish{i} with all its young lions{j} will ask you, “Have you come to seize spoil? Have you assembled your company to carry off plunder, to take away silver and gold, to seize livestock and goods, to take great spoil?”’
“So prophesy, son of man, and say to Gog: ‘The Lord Yahweh says this: On that day, when my people Israel are living securely, will you not take notice?{k}
You will come from your home in the remotest part of the north, you and a great many nations with you, all of them on horseback, an enormous crowd and a powerful army.

You will march against my people Israel like a cloud covering the earth. In the last days it will come about that I will lead you against my land, so that the nations will know me when I show my holiness through you, Gog, in front of them.
“‘The Lord Yahweh says this: Are you the one I was talking about long ago, through my servants the prophets of Israel? For years in those days they prophesied that I would lead you against them.
On that day, the day Gog comes against Israel’s land, declares the Lord Yahweh, my fury will flare up in my nostrils.
In my jealousy and in the fire of my wrath I declare: On that day there will surely be a great earthquake in Israel’s land.

Fish in the ocean, birds in the sky, wild animals, all the crawling creatures of the ground, and every person on earth will shake because of me. Mountains will be toppled, the cliffs{l} will collapse, and every wall will crash to the ground.
I will call for a sword against Gog on all my mountains,{m} declares the Lord Yahweh; each man’s sword will be turned against his brother.
With plague and bloodshed I will enter into judgment with him. I will rain down on him and on his troops and on the many peoples with him a torrential downpour, hailstones, fire, and sulfur.
Thus I will display my greatness and my holiness and reveal myself before the eyes of many nations. Then they will know that I am Yahweh.’

notes.text: Gog is otherwise unknown. Some link the name to Gyges (Gugu), a seventh-century BC king of Lydia in western Asia Minor; in Ezekiel he is a ruler of the far north who leads the nations against Israel in the last days (compare Rev 20:8).
Magog appears among the sons of Japheth in Gen 10:2. Here it seems to mean “the land of Gog.”
Or “the prince of Rosh”; Hebrew nesi rosh. The Greek takes Rosh as a name (“Rhos”). Also in v. 3 and 39:1. On Meshech and Tubal, peoples of central Asia Minor, see the note at 27:13.
Cush is the Upper Nile region, south of Egypt; Put is probably Libya.
Gomer is usually identified with the Cimmerians, and Beth-togarmah with a region in eastern Asia Minor (compare 27:14).
So the Hebrew; the Greek has “you will be a guard for me.”
Or “mustered”; or “punished.”
Hebrew “the navel”; compare 5:5.
The Greek has “Carthaginian merchants.” On Tarshish see the note at 27:12.
Or “its young warriors”; the Greek has “all their villages.”
So the Hebrew; the Greek has “will you not rise up?”
Or “the terraces”; the Hebrew word is rare.
Hebrew uncertain; the Greek has “I will summon every terror against him.”

verses.text: “And you, son of man, prophesy against Gog and say: ‘The Lord Yahweh says this: I am coming against you, Gog, chief prince of Meshech and Tubal.
I will turn you around and drive you on,{a} bring you up from the far reaches of the north, and lead you against Israel’s mountains.
Then out of your left hand I will knock your bow, and out of your right I will dash your arrows.
On Israel’s mountains you will fall, you and all your troops and the peoples with you. I will hand you over as food to every winged scavenger and to the beasts of the field.
In the open field you will fall, for I have spoken, declares the Lord Yahweh.
Fire I will send on Magog{b} and on those who dwell at ease in the coastlands, and they will know that I am Yahweh.
“‘I will make my holy name known among my people Israel, and never again will I allow my holy name to be dishonored. Then the nations will know that I am Yahweh, the Holy One in Israel.
It is coming! It will surely happen, declares the Lord Yahweh. This is the day I have spoken of.

“‘Then those who live in Israel’s towns will go out and make fires of the weapons and burn them—small and large shields, bows and arrows, war clubs and spears. For seven years they will make fires of them.

They will not have to collect firewood from the countryside or cut it in the forests, because they will burn the weapons for fuel. They will rob those who robbed them and plunder those who plundered them, declares the Lord Yahweh.

“‘On that day I will give Gog a grave site there in Israel, the Valley of the Travelers,{c} on the east side of the Sea.{d} It will bar the travelers’ way, for there Gog and all his horde will be buried, and it will be called the Valley of Hamon-gog.{e}
For seven months Israel’s house will be burying them, to cleanse the land.
All the land’s people will take part in the burying, and the day I display my glory will win them a name, declares the Lord Yahweh.
They will set apart men to pass continually through the land, burying those{f} left lying on the ground, so as to cleanse it. At the end of seven months they will begin their search.
As they travel through the land, if any of them sees a human bone, he will put up a sign next to it, and it will stay until the gravediggers have buried it in the Valley of Hamon-gog.
A city too will be named Hamonah.{g} So they will cleanse the land.’

“As for you, son of man, the Lord Yahweh says this: Tell every kind of bird and every wild animal: ‘Gather together and come! Assemble from every side for the sacrificial feast I am slaughtering for you, a huge feast on the mountains of Israel, where you will eat meat and drink blood.
You will eat the flesh of warriors and drink the blood of the rulers of the earth—rams, lambs, goats and bulls, every one of them well-fed animals from Bashan.{h}
At the feast I am slaughtering for you, you will eat fat until you are stuffed and drink blood until you are intoxicated.
At my table you will be filled with horses and riders,{i} with warriors and soldiers of every kind, declares the Lord Yahweh.’
“I will set my glory among the nations, and all the nations will see the judgment I carry out and the hand I lay on them.
From that day on, Israel’s house will know that I am Yahweh their God.

And the nations will know that Israel’s house went into exile for their iniquity, because they were unfaithful to me. So I hid my face from them and gave them into the hand of their foes, and all of them fell by the sword.
As their impurity and their rebellions deserved, I dealt with them and hid my face from them.
“So the Lord Yahweh says this: Now I will turn back the captivity{j} of Jacob and show mercy to all of Israel’s house, and I will be zealous for my holy name.
They will forget{k} their disgrace and all the unfaithfulness they showed me, when they live securely on their own soil with no one to frighten them.
When I bring them back from the peoples and gather them from their enemies’ lands, I will show myself holy through them in the sight of many nations.
Then they will know that I am Yahweh their God, who sent them into exile among the nations and then gathered them to their own soil, leaving none of them behind there any longer.{l}
Never again will I hide my face from them, for I will have poured out my Spirit on Israel’s house, declares the Lord Yahweh.”

notes.text: The Hebrew verb is found only here; the Greek has “guide you.”
The Greek has “on Gog.”
Hebrew Oberim; or, with a slight change, “the Valley of Abarim,” the mountain range east of the Dead Sea.
That is, the Dead Sea.
Meaning “Gog’s horde.”
Meaning “horde.” The Hebrew of this clause is difficult; the Greek has “the name of the city will be Burial-place.”
Hebrew “the passers-by, those left”; the Greek lacks “the passers-by.”
Bashan, east of the Sea of Galilee, was famed for its cattle (compare Amos 4:1).
Or “chariots.”
Or “restore the fortunes.”
So many interpreters, with a slight change of vowels; the Hebrew has “They will bear.”
The Greek lacks the last part of this verse, from “and then gathered them.”

verses.text: In the twenty-fifth year of our exile, at the beginning of the year, on the tenth day of the month,{a} in the fourteenth year after the city was struck down, on that very day Yahweh’s hand came on me, and he brought me there.
In visions of God he brought me to Israel’s land and set me down on a very high mountain, on which there was something like the structure of a city, to the south.{b}
When he had brought me there, I saw a man whose appearance shone like bronze, holding a linen cord and a measuring reed, standing in the gateway.

The man said to me, “Son of man, look with your eyes and listen with your ears, and give your attention to everything I am going to show you, for you were brought here so that I could show it to you. Tell Israel’s house everything you see.”

There was a wall surrounding the temple area{c} on all sides. In the man’s hand was a measuring reed 10.5 feet long, measured in long cubits, each a cubit and a handbreadth.{d} He measured the wall: it was 10.5 feet thick and 10.5 feet high.{e}
Then he came to the gate that faced east. He climbed its steps and measured the threshold{f} of the gate: 10.5 feet deep.{g}

Each guardroom{h} was 10.5 feet long and 10.5 feet wide, and between the guardrooms the space was 8.75 feet. The threshold of the gate beside the vestibule of the gate, on the inner side, was 10.5 feet.{i}
Then he measured the vestibule of the gate on the inner side: 10.5 feet.{j}{k}
He measured the vestibule of the gate: 14 feet; and its jambs:{l} 3.5 feet.{m} The vestibule of the gate was on the inner side.
The guardrooms of the east gate were three on each side, all three with the same measurement, and the jambs on each side had the same measurement.
He measured the width of the gate’s entrance, 17.5 feet, and the length{n} of the gateway, about 23 feet.{o}
In front of the guardrooms was a barrier 21 inches wide on each side, and the guardrooms were 10.5 feet square on each side.{p}
He measured the gate from the back{q} of one guardroom to the back of the other: the width was about 44 feet,{r} from one doorway to the opposite doorway.
He also measured{s} the jambs: 105 feet;{t} the court reached up to the jamb all around the gateway.
The distance from the face of the outer gateway to the face of the gate’s inner vestibule was 87.5 feet.{u}
The guardrooms and their jambs had narrow{v} windows all around on the inside of the gateway, and the vestibules likewise had windows all around on the inside. On each jamb were palm-tree carvings.
Then he brought me into the outer court, and there were rooms and a pavement laid all around the court; thirty rooms faced the pavement.
The pavement ran alongside the gates, matching the length of the gates; this was the lower pavement.
He measured the distance from the front of the lower gate to the front of the inner court on the outside: 175 feet,{w} on the east and on the north.{x}
Next, the gate of the outer courtyard that faced north: he measured both its length and its width.
Its guardrooms, three on each side, its jambs, and its vestibule had the same measurements as the first gate: 87.5 feet long and about 44 feet wide.{y}
Its windows, its vestibule, and its palm carvings were measured like the east-facing gate. People climbed up to it by seven steps, with its vestibule in front of them.
Across from the north gate, just as on the east side, there was a gate leading to the inner courtyard. He measured the distance from one gate to the other: 175 feet.{z}
Then he brought me around to the southern side, where there was a gate facing south. He measured its doorposts and its porch, and they matched the dimensions of the others.
It and its vestibule had windows all around, like the other windows. It was 87.5 feet long and about 44 feet wide.{aa}
Seven steps went up to it, with its vestibule in front of them, and it had palm carvings on its jambs, one on each side.
The inner court too had a gate facing south, and he measured from gate to gate toward the south: 175 feet.{ab}
Next he took me by the south gate into the inner court and measured that gate; its dimensions were like these.
Its guardrooms, jambs, and vestibule had the same measurements as the others, and it and its vestibule had windows all around. It was 87.5 feet long and about 44 feet wide.{ac}
There were vestibules all around, about 44 feet long and 8.75 feet{ad} wide.{ae}
Its vestibule faced the outer court; its jambs bore palm carvings, and eight steps formed its ascent.
Then he brought me into the inner court on the east side, and measured the gate there; its dimensions were like these.
Its guardrooms, jambs, and vestibule had the same measurements as the others, and it and its vestibule had windows all around. It was 87.5 feet long and about 44 feet wide.{af}
Its vestibule faced the outer court; palm carvings were on its jambs on each side, and its stairway had eight steps.
He took me to the north gate and measured it by the same dimensions,
as did its guardrooms, jambs, and vestibule. It had windows all around. It was 87.5 feet long and about 44 feet wide.{ag}
Its jambs{ah} faced the outer court; palm carvings were on its jambs on each side, and its stairway had eight steps.
There was a room with its doorway by the jambs of the gates;{ai} there they would wash the burnt offering.
In the porch of the gate, on each side, stood two tables, to be used for slaughtering the burnt offering, the sin offering and the guilt offering.
On the outer side, as one goes up to the entrance of the north gate, were two tables, and on the other side of the gate’s vestibule were two tables.
So there were four tables on one side and four on the other, beside the gate: eight tables on which they slaughtered.

There were also four tables of dressed stone for the burnt offering, 31.5 inches long, 31.5 inches wide, and 21 inches high.{aj} On them they would lay the implements used for slaughtering the burnt offering and the sacrifices.
Ledges{ak} 3 inches wide were fastened all around inside,{al} and on the tables was the flesh of the offerings.
Outside the inner gate, in the inner court, there were rooms for the singers.{am} One was beside the north gate and faced south; the other was beside the south{an} gate and faced north.
He said to me, “This room facing south is for the priests who keep charge of the temple,
and the room facing north is for the priests who keep charge of the altar. These are the sons of Zadok,{ao} who alone among Levi’s descendants may come near to Yahweh to minister to him.”
He measured the court: 175 feet long and 175 feet wide,{ap} a square. The altar stood in front of the temple.

Then he brought me to the temple’s vestibule and measured the jambs of the vestibule, 8.75 feet on each side. The width of the gateway was 24.5 feet, and its side walls were 5.25 feet{aq} on each side.{ar}
The vestibule was 35 feet wide{as} and 21 feet{at} deep.{au} It was reached by steps,{av} and there were pillars beside the jambs, one on each side.

verses.text: Then he brought me into the nave{a} and measured the jambs: 10.5 feet{b} wide on each side was the width of the jambs.{c}
The entrance was 17.5 feet wide, and the side walls of the entrance were 8.75 feet on each side. He measured the nave: 70 feet long and 35 feet wide.{d}
Then he went on inside and measured the jambs of the entrance, 3.5 feet; the entrance itself, 10.5 feet; and the width{e} of the entrance, about 12 feet.{f}
He measured its length, 35 feet, and its width, 35 feet,{g} facing the nave. And he said to me, “This is the most holy place.”
Then he measured the temple’s wall: 10.5 feet thick. The side rooms all around the temple were each 7 feet wide.{h}

The side rooms were in three stories, one above another, thirty in each story.{i} Offsets ran around the house’s wall, entering it to hold the rooms up, yet without the rooms being fastened into the house’s wall.

The side rooms grew wider as they rose, story by story, for the structure surrounding the temple went up by stages all around it. So the temple was broader toward the top, and one went up from the lowest story through the middle story to the highest.{j}
Looking, I saw a raised base encircling the house; the footings of the side rooms measured a full reed, 10.5 feet{k} to the joint.{l}
The outer wall of the side rooms was 8.75 feet thick.{m} The open area between the temple’s side rooms
and the priests’ rooms{n} was 35 feet wide all around the temple.{o}
The doors of the side rooms opened onto the free space, one door on the north and one on the south; and the free space was 8.75 feet wide all the way around.{p}
The building facing the temple yard{q} on the west side was about 123 feet wide, its wall was 8.75 feet thick all around, and it was about 158 feet long.{r}
Then he measured the temple: 175 feet long; and the yard and the building with its walls: 175 feet long.{s}
The width of the temple’s front, together with the yard on the east, was 175 feet.{t}

He measured the length of the building facing the yard at the rear, with its galleries{u} on either side: 175 feet.
¶The nave, the inner room,{v} and the vestibules of the court,

the thresholds, the narrow windows, and the galleries round the three of them opposite the threshold, had wood overlaying them on every side, from ground level as far as the windows (the windows were covered),{w}
to the space above the entrance, and on into the inner room and on the outside. On every wall all around, inside and out, were carvings in measured panels:{x}
cherubim alternating with palm trees, a palm standing between cherub and cherub. Every cherub had two faces:
a human face turned toward the palm tree on one side, and a young lion’s face turned to the palm on the far side. So it was carved over the entire house, round and round.
From ground level up over the entrance the cherubim and palms were carved, and on the nave’s wall.{y}
The nave had squared doorposts. Before the holy place stood what appeared to be
an altar of wood, 5.25 feet high and 3.5 feet{z} long.{aa} Its corners, its base,{ab} and its sides were of wood. He told me, “This is the table that stands before Yahweh.”
The nave and the holy place each had a double door.
Each door had two leaves, two swinging leaves, two for one door and two for the other.
Cherubim and palm trees were carved on the doors of the main hall, just as they were on the walls, and a wooden canopy{ac} stood over the front of the porch outside.
There were narrow windows and palm trees on both sides of the vestibule, on its side walls, and on the temple’s side rooms and canopies.

verses.text: Then he led me out into the outer court by the road going north and brought me to the rooms that lay opposite the restricted yard and opposite the building on the north.
Along its length of 175 feet was the north door,{a} and the width was 87.5 feet.{b}
Across from the 35-foot area{c} that belonged to the inner courtyard, and across from the paving that belonged to the outer courtyard, the galleries faced each other on three levels.
Before the rooms was a passage 17.5 feet wide on the inner side, a way of 21 inches;{d}{e} their doors faced north.
The uppermost rooms were cut short, since the galleries ate into them more than into the building’s lowest and middle rooms.
For they were in three stories and had no pillars like the courts’ pillars; so the upper rooms were set back from the ground more than the lower and the middle ones.
There was a wall outside, parallel to the rooms, toward the outer court, in front of the rooms; its length was 87.5 feet.{f}
For the rooms on the outer court’s side were 87.5 feet long, while those facing the nave were 175 feet.{g}
Below these rooms was the entrance{h} from the east, as one comes into them from the outer court.
In the thickness of the court’s wall on the east side,{i} facing the restricted yard and facing the building, there were rooms too,
with a passage before them. They looked like the rooms on the north, with the same length and width, and with all the same exits, arrangements, and doors.
Matching the doors of the rooms on the south side there was a door at the head of the passage, the way in front of the matching wall eastward, where one enters them.{j}

Then he told me, “The north rooms and the south rooms that face the restricted yard are the holy rooms, where the priests who draw near to Yahweh will eat the most holy offerings. There they will lay down the most holy offerings: the grain offering, the sin offering, and the guilt offering, for the place is holy.

Once the priests have gone in, they must not go out from the holy place into the outer court until they lay aside there the garments in which they minister, for these are holy. They must put on other clothes before they approach the area belonging to the people.”
When he had finished measuring the inner temple, he led me out by the gate facing east and measured the whole area round about.
With the measuring reed he measured the east side:{k} 5,250 feet by the measuring reed,{l} all around.
He measured the north side: 5,250 feet by the reed,{m} all around.
The south side he measured: 5,250 feet by the measuring reed.{n}
He turned to the west side and measured 5,250 feet by the measuring reed.{o}
On all four sides he measured it. It had a wall around it, 5,250 feet long and 5,250 feet wide,{p} to separate what is holy from what is common.

verses.text: Then he led me to the gate, the gate facing east.
And there was the glory of Israel’s God, coming from the east! Its sound was like the roar of many waters,{a} and the earth was lit up by his glory.
The vision was like the one I saw when I{b} came to destroy the city, and like the visions I saw beside the Kebar River; and I fell facedown.
Yahweh’s glory entered the temple by way of the gate that faced east.
Then the Spirit lifted me and brought me into the inner court, and there the glory of Yahweh had filled the temple!
I heard one addressing me out of the house, while the man was standing at my side.

He told me, “Son of man, here is my throne’s place, the spot where my feet rest, where I will make my home amid Israel’s people for all time. Never again will Israel’s house defile my holy name, neither they nor their kings, through their whoring and through their kings’ corpses{c} at their high places.{d}

They placed their doorsill next to my doorsill and their doorpost right beside my doorpost, with just a wall separating me from them. By the detestable things they did they made my holy name unclean, so I destroyed them in my anger.
Now let them put far from me their prostitution and the corpses of their kings,{e} and I will dwell among them forever.
“As for you, son of man, describe the temple to Israel’s house, so that they may be ashamed of their iniquities, and let them measure its plan.

If they are ashamed{f} of everything they have done, show them the temple’s plan and arrangement: its exits and entrances, all its forms, all its regulations and all its instructions. Write this down while they watch, so they can follow its complete plan and all its regulations and carry them out.
This is the law of the temple: on the mountaintop its whole territory all around will be most holy. Look, this is the law of the temple.

“These are the measurements of the altar in cubits (the cubit here is a cubit and a handbreadth{g}): its base{h} measures 21 inches in depth and 21 inches across, and the lip at its edge, all around, is 10.5 inches.{i} And this is the altar’s height:{j}
from the base on the ground up to the lower ledge, 3.5 feet, with a width of 21 inches; and from the smaller ledge to the larger ledge, 7 feet, with a width of 21 inches.{k}
The altar hearth{l} is 7 feet high,{m} and from the hearth four horns project upward.{n}
Four-square is the hearth: 21 feet in length, 21 feet in width,{o} on all four sides.
The ledge is also square, 24.5 feet long by 24.5 feet wide on its four sides, with a rim of 10.5 inches around it and a base of 21 inches all around.{p} Its steps face east.”
Then he said to me, “Son of man, this is what Lord Yahweh says: Here are the altar’s rules for the day it is made, for offering burnt offerings on it and for splashing blood on it.
You are to give to the Levitical priests of Zadok’s line, who come near to me to minister to me, declares Lord Yahweh, a young bull for a sin offering.
You will take some of its blood and put it on the four horns of the altar, on the four corners of the ledge, and on the rim all around; so you will purify it and make atonement for it.
You are then to take the bull for the sin offering and burn it at the designated place in the temple area, outside the holy place.
On the second day you will offer a male goat without defect{q} for a sin offering, and they will purify the altar as they purified it with the bull.
Once you have completed the cleansing, present an unblemished young bull and an unblemished ram from the flock.
You will present them before Yahweh, and the priests will throw salt on them and offer them as a burnt offering to Yahweh.
For seven days you will provide a goat each day as a sin offering; a young bull and a ram from the flock, both without defect, are also to be provided.
For seven days they are to make atonement for the altar and purify it; in this way they will dedicate it.{r}
When these days are over, from the eighth day onward the priests will offer your burnt offerings and your fellowship offerings on the altar, and I will accept you, declares Lord Yahweh.”

verses.text: Then he brought me back toward the sanctuary’s outer gate, the one facing east, and it was shut.
Yahweh told me, “This gate is to stay shut. It must not be opened, and no one may go in through it, because Yahweh, Israel’s God, has entered by it. So it must remain shut.
Only the prince{a} may sit in it, as prince, to eat bread before Yahweh. By the gate’s vestibule he will come in, and by the same way he will go out.”
Next he led me through the north gate to the house’s front. As I looked, there was Yahweh’s glory filling Yahweh’s house! I fell on my face.

Yahweh said to me, “Son of man, set your mind on this; look with your eyes and listen with your ears to all I am telling you about every statute of Yahweh’s house and all its laws. Take careful note of who may enter the house and of all who must be kept out of the sanctuary.{b}
Say to the rebellious ones,{c} to Israel’s house, ‘This is what Lord Yahweh says: Enough of all your detestable practices, house of Israel!

You brought in outsiders, people uncircumcised in heart and in body, to occupy my sanctuary and make my house unclean, while you presented my food—the fat and the blood. And they{d} violated my covenant, in addition to all your detestable practices.
You did not keep charge of my holy things yourselves, but you set them{e} as keepers of my charge in my sanctuary for yourselves.
This is what Lord Yahweh says: No foreigner uncircumcised in heart and flesh may enter my sanctuary, not one of the foreigners living among the Israelites.
“‘As for the Levites who went far from me when Israel strayed, who wandered from me after their idols,{f} they will bear their guilt.

They will be servants in my sanctuary, overseeing the gates of the house and serving the house. They will slaughter the burnt offering and the sacrifice for the people, and they will stand before the people to serve them.

Because they served them before their idols and became a stumbling block of guilt for Israel’s house, I have raised my hand in an oath against them, declares Lord Yahweh, that they will bear their guilt.
They must not come near me to serve me as priests, nor approach anything of mine that is holy, nor the most holy things. Their shame they must carry, and the detestable acts they committed.{g}
I will make them caretakers of the house’s duties, for all its work and all that is to be done in it.

“‘But the Levitical priests, the sons of Zadok, who kept charge of my sanctuary when the Israelites strayed from me, will come near me to serve me. They will stand before me to offer me fat and blood, declares Lord Yahweh.
They will enter my sanctuary, and they will come near my table to serve me and keep my charge.
When they come through the gates of the inner courtyard, they are to put on linen clothing. They must wear nothing made of wool while they are on duty at those gates or inside the courtyard.
Linen turbans will be on their heads and linen undergarments on their waists. They must not bind on anything that causes sweat.{h}

When they go out into the outer courtyard where the people are,{i} they must take off the clothing they served in, store it in the sacred chambers, and put on different clothing, so that they will not transmit holiness to the people by their clothing.
They must not shave their heads or let their hair grow long; they must keep their hair trimmed.
Wine is not for any priest to drink on entering the inner court.
They must not marry a widow or a divorced woman, but only virgins from the descendants of Israel’s house, or a widow who is a priest’s widow.{j}
They will teach my people the difference between holy and common, and show them how to tell unclean from clean.
In a dispute,{k} they will stand to judge, and they will judge it by my judgments. They will keep my laws and my statutes at all my appointed feasts, and they will keep my Sabbaths holy.
A priest must not go near a dead person and so become unclean. For a father or mother, son or daughter, brother or unmarried sister, however, they may make themselves unclean.
After he is cleansed, seven days are to be counted for him.{l}
On the day he enters the sanctuary, into the inner courtyard, to serve in the holy place, he is to present his own sin offering, declares Lord Yahweh.
“‘This will be their inheritance:{m} I am their inheritance. Grant them no holding in Israel; their holding is me.
They will eat the grain offering, the sin offering, and the guilt offering, and everything devoted{n} in Israel will be theirs.

The priests will have the best of all the firstfruits of everything, and of each gift you set apart, whatever it is. The first of your dough{o} you are to hand to the priest, and blessing will come to rest upon your household.
No carcass, nothing mauled, whether bird or beast, may the priests eat.

verses.text: “When you allot the land as an inheritance, you are to set apart a contribution for Yahweh, a holy portion of the land, about 8.3 miles long and about 3.3 miles{a} wide.{b} It will be holy throughout its whole area.{c}
Of this, a square plot 875 feet by 875 feet will belong to the sanctuary, with 87.5 feet of open land around it.{d}
From this measured area you are to measure off a strip about 8.3 miles long and about 3.3 miles wide;{e} in it will stand the sanctuary, the most holy place.

It is a holy portion of the land, and it will belong to the priests who minister in the sanctuary, who come near to serve Yahweh. It will be a place for their houses and a holy place for the sanctuary.
A strip about 8.3 miles long and about 3.3 miles wide will belong to the Levites who serve the house,{f} as their possession for towns to live in.{g}
“Alongside the holy contribution you are to assign as the city’s property an area about 1.7 miles wide and about 8.3 miles long.{h} It will belong to the whole house of Israel.

“The prince will have land on both sides of the holy contribution and the city’s property, bordering the holy contribution and the city’s property, on the west side westward and on the east side eastward, matching one of the tribal portions in length from the western border to the eastern border.
This land will be his possession in Israel. My princes will no longer oppress my people, but they will let Israel’s house have the land according to their tribes.
“This is what Lord Yahweh says: Enough, you princes of Israel! Put away violence and plunder, and do what is just and right. Stop evicting my people, declares Lord Yahweh.
Let your balances be true, your dry measure true, and your liquid measure true.{i}
The dry measure and the liquid measure are to be the same: the liquid measure is to hold a tenth of a homer, and the dry measure a tenth of a homer. Its standard will be set by the homer.{j}
The shekel is to be twenty gerahs, about 0.4 ounce. Twenty shekels, twenty-five shekels, and fifteen shekels are to make your mina, about 1.5 pounds.{k}
“This is the contribution you are to set apart: one-sixtieth of your wheat and one-sixtieth of your barley.{l}
The fixed share of oil is one-hundredth of your oil.{m}

And one sheep from every flock of two hundred from Israel’s well-watered pastures.{n} All this serves for grain offering, for burnt offering, and for fellowship sacrifices, to atone for them, declares Lord Yahweh.
The land’s whole population is to share in giving this gift to Israel’s prince.

On the prince will fall the duty of burnt offering, grain offering, and drink offering at festivals, at new moons, on Sabbaths, at all the appointed feasts of Israel’s house. He is to provide the sin offering, the grain offering, the burnt offering, and the fellowship offerings to make atonement for Israel’s house.
“Lord Yahweh says this: In the first month, on the first day of the month (in March–April),{o} take an unblemished young bull and cleanse the sanctuary.
The priest will take some of the blood of the sin offering and put it on the temple’s doorposts, on the four corners of the altar’s ledge, and on the posts of the gate of the inner court.
Repeat this on the month’s seventh day{p} on behalf of whoever errs without intent or is simple; thus you will make atonement for the temple.
“On the fourteenth day of the first month (in March–April){q} you will celebrate the Passover, a feast of seven days,{r} when bread made without yeast is to be eaten.
On that day the prince is to provide for himself and for all the people of the land a bull for a sin offering.
During the seven days of the feast he is to provide as a burnt offering to Yahweh seven bulls and seven rams without defect each day for the seven days, and a male goat each day as a sin offering.
As a grain offering he is to provide about 3/5 bushel of flour for each bull and the same for each ram, with about a gallon of oil for each measure of flour.{s}

“On the fifteenth day of the seventh month (in September–October),{t} at the feast, he is to provide likewise through seven days, matching the sin offering, the burnt offering, the grain offering, and the oil.

notes.text: Hebrew: “25,000” (about 13.1 km); “10,000” (about 5.3 km); the unit is not stated but is probably the long cubit.
So the Hebrew; the Greek has “twenty thousand.” Many interpreters follow the Greek, since vv. 3 and 5 give the priests and the Levites ten thousand each.

For the land allotments in 45:1–8 and 48:8–35, Ezekiel gives the numbers without naming the unit. Some take the unit to be the reed (as in 42:16–20 and in the Greek of 45:1–2), which would make the figures six times larger. See the note at 40:5.

Hebrew: “25,000” (about 13.1 km); “10,000” (about 5.3 km); the unit is not stated but is probably the long cubit.
Hebrew: “25,000” (about 13.1 km); “10,000” (about 5.3 km); the unit is not stated but is probably the long cubit.
So the Greek; the Hebrew has “as their possession, twenty rooms.” The difference is a matter of a few letters.
Hebrew: “5,000” (about 2.6 km); “25,000” (about 13.1 km); the unit is not stated but is probably the long cubit.
Hebrew “an honest ephah and an honest bath.” The ephah was a dry measure, and the bath a liquid measure of the same size, about 3/5 bushel or 6 gallons (22 liters). Ancient standards varied.

Hebrew “The ephah and the bath are to be one measure, so that the bath holds a tenth of a homer and the ephah a tenth of a homer; its measure is to be according to the homer.” A homer was about 6 bushels (220 liters).

A shekel was about 0.4 ounce (11.5 grams), and a gerah one-twentieth of a shekel; the mina here is sixty shekels, about 1.5 pounds (690 grams). The Greek has “your mina is to be five shekels, fifteen shekels, and fifty shekels.” Ancient standards varied.
Hebrew “a sixth of an ephah from a homer of wheat, and a sixth of an ephah from a homer of barley.”
Hebrew “a tenth of a bath from the kor; ten baths are a homer, for ten baths are a homer.” A kor was the same as a homer, about 6 bushels (220 liters).
So the Hebrew; the Greek has “one sheep from the flock out of ten, as an offering from all the tribes of Israel.”
The Hebrew has “in the first (month), on the first of the month.” The first month is Nisan in the spring-start calendar; this would fall in March–April.
So the Hebrew; the Greek has “in the seventh month, on the first day of the month” (September–October).
The Hebrew has “in the first (month), on the fourteenth day of the month,” Nisan in the spring-start calendar.
So the Greek; the Hebrew has “a feast of weeks of days,” perhaps a copying slip for “seven days.”
Hebrew “an ephah for the bull and an ephah for the ram, and a hin of oil for the ephah.” An ephah was about 3/5 bushel (22 liters), and a hin about 1 gallon (3.7 liters).
The Hebrew has “in the seventh (month), on the fifteenth day of the month,” Tishri in the spring-start calendar. This is the Feast of Booths (Leviticus 23:34).

verses.text: “This is what Lord Yahweh says: The inner court’s east-facing gate is to stay shut on the six working days, but on the Sabbath day it is to be opened, and on the day of the new moon it is to be opened.

The prince will come in from outside by way of the gate’s vestibule and take his stand at the gate’s doorpost. The priests will present his burnt offering and his fellowship offerings, and he will bow in worship on the gate’s threshold and then go out; but the gate is not to be shut until evening.
The people of the land will likewise bow in worship before Yahweh at that gate’s entrance on Sabbaths and new moons.
The burnt offering the prince brings to Yahweh on the Sabbath day is to be six lambs without defect and a ram without defect.
The grain offering is to be about 3/5 bushel of flour with the ram, and with the lambs whatever he is willing to give, with about a gallon of oil for each 3/5 bushel.{a}
On the new moon it is to be a young bull without defect, and six lambs and a ram, all without defect.
With the bull he is to provide a grain offering of about 3/5 bushel, with the ram the same, and with the lambs as much as he can afford, with about a gallon of oil for each 3/5 bushel.{b}
Whenever the prince comes in, his route is through the vestibule of the gate, and by that route he departs.

“When the people of the land come before Yahweh at the appointed feasts, whoever enters by the north gate to worship must leave by the south gate, and whoever enters by the south gate must leave by the north gate. No one is to go back through the gate he came in by; each must go straight out ahead.{c}
As for the prince, he will be in their midst: in with them as they enter, out with them as they leave.{d}

At the festivals and the appointed feasts the grain offering is to be about 3/5 bushel with a bull and the same with a ram, and with the lambs whatever he is willing to give, with about a gallon of oil for each 3/5 bushel.

“When the prince provides a freewill offering for Yahweh, be it burnt offering or fellowship sacrifices, someone must open for him the east-facing gate, and he will present his burnt offering and fellowship offerings as he does on the Sabbath day. Then he will go out, and after he has gone out the gate is to be shut.
“You{e} are to provide a year-old lamb without defect each day as a burnt offering to Yahweh; morning by morning you are to provide it.

With it you are to provide a grain offering morning by morning: about a gallon of flour, with about 1.25 quarts of oil to moisten the fine flour.{f} This is a grain offering to Yahweh, a lasting statute for all time.
So they{g} are to provide the lamb, the grain offering, and the oil morning by morning as a regular burnt offering.
“Lord Yahweh says this: Suppose the prince makes a gift from his own inheritance{h} to one of his sons; it will belong to his sons, and it will be their possession by inheritance.

But if he gives a gift from his inheritance to one of his servants, it will be the servant’s until the year of release;{i} then it will go back to the prince. His inheritance is for his sons alone; it will remain theirs.

The prince must not take any of the people’s inheritance, driving them off their property. From his own property he is to give his sons their inheritance, so that none of my people will be scattered from their property.”
Then he brought me through the entrance at the side of the gate to the holy rooms facing north, which belonged to the priests. There I saw a place at the far western end.{j}

He told me, “Here the priests will boil the guilt offering and the sin offering, and here they will bake the grain offering, so that nothing has to be carried out into the outer courtyard, where it would transmit holiness to the people.”
Next he took me out into the outer court and walked me around to its four corners, and in each corner of the court there was a smaller court.
In the four corners of the court were enclosed{k} courts, 70 feet long and 52.5 feet wide;{l} all four corner courts{m} were the same size.
A row of stonework ran around each of the four, and hearths for cooking were made under the rows all around.
He said to me, “These are the kitchens where those who serve the temple will boil the people’s sacrifices.”
