One might even say that Levi, who receives tithes, paid tithes through Abraham,
for he was still in the body of his ancestor when Melchizedek met him.{d}

If, then, the Levitical priesthood could have brought about perfection, for it was in connection with it that the people were given the law, why was there still need for a different priest to arise in the line of Melchizedek, and not one designated in the line of Aaron?
For when the priesthood is changed, a change of law necessarily follows as well.
The one these things are spoken of belonged to another tribe, from which no one has ever served at the altar.
For it is evident that our Lord arose from Judah, and Moses said nothing about priests in connection with that tribe.{e}
And this becomes still more evident when another priest arises who resembles Melchizedek,
one who has become priest, not by virtue of a rule about bodily descent, but by virtue of the power of a life that cannot be destroyed.{f}

For the testimony is,
“A priest you are forever,
in the line of Melchizedek.”
On the one side, a previous commandment is canceled because it was feeble and ineffective,
for the law brought nothing to completion. In its place a better hope is brought in, and by it we come near to God.
And it did not happen without an oath. Others became priests without an oath,

but this one became priest on oath, when God declared to him,
“The Lord has taken an oath
and will not go back on it:
‘A priest you are forever.’ ”{g}
To that same degree Jesus has become the guarantee of a better covenant.
Furthermore, the former priests were many in number, because death prevented them from continuing in office;
He, however, because he lives on forever, holds a priesthood that does not pass to another.
That is why he can save for all time those who come to God by him; he is always alive to plead on their behalf.{h}
It was fitting that we should have such a high priest: holy, innocent, undefiled, separated from sinners, and exalted above the heavens.
He has no need, as those high priests do, to offer sacrifices day after day, first for his own sins and then for those of the people; for he did this once for all when he offered up himself.
For the law appoints as high priests men who are subject to weakness, but the word of the oath, which came after the law, appoints a Son who has been made perfect forever.

notes.text: *Salem*: Hebrew, “peace”; usually identified with Jerusalem (Ps 76:2). *God Most High*: Hebrew *El Elyon*. See Gen 14:17–20.
Without father … genealogy: Genesis records no parents, ancestry, birth or death for him.
*Levi*: Hebrew, explained in Gen 29:34 as “attached.” *Descended from*: literally “have come out of the loins of.”
In the body of his ancestor: literally “in the loins of his father.”
*Judah*: Hebrew, explained in Gen 29:35 as “praise.” *Arose*: the Greek verb is used of the rising of a star or the springing up of a plant; compare Isa 11:1; Jer 23:5.
A rule about bodily descent: literally “a law of a fleshly commandment.”
Ps 110:4. *The Lord*: the Hebrew text has *Yahweh*. *Forever*: later manuscripts add “in the order of Melchizedek.”
For all time: or “completely.”

verses.text: The chief point of what we are saying is this: we have a high priest of this kind, who sat down at the right hand of the throne of the Majesty in heaven,
a minister in the sanctuary and in the true tent, which the Lord set up, not any human being.{a}
For every high priest is appointed to offer gifts and sacrifices, so it is necessary for this one too to have something to offer.
Now if he were on earth, he would not be a priest at all, since there are already priests who offer the gifts according to the law.

They minister in a sketch and shadow of what is in heaven, just as Moses was cautioned when he was about to build the tent: “Be sure to make everything after the model you were shown on the mountain.”{b}
As it is, however, the ministry Christ has received is far more excellent, to the same degree that the covenant of which he is mediator is better, resting as it does on better promises.
If that first covenant had been flawless, a second would never have been sought.

For he faults them when he says,
“Behold, days are coming, declares the Lord,
when I will make a new covenant
with Israel’s house and Judah’s house.{c}

For this is the covenant I will make with the house of Israel
when those days are over, says the Lord:
I will place my laws in their understanding,
and inscribe them upon their hearts;
I will be God to them,
and they will be a people to me.

No longer will each one teach his fellow townsman,
or each one his brother, saying, ‘Know the Lord.’
For all of them will know me,
from the smallest to the greatest.{e}

For I will be merciful toward their wrongdoings,
and I will remember their sins no more.”{f}
When he says “new,” he has made the first covenant old; and what is growing old and aging will soon disappear.

notes.text: The sanctuary: literally “the holy things” or “the holy places.” *Tent*: or “tabernacle,” the portable sanctuary of Israel in the wilderness; compare Num 24:6 in the Greek Old Testament.
Exod 25:40.
Jer 31:31–34 (38:31–34 in the Greek Old Testament). *The Lord*: the Hebrew text has *Yahweh*; so also in verses 9–10. *Israel*: Hebrew, explained in Gen 32:28 as “he struggles with God.”
I too disregarded them: so the Greek Old Testament; the Hebrew reads “though I was a husband to them.”
Know the Lord: the Hebrew text has *Yahweh*.
Their sins: later manuscripts add “and their lawless deeds,” as in 10:17.

verses.text: The first covenant, for its part, had rules for worship and a sanctuary belonging to this world.{a}
A tent was set up, the outer section, which held the lampstand, the table, and the loaves set out before God; this is called the Holy Place.{b}
Behind the second curtain was the room called the Most Holy Place,{c}

It contained the golden incense altar and the covenant chest, plated all over with gold. Inside the chest were the golden jar of manna, Aaron’s rod that had budded, and the stone tablets of the covenant.{d}
and over it the cherubim of the Glory cast their shadow over the mercy seat. We cannot speak about these things one by one at present.{e}
With these things arranged in this way, the priests go regularly into the first room in performing their duties,
Into the second room, however, the high priest alone goes, only once a year, and always with blood, which he brings as an offering for himself and for the sins of the people done in ignorance.{f}
The Holy Spirit is making it plain by this that the way into the sanctuary has not yet been opened as long as the first tent still has its standing.
This is a figure pointing to the present time. Under it gifts and sacrifices are brought that have no power to make the worshiper perfect in conscience,{g}
dealing only with foods and drinks and different kinds of washing. These are outward rules for the body, in force until the time comes to set things straight.
But when Christ appeared as a high priest of the good things that have now come, then through the greater and more perfect tent, not made with hands, that is, not of this creation,{h}
he entered the sanctuary once and for all, not with the blood of goats and calves but with his own blood, and secured an everlasting redemption.
For if the blood of goats and bulls and the sprinkled ashes of a heifer sanctify those who are defiled, so that their flesh is made clean,{i}
how much more will the blood of Christ, who through the eternal Spirit presented himself to God without fault, cleanse our consciences of dead works so that we may serve the living God!{j}

For this reason he mediates a new covenant, so that the called may receive the promised everlasting inheritance, now that a death has occurred to redeem them from the offenses committed under the first covenant.
In the case of a will, it is necessary to establish that the one who made it has died.{k}
A will is valid only once someone has died; it has no force as long as the one who made it is still living.
That is why not even the first covenant was put into effect without blood.

For when every command of the law had been spoken by Moses to all the people, he took the blood of calves and goats, with water and scarlet wool and hyssop, and sprinkled both the book itself and all the people,{l}
saying, “This is the blood of the covenant that God has commanded for you.”{m}
Likewise he sprinkled blood on the tent and on every vessel used in the ministry.
In fact, under the law nearly everything is made clean with blood, and apart from the pouring out of blood there is no forgiveness.
It was necessary, then, for the copies of the things in heaven to be cleansed by such means, but the heavenly things themselves needed better sacrifices than these.
For Christ did not enter a sanctuary built by human hands, a mere image of the true one, but heaven itself, now to stand before God for our sake.
Nor was it to offer himself many times over, as the high priest goes into the holy place each year with blood that is not his own;
if that were so, he would have needed to suffer many times since the world was founded. Instead he has been revealed once, at the end of the ages, to do away with sin by sacrificing himself.
And just as it is appointed for human beings to die once, and after that comes judgment,
so also Christ, having been offered once to bear the sins of many, will appear a second time, not to deal with sin, but to bring salvation to those who are eagerly waiting for him.{n}

notes.text: For its part: Westcott and Hort bracket the word “also” (or “even”) here. *A sanctuary belonging to this world*: or “an earthly sanctuary.”
The bread of the presence: literally “the setting out of the loaves” (Exod 25:30; Lev 24:5–9).
The Most Holy Place: literally “the holy of holies.”

Altar of incense: or “censer”; the Greek *thymiatērion* can mean either. In Exodus the incense altar stood in front of the curtain (Exod 30:6). *Manna*: Hebrew, explained in Exod 16:15, 31 from the question “What is it?” See Exod 16:33; Num 17:8–10; Deut 10:1–5.
Cherubim: Hebrew plural of *cherub*, winged heavenly beings. *Mercy seat*: Greek *hilastērion*, the gold lid of the ark, “place of atonement” (Exod 25:17–22).
Once a year: on the Day of Atonement (Lev 16), in the seventh month (September–October), on its tenth day.
Figure: Greek *parabolē*, “parable,” “figure.”
That have now come: so the Westcott–Hort text, with P46 and Vaticanus as reported; many manuscripts read “that are to come.”
Ashes of a heifer: see Num 19:1–10, 17–19.
Our conscience: so the Westcott–Hort text; many manuscripts read “your conscience.” *The eternal Spirit*: or “an eternal spirit.”
Will: the Greek *diathēkē* means both “covenant” and “will” (“testament”), and the writer plays on both senses in verses 15–18.
Hyssop: a small aromatic plant used for sprinkling. Compare Exod 24:3–8. *Calves and goats*: some manuscripts read only “calves.”
Exod 24:8.
To bear the sins of many: echoing Isa 53:12.

verses.text: The law holds only a shadow of the good things that were to come, not the very form of those realities. So by the same sacrifices, offered without end year by year, it can never make perfect those who come forward to worship.{a}
If they could, would the offering of them not have come to an end, since those who worship, once made clean, would have no further awareness of sins?
Instead, these sacrifices bring sins to mind again every year,
since the blood of bulls and goats cannot possibly take sins away.

in offerings burned whole and in offerings for sin
you found no pleasure.
First he says, “Sacrifices and offerings, whole burnt offerings and sin offerings you did not want and took no pleasure in,” though these are offered according to the law.
Then he adds, “Here I am; I have come to do your will.” He sets aside the first in order to establish the second.
By that will we have been made holy, through the sacrifice of Jesus Christ’s body, offered one time for all.
Every priest, moreover, stands daily performing his ministry, presenting over and over the identical sacrifices, which are never able to remove sins.{c}
But this one, having offered for all time a single sacrifice for sins, sat down at God’s right hand,{d}
and from then on he waits until his enemies are made a footstool for his feet.{e}
For by a single offering he has made perfect for all time those who are being made holy.
And the Holy Spirit testifies to us as well. For after he has said,

“This is the covenant I will make with them
when those days are over, says the Lord:
I will place my laws on their hearts,
and inscribe them upon their minds,”{f}

he goes on,
“Their sins and their lawless acts
I will call to mind no more.”
Where these have been forgiven, there is no longer any offering for sin.
So then, brothers, since by Jesus’ blood we have boldness to go into the holy place,
by a way newly made and living, which he has opened up for us through the curtain, which is his flesh,
and since we have a great priest over the house of God,
let us come near with a true heart, in the full assurance that faith gives, our hearts sprinkled clean from an evil conscience and our bodies washed with pure water.
Let us keep hold of the hope we confess without wavering, for the one who gave the promise can be trusted.
And let us take thought for one another, how to stir each other up to love and good works,
not giving up meeting together, as is the custom of some, but urging each other on, and doing so the more as you see the Day drawing near.{g}
If we keep on sinning willfully once we have come to know the truth, no sacrifice for sins remains any longer,
but only a terrifying expectation of judgment, and a raging fire that will consume the adversaries.{h}
Whoever rejected the law of Moses was put to death without pity, when two or three witnesses gave evidence.{i}
Imagine how much worse a punishment is deserved by someone who has trampled on the Son of God, treated as common the covenant blood that made him holy, and insulted the Spirit of grace.{j}
We know who it is that said, “Retribution belongs to me; I will pay back,” and again, “The Lord will judge his people.”{k}
It is a fearful thing to fall into the hands of the living God.
Remember the earlier days, when after being enlightened you endured a great struggle of suffering.
At times you were publicly exposed to insults and afflictions; at other times you stood alongside those who were treated in that way.
For you shared the sufferings of the prisoners, and you accepted with joy the seizure of your possessions, knowing that you yourselves had a better possession, and a lasting one.{l}
So do not throw away your confidence, which carries a great reward.
For you need to persevere, so that, having done what God wills, you may receive the promise.
We, however, are not people who draw back to their ruin, but people of faith who hold on to their souls.{o}

notes.text: The very form: literally “the image itself.”
Ps 40:6–8 in the Greek Old Testament. *A body you have made ready for me*: so the Greek Old Testament; the Hebrew reads “ears you have dug for me,” that is, “you have opened my ears.”
Every priest: some manuscripts read “every high priest.”
For all time: or, taken with what follows, “sat down for all time.”
Jer 31:33–34. *The Lord*: the Hebrew text has *Yahweh*.
The Day: the day of the Lord’s coming and judgment.
Raging fire: literally “zeal of fire”; compare Isa 26:11.
Compare Deut 17:6.
Counted as unclean: or “treated as common.” Compare Exod 24:8.
Deut 32:35–36. *The Lord*: the Hebrew text has *Yahweh*. *I will repay*: later manuscripts add “says the Lord.”
The prisoners: so the Westcott–Hort text, with Alexandrinus as reported; later manuscripts read “my chains.” *You yourselves had*: later manuscripts add “in heaven.”
In just a little while: literally “a little, how very little,” from Isa 26:20. The rest of verses 37–38 is from Hab 2:3–4 in the Greek Old Testament.
My righteous one: Westcott and Hort bracket “my”; some manuscripts place it after “faith” (“will live by my faith”), and later manuscripts omit it.
Hold on to their souls: or “gain their lives.”

verses.text: Faith is the assurance of things hoped for, the proof of things not seen.{a}
For it was for this that the elders of long ago were commended.{b}
By faith we grasp that the universe was formed by God’s word, so that the visible was not made from what is seen.{c}
By faith Abel presented to God a better sacrifice than Cain did. Through it he was declared righteous, with God commending his offerings; and through faith he still speaks, though he died.{d}
By faith Enoch was transferred so that he would not experience death, and “he could not be found, because God had transferred him.” For before the transfer he was commended as having pleased God.{e}
And without faith it is impossible to please him, for whoever draws near to God must believe that he exists and that he rewards those who seek him.

By faith Noah, when he had been divinely warned about things as yet unseen, reverently prepared an ark for the rescue of his family. Through his faith he passed sentence on the world, and he became heir to the righteousness that accords with faith.{f}
By faith Abraham obeyed when he was called to go out to a place he was going to receive as an inheritance, and he went out without knowing where he was going.
By faith he lived as a foreigner in the land of promise, as in a land not his own, living in tents with Isaac and Jacob, fellow heirs of the same promise.{g}
He was awaiting the city with firm foundations, whose architect and maker is God.
By faith Sarah herself, too, received power to conceive offspring, even beyond the age for it, since she judged the one who had promised to be faithful.{h}
And so from one man, and he as good as dead, there came descendants as many as the stars of heaven and as countless as the grains of sand on the seashore.{i}
These all died in faith without having received the promises, but they saw them and greeted them from afar, and they confessed that they were strangers and exiles on the earth.{j}
Those who talk like this show plainly that they are searching for a homeland.
If they had been thinking of the land they had left behind, they would have had opportunity to return.
But as it is, they long for a better country, a heavenly one. That is why God is not ashamed to be called their God, for he has prepared a city for them.
By faith Abraham, when tested, offered Isaac as a sacrifice. The man who had welcomed the promises was offering up his one and only son,{k}
the one of whom it had been said, “Through Isaac your descendants will be named.”{l}
He reckoned that God was able even to raise people from the dead; and figuratively speaking, he did receive Isaac back from the dead.{m}
By faith Isaac blessed Jacob and Esau with regard to things still to come.{n}
By faith Jacob, as he lay dying, blessed each of Joseph’s sons, and leaning on the top of his staff he worshiped.{o}
By faith Joseph, as his end drew near, spoke of the exodus of the Israelites and gave instructions about his bones.{p}
By faith, when Moses was born, his parents kept him hidden three months, for they saw what a fine child he was, and they did not fear the decree of the king.{q}
By faith Moses, when he had grown up, refused to be called the son of Pharaoh’s daughter,{r}
choosing rather to share ill-treatment with the people of God than to enjoy the passing pleasures of sin.
He considered the reproach of the Christ greater wealth than the treasures of Egypt, for he was looking ahead to the reward.{s}
By faith he left Egypt, not fearing the king’s anger, for he persevered as one who sees him who is invisible.
By faith he kept the Passover and the sprinkling of the blood, so that the destroyer of the firstborn would not touch them.{t}
By faith they passed through the Red Sea as though on dry land, but when the Egyptians tried to do the same, they drowned.{u}
By faith Jericho’s walls collapsed after the people had marched around them for seven days.{v}
By faith Rahab the prostitute did not die with the disobedient, because she had given the spies a peaceful welcome.{w}
And what more shall I say? For time would fail me to tell of Gideon, Barak, Samson and Jephthah, of David and Samuel and the prophets,{x}
Through faith they overcame kingdoms, carried out justice, gained what was promised, closed the jaws of lions,
put out raging fire, got away from the sword’s edge, found strength in weakness, grew powerful in battle, routed the armies of foreigners.
Women had their dead given back to them, raised to life. Others were tortured to death, turning down release so as to gain a better resurrection.{y}
Others again had to face jeers and whips, as well as chains and prison.
Some were stoned; some were tested; some were sawn apart; some died by the sword. They roamed about clothed in the skins of sheep and goats, in need, in distress, ill-treated,{z}
the world did not deserve them; they roamed through deserts, mountains, caves, and holes in the ground.
Yet none of these, though they won approval through their faith, received the promise,
because God had in view something better for us, that they should not be brought to perfection without us.

notes.text: Assurance: Greek *hypostasis*, “substance,” “firm ground,” “title deed”; compare 1:3; 3:14. *Proof*: or “conviction.”
Commended: literally “testified to,” that is, by God; so also in verses 4–5, 39.
The ages: or “the universe”; compare 1:2.
*Abel*: Hebrew *Hevel*, “breath,” “vapor.” *Cain*: Hebrew *Qayin*, explained in Gen 4:1 by the word for “acquired.” See Gen 4:3–10.
*Enoch*: Hebrew *Hanokh*, perhaps “dedicated.” Gen 5:24 in the Greek Old Testament.
*Noah*: Hebrew *Noach*, related in Gen 5:29 to a word for “comfort” or “rest.” *Took heed*: or “in reverent fear.”
*Isaac*: Hebrew *Yitschaq*, “he laughs” (Gen 17:17–19; 21:6). *Jacob*: Hebrew *Yaʿaqov*, explained in Gen 25:26; 27:36 as “heel-grabber,” “supplanter.”

*Sarah*: Hebrew, “princess” (Gen 17:15). *Sarah herself … received power to conceive*: or, as many interpreters read the Greek, “by faith he (Abraham), together with Sarah herself, received power to beget offspring.” Some manuscripts add that Sarah was barren; later manuscripts add “gave birth.”
Compare Gen 22:17; 32:12.
Strangers and exiles: compare Gen 23:4; 1 Chr 29:15; Ps 39:12.
Only son: Greek *monogenēs*, “one and only.” See Gen 22:1–14.
Gen 21:12. *Descendants*: literally “seed.”
Figuratively speaking: literally “in a parable.”
*Esau*: Hebrew, perhaps “hairy” (Gen 25:25). See Gen 27:27–40.

*Joseph*: Hebrew *Yosef*, explained in Gen 30:23–24 as “may he add.” *Leaning on the top of his staff*: Gen 47:31 in the Greek Old Testament; the Hebrew vowels as traditionally read give “at the head of his bed.” See also Gen 48:8–20.
See Gen 50:24–25; Exod 13:19. *The Israelites*: literally “the sons of Israel.”

What a fine child: literally “that the child was beautiful” or “well pleasing”; compare Exod 2:2; Acts 7:20. *Edict*: compare Exod 1:22. Some later manuscripts add here a sentence about Moses killing the Egyptian.
Pharaoh: Egyptian, “great house,” the title of the king of Egypt.
The reproach of the Christ: or “the reproach of the Anointed One”; compare Ps 89:50–51.
Passover: Greek *pascha*, from Hebrew *pesach* (Exod 12:11–13, 21–23).
Red Sea: so the Greek Old Testament; the Hebrew has *Yam Suph*, “Sea of Reeds” (Exod 14:21–29).
*Jericho*: Hebrew, perhaps related to the word for “moon” or “fragrance.” See Josh 6:12–21.
*Rahab*: Hebrew, “broad,” “wide.” See Josh 2:1–21; 6:22–25.

*Gideon*: Hebrew, “hewer.” *Barak*: Hebrew, “lightning.” *Samson*: Hebrew *Shimshon*, from the word for “sun.” *Jephthah*: Hebrew *Yiftach*, “he opens.” *Samuel*: Hebrew *Shemuel*, explained in 1 Sam 1:20 by the words “asked of God,” more probably “name of God.”
Compare 1 Kgs 17:17–24; 2 Kgs 4:18–37. *Tortured*: probably on the rack or drum; compare 2 Macc 6:18–7:42.

Some were tested: Greek *epeirasthēsan*. Some manuscripts omit it, and some scholars suspect an early copying error for *eprēsthēsan*, “they were burned.” *Sawn in two*: a Jewish tradition tells of Isaiah being sawn in two.

verses.text: With so vast a cloud of witnesses around us, then, let us too throw off every burden and the sin that entangles so easily, and let us run with perseverance the course laid out for us,{a}

keeping our gaze on Jesus, who leads the way in faith and brings it to completion. For the sake of the joy that lay ahead of him he bore the cross, scorning the shame, and he is seated at the right of God’s throne.{b}
Consider him who endured such hostility from sinners against themselves, so that you do not grow weary and lose heart.{c}
You have not yet, in your contest with sin, stood firm to the point of bloodshed.

because the Lord disciplines those he loves,
and chastises every child he accepts.”{e}
Endure it as discipline. God is dealing with you as his children. For what child is not disciplined by a father?
If you are without the discipline that all have received, you are not true sons but illegitimate.
Again, we had human fathers who corrected us, and we treated them with respect. Should we not be far more ready to submit to the Father of spirits, and so live?{f}
Our fathers corrected us for a brief time as they judged fit, but God does it for our benefit, that we may have a share in his holiness.
No discipline, while it lasts, seems a matter for joy; it is painful. Afterward, though, those who have been schooled by it reap from it a harvest of righteousness and peace.
So strengthen the hands that hang limp and the knees that give way,{g}
and make level tracks for your feet, so that the limb that is lame may not be dislocated, but may instead be healed.{h}
Strive for peace with all people, and for holiness, for apart from holiness none will see the Lord.
Watch that no one falls short of God’s grace, and that no “bitter root sprouts up to cause trouble,” poisoning many through it;{i}
that no one is sexually immoral or godless like Esau, who sold his birthright for a single meal.{j}
You know that later on, when he wished to receive the blessing as heir, he was turned away; he found no room for a change of mind, though he sought the blessing with tears.{k}
You have not come to what can be touched by the hand, to fire that burns, to darkness, deep gloom and storm,{l}
and a trumpet blast and a voice speaking words, so that the listeners pleaded that nothing more be said to them.
They could not endure the order that was given: “Even an animal that touches the mountain must be stoned.”{m}
Indeed, so terrifying was the sight that Moses said, “I am terrified and trembling.”{n}
But you have come to Mount Zion and to the city of the living God, the heavenly Jerusalem, and to myriads of angels in festal gathering,{o}
and to the assembly of the firstborn who are enrolled in heaven, and to God, the judge of all, and to the spirits of the righteous made perfect,
and to Jesus, who mediates a new covenant, and to the blood of sprinkling, which speaks better things than Abel’s blood.{p}
Take care not to reject the one who speaks. If those who rejected him when he gave warning on earth did not get away, much less will we, if we turn our backs on the one who warns us from heaven.
His voice shook the earth then, but now he has promised, “Once more I will shake not just the earth but the heavens too.”{q}
The words “Yet once more” point to the removing of things that are shaken, as things that have been made, so that the things not shaken may endure.
Therefore, since we are receiving a kingdom that cannot be shaken, let us be grateful, and so offer to God worship that pleases him, with reverence and awe;{r}
for our God is a consuming fire.{s}

notes.text: Witnesses: Greek *martyres*, people who testify; here those whose faith is attested in chapter 11. *Clings so closely*: the meaning of the rare Greek word *euperistatos* is uncertain; perhaps “easily distracting.” One early papyrus, P46 as reported, reads “easily distracting.”
Leads the way: Greek *archēgos*, “pioneer,” “founder”; see 2:10. *For the sake of the joy*: or “instead of the joy.”
Against themselves: so the Westcott–Hort text, following Sinaiticus and other early witnesses as reported; most manuscripts read “against himself.”
Prov 3:11–12 in the Greek Old Testament. *The Lord*: the Hebrew text has *Yahweh*; so also in verse 6.

Punishes … receives: so the Greek Old Testament; the Hebrew reads “as a father the son in whom he delights.” *Son*: so throughout this passage the Greek speaks of sons, but the teaching applies to all God’s children.
Human fathers: literally “fathers of our flesh.”
Prov 4:26 in the Greek Old Testament.
Deut 29:18 in the Greek Old Testament.
See Gen 25:29–34.

Room for a change of mind: literally “place of repentance,” perhaps meaning no way to change his father’s decision. *Sought the blessing*: or “sought repentance”; the Greek pronoun could refer to either. See Gen 27:30–40.
What can be touched: later manuscripts read “a mountain that can be touched.” See Exod 19:16–22; Deut 4:11; 5:22–26.
Deut 9:19.

*Zion*: Hebrew, perhaps “fortress”; the hill of Jerusalem. *Jerusalem*: Hebrew *Yerushalayim*, perhaps “foundation of Shalem” or “foundation of peace.” *Myriads*: literally “tens of thousands.” *Of angels in festal gathering*: or “of angels, to the festal gathering and assembly of the firstborn.”
Compare Gen 4:10.
Hag 2:6.
Let us be grateful: or “let us hold on to grace.”

verses.text: Let love for one another as brothers continue.{a}
Do not forget to welcome strangers, for in doing so some have had angels as their guests without realizing it.{b}
Keep in mind those in prison, as if you shared their chains, and those who are ill-treated, since you too have bodies of your own.
Let marriage be honorable in everyone’s eyes, and the bed of marriage undefiled; God will bring judgment on the sexually immoral and on adulterers.
Keep your manner of life clear of greed for money, and be satisfied with what is at hand. For he has said, “I will never let you go, nor will I ever desert you.”{c}
Remember those who led you, who told you God’s word. Look at how their lives turned out, and follow the example of their faith.
Jesus Christ is the same yesterday and today and forever.

Do not be swept aside by teachings that are various and foreign. It is a fine thing for the heart to be made firm by grace, rather than by foods, which have brought no benefit to those who live by them.{e}
We possess an altar, but the ones who serve at the tent are not allowed to eat from it.
For the bodies of those animals whose blood is brought into the sanctuary by the high priest as an offering for sin are burned outside the camp.{f}
Therefore Jesus also suffered outside the city gate, to sanctify the people with his own blood.
Let us, then, go out to him outside the camp, bearing the reproach he bore.
We have here no city that endures; we are searching for the one still to come.
Through him let us continually offer up a sacrifice of praise to God, that is, the fruit of lips that confess his name.{g}
And do not forget kindness and sharing, for these are the sacrifices in which God delights.

Be obedient to your leaders and defer to them, since they keep watch over your souls, knowing they must render an account. Let them do it gladly and not with sighs, for that would bring you no profit.
Keep praying for us. We are persuaded that our conscience is good, since we wish to conduct ourselves well in every way.
I especially ask you to pray, so that I may be given back to you more quickly.
Now may the God of peace, who brought up from the dead the great shepherd of the sheep by the blood of the eternal covenant, our Lord Jesus,{h}
fit you with all that is good for doing his will, producing in us what delights him, through Jesus Christ; glory be his forever and ever. Amen.{i}
I urge you, brothers, bear with my word of exhortation, for I have written to you briefly.
You should know that our brother Timothy has been set free, and if he comes soon, I will see you with him.{j}
Give our greetings to all who lead you and to all the saints. Those from Italy greet you.{k}
Grace be with all of you.{l}

notes.text: Love … as brothers: Greek *philadelphia*.
Compare Gen 18:1–8; 19:1–3.
Deut 31:6, 8; Josh 1:5.
Ps 118:6 (117:6 in the Greek Old Testament). *The Lord*: the Hebrew text has *Yahweh*.
Foods: probably rules about clean and unclean foods or sacrificial meals.
Through him: some manuscripts add “then.” *The fruit of lips*: compare Hos 14:2 in the Greek Old Testament.
Compare Isa 63:11; Zech 9:11.
In us: some manuscripts read “in you.”
*Timothy*: Greek *Timotheos*, “honoring God.” *Set free*: or “has set out.”
Those from Italy: either people in Italy or Italians living elsewhere; the phrase does not settle where the letter was written.
With all of you: later manuscripts add “Amen.”

books.name: James
books.sourceNote: Translated from the Greek text of B. F. Westcott and F. J. A. Hort, *The New Testament in the Original Greek* (1881; public domain), with Tischendorf’s eighth edition (1869–72; public domain) consulted. Variant readings were also compared with the SBL Greek New Testament, the Nestle–Aland *Novum Testamentum Graece*, and the Byzantine text of Robinson and Pierpont, which were consulted for variants only. Where manuscript readings are cited in the notes, they are reported from the standard editions and have not been verified against the manuscripts. Greek *kyrios* is rendered “Lord”; where an Old Testament passage with the divine name is quoted or echoed, a note gives the Hebrew *Yahweh*. *Christos* is rendered “Christ” where it functions as part of Jesus’ name. The letter names its author as James (Greek *Iakōbos*, the Greek form of the Hebrew name Jacob). Early tradition identifies him with James the brother of Jesus, leader of the church in Jerusalem (Gal 1:19; Acts 15:13; 21:18); some scholars hold that it was written later in his name. The chief early witnesses include the papyri P20, P23 and P74 and Codices Sinaiticus, Alexandrinus and Vaticanus. The letter uses no units of measure or coins; its sums are left general.

verses.text: James,{a} a slave of God and of the Lord Jesus Christ, to the twelve tribes living scattered abroad: greetings.{b}
Count it nothing but joy, my brothers,{c} whenever you run into trials of many kinds,
since you know that the testing of your faith produces staying power.
Let staying power finish its work, so that you may be mature and whole, lacking in nothing.{d}
If any of you is short of wisdom, let him ask God, who gives to everyone freely and without reproach, and it will be given him.
But let him ask in faith, with no doubting, for the doubter is like a wave of the sea, blown and tossed by the wind.
Such a person must not suppose that he will get anything from the Lord;
he is a man of two minds, unsteady in all his ways.{e}
Let the brother of low standing take pride in being raised up,
and the rich in being brought low, because like a flower of the grass he will pass away.
For the sun comes up with its scorching heat and withers the grass; its flower drops, and the beauty of its look is lost. So too the rich man will fade away in the middle of his pursuits.{f}
Happy the man who holds out under trial, because once he has stood the test he will receive the crown of life, which he promised to those who love him.{g}
Let no one say when tempted, “God is tempting me.” For God cannot be tempted by evil, and he himself tempts no one.{h}
Each person is tempted by being dragged off and lured by his own desire.
Then desire, having conceived, gives birth to sin, and sin, once full grown, brings forth death.
Do not be misled, my dear brothers.
Every good gift and every perfect present is from above, coming down from the Father of lights, in whom there is no variation or shadow cast by turning.{i}
By his own choice he brought us to birth through the word of truth, so that we should be a kind of firstfruits of his creatures.
Know this, my dear brothers: everyone should be swift to hear, unhurried to speak, unhurried to grow angry;{j}
for human anger does not accomplish the justice that God requires.
Therefore put away all filth and the excess of malice, and with gentleness accept the word planted in you, which is able to save your souls.
Be people who do the word, and not only hearers who deceive themselves.
For anyone who hears the word and does not do it is like a man who looks at the face he was born with in a mirror;
he takes a look at himself, walks off, and straightaway forgets what sort of man he was.
But the one who has looked closely into the perfect law, the law of freedom, and stays with it, proving to be no forgetful hearer but a doer who acts, will be happy in what he does.
If anyone thinks he is religious and does not put a bridle on his tongue, but deceives his own heart, his religion is worthless.
Religion that is pure and unstained before God the Father is this: to look after orphans and widows in their trouble, and to keep oneself unspotted by the world.

notes.text: *James*: Greek *Iakōbos*, from the Hebrew *Yaʿaqov* (Jacob), traditionally explained as “he takes the heel” or “he supplants” (Gen 25:26; 27:36).
Slave: Greek *doulos*, “slave,” “servant.” *Living scattered abroad*: literally “in the dispersion” (Greek *diaspora*), the term for Jews living outside the land of Israel, here applied to believers.
Brothers: Greek *adelphoi*, which includes sisters; so throughout the letter.
Mature: Greek *teleios*, “complete,” “perfect.”
Of two minds: Greek *dipsychos*, literally “double-souled.”
Scorching heat: or “the scorching wind” (Greek *kausōn*). Compare Isa 40:6–8.
Happy: or “blessed.” *He promised*: later manuscripts read “the Lord promised.”
Tempted: the same Greek word as “trial” in verse 12; it means both testing and temptation.
Father of lights: that is, the Creator of the heavenly lights. *Shadow cast by turning*: the image is of the shifting shadows of the heavenly bodies.
Know this: or “You know this.” Later manuscripts read “So then.”

verses.text: My brothers, do not hold the faith of our Lord Jesus Christ, the Lord of glory, while showing favoritism.{a}
Suppose a man comes into your assembly wearing gold rings and splendid clothes, and a poor man also comes in, in shabby clothes,{b}
and you pay attention to the one in the splendid clothes and say, “Sit here in this good place,” while to the poor man you say, “You stand there,” or, “Sit down on the floor by my footstool.”
Have you not made distinctions among yourselves and become judges with evil reasoning?
Listen, my dear brothers. Has not God chosen those who are poor in the world’s eyes to be rich in faith and heirs of the kingdom he promised to those who love him?
But you have treated the poor man with contempt. Are the rich not the ones who lord it over you, and the very ones who drag you before the courts?
Is it not they who slander the honorable name that was called over you?{c}
If indeed you carry out the royal law according to the scripture, “You shall love your neighbor as yourself,” you are doing well.{d}
But if you show favoritism, you commit sin, and the law convicts you as transgressors.
For whoever keeps the whole law but stumbles on a single point has become guilty of all of it.
The one who said, “Do not commit adultery,” also said, “Do not murder.” If you avoid adultery but commit murder, you have broken the law.{e}
Speak and act as people who are going to be judged by the law of freedom.
For judgment is merciless to the one who has shown no mercy; mercy triumphs over judgment.
What good is it, my brothers, if someone claims to have faith but has no deeds? Can that faith save him?{f}
If a brother or sister is without clothes and short of daily food,
and one of you says to them, “Go in peace; keep warm and eat well,” without giving them what the body requires, what good is that?
So it is with faith: on its own, without deeds, it is a dead thing.
But someone will say, “You have faith, and I have deeds.” Show me your faith apart from deeds, and I will show you my faith by my deeds.{g}
You believe that God is one; good for you. Even the demons believe that, and they shudder.{h}
Do you want to be shown, you empty fellow, that faith without deeds is useless?{i}
Was not Abraham our father declared righteous by deeds, when he offered his son Isaac on the altar?{j}
You see that faith was working along with his deeds, and by the deeds faith was brought to completion,
and the scripture was fulfilled which says, “Abraham trusted God, and this was reckoned to him as righteousness”; and he came to be called the friend of God.{k}
You see that a person is declared righteous by deeds and not by faith alone.
And in the same way, was not Rahab the prostitute also declared righteous by deeds, when she took in the messengers and sent them off by a different road?{l}
For as the body without the spirit is dead, so faith without deeds is dead.

notes.text: The Lord of glory: literally “our Lord Jesus Christ of glory”; or “our glorious Lord Jesus Christ.” The Greek may also be read as a question.
Assembly: Greek *synagōgē*, “gathering,” “synagogue.”
The honorable name that was called over you: that is, the name of Christ, invoked over believers, perhaps at baptism.
Deeds: Greek *erga*, “works”; so throughout this passage.
The extent of the objector’s words is uncertain; the quotation may continue further.
God is one: compare Deut 6:4. Some manuscripts read “there is one God.”
Useless: Greek *argē*, “idle,” “unproductive.” Later manuscripts read “dead.”
Gen 22:9–12. *Abraham*: “father of a multitude” (Gen 17:5). *Isaac*: “he laughs.”
Gen 15:6; compare Isa 41:8; 2 Chr 20:7.
Josh 2:1–21. *Rahab*: “broad,” “wide.”

verses.text: Do not let many of you become teachers, my brothers; you are aware that those of us who teach will face a stricter judgment.
Every one of us trips up in many respects. Whoever never trips up in speech is a mature man, one able to keep the whole body in check as well.
When we put bits into horses’ mouths to make them obey us, we steer their whole body too.{a}
Look at ships as well: large as they are, and driven by strong winds, they are steered by a very small rudder wherever the pilot’s impulse wants to go.
Just so the tongue is a little member, yet its boasts are grand.
The tongue too is a fire, a whole world of evil placed among our body parts; it contaminates the entire person, sets the course of life ablaze, and is itself ignited by Gehenna.{b}
Every species of wild animal and bird, of reptile and sea creature, is tamed and has been tamed by humankind,
but no human being can tame the tongue. It is a restless evil, full of deadly poison.{c}
With the tongue we praise the Lord and Father, and with it we curse people who were created in God’s likeness.{d}
From the same mouth come blessing and curse. My brothers, it should not be this way.
Does a spring gush both fresh and bitter water from the same opening?
Can a fig tree, my brothers, yield olives, or a vine yield figs? Neither can salt water give fresh.{e}
Who among you is wise and understanding? Let him show his deeds by a good way of life, in the gentleness that comes from wisdom.
But if you have bitter jealousy and selfish ambition in your hearts, do not boast and lie against the truth.
Such wisdom does not descend from above; it belongs to the earth, to the merely natural, to demons.{f}
For where jealousy and selfish ambition are, there you find disorder and every vile practice.

The wisdom that comes from above, on the other hand, is pure first and foremost, then peace-loving, considerate, willing to yield, brimming with mercy and with good fruit, free of partiality and of pretense.
And the fruit of righteousness is sown in peace by those who make peace.

notes.text: When: later manuscripts read “Look.”

World of wrongdoing: the Greek of this verse is difficult and its punctuation uncertain. *Wheel of existence*: or “the course of life,” literally “the wheel of birth.” *Gehenna*: the Valley of Hinnom outside Jerusalem, used as a name for the place of final punishment.
Restless: some manuscripts read “uncontrollable.”
Neither can salt water give fresh: later manuscripts read “So no spring yields both salt water and fresh.”
Merely natural: Greek *psychikē*, “natural,” “belonging to the soul” as opposed to the Spirit.

verses.text: Where do the fights and quarrels among you come from? Do they not come from your pleasures that wage war in your members?{a}
You crave and go without, so you commit murder. You burn with envy and cannot get what you want, so you battle and wrangle. You go without because you do not ask.{b}
You ask and do not receive, because you ask with wrong motives, to spend it on your pleasures.
Adulteresses! Do you not know that friendship with the world is hostility toward God? So whoever chooses to be a friend of the world makes himself God’s enemy.{c}
Or do you think the scripture speaks to no purpose? Does the spirit he made to dwell in us long with envy?{d}
So submit yourselves to God. Stand against the devil, and he will flee from you.
Draw near to God, and he will draw near to you. Wash your hands, you sinners; purify your hearts, you divided in mind.
Be wretched, mourn and weep. Let your laughter be turned into mourning and your joy into gloom.
Humble yourselves before the Lord, and he will lift you up.

Do not speak against one another, brothers. Whoever speaks against a brother or judges his brother speaks against the law and judges the law. And if you judge the law, you are not a doer of the law but its judge.
There is one lawgiver and judge, the one able to save and to destroy. But you, who are you to judge your neighbor?{f}
Come now, you who say, “Today or tomorrow we will go into such and such a city, spend a year there, do business and make money,”
when you have no idea what tomorrow holds. What is your life? You are a vapor that appears briefly and then disappears.{g}
Instead you ought to say, “If the Lord wills, we will live and do this or that.”
But now you take pride in your boastful schemes. All boasting of that kind is wicked.
Anyone, then, who knows what is good and does not do it is guilty of sin.

notes.text: Pleasures: Greek *hēdonai*, “desires for pleasure”; so in verse 3.
Commit murder: some propose the reading “you are jealous” (Greek *phthoneite* for *phoneuete*), but no manuscript is reported to have it.
Adulteresses: the image is of unfaithfulness to God as unfaithfulness in marriage, as in the prophets. Later manuscripts read “Adulterers and adulteresses.”

The Greek of this verse is difficult, and no Old Testament passage matches it. Other possible renderings: “The spirit that he made to dwell in us yearns jealously,” or “He yearns jealously for the spirit that he made to dwell in us.”
Prov 3:34 in the Greek Old Testament.
One lawgiver and judge: later manuscripts lack “and judge.”
What tomorrow will bring: the Greek is variously read and punctuated in the manuscripts. *You are a mist*: later manuscripts read “It is a mist.”

verses.text: Come now, you rich, weep and howl over the miseries that are coming upon you.
Your wealth has rotted, and your clothes have become moth-eaten.
Your gold and silver are rusted, and the rust will testify against you and consume your flesh like fire. You have stored up wealth in the final days.
Listen! The pay you cheated from the workers who harvested your fields cries out against you, and the shouts of the reapers have come to the ears of the Lord of Armies.{a}
You have lived soft lives on earth and indulged yourselves; you have fattened your hearts for the day of slaughter.
You have condemned and murdered the righteous one; he does not resist you.{b}
Be patient, then, brothers, until the coming of the Lord. See how the farmer waits for the precious crop from the ground, being patient over it until it receives the early and the late rains.{c}
You also be patient. Make your hearts firm, for the coming of the Lord is near.
Brothers, do not complain about one another, or you may be judged. The judge stands at the door already!
Brothers, for a pattern of patient endurance under hardship, look to the prophets who spoke in the Lord’s name.
We call those who held out happy. You have heard of the endurance of Job, and you have seen the outcome the Lord brought about: the Lord is full of compassion and mercy.{d}
Above all, my brothers, do not swear oaths, either by heaven or by the earth or with any other oath. Let your “yes” be yes and your “no” be no, so that you do not fall under judgment.{e}
Is one of you in trouble? Let him pray. Is one in good spirits? Let him sing songs of praise.
Is someone among you ill? Let that person summon the church’s elders, who should pray over him and anoint him with oil in the Lord’s name.{f}
And the prayer offered in faith will rescue the sick person, and the Lord will raise him up; and if he has committed sins, he will be forgiven.
Confess your sins to each other and pray for each other, so that you may be healed. A righteous person’s prayer is powerful and effective.{g}
Elijah was a human being with feelings like ours, and he prayed earnestly that it would not rain, and it did not rain on the land for three years and six months.{h}
Then he prayed again, and the sky gave rain and the land produced its crop.{i}
My brothers, if any one of you wanders from the truth and someone turns him back,
let him know that whoever turns a sinner back from the error of his way will save his soul from death and will cover a multitude of sins.{j}

notes.text: Lord of Armies: Greek *kyrios sabaōth*, from the Hebrew *Yahweh tsevaʾot*, “Yahweh of Armies” (traditionally “Lord of hosts”); compare Isa 5:9. The wages were due at the end of each working day (Deut 24:14–15).
He does not resist you: or, as a question, “Does he not resist you?”

The early and the late rains: in the land of Israel, the autumn rains after sowing and the spring rains before harvest (Deut 11:14). Westcott and Hort have only “the early and the late”; later manuscripts add “rain,” and some add “fruit.”

Happy: or “blessed.” *Job*: the meaning of the name is uncertain; it has been explained as “where is the father?” *Full of compassion and mercy*: compare Ps 103:8; Exod 34:6, where the Hebrew has *Yahweh*.
Compare Matt 5:34–37. *Under judgment*: later manuscripts read “into hypocrisy.”
Of the Lord: Westcott and Hort bracket these words; Vaticanus is reported to lack “the Lord.”
As it does its work: or “when it is set in motion.”
1 Kgs 17:1; 18:1; compare Luke 4:25. *Elijah*: “my God is Yahweh.”
Let him know: some manuscripts read “know” (plural). *His soul*: that is, probably the sinner’s soul; Westcott and Hort place “his” in the margin, and some manuscripts lack it. Compare Prov 10:12.

books.name: 1 Peter
books.sourceNote: Translated from the Greek text of B. F. Westcott and F. J. A. Hort, *The New Testament in the Original Greek* (1881; public domain), with Tischendorf’s eighth edition (1869–72; public domain) consulted. Variant readings were also compared with the SBL Greek New Testament, the Nestle–Aland *Novum Testamentum Graece*, and the Byzantine text of Robinson and Pierpont, which were consulted for variants only. Where manuscript readings are cited in the notes, they are reported from the standard editions and have not been verified against the manuscripts. Greek *kyrios* is rendered “Lord”; where an Old Testament passage with the divine name is quoted or echoed, a note gives the Hebrew *Yahweh*. *Christos* is rendered “Christ” where it functions as part of Jesus’ name. The letter names its author as Peter, the apostle (1:1), writing with the help of Silvanus (5:12) from “Babylon” (5:13), probably a figurative name for Rome. Many scholars accept it as Peter’s, perhaps in the early 60s AD; others date it later and regard it as written in his name. The chief early witnesses include the papyrus P72 (3rd–4th century) and Codices Sinaiticus, Alexandrinus and Vaticanus.

verses.text: Peter,{a} an apostle of Jesus Christ, to God’s chosen ones living as foreigners scattered through Pontus, Galatia, Cappadocia, Asia and Bithynia,{b}
whom God the Father chose as he knew beforehand, set apart by the Spirit to obey Jesus Christ and to be sprinkled with his blood. Grace and peace be multiplied to you.{c}
Praise be to the God and Father of our Lord Jesus Christ! Because of his abundant mercy he has given us a new birth into a living hope through the resurrection of Jesus Christ from the dead,
to an inheritance that cannot decay or be defiled or fade, kept safe in the heavens for you,
you who are protected by God’s power through faith until the arrival of salvation, prepared to be revealed when time comes to its close.
In this you are overjoyed, even though now for a little while, if it must be, you have been grieved by trials of various kinds,

Their purpose is that your faith, once proven genuine, a thing of greater value than gold (which perishes, though fire tests it), may bring praise and glory and honor at the unveiling of Jesus Christ.
You have not seen him, yet you love him; and though you do not see him now, you trust him and are overjoyed with a joy beyond words and filled with glory,{d}
as you receive the goal of your faith, the salvation of your souls.
Concerning this salvation the prophets who spoke beforehand of the grace meant for you searched and inquired with care,
They probed what person or what period the Spirit of Christ in them meant, when it bore witness ahead of time to the sufferings Christ would undergo and the glories that would come after them.

To them it was disclosed that their ministry was not for their own benefit but for yours, in those matters now reported to you by the ones who preached the gospel to you through the Holy Spirit sent from heaven; into these things angels yearn to peer.
So gird up the loins of your mind, keep sober, and set your hope fully on the grace that is being brought to you when Jesus Christ is unveiled.{e}
As obedient children, do not shape yourselves to the desires you once had in your ignorance.
Rather, as the one who called you is holy, become holy yourselves in all your conduct,
since it is written, “You shall be holy, because I am holy.”{f}
And if you call on him as Father who judges each person’s work impartially, live out the time of your stay as foreigners in reverent fear,
knowing that it was not with perishable things like silver or gold that you were ransomed from the empty way of life handed down from your ancestors,
but with precious blood, as of a lamb without blemish or spot, the blood of Christ.
He was chosen before the world was founded but appeared in the final period of time for your benefit,
who through him trust in God, who raised him from the dead and gave him glory, so that your faith and hope are in God.
Now that you have purified your souls by obeying the truth, so as to have a sincere love for the brothers, love one another earnestly from the heart,{g}
You have been begotten again from seed that does not perish rather than seed that does, by means of God’s word, which lives and abides.

For
“all humankind is grass,
and all its splendor like a wildflower.
The grass dries up,
and the flower falls,

but what the Lord has spoken stands for all time.”
That spoken word is the gospel which was preached to you.{h}

notes.text: *Peter*: Greek *Petros*, “rock,” “stone,” the name Jesus gave to Simon (John 1:42), the Greek equivalent of Aramaic *Kēphas*.
Living as foreigners scattered: literally “sojourners of the dispersion” (Greek *diaspora*). The places named are Roman provinces in what is now Turkey.
Sprinkled with his blood: compare Exod 24:7–8.
Not seen him: later manuscripts read “not known him.”
Gird up the loins of your mind: the image is of tucking up a long robe to be ready for action.
Lev 11:44–45; 19:2. Westcott and Hort bracket the Greek word introducing the quotation.

Brothers: Greek *adelphoi*, here in the compound *philadelphia*, “love of brothers,” which includes sisters. *From the heart*: some manuscripts read “from a pure heart.” Later manuscripts add “through the Spirit” after “the truth.”
Isa 40:6–8 in the Greek Old Testament, where the Hebrew reads “the word of our God.”

verses.text: So put away all malice and all deceit, hypocrisy, envy and all slander.
As babies just born crave milk, crave the unadulterated milk of the word, so that you may be nourished by it and grow toward salvation,{a}
if indeed you have tasted that the Lord is good.{b}
Come to him, a living stone rejected by people but chosen and precious in God’s sight,
and you yourselves, like living stones, are being built up as a spiritual house, to be a holy priesthood, offering spiritual sacrifices acceptable to God through Jesus Christ.

and
“a stone over which they stumble,
a rock that makes them fall.”
They stumble by refusing to obey the word, and to this end they were appointed.{e}

But you are a chosen race, a royal priesthood, a holy nation, a people God has made his own, so that you may declare the excellencies of the one who called you out of darkness into his marvelous light.{f}
You were once “not a people,” and now you are the people of God; you were “shown no mercy,” and now mercy has been shown you.{g}
Dear friends, I appeal to you as foreigners and exiles to keep away from the desires of the flesh, which wage war against the soul.

Let your way of life among the nations be honorable, so that in the very matter in which they accuse you of evildoing they may observe your fine actions and give glory to God on the day of his coming.{h}
For the Lord’s sake submit to every human institution, whether to the emperor as supreme,{i}
or to governors as sent by him to punish wrongdoers and to praise those who do good.
It is God’s purpose that by your good conduct you muzzle the ignorant talk of senseless people.
Live as free people, yet not using your freedom as a cover for evil, but as slaves of God.
Show honor to all. Love the brotherhood. Revere God. Give the emperor his due honor.{j}
Slaves, accept the authority of your masters with complete respect, whether they are gentle and fair or harsh.{k}
For it is a mark of grace when someone, because he is conscious of God, endures pain while suffering unjustly.
What credit is there if you endure a beating for doing wrong? But if you endure suffering when you do good, this is grace in God’s sight.
For it was to this that you were called, since Christ also suffered for you, leaving you an example so that you should follow in his footsteps.{l}

“No sin did he commit,
nor was any lie detected on his lips.”{m}
Reviled, he hurled back no abuse; suffering, he made no threats; instead he left his cause with the one whose judgment is just.
In his own body he bore our sins up onto the tree, so that we, having parted from sins, might live to righteousness. By his bruises you have been made whole.{n}
For you were straying like sheep, but now you have returned to the shepherd and guardian of your souls.{o}

notes.text: Of the word: or “spiritual” (Greek *logikon*). *Into salvation*: later manuscripts omit these words.
Ps 34:8 (Greek Old Testament 33:9), where the Hebrew has *Yahweh*.
Isa 28:16 in the Greek Old Testament.
Ps 118:22 (Greek Old Testament 117:22). *There is honor*: or “he is precious.”
Exod 19:5–6; Isa 43:20–21. *Excellencies*: or “praises,” “mighty deeds.”
Compare Hos 1:6, 9; 2:23.
Nations: or “Gentiles,” here meaning those who do not know God. *The day of his coming*: literally “the day of visitation.”
Emperor: Greek *basileus*, “king,” the usual title for the Roman emperor in the Greek-speaking east.
Brotherhood: Greek *adelphotēs*, the community of believers.
Household servants: Greek *oiketai*, slaves in a household.
Suffered: some manuscripts read “died.”
Isa 53:4–5, 12. *Tree*: that is, the cross.
Isa 53:6. *Guardian*: Greek *episkopos*, “overseer.”

verses.text: Wives, likewise, be subject to your husbands, so that if any of them refuse to believe the message, they may be won without words through the way their wives live,
when they see your pure and reverent conduct.
Do not let your beauty be the outward kind, braided hair and gold ornaments and fine clothing,
Let it rather be the inner self hidden in the heart, adorned with the lasting beauty of a meek and tranquil spirit, which God counts as costly.
For this is how the holy women of old who hoped in God used to adorn themselves, submitting to their own husbands,
as Sarah obeyed Abraham, calling him lord. You have become her daughters if you do good and do not give way to fear.{a}

In the same way, husbands, live with your wives considerately, honoring the woman as the more delicate partner, because they too are co-heirs of the gift of life, so that nothing will block your prayers.
Finally, all of you, be of one mind, sympathetic, loving as brothers, tenderhearted and humble.
Do not repay evil for evil or insult for insult, but bless instead, because it was for this that you were called, so that you may inherit a blessing.

For
“whoever wants to love life
and see good days
must keep his tongue from evil
and his lips from speaking deceit;

let him shun evil and do right;
let him look for peace and go after it.
And who will do you harm if you are zealous for the good?
Yet even if you have to suffer because you do right, you are happy. “Have no fear of them, and do not be shaken,”{c}
but in your hearts revere Christ as holy, as Lord, and be prepared at all times to make a defense to anyone who asks you to account for your hope,{d}
yet doing it with gentleness and reverence, keeping a good conscience, so that when you are slandered, those who abuse your good conduct in Christ may be put to shame.
It is better, should God so will, to suffer for doing right than to suffer for doing wrong.
Christ also suffered for sins once and for all, an upright person for the unrighteous, in order to lead you to God. He was killed in the body but brought to life by the spirit,{e}
in which he went also to the spirits held in prison and preached to them,{f}
who refused to obey long ago, while God waited patiently in Noah’s time as the ark was under construction. Only a few, eight people, were rescued through the water.{g}
And baptism, which corresponds to this, now saves you also, not as a removal of dirt from the flesh but as the pledge of a good conscience toward God, through the resurrection of Jesus Christ,{h}
He has passed into heaven and sits at God’s right hand, and angels and authorities and powers have been placed under him.

notes.text: Gen 18:12. *Sarah*: “princess.” *Abraham*: “father of a multitude.” *Give way to fear*: compare Prov 3:25.
Ps 34:12–16 (Greek Old Testament 33:13–17), where the Hebrew has *Yahweh*.
Isa 8:12. *Have no fear of them*: literally “do not fear their fear,” that is, either what they fear or the fear they cause. *Happy*: or “blessed.”
Isa 8:13, where the Hebrew has *Yahweh*. Later manuscripts read “the Lord God” in place of “Christ as Lord.”

Died: Westcott and Hort read *apethanen*, “died,” with Sinaiticus and Alexandrinus as reported; many manuscripts read *epathen*, “suffered.” *You*: some manuscripts read “us.” *In the spirit*: or “by the Spirit.”

In which: or “in whom,” that is, in the spirit. The passage is much debated. The spirits have been understood as the fallen angels of Gen 6:1–4 (compare 2 Pet 2:4; Jude 6 and the book of 1 Enoch), as the dead of Noah’s generation, or as those to whom Christ spoke through Noah; the proclamation as either a message of victory or the good news (compare 4:6).
Gen 6–8. *Noah*: “rest.”
Corresponds to this: Greek *antitypon*, “antitype,” “counterpart.” *Pledge*: or “appeal” (Greek *eperōtēma*).

verses.text: So, since Christ has suffered in the flesh, you too must arm yourselves with that same resolve, because the one who has suffered in the flesh has broken with sin,{a}
so as to live the rest of his time in the flesh no longer for human desires but for the will of God.
For the time already past is enough for doing what the Gentiles want to do, living in debauchery, lusts, drunkenness, wild parties, drinking bouts and lawless idolatry.
They are surprised that you do not plunge with them into the same flood of reckless living, and they abuse you;
but they will answer to the one prepared to judge both the living and the dead.
For this is why the good news was proclaimed even to the dead, that though they had been judged in the flesh as human beings are, they might live in the spirit as God does.
The end of all things has drawn near. So be sensible and sober for the sake of your prayers.
Above all, keep your love for one another constant, since love covers a multitude of sins.{b}
Be hospitable to one another without grumbling.
Each of you has received a gift; employ it to serve one another, like faithful managers of God’s many-sided grace:

if you speak, speak as if delivering God’s own words; if you serve, serve with the strength God provides, so that God may receive honor in all you do through Jesus Christ. Glory and might are his forever and ever. Amen.
Dear friends, do not be bewildered by the blaze of trial that has come among you to test you, as if something unheard of were befalling you.
But to the extent that you share the sufferings of Christ, rejoice, so that you may also rejoice and be overjoyed when his glory is revealed.
If you are insulted for the name of Christ, you are blessed, because the Spirit of glory, the Spirit of God, rests on you.{c}
But let none of you suffer as a murderer or thief or evildoer or as a meddler.
But if anyone suffers as a Christian, he should not be ashamed but should glorify God in that name.{d}
For it is time for the judgment to start with God’s own household; and if it starts with us, how will it end for those who refuse to obey God’s good news?{e}
Let those, then, who suffer as God wills commit their souls to the Creator, who is faithful, and go on doing good.

notes.text: In the flesh: later manuscripts add “for us” after “suffered.”
Prov 10:12.
Compare Isa 11:2. Later manuscripts add “and of power” after “glory,” and some add “On their part he is blasphemed, but on your part he is glorified.”
Christian: Greek *Christianos*, “follower of Christ”; compare Acts 11:26; 26:28. *In that name*: later manuscripts read “in this respect.”
It is time: Westcott and Hort bracket the Greek article before “time.”
Prov 11:31 in the Greek Old Testament.

verses.text: To the elders among you, then, I make my appeal, as one who is an elder with you, who witnessed Christ’s sufferings and will share also in the glory soon to be disclosed:
shepherd the flock of God among you, watching over it not under compulsion but willingly, as God would have it, not for shameful gain but eagerly,{a}
not domineering over the portions allotted to you, but setting a pattern for the flock.
Then when the head shepherd is made manifest, you will win the crown of glory that never withers.
So bow down beneath God’s powerful hand, so that at the right moment he may raise you up,
casting all your anxiety on him, because he cares for you.{c}
Stay sober and alert. The devil, your opponent, roams about like a lion roaring in search of someone to swallow.
Resist him, firm in the faith, knowing that the same kinds of suffering are being laid on your family of believers throughout the world.{d}
And after you have suffered a little while, the God of all grace, who called you to his eternal glory in Christ, will himself restore, establish, strengthen and settle you.
To him be the power forever. Amen.
With the help of Silvanus, whom I consider a trustworthy brother, I have written you this short letter to encourage you and to affirm that this is God’s true grace. Hold your ground in it.{e}
She who is in Babylon, chosen together with you, sends you greetings, and so does Mark my son.{f}
Greet one another with a kiss of love. Peace to all of you who are in Christ.{g}

notes.text: Watching over it: some manuscripts lack these words. *As God would have it*: some manuscripts lack these words.
Prov 3:34 in the Greek Old Testament.
Compare Ps 55:22 (Greek Old Testament 54:23).
Family of believers: Greek *adelphotēs*, “brotherhood.”
*Silvanus*: a Latin name, perhaps from *silva*, “forest”; probably the Silas of Acts 15:22–40. *Through Silvanus*: that is, either as secretary or as bearer of the letter.
*She who is in Babylon*: probably the church in Rome, called by the name of the ancient capital of exile; compare Rev 17:5. *Mark*: Latin *Marcus*, perhaps “of Mars”; compare Acts 12:12.
Later manuscripts add “Jesus. Amen.”

books.name: 2 Peter
books.sourceNote: Translated from the Greek text of B. F. Westcott and F. J. A. Hort, *The New Testament in the Original Greek* (1881; public domain), with Tischendorf’s eighth edition (1869–72; public domain) consulted. Variant readings were also compared with the SBL Greek New Testament, the Nestle–Aland *Novum Testamentum Graece*, and the Byzantine text of Robinson and Pierpont, which were consulted for variants only. Where manuscript readings are cited in the notes, they are reported from the standard editions and have not been verified against the manuscripts. Greek *kyrios* is rendered “Lord”; where an Old Testament passage with the divine name is quoted or echoed, a note gives the Hebrew *Yahweh*. *Christos* is rendered “Christ” where it functions as part of Jesus’ name. Authorship: the letter names its author as Simon Peter (1:1), who recalls the transfiguration (1:16–18) and refers to an earlier letter (3:1). Its authorship was questioned in the early church (Origen and Eusebius report doubts), and many modern scholars regard it as written in Peter’s name after his death, while others defend it as Peter’s own; this translation takes no position. Much of chapter 2 closely parallels the letter of Jude. The chief early witnesses include the papyrus P72 (3rd–4th century) and Codices Sinaiticus, Alexandrinus and Vaticanus.

verses.text: Simon Peter, a servant and apostle of Jesus Christ, to those who have received a faith as precious as ours through the fairness of our God and Savior Jesus Christ:{a}
grace and peace be multiplied to you in the knowledge of God and of Jesus our Lord.
His divine power has granted us all that we need for life and devotion, through knowing the one who summoned us by his own splendor and moral excellence.{b}
By these means he has given us promises of great value and greatness, so that by them you might become partakers of the divine nature, having fled the decay that lust has spread through the world.
For this very reason, make every effort to add excellence to your faith, and knowledge to excellence,
and self-control to knowledge, and endurance to self-control, and godliness to endurance,
and affection for the brothers to godliness, and love to affection for the brothers.{c}
If these qualities are yours and keep increasing, they keep you from being idle or fruitless in the knowledge of our Lord Jesus Christ.
Whoever lacks them is blind, shortsighted, having forgotten that he was cleansed from his past sins.
So, brothers and sisters, work even harder to make your calling and choice certain; if you do these things, you will never fall.
For in this way entry into the eternal kingdom of our Lord and Savior Jesus Christ will be richly furnished for you.
That is why I mean to keep reminding you of these things, though you know them and are established in the truth you now have.
I think it right, as long as I am in this tent, to stir you up by way of reminder,{d}
since I know that the putting off of my tent will come soon, as our Lord Jesus Christ also made clear to me.{e}
And I will be diligent to make sure that, once I have gone, you can call these things to mind whenever you need.{f}
For it was not cleverly invented myths that we followed when we made known to you the power and coming of our Lord Jesus Christ; we were eyewitnesses of his majesty.
He received honor and glory from God the Father when the Majestic Glory spoke to him: “This is my beloved Son, with whom I am delighted.”{g}
We ourselves heard this voice carried from heaven when we were with him on the holy mountain.
And we have the prophetic word made more certain, and you do well to pay attention to it as to a lamp shining in a dark place, until the day dawns and the morning star rises in your hearts.{h}
Know this first of all, that no prophecy of scripture comes from one’s own interpretation.
No prophecy ever came about because a human being willed it; rather, borne along by the Holy Spirit, human beings spoke as messengers from God.{i}

notes.text: *Simon*: Greek form of the Hebrew *Shimʿon*, “he has heard.” Some manuscripts read *Symeōn*, “Simeon,” the form closer to the Hebrew. *Peter*: “rock.” *Our God and Savior Jesus Christ*: or “our God and the Savior Jesus Christ.”
By his own glory and excellence: some manuscripts read “to glory and excellence.” *Excellence*: Greek *aretē*, “virtue,” “moral excellence.”
Brothers: Greek *adelphoi*, here in the compound *philadelphia*, which includes sisters.
Tent: that is, the body; compare 2 Cor 5:1, 4.
Compare John 21:18–19.
Gone: Greek *exodos*, “departure,” “exodus,” here meaning death.
Compare Matt 17:5; Mark 9:7; Luke 9:35. *Majestic Glory*: a reverent way of referring to God.
Morning star: Greek *phōsphoros*, “light-bringer,” the planet Venus seen before dawn.
Human beings spoke as messengers from God: some manuscripts read “holy people of God spoke.”

verses.text: But false prophets also appeared among the people, and likewise false teachers will arise among you. They will quietly introduce destructive heresies, even denying the Master who bought them, bringing swift destruction on themselves.{a}
Many will take up their licentious ways, and through them the way of the truth will be brought into disrepute.
In their greed they will exploit you with fabricated words. Their condemnation, pronounced long ago, is not idle, and their destruction is not asleep.
For if God did not spare angels when they sinned, but cast them into Tartarus and committed them to pits of gloom to be kept until the judgment;{b}
if he did not hold back from punishing the world of old, but kept Noah safe, a preacher of righteousness, together with seven others, when he let loose the flood upon a godless world;{c}
if by reducing the cities of Sodom and Gomorrah to ashes he condemned them, making them an example of what is coming for the ungodly;{d}
and if he rescued righteous Lot, who was worn down by the debauched conduct of lawless people{e}
(that good man, dwelling in their midst, was in anguish of soul from day to day at the lawless acts he witnessed and heard of),
then the Lord is well able to deliver the devout out of testing and to hold the wicked in custody for punishment on the day of judgment,
and above all those who chase after the flesh with polluted craving and treat lordship with contempt. ¶Insolent and headstrong, they have no fear in reviling the glorious ones,{f}
whereas angels, though greater in strength and power, do not bring a blasphemous judgment against them before the Lord.{g}

These people, though, are like brute beasts, mere creatures of nature, born to be trapped and killed; they rail at what they know nothing about, and like those beasts they will perish in their corruption,
being wronged as the reward of their own wrong. Indulgence in broad daylight is their idea of pleasure. They are spots and disgraces, luxuriating in their deceits even as they share your table.{h}
Their eyes are full of an adulteress and never stop sinning. They lure the unsteady. Their hearts are well practiced in greed. Children under a curse!
They have left the straight path and wandered off, following the path of Balaam son of Beor, who loved payment for wickedness,{i}
but he was taken to task for his offense: a dumb beast of burden spoke in a man’s voice and checked the prophet’s folly.
These people are dried-up springs and clouds blown by a gale. The deepest darkness is kept in store for them.{j}
For, uttering loud boasts of folly, they entice by sensual desires of the flesh those who are barely escaping from people who live in error.
Freedom is what they offer, while they are themselves in bondage to decay; for a person is the slave of whatever has mastered him.

For if they have escaped the world’s corruptions by knowing our Lord and Savior Jesus Christ, and then become entangled in them again and are defeated, their final condition is worse than their first.{k}
Better for them never to have come to know the road of righteousness than to know it and then turn their backs on the holy command handed down to them.
In them the true proverb has come to pass: “The dog has gone back to what it threw up,” and, “The washed pig has gone back to roll in the mud.”{l}

notes.text: Heresies: or “factions.” *Master*: Greek *despotēs*.

Tartarus: in Greek myth, the deepest part of the underworld, where rebellious powers were confined; compare 1 Enoch 10:4–6; 20:2. *Pits*: Westcott and Hort read *sirois*, “pits,” with Sinaiticus, Alexandrinus and Vaticanus as reported; other manuscripts read *seirais*, “chains.”
Gen 6–8. *Noah*: “rest.” *With seven others*: literally “as the eighth.”
Gen 19:24–28. *Sodom* and *Gomorrah*: the meanings of the names are uncertain. *Of what is coming for the ungodly*: some manuscripts read “to those who would live ungodly lives.”
*Lot*: perhaps “covering.”
Glorious ones: Greek *doxai*, “glories,” probably angelic beings.
Before the Lord: Westcott and Hort bracket these words; some manuscripts lack them. Compare Jude 9.

Being wronged: Westcott and Hort read *adikoumenoi* with P72 and Vaticanus as reported; many manuscripts read *komioumenoi*, “receiving.” *Deceptions*: some manuscripts read “love feasts,” as in Jude 12.
Num 22–24. *Balaam*: of uncertain meaning, perhaps “devourer.” *Beor*: perhaps “burning.” Some manuscripts read *Bosor*.
Later manuscripts add “forever.”
Compare Matt 12:45; Luke 11:26.
Prov 26:11. The second saying is not from the Old Testament; a similar proverb appears in the story of Ahiqar.

verses.text: Dear friends, this is already my second letter to you, and in each I aim to rouse your pure minds by reminding you,{a}
so that you will recall what the holy prophets said long ago and the command of the Lord and Savior delivered by your apostles.
Above all, understand this: in the final days mockers will come, ridiculing and following their own desires,
and saying, “Where is the promise of his coming? Since the fathers fell asleep, everything goes on as it has since the beginning of creation.”{b}
For they deliberately overlook this fact, that long ago the heavens existed and the earth was formed out of water and through water by the word of God,{c}
and that through these the world of that time was flooded with water and perished.
But by the same word the present heavens and earth are being stored up for fire, kept until the day of judgment and destruction of the ungodly.
Dear friends, do not let this one thing escape your notice: with the Lord a single day is as a thousand years, and a thousand years as a single day.{d}
The Lord is not slow to keep his promise, as some reckon slowness. He is patient toward you, not wanting anyone to be lost, but wanting all to find their way to repentance.{e}

But the day of the Lord will come like a thief, and on it the heavens will pass away with a roar, and the elements will be dissolved with burning heat, and the earth and the works in it will be found.{f}
