Every inhabitant of the earth will worship it, all those whose names were not recorded, from the world’s founding, in the book of life belonging to the slaughtered Lamb.{h}
If anyone has an ear, let him listen:
Then I saw a second beast ascending from the earth, with two horns like those of a lamb, yet it spoke like a dragon.
It wields all the authority of the first beast, acting before its eyes, and it causes the earth and those living on it to worship the first beast, the one whose deadly wound had been healed.{j}
It performs great signs, even bringing fire down out of heaven onto the earth in full view of everyone.{k}
Through the signs it was permitted to do before the beast, it misleads those living on the earth, instructing them to fashion an image of the beast who had received the sword stroke and yet lived.
It was also permitted to impart a spirit to the beast’s statue, so that the statue itself would talk and would bring about the execution of all who would not bow before it.{l}
Everyone, the lowly and the mighty, the wealthy and the needy, the free and the enslaved, it compels to receive a mark on the right hand or the forehead,{m}
so that nobody can buy or sell without having the mark—the name of the beast or the number that stands for its name.{n}
Here is wisdom: whoever has insight should calculate the beast’s number, for it stands for a person; its number is 666.{o}

notes.text: And it took its stand on the sand of the seashore: many modern editions number these words 12:18. *It* is the dragon; later manuscripts read “I stood,” attaching the words to John’s vision. *Names of blasphemy*: some manuscripts read “a name of blasphemy.” Compare Dan 7:2–7.
Compare Dan 7:4–6.
Slaughtered to death: the same Greek word that is used of the Lamb in 5:6.
Compare Exod 15:11.
Compare Dan 7:8, 11, 20, 25. Westcott and Hort bracket “and” in the Greek number.
His tent: that is, his dwelling place. Later manuscripts read “his tent and those who live in heaven.”
Leave was given it, too, to make war on the saints and defeat them: Westcott and Hort bracket these words, which P47, Alexandrinus and Ephraemi omit. Compare Dan 7:21.

Since the founding of the world: these words may instead go with “slain,” “the Lamb slain since the founding of the world”; compare 17:8. *Everyone whose name*: literally “whose name,” in the singular.

Jer 15:2; 43:11. *Kills*: Westcott and Hort read “will kill”; Alexandrinus, as reported, reads “is to be killed,” which would yield the sense that anyone fated to be slain by the sword is slain by it. *Here the saints are called to*: literally “here is the endurance and the faith of the saints.”
On its behalf: literally “before it,” “in its presence.”
Compare 1 Kgs 18:38.
Breath: or “spirit.” Westcott and Hort bracket the Greek conjunction before “everyone.” Compare Dan 3:5–6.
Mark: Greek *charagma*, a brand or stamp; the word was also used of the impression on coins and official seals.
So that: Westcott and Hort bracket “and” before these words.

Work out: literally “count,” “reckon,” using the ancient practice of giving each letter a numerical value (gematria). *A human number*: or “the number of a person.” *Six hundred and sixty-six*: so Westcott and Hort and most manuscripts. P115 (3rd–4th century), Codex Ephraemi and some others read “six hundred and sixteen,” and Irenaeus (about AD 180) knew of copies with that number. Both totals can be obtained from the Hebrew letters of “Nero Caesar” in different spellings, though many other solutions have been proposed.

verses.text: I looked, and the Lamb was there, standing on Mount Zion! Along with him, 144,000 people bore on their foreheads his name and the name of his Father.{a}
And out of heaven I heard a sound like the rushing of great waters and like loud thunder rolling; the voice that I heard was like that of harpists accompanying themselves on their harps.

They sing what seems a new song before the throne and before the four living creatures and the elders. And none was able to learn the song except for those 144,000 who have been bought out of the earth.

They are the ones who kept themselves unsoiled by women, being virgins; they are the followers of the Lamb, going wherever he leads. They were bought out of humanity as firstfruits offered to God and to the Lamb,{b}
and in their speech no lie was found; they are without blemish.{c}
Next I saw another angel in flight high overhead, bringing an everlasting gospel to announce to earth’s inhabitants, to every nation, tribe, tongue and people.{d}
With a loud voice he said, “Fear God and give him glory, for the hour of his judgment has arrived. Worship the maker of heaven and earth, of the sea and the springs of water.”{e}
Another angel, a second, followed and said, “She has fallen! Fallen is Babylon the great, who gave all the nations a drink of the wine of her raging immorality!”{f}
Next, a third angel came after them, saying in a mighty voice, “If anyone worships the beast and its statue, and gets a mark on his forehead or on his hand,
he too will drink the wine of God’s anger, mixed full strength in the cup of his wrath. He will be tortured in fire and brimstone before the holy angels and before the Lamb.{g}
The smoke of their torment goes up forever and ever. Day and night there is no rest for those who worship the beast and its image, or for anyone who takes the mark of its name.”{h}
Here is the call for endurance on the part of the holy people, who keep God’s commandments and the faith of Jesus.{i}

And I heard a voice speak from heaven: “Write: Blessed from this moment are the dead who die in the Lord.” “Yes,” the Spirit says, “let them find relief from their labors, for their deeds accompany them.”{j}
As I watched, a white cloud appeared, and on it sat someone resembling a son of man; on his head was a crown of gold, and in his hand a keen-edged sickle.{k}

And a different angel emerged from the temple, shouting with a powerful voice to the one who sat upon the cloud: “Send out your sickle and harvest, for the hour to harvest has come, because the earth’s crop has dried out.”{l}
He who sat on the cloud cast his sickle onto the earth, and the earth’s harvest was gathered in.
Out of the heavenly temple came yet another angel, and he as well held a keen-edged sickle.

And from the altar there came out yet another angel, who has charge over the fire. He called out with a strong voice to the holder of the sharp sickle, “Send out your sharp sickle and collect the clusters of grapes on the earth’s vine, for its grapes have reached full ripeness.”{m}
The angel cast his sickle onto the earth and harvested its grapes, flinging them into the vast winepress of God’s fury.
Outside the city the grapes were trampled in the press, and out of it poured blood, rising to the horses’ bridles, across a distance of about 180 miles.{n}

notes.text: Zion: the hill of Jerusalem’s temple, and a name for the city; perhaps “fortress.” *His name and*: later manuscripts omit these words.
Virgins: Greek *parthenoi*, here masculine, perhaps picturing holy-war purity (compare Deut 23:9–10; 1 Sam 21:5) or faithfulness to God in contrast with spiritual prostitution.
Compare Zeph 3:13; Isa 53:9. Later manuscripts add “before the throne of God.”
Gospel: Greek *euangelion*, “good news.” *Another*: some manuscripts omit this word.
The hour: the appointed time, not a time of day. Compare Exod 20:11; Ps 146:6.

Isa 21:9; Jer 51:7–8. *Babylon*: the Greek form of the Hebrew *Bavel*; the Akkadian *Bab-ili* means “gate of god,” while Gen 11:9 links it with Hebrew *balal*, “confuse.” Here it is a code name for a great city, probably Rome (compare 1 Pet 5:13). *Passionate immorality*: literally “the wine of the passion of her immorality”; the Greek *thymos* can mean both “passion” and “wrath.” *A second angel*: Westcott and Hort bracket “angel.”
Compare Isa 51:17; Jer 25:15; Gen 19:24.
Compare Isa 34:10.
The faith of Jesus: or “their faith in Jesus,” or “faithfulness to Jesus.”
From now on: the Greek *ap’ arti* may instead go with what follows: “From now on, yes, says the Spirit.”
Ripe: literally “dried,” that is, fully ripe. Compare Joel 3:13.
Came: Westcott and Hort bracket this verb and the article before “who has authority.” *Authority over the fire*: compare 8:3–5.
About 180 miles: Greek “1,600 stadia,” about 300 km; a stadion was about 607 feet (185 m). The number may be symbolic (40 × 40, or 4 × 4 × 100). Compare Isa 63:1–6; Joel 3:13.

verses.text: And I saw another portent in heaven, large and astonishing: seven angels holding the seven final plagues, since by them God’s wrath is completed.
I also saw what looked like a glassy sea mingled with fire, and the victors over the beast, over its likeness, and over its name’s number stood beside the glassy sea, holding God’s harps.{a}

They are chanting the song of Moses, God’s slave, and the song of the Lamb:
“Mighty and astonishing are the things you do,
O Lord God, Ruler over all!
Upright and true are your paths,
King of the ages!{b}

Lord, who will fail to fear you
and give glory to your name?
You alone are holy.
Every nation will come
and bow low before you,
for your judgments stand revealed.”{c}
After these things I saw it: the sanctuary of the tent of testimony in heaven was opened,{d}
and the seven angels holding the seven plagues emerged from it, clothed in stone, pure and shining, and wearing gold sashes about their breasts.{e}
Then one of the four living creatures gave the seven angels seven golden bowls full of the wrath of God, who lives forever and ever.
And the temple was filled with smoke from the glory of God and from his power, and no one could enter the temple until the seven plagues of the seven angels were completed.{f}

notes.text: Beside: or “on.” *Harps of God*: that is, harps given by God, or harps for the worship of God.

Exod 15:1–18; Deut 32:4; Ps 111:2; 139:14. *Moses*: explained in Exod 2:10 by Hebrew *mashah*, “draw out.” *Lord God Almighty*: see the note on 1:8. *King of the ages*: so Westcott and Hort, with P47 and Sinaiticus as first written; Alexandrinus and many others read “King of the nations,” and later manuscripts “King of the saints.”
Jer 10:7; Ps 86:9; Mal 1:11. In Jer 10:7 the Hebrew has no divine name; in Ps 86:9 it has *ʾAdonay*, “Lord.”
Tent of testimony: the tabernacle (Exod 38:21; 40:34–35 in the Greek Old Testament).

Clothed in stone: so Westcott and Hort, following Alexandrinus and Ephraemi, perhaps picturing robes set with precious stones (compare Ezek 28:13). Many manuscripts read *linon*, “linen,” for *lithon*, “stone.” Westcott and Hort bracket the article before “with the seven plagues.”
Compare Exod 40:34–35; 1 Kgs 8:10–11; Isa 6:4.

verses.text: A loud voice from the temple then called to the seven angels, “Go, empty the seven bowls of God’s fury onto the earth.”
The first angel went off and emptied his bowl onto the land, and ugly, festering sores appeared on those who wore the beast’s mark and bowed down to its image.{a}
Then the second angel emptied his bowl into the sea, and the water turned into blood like a dead man’s, and every living creature in the sea perished.{b}
Then the third emptied his bowl into the rivers and the water sources, and these turned into blood.
The fourth emptied his bowl onto the sun, and the sun was permitted to burn people with its fire.
People were seared by tremendous heat, and they cursed God’s name—the God who holds power over these plagues—and refused to repent and to glorify him.
Then the fifth emptied his bowl onto the throne of the beast, and its realm was darkened. People chewed their tongues in anguish{e}
and reviled the God of heaven for their sufferings and sores, yet they did not repent of their works.
Then the sixth emptied his bowl onto the great Euphrates River. Its water dried up, so that a road lay ready for the kings from the east.{f}
And from the dragon’s mouth, from the mouth of the beast, and from the mouth of the false prophet, I watched three unclean spirits emerge, which resembled frogs.{g}
These are spirits of demons that do signs; they travel out to the rulers of the entire world to gather them for the war of that great day belonging to God, the Almighty.
(“Notice, I come as a thief does! Happy is the one who stays alert and holds on to his clothing, so that he need not walk naked and have his shame seen.”)
And they gathered the kings together at the place that is called Harmagedon in Hebrew.{h}
The seventh angel emptied his bowl upon the air, and from the sanctuary, from the throne, a great voice called, “It is finished!”{i}
Lightning flashed, there was rumbling and thunder, and a great earthquake struck, the like of which had not happened since humans first lived on the earth, so violent was the quake.{j}
The great city broke into three pieces, and the nations’ cities collapsed. Babylon the great came to mind before God, and he made her drink the cup brimming with the wine of his fierce anger.
Every island vanished; the mountains were nowhere to be seen.
And great hailstones, weighing about a talent, fell from the sky upon people, and people blasphemed God because of the plague of hail; for that plague was extremely severe.{k}

notes.text: Compare Exod 9:9–11.
Compare Exod 7:17–21.
The Holy One: Westcott and Hort bracket the article. Later manuscripts read “and who will be.”
Lord God, the Almighty: see the note on 1:8. Compare Ps 19:9.
Compare Exod 10:21–23.
From the east: literally “from the rising of the sun.” Westcott and Hort bracket the article before “Euphrates.” Compare Isa 11:15; Jer 50:38.
Compare Exod 8:2–7.
Harmagedon: traditionally “Armageddon”; probably Hebrew *har Megiddo*, “mountain of Megiddo,” the site of famous battles (Judg 5:19; 2 Kgs 23:29). Some manuscripts read “Mageddon.”
From the throne: later manuscripts read “of heaven, from the throne.”
Compare Dan 12:1.
About seventy pounds: literally “about a talent’s weight”; the talent was the largest ancient unit of weight, about 30–35 kg (65–75 pounds), though its value varied. Compare Exod 9:23–25.

verses.text: Then there came one of the seven angels who had been carrying the seven bowls, and he told me, “Come along! I will let you see the condemnation of the notorious prostitute who sits beside the many waters,{a}
the one with whom earth’s kings have committed immorality, and with the wine of whose immorality the earth’s inhabitants have grown drunk.”
In the Spirit he took me away to a wilderness. There I noticed a woman seated upon a scarlet beast that was covered with blasphemous names and had seven heads and ten horns.
The woman wore purple and scarlet, and was resplendent with gold, jewels, and pearls. A gold cup brimming with detestable things and with the foulness of her immorality was in her hand.{b}
Across her forehead a name was written, a mystery: “Babylon the great, mother of the prostitutes and of the abominations of the earth.”{c}
The woman, I noticed, was drunk with the blood of the holy people and with the blood of Jesus’s witnesses. And when I saw her, I wondered greatly.{d}
The angel said, “Why do you wonder? Let me explain the secret of the woman, and of the beast that bears her, which has seven heads and ten horns.

The beast that you saw existed once and exists no longer; it is going to rise from the abyss and then head for ruin. Earth’s inhabitants whose names have not, since the world was founded, been entered in the book of life will marvel at the sight of the beast, because it existed once, exists no longer, and yet will appear.{e}
Here is something that calls for a mind with insight: the seven heads stand for seven hills, where the woman has her seat. They also stand for seven kings;{f}
five are fallen, one is living, and the last has still to come; and whenever he comes, he is to remain a little while.
As for the beast that once was and now is not, it is itself an eighth, but it springs from the seven, and it is heading for destruction.
The ten horns that you saw are ten kings. They have not yet received a kingdom, but for a single hour they receive authority as kings alongside the beast.{g}
They share a single purpose, and they surrender their might and their authority to the beast.
These will fight against the Lamb, yet the Lamb will triumph over them, because Lord of lords he is, and King of kings; and with him are the called, the chosen, and the faithful ones.”{h}
He says to me: “Those waters that you saw, on which the prostitute is seated, stand for peoples and crowds and nations and languages.
And the ten horns you saw, along with the beast—they will hate the prostitute, strip her of everything and leave her naked, eat her flesh, and burn what remains of her with fire.{i}
It is God who has moved their hearts to accomplish his intention, to act with one accord and yield their royal power to the beast until what God has spoken comes to pass.
The woman you saw is the great city that holds sovereignty over the kings of the earth.”

notes.text: Beside many waters: compare Jer 51:13, of Babylon on the Euphrates and its canals.
Compare Jer 51:7.
A mystery: or “a name of mystery,” that is, a symbolic name.
Witnesses: Greek *martyres*, the source of the English word “martyrs.”
Compare Dan 7:3.
Mountains: Greek *orē*, “mountains” or “hills”; Rome was famous as the city of seven hills. *They are also seven kings*: in the Greek these words begin verse 10.
For a single hour: that is, for a very short time. Compare Dan 7:24.
Compare Deut 10:17; Dan 2:47.
In fire: Westcott and Hort bracket the Greek preposition.

verses.text: After these things I saw a different angel coming down out of heaven. He possessed great authority, and the earth shone with his glory.{a}

He shouted in a mighty voice:
“Fallen, fallen is Babylon the great!
She has turned into a dwelling for demons,
a lockup for every unclean spirit,
a lockup for every unclean and loathsome bird,
and a lockup for every unclean and loathsome beast.{b}

For from the wine of her passionate immorality
all the nations have drunk,
and the kings of the earth fornicated with her,
and the merchants of the earth grew rich
from the power of her luxury.”{c}

Another voice from heaven I heard, crying,
“My people, leave her,
so you take no part in her sins
and no portion of her plagues;{d}

For her sins have piled up to the sky,
and God has recalled her crimes.{e}

Therefore, in a single day her plagues will arrive:
pestilence, mourning, and famine,
and she will be consumed by fire,
for strong is the Lord God who has judged her.”{h}
The kings of the earth, who were immoral with her and shared her luxury, will weep and mourn over her as they see the smoke of her burning.

Keeping their distance for terror at her torment, they will cry,
“Alas, alas, great city,
Babylon, city of might!
In a single hour your doom has fallen!”{i}
And the merchants of the earth are weeping and mourning over her, because nobody buys their merchandise any longer:{j}

a cargo of gold, silver, jewels, and pearls; of fine linen, purple cloth, silk, and scarlet; of all kinds of citron wood and every article of ivory; of every article of expensive wood, and of bronze, iron, and marble;{k}
and cinnamon, spices, incense, perfume, and frankincense; and wine, oil, fine flour, and grain; and cattle and sheep and horses and carriages; and bodies—that is, human souls.{l}

“The ripe fruit you craved with all your soul
has left you,
and all your rich and dazzling things
are lost to you,
and never again will people find them.”{m}
Those who traded in these goods and made their fortunes from her will keep their distance, terrified at her torment, crying and mourning,

saying,
“Alas, alas, that great city,
which wore fine linen, purple, and scarlet,
and was gilded with gold,
with precious stones and pearls!{n}
In a single hour such great wealth was devastated!” ¶Every shipmaster, everyone sailing to any destination, the sailors, and all who make their living from the sea remained at a distance{o}
and shouted, as they saw the smoke rising from her burning, “Which city was like this great city?”{p}

They flung dust on their heads, crying and mourning, and they shouted,
“Alas, alas, great city,
whose costly wealth made rich
all who owned ships at sea!
In a single hour she is ruined.”{q}

Then one mighty angel picked up a boulder like a huge millstone and flung it into the sea, with these words:
“Just so, in a violent plunge,
Babylon the great city will be hurled down,
and nobody will find her again.{s}

In her the blood of prophets and of holy people was found,
together with the blood of everyone slaughtered on earth.”

notes.text: Compare Ezek 43:2.

Isa 21:9; 13:21; 34:11–15; Jer 50:39. *Prison*: or “lair.” *And a prison for every foul and hated beast*: so Alexandrinus and some other manuscripts; Westcott and Hort place these words in the margin and read “a prison for every foul and hated bird.”
Have fallen: so Westcott and Hort; many manuscripts read “have drunk.” *Wine*: Westcott and Hort bracket “the wine.”
Compare Jer 51:9.
Jer 50:29; Ps 137:8. Westcott and Hort bracket the article before “double.”
Single day: compare Isa 47:9. *The Lord God*: Westcott and Hort bracket “Lord.” Compare Jer 50:34, where the Hebrew has *Yahweh*.
Alas: Greek *ouai*, translated “woe” elsewhere. *In a single hour*: that is, suddenly; not a clock time. So also verses 17 and 19.
Compare Ezek 27:1–36, the lament over Tyre.
Citron wood: a fragrant North African wood prized for luxury tables.

Spice: Greek *amōmon*, an aromatic plant from India. *Ointment*: Greek *myron*, perfumed oil. *Bodies*: Greek *sōmata*, a common term for slaves in commercial documents. *Even human lives*: literally “and souls of people”; compare Ezek 27:13.
No one will find them: literally “they will never find them.”
With gold: Westcott and Hort bracket the Greek preposition.
Everyone who sails anywhere: literally “everyone sailing to a place”; later manuscripts read “all the company on ships.”
Compare Ezek 27:32.
Compare Ezek 27:30.
Has given judgment for you against her: literally “has judged your judgment from her.” Compare Deut 32:43.
Compare Jer 51:63–64.
Of any trade: Westcott and Hort bracket these words. Compare Ezek 26:13; Jer 25:10.
Jer 7:34; 16:9; 25:10; Isa 23:8. Westcott and Hort bracket the article before “merchants.”

verses.text:
because true and just are his judgments.
He condemned the great prostitute,
the one who corrupted the earth by her immorality,
and he has taken vengeance on her for the blood of his slaves.”{b}

The twenty-four elders and the four living creatures fell prostrate and worshiped the God seated on the throne, saying,
“Amen! Hallelujah!”{d}

A voice came out of the throne, and it said,
“Give praise to our God,
all his slaves,
and those who fear him,
the small and the great.”{e}

Then I heard what seemed the voice of an immense multitude, like the sound of rushing water and like the rumble of loud thunder, saying,
“Hallelujah!
Because the Lord our God,
the Almighty, has taken up his reign.{f}

and she was given clothing
of bright, clean fine linen to wear.”
(The fine linen, you see, stands for the righteous deeds of the holy people.)
Then he told me, “Write: Blessed are the people invited to the marriage banquet of the Lamb!” And he told me, “These words are God’s own truth.”{h}

I threw myself down in front of his feet to worship him. But he told me, “Never do that! I am only a slave like you and your brothers who maintain the testimony of Jesus. Worship God! The testimony about Jesus is what inspires prophecy.”{i}
Then I saw heaven standing open, and a white horse appeared. Its rider is named Faithful and True, and he judges and wages war in righteousness.{j}
His eyes blaze like fire, and many diadems are on his head. A name is inscribed on him that no one understands but he himself.{k}
He is clothed in a robe sprinkled with blood, and his name is called the Word of God.{l}
Heaven’s armies rode behind him on white horses, dressed in pure white linen.

A sharp sword extends from his mouth, so that with it he may strike the nations; he will shepherd them with a rod of iron. And he himself treads the winepress that holds the fierce wrath of God the Almighty.{m}
The title “King of kings and Lord of lords” is inscribed upon his cloak, on his thigh.
Then I noticed an angel standing in the sun. He called out in a mighty voice to every bird that flies across midheaven: “Come, assemble for God’s great banquet,{n}
so that you may eat the flesh of kings, of generals, and of the strong; the flesh of horses and of those who sit on them; and the flesh of everyone, free and slave, small and great.”{o}
I saw the beast as well, and earth’s kings and their armies, mustered to do battle with the horse’s rider and his army.

The beast was seized, and so was the false prophet who had done the signs in its presence, signs that had misled those who took the beast’s mark and bowed down to its image. Both of them were flung alive into the fiery lake that blazes with sulfur.
All the others were slain by the sword that issues from the rider’s mouth, and every bird ate its fill of their flesh.

notes.text: Hallelujah: Hebrew *halelu-yah*, “praise Yah,” *Yah* being a short form of *Yahweh*. In the New Testament the word occurs only in this chapter (verses 1, 3, 4, 6).
Deut 32:43; 2 Kgs 9:7. *On her*: literally “from her hand.”
Our God: Westcott and Hort bracket “our.” *The Lord our God, the Almighty*: see the note on 1:8. Compare Ps 93:1; 97:1, where the Hebrew has *Yahweh*.
Bride: literally “wife.”
The angel: Greek “he”; compare 17:1.
Brothers: Greek *adelphoi*, which includes sisters. *The testimony of Jesus*: either the witness Jesus gave, or the witness borne to him.
Is called: Westcott and Hort bracket this word. Compare Isa 11:4.
Later manuscripts add “names written and” before “a name written.”
Sprinkled: so Westcott and Hort, following some manuscripts; Alexandrinus and most others read “dipped in.” Compare Isa 63:1–3.
Ps 2:9; Isa 11:4; 63:3. Later manuscripts read “two-edged sword.”
With a loud voice: Westcott and Hort bracket the Greek preposition.
Ezek 39:17–20. *Commanders*: see the note on 6:15.

verses.text: And I saw an angel come down from heaven; in his hand he held the key of the abyss, together with a massive chain.
He seized the dragon, that ancient serpent, who is the devil and Satan, and bound him fast for a thousand years.{a}

He flung it into the abyss, closed it up, and set a seal over it, so that it could no longer mislead the nations until the thousand years should be completed. After that it must be let loose for a short while.

I saw thrones, and they sat upon them, and judgment was given to them. I saw too the souls of those beheaded for the testimony of Jesus and for the word of God, and of those who did not bow to the beast or to its image, and did not accept the mark upon their forehead and upon their hand. They lived and ruled with Christ a thousand years.{b}
The rest of the dead had no new life until the thousand years ended. This is the first resurrection.

Blessed—and holy—are those who have a place in the first resurrection. Over them the second death holds no authority; instead they will be priests belonging to God and to Christ, and for those thousand years they will reign with him.{c}
When the thousand years have run their course, Satan will be released from his prison.
He will go out to mislead the nations at the earth’s four corners, Gog and Magog, and to muster them for battle; they are as countless as the sand along the sea.{d}
They advanced over the breadth of the earth and besieged the camp of the holy people, the city that he loves. Then fire fell from heaven and consumed them.{e}

As for the devil who had led them astray, he was cast into the lake of burning sulfur, in which the beast and the false prophet are also found; there they will be in torment by day and by night through all the ages.
Then I saw a great white throne, with the one seated upon it. Earth and heaven fled from his face, and no place could be found for them.

And I saw the dead, important and unimportant alike, standing before the throne. Scrolls were unrolled; then another scroll was unrolled—the scroll of life. By the contents of the scrolls the dead were judged, each according to his deeds.{f}
The sea yielded up the dead it held; Death and Hades yielded up the dead they held; and each person was judged by what he had done.
Death and Hades were thrown into the lake of fire. This is the second death, the lake of fire.{g}
Whoever was not listed in the scroll of life was hurled into the pool of fire.

notes.text: A thousand years: Latin *millennium*; so also in verses 3–7.
Beheaded: literally “executed with the axe.” Compare Dan 7:9, 22.
For the thousand years: Westcott and Hort bracket “the.”
Gog and Magog: compare Ezek 38–39, where Gog is a ruler “of the land of Magog”; the meaning of the names is uncertain. Here both stand for the hostile nations.
Compare 2 Kgs 1:10–12; Ezek 38:22. Later manuscripts read “from God out of heaven.”
Compare Dan 7:10; 12:1.
The lake of fire: Westcott and Hort print these words at the end of the verse; some manuscripts omit them.

verses.text: Then I saw a new heaven and a new earth, for the first heaven and the first earth had vanished, and the sea is no more.{a}
I saw the holy city too—a new Jerusalem—descending from God out of heaven, adorned like a bride made ready for her husband.{b}

A loud voice from the throne declared:
“Look! God’s tent is among human beings.
He will pitch it among them,
and they will be his peoples,
with God himself present among them as their God.{c}
Then the one seated on the throne declared, “Look, I make everything new!” And he said, “Write this down, because these words are faithful and true.”{e}
Then he said to me, “They have come to pass! I am the Alpha and the Omega, the beginning and the end. To the thirsty one I will give as a gift out of the spring of life-giving water.{f}
Whoever conquers will have this as an inheritance; I will be his God, and he will be my son.{g}

But for the cowards, the unbelieving, the vile, murderers, fornicators, sorcerers, idolaters, and all liars: the lake that blazes with fire and sulfur will be their portion—this is the second death.”{h}

And there approached me one of those seven angels, those having the seven bowls that were filled with the final seven plagues; he spoke with me and said, “Come here; I will point out to you the bride, the Lamb’s wife.”
And in the Spirit he carried me off to a mountain great and high, and he displayed to me the holy city Jerusalem as it came down out of heaven from God,{i}
shining with the glory of God. Its radiance was like a rare jewel, like jasper, crystal clear.{j}
It had a wall, great and high; it had twelve gates, and over the gates twelve angels, and engraved names, which are those of the twelve tribes of Israel’s sons.{k}
There were three gates facing east, three facing north, three facing south, and three facing west.
The city’s wall rested on twelve foundations, and written on them were twelve names: those of the twelve apostles of the Lamb.
The one speaking with me had a golden measuring rod, in order to measure the city, along with its gates and its wall.{l}
The city lies foursquare, with its length equal to its width. With the rod he measured the city: about 1,400 miles. Its length, width, and height are identical.{m}
Its wall he also measured, 216 feet, using a human unit of measure, which was the angel’s.{n}
Its wall was constructed of jasper, and the city itself was pure gold, resembling clear glass.
The foundations of the city’s wall were adorned with all kinds of precious stones: the first foundation was jasper; the second, sapphire; the third, chalcedony; the fourth, emerald;{o}
the fifth sardonyx, the sixth carnelian, the seventh chrysolite, the eighth beryl, the ninth topaz, the tenth chrysoprase, the eleventh jacinth, the twelfth amethyst.{p}
And twelve pearls were the twelve gates—every gate fashioned from one single pearl. The city’s broad street was pure gold, transparent as glass.{q}
No temple did I see in it, for the Lord God, the Almighty, is its temple, and so is the Lamb.{r}
The city requires neither sun nor moon to shine upon it, since God’s glory gave it light, and it has the Lamb as its lamp.{s}
The nations will walk by means of its light, and the kings of the earth carry their glory into it.{t}
Its gates will not be closed by day—and night will not exist there.{u}
They will carry the glory and the honor of the nations into it.
Nothing profane will ever enter it, nor anyone who commits abomination and falsehood, only those whose names are written in the Lamb’s book of life.{v}

notes.text: Compare Isa 52:1; 61:10.
Lev 26:11–12; Ezek 37:27; Zech 2:10–11. *Dwelling*: literally “tent.” *Peoples*: so Westcott and Hort; many manuscripts read “people.” Some manuscripts add “as their God” at the end.
Compare Isa 43:19.
Isa 55:1. *They are accomplished*: literally “they have come to be.” *Alpha … Omega*: see the note on 1:8.
Echoing Ps 89:26–27 and 2 Sam 7:14.
The faithless: or “the unbelieving.” Later manuscripts add “and sinners” after “cowards.”
Compare Ezek 40:2.
Compare Isa 60:1–2, 19.
Compare Ezek 48:30–35.
Compare Ezek 40:3–5.

About 1,400 miles: Greek “12,000 stadia,” about 2,200 km; a stadion was about 607 feet (185 m). The number is symbolic (12 × 1,000). The city is a cube, like the inner sanctuary of Solomon’s temple (1 Kgs 6:20).

216 feet: Greek “144 cubits,” about 65 m; a cubit was about 18 inches (45 cm). The figure (12 × 12) may refer to the wall’s height or its thickness. *A human unit of measure, which was the angel’s*: literally “a measure of a man, which is of an angel.”

The identification of several of these stones with their modern namesakes is uncertain. Compare the stones of the high priest’s breastpiece (Exod 28:17–20) and of Ezek 28:13. *Sapphire*: probably lapis lazuli.
Carnelian: Greek *sardion*; see the note on 4:3. *Chrysolite*: literally “gold stone,” perhaps a yellow topaz. *Topaz*: perhaps peridot. *Jacinth*: Greek *hyakinthos*, a blue or violet stone.
Compare Isa 54:11–12.
The Lord God, the Almighty: see the note on 1:8.
Isa 60:3, 5, 11. Later manuscripts read “the nations of those who are saved.”
Isa 52:1. *Anyone who commits*: Westcott and Hort bracket the article.

verses.text: Then he showed me a river of water that gives life, as clear as crystal, issuing from the throne belonging to God and to the Lamb{a}

midway along the city’s broad street; and on this bank and that of the river stood a tree of life, which yields twelve harvests, rendering its fruit month by month. The tree’s leaves serve to heal the nations.{b}
No accursed thing will exist any longer. In the city will stand the throne of God and the Lamb, and his slaves will worship him;{c}
they will see his face, and his name will be on their foreheads.{d}
And night will exist no longer; nor will they need the light of a lamp or of the sun, for the Lord God will cast his light on them; and they will rule as kings for ever and ever.{e}
And the angel said to me, “These words are faithful and true. The Lord, the God of the spirits of the prophets, commissioned his angel to show his slaves the things that must soon take place.”{f}
“Look, I am on my way soon! Blessed is whoever heeds the prophetic words of this book.”
I, John, am the one who heard these things and saw them. After I had heard and seen, I prostrated myself in homage at the angel’s feet—the angel who was pointing these things out to me.
But he said to me, “Do not do that! I am a slave together with you, with your brothers the prophets, and with those who keep the words of this book. Worship God.”{g}
And he told me, “Do not seal up the words of this book’s prophecy, for the time is near.{h}
Let the one who does wrong go on doing wrong, and let the one who is filthy go on being filthy; let the righteous go on practicing righteousness, and let the holy go on being made holy.”{i}
“Look, I am on my way soon, and my reward is with me, to give to each one as his work deserves.{j}
I am the Alpha and the Omega, the first and the last, the beginning and the end.”
Blessed are those who wash their robes, so that the tree of life will be theirs by right, and they may enter the city through its gates.{k}
Outside are the dogs, the sorcerers, the sexually immoral, the murderers, the idolaters, and everyone who loves and practices falsehood.{l}
“I, Jesus, have sent my angel to testify these things to you about the churches. I am the descendant of David and the root from which he sprang, the bright star of the morning.”{m}
The Spirit and the bride are saying, “Come!” And whoever hears should also say, “Come!” Whoever is thirsty should come; whoever wishes should receive the water of life as a gift.{n}
I give this warning to everyone who hears the words of this book’s prophecy: should anyone add to them, God will lay on him the plagues described in this book;{o}
and if anyone cuts anything from the words of the book containing this prophecy, God will cut off his allotment, whether in the tree of life or in the holy city—things written about in this book.{p}
The one who gives these testimonies says, “Certainly, I am on my way soon.” Amen! Come, Lord Jesus!{q}
The grace of the Lord Jesus be with the saints.{r}

notes.text: Tree of life: Gen 2:9; compare Ezek 47:12. *Down the middle of the city’s street*: these words may instead go with what follows: “Between the street and the river, on either side, stood the tree of life.” *Tree*: the Greek may be collective, “trees.”
Compare Zech 14:11.
Compare Ps 17:15; Exod 33:20.
Isa 60:19; Dan 7:18, 27. *Give them light*: Westcott and Hort bracket the Greek preposition “upon.”
The God of the spirits of the prophets: compare Num 16:22; 27:16. Later manuscripts read “the God of the holy prophets.”
Brothers: Greek *adelphoi*, which includes sisters.
Contrast Dan 12:4, 9.
Compare Dan 12:10.
Who wash their robes: so Westcott and Hort, with Sinaiticus and Alexandrinus; later manuscripts read “who do his commandments.”
Dogs: a term of contempt for the impure; compare Deut 23:18; Phil 3:2.
Isa 11:1, 10; Num 24:17. *To you*: the Greek is plural.
Compare Deut 4:2; 12:32.

Tree of life: so Westcott and Hort and the early Greek manuscripts. The King James Version’s “book of life” goes back to Erasmus, whose single Greek manuscript lacked the last verses of the book; he translated them from the Latin Vulgate, whose text in many copies reads *libro*, “book,” for *ligno*, “tree.”
Quickly: Greek *tachy*, also “soon,” as in 22:7, 12.

Lord Jesus: Westcott and Hort bracket “Christ” after “Jesus.” *With the saints*: so Westcott and Hort, with Sinaiticus; Alexandrinus reads “with all,” and later manuscripts “with you all” or “with all the saints.” Later manuscripts add “Amen.”

books.name: 1 Enoch
books.sourceNote: Translated from the Ethiopic (Ge‘ez) text of 1 Enoch as edited by R. H. Charles, *The Ethiopic Version of the Book of Enoch* (1906), with his revised translation-base of 1912, and A. Dillmann, *Liber Henoch aethiopice* (1851), both public domain. The Greek witnesses were compared where they survive: the Akhmim (Panopolitanus) codex for chapters 1–32, the excerpts in George Syncellus for parts of chapters 6–16, and the Chester Beatty–Michigan papyrus for chapters 97–107, as printed by Swete (1891–94), Charles (1912), and Flemming and Radermacher (1901). The Aramaic fragments from Qumran Cave 4 (4QEnᵃ⁻ᵍ and 4QEnastrᵃ⁻ᵈ, about 200 BC to the turn of the era) cover parts of every section except the Parables (chapters 37–71); readings from them are cited as reported in the standard editions and have not been checked against the manuscripts. R. H. Charles’s 1913 English translation (public domain) was consulted, but the English here is new. Ge‘ez *Egzi’abḥer* is rendered “the Lord” and *Amlāk* “God”; the divine name Yahweh does not appear in any surviving text of 1 Enoch, which prefers titles such as “the Great Holy One,” “the Lord of Spirits,” and “the Most High,” so it is not supplied here. **About the book.** 1 Enoch is a collection of five books ascribed to Enoch, the seventh from Adam (Gen 5:18–24): the Book of the Watchers (chapters 1–36, 3rd century BC), the Book of Parables or Similitudes (37–71, probably late 1st century BC or 1st century AD), the Astronomical Book (72–82, 3rd century BC or earlier), the Book of Dreams (83–90, about 165–160 BC), and the Epistle of Enoch (91–108, 2nd century BC), with an appendix on the birth of Noah (106–107) and a closing exhortation (108). It was composed in Aramaic (perhaps partly Hebrew), translated into Greek, and from Greek into Ge‘ez, probably in the 5th–6th centuries AD; the complete book survives only in Ethiopic manuscripts, the oldest from about the 15th century. The Letter of Jude quotes 1 Enoch 1:9 as a prophecy of “Enoch, the seventh from Adam” (Jude 14–15), and several early Christian writers valued the book. It is part of the Old Testament of the Ethiopian Orthodox Tewahedo Church and the Eritrean Orthodox Church, and of the Scriptures of Beta Israel; it is not in the canon of other Jewish or Christian communities. Verse numbering follows Charles. Chapters 91–93 are printed in the Ethiopic order; the Aramaic copy 4QEnᵍ reportedly places 91:11–17 after 93:1–10, which restores the “Apocalypse of Weeks” to its natural sequence (see the notes there). Calendar dates are given with modern-month equivalents and clock-like divisions are explained in notes, according to the CJT conventions.

verses.text: The words of blessing of Enoch,{a} with which he blessed the chosen{b} and the righteous who will be living in the day of distress, when all the wicked and the godless are to be removed.

He took up his discourse{c} and said: Enoch was a righteous man; God opened his eyes, and he saw a vision of the Holy One in heaven, which the angels showed me. From them I heard everything, and from them I understood what I saw, not for this generation but for one far off that is yet to come.

Concerning the chosen I spoke, and I took up my discourse about them:
The Great Holy One{d} will come out from his dwelling,

All will be struck with fear,
and the Watchers{g} will tremble,
and great fear and shaking will seize them to the ends of the earth.

notes.text: *Enoch*: Hebrew *Ḥanokh*, probably “dedicated” or “initiated.” He is the son of Jared and the seventh from Adam, who “walked with God” and was taken by God (Gen 5:18–24).
Chosen: Ge‘ez *ḥeruyān*, traditionally “the elect”; so throughout the book.
Discourse: Ge‘ez *messālē*, Greek *parabolē*, Aramaic *matla*: a solemn oracle or figurative speech, traditionally “parable.” So throughout.
The Great Holy One: so the Greek; the Ethiopic has “the Holy and Great One.” The Aramaic fragments reportedly use *qaddisha rabba*, “the Great Holy One,” a favorite title for God in this book.
Mount Sinai: compare Deut 33:2; Mic 1:3.
He will appear with his host: so the Greek, “he will appear out of his camp”; Charles regarded the line as a doublet of the next.
Watchers: Aramaic *‘irin*, “wakeful ones,” a class of angels (Dan 4:13, 17, 23). In this book the word usually refers to the angels who sinned (chapters 6–16).
Split wide apart: so the Greek; the Ethiopic reads “sink.”
Myriads of his holy ones: literally “ten thousands.” This verse is quoted in Jude 14–15. A fragment of the Aramaic (4QEnᶜ) reportedly preserves part of it.

verses.text: Consider everything that takes place in the sky: how the lights in the heavens do not change their paths, how each rises and sets in order at its own time and does not depart from its appointed law.
Look at the earth and pay attention to the things that happen on it from first to last: how steady they are, how nothing on earth changes, but all the works of God appear before you.
Consider summer and winter: in them the whole earth is full of water, and cloud, dew, and rain lie over it.

Observe and see how in winter every tree appears dried up, having dropped all its leaves, except fourteen trees that do not lose their foliage but keep the old leaves for two or three years until the new ones come.{a}

notes.text: Fourteen trees: so the Ethiopic; the Greek is lost here. The number may come from a list of evergreens in the Aramaic original, now lost.

verses.text: Observe again the days of summer, how the sun stands over the earth opposite it. You look for shade and shelter because of the heat of the sun, and the earth too burns with scorching heat, so that you cannot walk on the ground or on a rock because of its heat.
Observe how the trees clothe themselves with green leaves and bear fruit. So pay attention and understand all his works, and recognize that he who lives forever made them this way.
All his works go on in this way from year to year forever, and all the tasks that they perform for him; their tasks do not change, but everything is done as God has ordained.
See how the sea and the rivers likewise perform their tasks and do not depart from his commands.

But you have not stood firm,
and you have not done the commandments of the Lord.
You have turned aside and spoken proud and harsh words
with your unclean mouths against his greatness.
You hard-hearted, you will find no peace!

Therefore you will curse your days,
and the years of your life will perish;
the years of your destruction will be multiplied in an everlasting curse,
and you will find no mercy.

For the chosen there will be light and grace and peace,
and they will inherit the earth.

Then wisdom will be given to the chosen,
and they will all live and never sin again,
neither through godlessness nor through pride;
but those who have wisdom will be humble.

They will not go wrong again,
nor will they sin all the days of their life,
nor will they die from anger or wrath,
but they will complete the number of the days of their life.
Their lives will grow long in peace,
and the years of their joy will be many,
in everlasting gladness and peace,
all the days of their life.

notes.text: The righteous: this word is missing in the Ethiopic, which leaves a gap here; it is supplied from the sense and the Greek.

verses.text: Now when the human race had multiplied, in those days beautiful and lovely daughters were born to them.
The angels, the sons of heaven,{a} saw them and desired them, and they said to one another, “Come, let us choose wives for ourselves from the daughters of men and father children for ourselves.”
Shemihazah,{b} who was their leader, said to them, “I fear that you will not really agree to do this deed, and I alone will have to pay the penalty for a great sin.”
They all answered him, “Let us all swear an oath and bind ourselves by curses on one another not to give up this plan, but to carry it out.”
Then they all swore together and bound themselves by curses on one another to it.

They numbered two hundred in all, and in the days of Jared they descended{c} onto the peak of Mount Hermon.{d} They named it Mount Hermon because on it they had taken the oath and put themselves under curses.

These are the names of their leaders: Shemihazah, their leader; Arteqoph,{e} Ramtel, Kokabel, Tamiel, Ramiel, Danel, Ziqiel, Baraqel, Asael, Armaros, Batriel, Ananel, Zeqiel, Shamshiel, Sahriel, Turiel, Yomiel, and Sariel.
These are their chiefs over tens.{f}

notes.text: Sons of heaven: the angels; compare “sons of God” in Gen 6:2. Chapters 6–11 retell Gen 6:1–4.
*Shemihazah*: so the Aramaic and Greek; Ethiopic *Semyāzā*. The name probably means “the Name has seen” or “my name has seen.”
*Jared*: Hebrew *Yered*, “descent,” the father of Enoch (Gen 5:15–18). The book plays on the name: in his days the angels “descended.”
Hermon: the mountain is named from a root meaning “ban” or “devote under oath” (*ḥerem*); hence the wordplay with the curse-oath that they swore there. Compare Jubilees 4:15.

The names are given in the Aramaic forms where these are reported from the fragments, otherwise in the Greek or Ethiopic forms; the Ethiopic spellings are badly corrupted. Most are formed with *-el*, “God,” and a word for a natural phenomenon or skill. *Arteqoph* (Ethiopic *Arākiba*): “earth of the mighty one” (uncertain). *Ramtel* (Ethiopic *Rāmē’ēl*): “burning ash of God.” *Kokabel*: “star of God.” *Tamiel*: “perfection of God” (uncertain). *Ramiel*: “thunder of God” or “exalted of God.” *Danel*: “God has judged.” *Ziqiel* (Ethiopic *Ezeqeel*): “lightning flash of God.” *Baraqel*: “lightning of God.” *Asael*: “God has made.” *Armaros*: perhaps from *Hermoni*, “the one of Hermon.” *Batriel*: “rain of God” (uncertain). *Ananel*: “cloud of God.” *Zeqiel* (Ethiopic *Zaqiel*): “sparks of God.” *Shamshiel* (Ethiopic *Samsapeel*): “sun of God.” *Sahriel* (Ethiopic *Satarel*): “moon of God.” *Turiel*: “mountain of God.” *Yomiel*: “day of God.” *Sariel* (Ethiopic) or *Yehaddiel* (reported Aramaic): meaning uncertain.
Chiefs over tens: each of the twenty leaders (counting Shemihazah) commanded ten of the two hundred.

verses.text: These, and all the others with them, took wives for themselves; each chose one for himself, and they began to go in to them and to defile themselves with them. They taught them sorcery and spells, and the cutting of roots, and showed them plants.{a}
The women became pregnant and bore great giants, whose height was three thousand cubits.{b}
They consumed everything that people had produced, and when people could no longer support them,
the giants turned against them and devoured human beings.
They began to sin against the birds, the animals, the creeping things, and the fish, and to devour one another’s flesh, and they drank the blood.
Then the earth brought an accusation against the lawless ones.

notes.text: Plants: that is, the use of herbs for magic and medicine.

Three thousand cubits: about 4,500 feet (1,350 m), reckoning the cubit at 18 inches (45 cm). The Ethiopic has “ells” (cubits); some Greek witnesses, in Syncellus, add that the giants fathered Nephilim, and the Nephilim fathered the Eliud.

verses.text: Asael{a} taught people to make swords and knives, shields and breastplates. He showed them the metals of the earth and how to work them, and bracelets and ornaments, the use of antimony{b} and the painting of the eyelids, all kinds of precious stones, and all coloring dyes.
There was a great deal of godlessness; they committed sexual immorality, they were led astray, and they became corrupt in all their ways.

Shemihazah taught spells and the cutting of roots; Armaros, the undoing of spells; Baraqel, the reading of lightning; Kokabel, the signs of the stars; Ziqiel, the signs of the flashes; Arteqoph, the signs of the earth; Shamshiel, the signs of the sun; and Sahriel, the courses of the moon.{c}
As people were perishing, they cried out, and their cry went up to heaven.

notes.text: *Asael*: so the Aramaic, reportedly, and the Greek (*Asaēl*), one of the leaders listed at 6:7; the Ethiopic has *Azazel* here and elsewhere, the name of the figure in the Day of Atonement ritual (Lev 16:8–10), and the two figures were merged in the tradition. *Asael* means “God has made.”
Antimony: a black powder used as eye paint; compare 2 Kgs 9:30.

The skills match the names of the angels (see the note at 6:7). The Ethiopic list is shorter and corrupt (it has “Baraqiyal taught astrology, Kokabel the constellations, Ezeqeel the knowledge of the clouds”); this rendering follows the Greek more closely.

verses.text: Then Michael, Sariel,{a} Raphael, and Gabriel looked down from heaven and saw a great deal of blood being shed on the earth and all the lawlessness being done on the earth.
They said to one another, “The earth, stripped of its inhabitants,{b} raises the sound of their cry to the gates of heaven.
Now the souls of humankind are pleading with you, the holy ones of heaven: ‘Bring our case before the Most High.’”

They said to the Lord of the ages:{c} “You are Lord of lords, God of gods, King of kings, God of the ages! Your glorious throne stands for every generation of the ages, and your name is holy, glorious, and blessed for all the ages!
You made everything, and you have authority over everything. All things are bare and open before you; you see everything, and nothing can hide from you.
You see what Asael has done: he has taught all wrongdoing on the earth and revealed the eternal secrets that were kept in heaven, which human beings were striving to learn.{d}
And Shemihazah, to whom you gave authority to rule over those who are with him, has taught spells.
They have gone in to the daughters of men on the earth, lain with the women, defiled themselves, and revealed to them every kind of sin.
The women have borne giants,{e} and through this the whole earth has been filled with blood and wrongdoing.

And now, look: the souls of those who have died are crying out and making their appeal to the gates of heaven. Their groaning has gone up and cannot cease because of the lawless deeds done on the earth.
You know all things before they happen. You see these things and allow them, and you do not tell us what we ought to do to them about these things.”

notes.text: *Michael*: “Who is like God?” *Sariel*: “prince of God”; so the Greek and, reportedly, the Aramaic. The Ethiopic has *Uriel*, “God is my light.” *Raphael*: “God has healed.” *Gabriel*: “God is my strength” or “man of God.”
Stripped of its inhabitants: or “laid waste.” The Greek reads “The voice of their cry, as they are destroyed on the earth, reaches the gates of heaven.”
The Lord of the ages: so the Ethiopic; the Greek has “to the Lord, the King.”
Which human beings were striving to learn: so the Ethiopic; one Greek text reads “which the sons of men practice.”
Giants: the Greek of Syncellus adds “bastards.”

verses.text: Then the Most High, the Great Holy One, spoke. He sent Sariel{a} to the son of Lamech,{b}

saying, “Go to Noah{c} and tell him in my name, ‘Hide yourself!’ Reveal to him the end that is coming: that the whole earth will be destroyed, and a flood is about to come upon the whole earth and destroy everything on it.
Now teach him so that he may escape and his offspring may be preserved for all the generations of the world.”
To Raphael the Lord said, “Bind Asael hand and foot and throw him into the darkness. Make an opening in the desert that is in Dudael,{d} and throw him into it.
Lay rough and jagged rocks on him, cover him with darkness, and let him stay there forever. Cover his face so that he cannot see the light.
On the great day of judgment he will be thrown into the fire.

Heal the earth that the angels have ruined, and announce the healing of the earth, that I will heal the earth,{e} so that not all human beings will perish through all the secret things that the Watchers revealed and taught their sons.
The whole earth has been ruined by the teaching of the works of Asael; charge all sin to him.”

To Gabriel the Lord said, “Go against the bastards and the outcasts, the children of fornication. Destroy the children of the Watchers from among human beings. Send them against one another, so that they destroy each other in battle, for they will not have length of days.
No request that their fathers make of you for them will be granted, for they hope to live an everlasting life, and that each of them will live five hundred years.”
To Michael the Lord said, “Go, inform Shemihazah{f} and the others with him who have united themselves with women, so that they defiled themselves with them in all their uncleanness.

When their sons have killed one another and they have seen the destruction of their loved ones, bind them for seventy generations under the hills of the earth{g} until the day of their judgment and their end, until the judgment that is forever and ever is completed.
In those days they will be led away to the abyss of fire, to the torment, and to the prison where they will be shut up forever.
Whoever is condemned and destroyed will from then on be bound together with them until the end of all generations.
Wipe out every spirit of the outcasts{h} and of the Watchers’ children, for they have done wrong to the human race.

Rid the face of the earth of all wrongdoing; put an end to every evil deed, and let the plant of righteousness and truth come into view. It will become a blessing: deeds of righteousness and truth will be planted in truth and joy forever.

Then all the righteous will escape,
and they will live until they father thousands,
and all the days of their youth and their old age
they will complete in peace.
Then the whole earth will be farmed in righteousness; it will all be planted with trees and be full of blessing.

All pleasant trees will be planted on it, and they will plant vines on it. The vine that they plant on it will yield wine in abundance, and of all the seed that is sown on it each measure will yield a thousand, and each measure of olives will yield ten presses of oil.
Cleanse the earth from all oppression, from all wrongdoing, from all sin and godlessness; remove from the earth all the uncleanness that is done on it.
All human beings will become righteous, and all the nations will worship me and bless me, and all will bow down to me.
The earth will be cleansed from all defilement and from all sin, from all punishment and all torment, and I will never again send these upon it, from generation to generation and forever.

notes.text: *Sariel*: so the Greek (*Istraēl*, a corruption); the Ethiopic has *Arsyalalyur*, an unexplained name. See the note at 9:1.
*Lamech*: Hebrew *Lemekh*, meaning uncertain, perhaps “strong youth.” His son is Noah (Gen 5:28–29).
*Noah*: Hebrew *Noaḥ*, “rest,” linked in Gen 5:29 with *naḥam*, “to comfort.”
*Dudael*: perhaps “cauldron of God” or “jagged ground of God”; the place cannot be identified. Compare the wilderness of the scapegoat in Lev 16:10, 22.
That I will heal the earth: so the Greek; the Ethiopic reads “that they may heal the plague.”
Inform: so the Greek; the Ethiopic has “bind.”
Under the hills of the earth: so the Greek; the Ethiopic has “in the valleys of the earth.”
The outcasts: or “the lustful,” the giants; the word is uncertain.

verses.text: “In those days I will open the storehouses of blessing that are in heaven, to send them down upon the earth, upon the work and labor of human beings.
Truth and peace will be joined together through all the days of the world and through all the generations of humankind.”
Before these things Enoch was hidden,{a} and none of the human race knew where he was hidden, where he lived, or what had become of him.
He spent all his time with the Watchers, and his days were passed among the holy ones.{b}
While I, Enoch, stood blessing the great Lord, the King of the ages, the Watchers summoned me, Enoch the scribe, and told me,

“Enoch, scribe of righteousness, go and announce to the Watchers of heaven, who abandoned the high heaven and the holy, everlasting sanctuary, and have defiled themselves with women, and have done as human beings do, and have taken wives for themselves: ‘You have brought great destruction on the earth,
and you will have no peace or forgiveness of sin.’ Since they delight in their children,
they will see the slaughter of their loved ones and mourn over the destruction of their sons. They will plead forever, but they will obtain neither mercy nor peace.”

notes.text: Was hidden: or “was taken,” echoing Gen 5:24, “he was not, for God took him.”
The Watchers... the holy ones: here the faithful angels of heaven.

verses.text: Enoch went and said to Asael, “You will have no peace. A severe sentence has gone out against you, to bind you.
You will have no relief and no request granted, because of the wrongdoing that you taught and because of all the works of godlessness, wrongdoing, and sin that you showed to human beings.”
Then I went and spoke to all of them together, and they were all afraid; fear and trembling seized them.
They begged me to write a petition for them, so that they might find forgiveness, and to read their petition aloud in the presence of the Lord of heaven.
For from that time on they could not speak with him or lift up their eyes to heaven, out of shame for their sins for which they had been condemned.
So I wrote out their petition and the prayer concerning their spirits and their deeds one by one, and concerning their requests, that they might have forgiveness and length of days.
I went off and sat down by the waters of Dan,{a} in the land of Dan, to the southwest of Hermon, and I read their petition aloud until I fell asleep.
And look, a dream came to me, and visions fell upon me. I saw visions of punishment, and a voice came, telling me to speak to the sons of heaven and rebuke them.
When I woke up, I went to them. They were all sitting together weeping at Abel-main,{b} which is between Lebanon and Senir, with their faces covered.
I related to them every vision I had seen while asleep, and I began to speak words of righteousness and to rebuke the heavenly Watchers.

notes.text: *Dan*: “judge.” The waters of Dan are the springs of the Jordan at Tel Dan, at the foot of Mount Hermon.

*Abel-main*: “meadow of waters,” probably Abel-beth-maacah near Dan (2 Sam 20:14–15); the Ethiopic has *’Ubelseyāel* and the Greek *Ebelsata*, corruptions of the same name. *Senir*: the Amorite name of Hermon (Deut 3:9).

verses.text: This book is the word of righteousness and of the rebuke of the Watchers who are from eternity, according to the command of the Great Holy One in that vision.
In my sleep I saw what I now tell with a tongue of flesh and the breath of my mouth, which the Great One gave to humankind for speaking and for understanding in the heart.
As he created human beings and gave them the power to understand the word of knowledge, so he created me also and gave me the power to rebuke the Watchers, the sons of heaven.

I wrote out your petition, and in my vision it was shown to me that your petition will not be granted to you through all the days of eternity, and that judgment has been passed on you; your request will not be granted.
From now on you will not go up into heaven for all eternity. The decree has gone out to bind you in the earth for all the days of the world.
Before that, you will see the destruction of your beloved sons; you will have no pleasure in them, but they will fall before you by the sword.
Your plea for them will not be granted, nor your plea for yourselves, even if you weep and pray and recite every word of the document I wrote.

The vision was shown to me in this way. Look, in the vision clouds called me, and mist summoned me; the course of the stars and the lightning hurried me along and drove me on, and the winds in the vision made me fly, lifted me upward, and carried me into heaven.
I went in until I came near a wall built of hailstones{a} and surrounded by tongues of fire, and it began to frighten me.
I went into the tongues of fire and came near a great house built of hailstones. The walls of the house were like a mosaic floor of hailstones, and its floor was of snow.{b}
Its ceiling was like the path of the stars and the lightning, and among them were fiery cherubim,{c} and their sky was water.
Flaming fire surrounded the walls, and its doors blazed with fire.
I entered that house. It was hot as fire and cold as snow, and there was nothing of the pleasures of life in it. Fear covered me, and trembling took hold of me.
As I was shaking and trembling, I fell on my face. And I saw in the vision,
and look, there was a second house, greater than the first. Its whole doorway stood open before me, and it was built of tongues of fire.
In every respect it so surpassed the first in splendor, magnificence, and size that I cannot describe to you its splendor and its size.
Its floor was of fire; above it were lightning and the path of the stars, and its ceiling too was blazing fire.
I looked and saw in it a lofty throne. Its appearance was like frost,{d} and its wheels were like the shining sun, and there was the sound{e} of cherubim.
From beneath the throne came out rivers of blazing fire, so that I could not look at it.{f}
The Great Glory was seated on it. His robe was brighter than the sun and whiter than any snow.
None of the angels could enter that house or look at his face because of its majesty and glory, and no flesh could look at him.
Flaming fire encircled him, a great fire burned in front of him, and no one around him could come near him. Myriads upon myriads stood in his presence, yet he needed no counselor.{g}
The holiest ones who were near him did not leave by night or depart from him.
All this while I had lain face down, trembling. Then the Lord himself called me, speaking with his own mouth: “Come here, Enoch, and hear my word.”
One of the holy ones came to me and roused me; he made me get up and come to the door, and I bowed my face downward.

notes.text: Hailstones: so the Greek; the Ethiopic has “crystals.”
Its floor was of snow: so the Greek; the Ethiopic has “its foundation was of crystal.”
Cherubim: Hebrew plural of *kerub*, winged heavenly beings who guard God’s throne (Exod 25:18–22; Ezek 1; 10).
Frost: or “ice” (Greek *krystallinon*, “ice-like”).
The sound: so the Greek, reading *phōnē*, “voice”; the Ethiopic has “vision.”
Compare Dan 7:9–10; Ezek 1:26–28.
He needed no counselor: so the Greek, “every word of his is deed”; the Ethiopic reads “and he needs no holy counsel.”

verses.text: He answered and said to me, and I heard his voice, “Do not be afraid, Enoch, righteous man and scribe of righteousness. Come here and hear my voice.
Go and say to the Watchers of heaven who sent you to intercede for them: ‘You ought to intercede for human beings, not human beings for you.

Why have you left the high, holy, and eternal heaven, lain with women, defiled yourselves with the daughters of men, taken wives for yourselves, and acted like the children of earth, and fathered giants as your sons?

Though you were holy and spiritual, living eternal life, you defiled yourselves with the blood of women; you fathered children with the blood of flesh, and like human beings you longed for flesh and blood, as those who die and perish do.
That is why I gave them wives, so that they might make them pregnant and have children by them, so that nothing would be lacking to them on the earth.
But you were formerly spiritual, living eternal life, immortal for all the generations of the world.
Therefore I did not appoint wives for you, for the spiritual beings of heaven have their dwelling in heaven.
But now the giants, who were born from spirit and flesh, will be called evil spirits on the earth, and their dwelling will be on the earth.

Evil spirits have come out of their bodies, because they were created from above;{a} their beginning and first origin is from the holy Watchers. They will be evil spirits on the earth, and they will be called evil spirits.
The spirits of heaven have their dwelling in heaven, but the spirits of the earth, which were born on the earth, will have their dwelling on the earth.{b}
The spirits of the giants oppress, destroy, attack, wage war, and crush on the earth, and they cause sorrow. They eat no food, yet they hunger and thirst, and they cause offenses.{c}
These spirits will rise up against human beings and against women, because they came out from them.

notes.text: Because they were created from above: so the Greek; the Ethiopic reads “because they were born from men.”
Charles regarded this verse as an addition, since it repeats verses 7–8.
They hunger and thirst: so the Ethiopic. The Greek is obscure and is sometimes taken to mean that they do not hunger, but cause illnesses.

verses.text: “‘From the day of the slaughter and destruction and death of the giants, the spirits that have gone out from their bodies{a} will destroy without facing judgment. In this way they will destroy until the day of the completion, the great judgment, in which the great age will be completed upon the Watchers and the godless; it will be wholly completed.’
And now say to the Watchers who sent you to intercede for them, who were formerly in heaven,

‘You were in heaven, but not all the mysteries had been revealed to you. You knew a worthless mystery,{b} and in the hardness of your hearts you made it known to the women, and through this mystery women and men are doing much evil on the earth.’
So say to them, ‘You have no peace.’”

notes.text: From their bodies: literally “from the souls of their flesh.”
A worthless mystery: so the Greek; the Ethiopic has “rejected mysteries.”

verses.text: They took me and brought me to a place where those who were there looked like blazing fire, and whenever they wished, they took on the appearance of men.
They led me to the place of storm{a} and to a mountain whose highest peak reached into heaven.
I saw the places of the lights, the storehouses of the stars and of the thunder, and in the farthest depths a bow of fire, arrows with their quiver, a sword of fire, and all the lightning flashes.
They brought me to the waters of life,{b} and to the fire of the west, where the sun goes down each evening.
I came to a river of fire whose fire flows like water and pours out into the great sea in the west.
I viewed the great rivers; I reached the great river and the great darkness and went on to where no living creature walks.
I saw the mountains of the winter darkness and the place from which the water of every abyss pours out.
Every river on earth, I saw where it emptied, and where the abyss opens.

notes.text: Storm: so the Greek (*zophōdē*, “gloomy, stormy”); the Ethiopic has “darkness.”
The waters of life: literally “living waters,” that is, running water; here perhaps the waters at the edge of the world.

verses.text: I saw the storerooms of all the winds, and I saw how with them he has adorned the whole creation, and the foundations of the earth.
I saw the cornerstone of the earth. I saw the four winds that hold up the earth and the vault of the sky.
I saw how the winds spread out the height of heaven and stand between heaven and earth; they are the pillars of the sky.
I saw the winds of heaven that turn and lead the circle of the sun and all the stars to their setting.
I saw the earthly winds bearing the clouds along, and the roads the angels travel, and, at the earth’s edge, the sky’s vault overhead.
I went on toward the south{a} and saw a place burning day and night, where there were seven mountains of precious stones, three toward the east and three toward the south.
Of those toward the east, one was of colored stone, one of pearl, and one of healing stone;{b} those toward the south were of red stone.
The middle one reached to heaven like the throne of God; it was of antimony,{c} and the top of the throne was of sapphire.
I saw a blazing fire. Beyond these mountains
lies a region where the great earth stops and the heavens are finished.
I saw a great chasm among pillars of heavenly fire, and I saw in it pillars of fire falling, beyond measure both in height and in depth.
Beyond that chasm I saw a place that had no vault of heaven above it and no solid ground beneath it. There was no water on it and no birds; it was a desolate and dreadful place.
Seven stars were there, like huge mountains on fire. When I inquired about them,
the angel told me, “Here heaven and earth come to their limit. This place now serves as a jail for the stars and the heavenly host.
The stars that roll over the fire are those that disobeyed the command of the Lord at the beginning of their rising, because they did not come out at their proper times.
He was angry with them and bound them until the time when their sin is completed, for ten thousand years.”{d}

notes.text: Toward the south: so the Greek; the Ethiopic lacks the direction.
Healing stone: so the Greek (*iaseōs*); the Ethiopic has “jacinth” or “antimony.” The identification of these stones is uncertain.
Antimony: so the Ethiopic; the Greek has *phouka*, perhaps a dark stone. Compare the sapphire of the divine throne in Exod 24:10 and Ezek 1:26.
Ten thousand years: so the Greek; the Ethiopic has “in the year of the mystery.”

verses.text: Sariel{a} said to me, “Here will stand the angels who mixed with women. Their spirits, taking many forms, defile humankind and lead people astray into sacrificing to demons as to gods. Here they will stand until the day of the great judgment, when they will be judged until they are finished.
Their women, the wives of the angels who went astray, will become sirens.”{b}
I, Enoch, alone saw the sight, the ends of all things, and no human being will see what I have seen.

notes.text: *Sariel*: “prince of God”; so the Aramaic and Greek here, reportedly; the Ethiopic has *Uriel*. Compare 9:1.
Sirens: so the Greek (*seirēnas*); in the Greek Old Testament the word renders desert creatures (Isa 13:21). The Ethiopic reads “will become peaceful,” a misreading of the Greek.

verses.text: Here are the names of the holy angels who stand watch:
Uriel,{a} one of the holy angels, in charge of the world and of Tartarus.{b}
Raphael, a holy angel, in charge of human spirits.
Raguel, a holy angel, who brings punishment on the world of the lights.
Michael, a holy angel, placed in charge of the finest of humankind, the people.{c}
Saraqael, a holy angel, in charge of the spirits of those who sin in spirit.
Gabriel, a holy angel, in charge of Paradise, the serpents, and the cherubim.
Remiel, a holy angel, whom God put in charge of those who rise.{d}

notes.text: *Uriel*: “God is my light.” For the other names see the note at 9:1. *Raguel*: “friend of God.” *Saraqael* (Greek *Sariēl*): perhaps “God has struck” or “prince of God.” *Remiel*: “God has raised up” or “mercy of God.”
Tartarus: in Greek thought the deepest part of the underworld, where rebel powers are imprisoned; compare 2 Pet 2:4. The Ethiopic has “thunder and trembling.”
Over the people: so the Greek; the Ethiopic has “over chaos.” Michael is the guardian of Israel (Dan 10:21; 12:1).
Verse 8 is found only in one Greek copy, which also gives the total as seven archangels.

verses.text: I traveled on to where there was nothing made.{a}
There I saw something dreadful: I saw neither a heaven above nor solid ground below, but a desolate and fearful place.
In it seven heavenly stars lay tied together, burning, as large as great mountains.
Then I asked, “For what sin have they been bound, and why have they been thrown here?”
Uriel, a holy angel who accompanied me and who led them, replied, “Enoch, what is your question for, and why are you so eager for the truth?
These are some of the stars of heaven that disobeyed the command of the Lord. They have been bound here until ten thousand years are completed, the time required by their sins.”

From there I went to another place, more dreadful than the first. I saw a terrible thing there: a great fire burning and blazing. The place had a cleft reaching down to the abyss, full of great columns of fire falling downward. I could not see its size or its extent, nor could I estimate it.
Then I said, “How frightening this place is, and how terrible to look at!”
Uriel, one of the holy angels who was with me, answered, “Enoch, why are you so afraid and terrified?” I answered, “Because of this frightening place and this sight of pain.”
He said to me, “This place is the prison of the angels. They will be held here forever.”

notes.text: Where there was nothing made: or “to the place of chaos”; literally “to the formless.”

verses.text: Next I traveled to another place, where he pointed out to me in the west a great, high mountain and a hard rock.{a}

In it were four hollow places, deep and very smooth: three of them were dark and one was bright, with a spring of water in the middle of it.{b} I said, “How smooth these hollows are, how deep and dark to look at!”

Raphael, a holy angel who accompanied me, replied, “These hollows were made for exactly this: that the spirits of the souls of the dead might gather in them. They were made so that all the souls of human beings might gather here.
These places were made to hold them until the day of their judgment and until their appointed time, until the great judgment comes upon them.”
I saw the spirit of a dead man pleading, and its voice went out to heaven, making its case.{c}
I asked Raphael, the angel who was with me, “Whose spirit is this, whose voice goes up to heaven making its plea?”

He answered me, “This is the spirit that came out of Abel,{d} whom his brother Cain killed. He goes on accusing him until his offspring is destroyed from the face of the earth and his descendants have disappeared from the descendants of humankind.”
Then I asked about all the hollows: “Why is each one separated from the others?”
He answered me, “These three{e} were made to separate the spirits of the dead. This one has been set apart for the spirits of the righteous, where the bright spring of water is.
This one is for sinners who die and are laid in the ground without having been judged while they lived.

Here their spirits are kept apart in this great pain until the great day of judgment, of punishment, and of torment for those who curse forever, and of vengeance on their spirits. There he will bind them forever.
This one has been set apart for the spirits of those who make accusation, who disclose how they were destroyed, when they were murdered in the days of the sinners.

This one was made for the spirits of people who were not godly but sinners, complete in lawlessness, who will be companions of the lawless. Their spirits will not be punished on the day of judgment, nor will they be raised from here.”
Then I blessed the Lord of glory and said, “Blessed are you, Lord, the righteous Judge, who rules forever.”{f}

notes.text: A great, high mountain and a hard rock: so the Greek; the Ethiopic reads “a great and high mountain of hard rock.”
Three of them were dark... in the middle of it: so the Greek; the Ethiopic lacks these words. An Aramaic fragment (4QEnᵉ) is reported to read “deep and wide.”
So the Greek; the Ethiopic reads “I saw the spirits of the sons of men who were dead.”

*Abel*: Hebrew *Hevel*, “breath” or “vapor.” *Cain*: Hebrew *Qayin*, connected in Gen 4:1 with *qanah*, “to acquire.” Compare Gen 4:10, “Your brother’s blood cries out to me from the ground,” and Heb 12:24.
These three: some take this to mean “these”; four places are described in verses 9–13.
So the Greek, approximately; the Ethiopic reads “Blessed be my Lord, the Lord of righteousness, who rules forever.”

verses.text: From there I went to another place, to the west, at the ends of the earth.
I saw a fire blazing and running without rest; it did not stop its course day or night but kept on in the same way.
I asked, “What is this that never rests?”
Raguel, a holy angel who accompanied me, replied, “This running fire before you is the fire in the west that drives on all the lights of heaven.”
From there I went to another place on the earth, and he showed me a range of mountains of fire that burned day and night.

I went beyond it and saw seven splendid mountains, each different from the others. Their stones were precious and beautiful, the whole range splendid, glorious to look at and lovely in form: three toward the east, set firmly one on another, and three toward the south, one on another, with deep, winding ravines, none of which joined any other.
The seventh mountain stood in the middle of them and rose above them in height, like the seat of a throne, and fragrant trees surrounded the throne.
