I answered, “For whom, and for how many, will these things be? Who will be worthy to live at that time?
I will say before You everything I am thinking, and I will ask You about what I am pondering.
I see many of Your people who have turned from Your covenant and thrown off the yoke of Your law.
But I have seen others who gave up their emptiness and fled for shelter under Your wings.
What will happen to them? How will the last time receive them?
Or perhaps their time will be weighed, and they will be judged as the balance tips?”
He answered me, “I will show you this too.
As for what you said, ‘For whom will these things be, and for how many?’ To those who have believed, the good that was promised long ago will come, and to those who despise it, the opposite.
As for what you said about those who have drawn near and those who have withdrawn, this is the answer.
Those who were first subject to Me and afterward turned away and mingled with the seed of mixed peoples: the time of these was the former time, and it was counted as something exalted.

And those who did not know before, but afterward came to know life and mingled only with the seed of the people that had set itself apart: the time of these is the latter time, and it is counted as something exalted.

Time will follow time and season will follow season. One will receive from another, and then, with the end in view, everything will be compared by the measure of the times and the hours of the seasons.
For corruption will take what belongs to it, and life will take what belongs to it.
The dust will be called and told, ‘Give back what is not yours, and raise up everything you have kept until its time.’”

chapters.heading: Baruch is told of his death

verses.text: “But you, Baruch, turn your heart to what has been said to you, and understand what has been shown to you, for there are many everlasting comforts for you.
You will leave this place and pass from the regions you now see. You will forget whatever is corruptible and will no longer remember what happens among mortals.
So go and command your people, and come to this place. After that, fast for seven days, and then I will come to you and speak with you.”

chapters.heading: Baruch tells the elders of his coming death

verses.text: I, Baruch, went from there and came to my people. I called my firstborn son, and the Gedaliahs, my friends, and seven of the elders of the people, and I said to them,
“See, I am going to my fathers, the way of all the earth.
But do not leave the way of the law. Guard the people who remain and warn them, so that they do not turn from the commands of the Mighty One.
You see that the One we serve is just, and that our Creator shows no favoritism.
See what has happened to Zion, and what has come upon Jerusalem.
By this the judgment of the Mighty One will be made known, and His ways, which cannot be traced out yet are right.
If you endure and keep on in His fear and do not forget His law, the times will change for the better over you, and you will see the comfort of Zion.
For whatever exists now is nothing, but what is to come is very great.
Everything corruptible will pass away and everything that dies will go. All the present time will be forgotten, and there will be no memory of the present time, which is stained with evils.
For what runs on now runs toward emptiness, and what prospers will quickly fall and be humbled.
What is to come will be the object of desire, and we will hope for what comes after. It is a time that does not pass away.

The hour comes that lasts forever, and the new world comes, which does not turn to corruption those who go to its blessing, has no mercy on those who go to torment, and does not lead to ruin those who live in it.
These are the ones who will inherit the time that has been spoken of, and theirs is the inheritance of the promised time.

These are the ones who have gathered for themselves treasures of wisdom, and with them are found stores of understanding. They have not turned away from mercy, and they have kept the truth of the law.
To them the world to come will be given, but the dwelling of the rest, who are many, will be in the fire.”
“So, as far as you can, teach the people, for that work is ours.
If you teach them, you will give them life.”
My son and the elders of the people answered me, “Has the Mighty One humbled us so much as to take you from us so quickly?
We will truly be in darkness, with no light for the people who are left.
Where will we look for the law again, and who will tell us the difference between death and life?”
I said to them, “I cannot resist the throne of the Mighty One. Even so, Israel will never lack a wise man, nor the family of Jacob a son of the law.
Only prepare your hearts to obey the law, and be subject to those who are wise and understanding in fear of Him. Prepare your souls so that you do not leave them.
If you do these things, good news will come to you.
That is what I told you before, and you will not fall into the torment of which I warned you earlier.
But about the word that I was to be taken, I did not tell them or my son.
When I had gone out and sent them away, I went there and said to them, “See, I am going to Hebron{a}, for the Mighty One has sent me there.”
I came to the place where the word had been spoken to me, sat there, and fasted for seven days.

notes.text: “Hebron” (Hebrew *Chevron*) is related to “association” or “league.” It is a city in the hills south of Jerusalem.

verses.text: After the seventh day I prayed before the Mighty One and said,
“O my Lord, You call the coming of the times, and they stand before You. You make the power of the ages pass away, and they do not resist You. You set the order of the seasons, and they obey You.
You alone know how long the generations last, and You do not reveal Your mysteries to many.
You make known how great the fire is, and You weigh how light the wind is.
You search out the limits of the heights, and You examine the depths of the darkness.
You look after the number of those who pass away, so that they may be kept, and You prepare a home for those who are to come.
You remember the beginning that You made, and You do not forget the destruction that is to come.
At Your nod, in fear and anger, You command the flames, and they change into spirits. With a word You bring to life what was not, and with mighty power You hold back what has not yet come.
You teach created things to understand You, and You make the heavenly spheres wise so that they serve in their ranks.
Countless armies stand before You and quietly serve in their ranks at Your nod.
Hear Your servant and listen to my plea.
We are born in a short time, and in a short time we return.
But with You hours are like an age, and days are like generations.
So do not be angry with humanity, for it is nothing,
and do not hold our deeds against us. What are we? It is by Your gift that we come into the world, and we do not leave by our own will.
We never said to our parents, ‘Give birth to us,’ and we never sent word to Sheol, saying, ‘Take us in.’
What is our strength, that we could bear Your wrath? What are we, that we could stand Your judgment?
Shelter us in Your compassion, and help us in Your mercy.
Look at the little ones who are subject to You, and save everyone who comes near You. Do not destroy our people’s hope, and do not cut short the times of our help.
This is the nation You chose, and these are the people for whom You find no equal.
But now I will speak before You and say what my heart thinks.
We trust in You, for Your law is with us, and we know that we will not fall as long as we keep Your statutes.
We are blessed forever in this at least, that we have not mingled with the nations.
For we are all one famous people who received one law from the One. The law among us will help us, and the surpassing wisdom in us will assist us.”
When I had prayed and said these things, I was greatly weakened.
He answered me, “You have prayed simply, Baruch, and all your words have been heard.
But My judgment claims what is its own, and My law claims its rights.
I will answer you from your own words, and speak to you from your own prayer.
It is like this: one who is corrupted is no more. He has done wrong as far as he was able, and he has not remembered My goodness or accepted My patience.
So you will surely be taken up, as I told you before.
For a time will rise that brings affliction. It will come and pass by with swift violence, and it will be stormy, coming in the heat of anger.
In those days all the inhabitants of the earth will be stirred up against one another, because they do not know that My judgment has come near.
Not many wise people will be found in that time, and the intelligent will be only a few. Even those who know will mostly stay silent.
There will be many rumors and plenty of news. Illusions will be seen at work, and many promises will be told. Some will turn out empty, and some will be confirmed.
Honor will turn into shame, strength will be crushed into contempt, integrity will be destroyed, and beauty will become ugliness.
In that time many will say to many, ‘Where has the multitude of understanding hidden itself, and where has the multitude of wisdom gone?’

While they are thinking this over, envy will rise in those who thought nothing of themselves, and passion will seize the peaceful. Many will be stirred up in anger to hurt many, and they will raise armies to shed blood, and in the end they will perish along with them.

At that same time a change of the times will be plain to everyone, because throughout those times they made themselves unclean, practiced oppression, each walked in his own works, and did not remember the law of the Mighty One.
So a fire will consume their thoughts, and in flames the plans of their inmost being will be tested. For the Judge will come and will not delay.
Each of the inhabitants of the earth knew when he was breaking the law, but in their pride they did not know My Law.
Then many will certainly weep, more over the living than over the dead.”
I answered, “O Adam, what have you done to all those born from you? And what will be said to the first Eve{a}, who listened to the serpent?
This whole multitude is heading toward corruption, and there is no counting those the fire devours.
But I will speak again in Your presence.
You, O Lord, my Lord, know what is in Your creature.
Long ago You commanded the dust to bring forth Adam, and You know the number of those born from him, and how far they have sinned before You, who lived and did not confess You as their Creator.
As for all of these, their end will convict them, and Your law, which they broke, will repay them on Your day.”
“But now let us set the wicked aside and ask about the righteous.
I will describe their blessedness and will not be silent in celebrating their glory, which is kept for them.
For just as you have endured much labor for a little time in this passing world where you live, so in that world that has no end you will receive great light.”

notes.text: “Eve” (Hebrew *Chavvah*) is traditionally linked to “life” or “living.”

chapters.heading: The nature of the resurrection body

verses.text: “Even so, I will ask You again, Mighty One, and I will ask You, who made all things.
In what form will those live who live in Your day? How will the splendor of those who come after that time continue?

Will they take on this present form again and put on these tangled limbs, which are now caught up in evils and in which evils reach their peak? Or will You perhaps change these things that have been in the world, just as You change the world?”
He answered me, “Listen to this word, Baruch, and write in the memory of your heart everything you will learn.

The earth will then surely give back the dead, which it now receives to keep. It will make no change in their form, but as it received them, so it will return them. As I handed them over to it, so it will raise them.
For then it will be necessary to show the living that the dead have come back to life and that those who had departed have returned.
When they have each recognized those they know now, then the judgment will grow strong, and the things that were spoken of before will come.”
“When that appointed day has passed, the appearance of those who are condemned will be changed, and so will the glory of those who are declared righteous.
The appearance of those who now do evil will become worse than it is, since they will suffer torment.

As for the glory of those who have now been made righteous in My law, who have had understanding in their lives and have planted the root of wisdom in their hearts, their splendor will be glorified in changes, and the form of their faces will be turned into the light of their beauty, so that they may gain and receive the world that does not die, which is then promised to them.
Above all, those who come then will grieve over this: that they rejected My law and stopped their ears so as not to hear wisdom or receive understanding.

When they see those whom they now look down on, who will then be lifted up and glorified more than they are, the righteous will be transformed into the splendor of angels, and the wicked will waste away still more in wonder at the sights and the forms they behold.
For they will see first, and afterward go away to be tormented.
But those who were saved by their works, for whom the law has been a hope, understanding an expectation, and wisdom a confidence, will see wonders appear in their time.
They will see the world that is now invisible to them, and they will see the time that is now hidden from them.
Time will no longer age them.

They will live in the heights of that world, and they will be made like the angels and equal to the stars. They will be changed into any form they wish, from beauty into loveliness, and from light into the splendor of glory.

The wide spaces of Paradise will be spread out before them, and the beauty of the majesty of the living creatures beneath the throne will be shown to them, along with all the armies of angels, who are now held back by My word so that they do not appear, and are held by a command to stand in their places until their coming arrives.
Moreover, there will then be an excellence in the righteous that surpasses that of the angels.
For the first will receive the last, whom they were expecting, and the last will receive those of whom they used to hear that they had passed away.
For they have been rescued from this world of tribulation and have laid down the burden of anguish.
What have people lost their lives for, and what have those on the earth traded their souls for?

They did not choose for themselves that time which, beyond the reach of anguish, could never pass away. They chose for themselves the time whose outcomes are full of lamentation and evil. They denied the world that does not age those who come to it, and they rejected the time of glory, so that they will not come to the honor of which I told you before.”
I answered, “How could we forget those for whom woe is then kept in store?
Why, then, do we mourn again for those who die? Why do we weep for those who go down to Sheol?
Let the lamentations be kept for the start of that coming torment, and let the tears be stored up for the arrival of the destruction of that time.
But even in the face of these things I will speak.
And as for the righteous, what will they do now?
Rejoice in the suffering you now endure. Why do you look for the decline of your enemies?
Make your souls ready for what is kept for you, and prepare them for the reward laid up for you.”

chapters.heading: The vision of the cloud with dark and bright waters

verses.text: After I had said these things, I fell asleep there, and I saw a vision. A cloud was rising from a very great sea. I kept looking at it, and it was full of white and black waters, with many colors in those same waters, and at its top there was what looked like great lightning.
I saw the cloud moving swiftly in quick courses, and it covered all the earth.
After this the cloud began to pour out on the earth the waters it held.
I saw that the waters coming down from it were not all alike.
At the first they were black and many. Then I saw the waters become bright, but they were not many. After this I saw black waters again, then bright, then black again, and bright again.
This happened twelve times, but the black were always more numerous than the bright.
At the end of the cloud it rained black waters, darker than all the earlier waters, and fire was mixed with them. Where those waters came down, they brought devastation and destruction.
After this I saw the lightning I had seen at the top of the cloud seize the cloud and hurl it to the earth.
That lightning shone so brightly that it lit up the whole earth, and it healed the regions where the last waters had come down and brought devastation.
It took hold of the whole earth and ruled over it.
After this I saw twelve rivers rising from the sea, and they began to surround the lightning and become subject to it.
In my fear I woke up.

chapters.heading: Baruch asks for the meaning of the vision

verses.text: I pleaded with the Mighty One and said, “You alone, Lord, know the deep things of the world from ages past. You bring about by Your word what happens in its times. In response to the works of the inhabitants of the earth You hurry the beginnings of the times, and You alone know the end of the seasons.
Nothing is too hard for You, and You do everything easily with a nod.
To You the depths are like the heights, and the beginnings of the ages serve Your word.
You reveal to those who fear You what is prepared for them, so that from then on they may be comforted.

You show great deeds to those who do not know. You break open the walls around the ignorant. You light up what is dark and reveal what is hidden to the pure, who in faith have submitted to You and Your law.
You have shown this vision to Your servant. Show me its meaning as well.
I know that I have received an answer about the things I asked, and in answer to my request You showed me with what voice to praise You and with what limbs to send up praises and hallelujahs to You.

Even if my limbs were mouths and the hairs of my head were voices, I still could not give You the praise You deserve, nor honor You as is fitting. I could not recount Your praise or tell the glory of Your beauty.
What am I among people, or why am I counted among those better than I am, that I have heard all these marvelous things from the Most High and countless promises from the One who made me?
Blessed be my mother among those who bear children, and praised among women be she who gave birth to me.
I will not be silent in praising the Mighty One, and with the voice of praise I will tell of His marvelous deeds.
Who does anything like Your marvelous deeds, O God? Who can grasp Your deep thought about life?
By Your counsel You govern all the creatures that Your right hand made. You set every fountain of light beside You, and You prepared the treasures of wisdom beneath Your throne.
Those who have not loved Your law rightly perish, and the torment of judgment awaits those who have not submitted to Your power.
Adam sinned first and brought early death on everyone, but of those born from him, each one has prepared torment to come for his own soul, and each has also chosen glories to come for himself.
Whoever believes will certainly receive a reward.
But as for you wicked ones who live now, go and turn toward destruction, because you will soon be visited, since you rejected the understanding of the Most High.
His works have not taught you, and the skill of His creation, always before you, has not persuaded you.
So Adam is not the cause except of his own soul, but each of us has become the Adam of his own soul.
But You, Lord, explain to me the things You have revealed to me, and tell me about what I asked You.
At the completion of the world, vengeance will be taken on those who have done wickedness, according to their wickedness, and You will glorify the faithful according to their faithfulness.
You rule over those who belong to You, and You blot out from among Your own those who sin.”
When I had finished speaking the words of this prayer, I sat down there under a tree to rest in the shade of its branches.

I wondered and was amazed, and I thought about the abundance of goodness that sinners on the earth have rejected, and about the great torment they have despised, although they knew they would be tormented because of the sin they had committed.
While I was thinking about these and similar things, the angel Ramiel{a}, who is in charge of true visions, was sent to me, and he said to me,
“Baruch, why does your heart trouble you, and why does your thought disturb you?
If you are so moved by a mere report of the judgment, what will you do when you see it clearly with your own eyes?
If you are so overcome by waiting for the day of the Mighty One, what will you do when you come to its arrival?
If you are so completely distraught at the word announcing the torment of those who have acted foolishly, how much more when the event itself shows its marvels?
If you have heard news of the good and evil things that are then coming and are grieved, what will you do when you see what the Majesty will reveal, which will convict some and make others rejoice?”

notes.text: “Ramiel” (Hebrew *Remiel*) is thought to mean “thunder of God” or “God has raised up.”

chapters.heading: Interpretation: the dark and bright waters

verses.text: “Since you asked the Most High to explain the vision you saw, I have been sent to tell you.

The Mighty One has truly made known to you the course of the times that have passed and those that are meant to pass in His world, from the beginning of its creation to its completion, both what is deceit and what is truth.
The great cloud you saw rising from the sea and going on to cover the earth is the duration of the world, which the Mighty One made when He decided to make the world.
When the word went out from His presence, the duration of the world came into being in a small way, and it was established according to the fullness of the understanding of the One who sent it.
The black waters you saw first at the top of the cloud, which came down on the earth first, are the transgression that Adam, the first man, committed.

For from the time he transgressed, early death came into being, grief was given a name, anguish was prepared, pain was created, trouble was brought to its height, and disease began to take hold. Sheol kept demanding to be renewed with blood. The bearing of children came about, the passion of parents arose, human greatness was brought low, and goodness withered.
What could be blacker or darker than these things?
This is the beginning of the black waters you saw.
From these black waters, black waters came again, and the darkness of darkness was produced.
He became a danger to his own soul, and even to the angels.
At that time, when he was created, they had enjoyed freedom.
Because he became a danger to them, some of them came down and mingled with the women.
Then those who did this were tormented in chains.
But the rest of the multitude of angels, who cannot be counted, held themselves back.
Those who lived on the earth perished together with them in the waters of the flood.
These are the first black waters.”
“After these waters you saw bright waters. This is the fountain of Abraham, together with his generations and the coming of his son and his son’s son, and of those like them.

At that time the unwritten law was known among them, the works of the commandments were fulfilled, belief in the coming judgment arose, hope in the world that was to be renewed was built up, and the promise of the life to come was planted.
These are the bright waters you saw.”

“The black third waters you saw are the mixing together of all sins that the nations committed after the death of those righteous men, and the wickedness of the land of Egypt{a}, where they acted wickedly in the service by which they made their sons serve.
Yet even these perished in the end.”

notes.text: “Egypt” translates the Hebrew *Mitsrayim*, of uncertain meaning.

verses.text: “The bright fourth waters you saw are the coming of Moses, Aaron{a}, Miriam{b}, Joshua{c} son of Nun, Caleb{d}, and all those like them.
At that time the lamp of the eternal law shone on all who sat in darkness. It announced the promised reward to those who believe, and the torment of fire kept for them to those who deny.
At that time even the heavens were shaken from their place, and those under the throne of the Mighty One were disturbed when He took Moses to Himself.

He showed him many warnings, together with the principles of the law and the end of the times, as He has to you also, and likewise the pattern of Zion and its measurements, on the pattern of which the sanctuary of the present time was to be made.
He also showed him the extent of the fire, the depths of the abyss, the weight of the winds, and the number of the drops of rain,
the restraint of anger, the abundance of patience, and the truth of judgment,
the root of wisdom, the riches of understanding, and the spring of knowledge,
the height of the air, the greatness of Paradise, the end of the ages, and the start of the day of judgment,
the number of the offerings, and the worlds that have not yet come,
the mouth of Gehenna, the place where vengeance stands, the place of faith, and the region of hope,

the likeness of future torment, the multitude of countless angels, the flaming hosts, the splendor of the lightnings, the voice of the thunders, the ranks of the chief angels, the treasuries of light, the changes of the times, and the study of the law.
These are the bright fourth waters you saw.”

notes.text: “Aaron” (Hebrew *Aharon*) is of uncertain meaning.
“Miriam” (Hebrew *Miryam*) is of uncertain meaning; it may be related to “bitter” or “beloved.”
“Joshua” (Hebrew *Yehoshua*) means “Yahweh saves.”
“Caleb” (Hebrew *Kalev*) is often taken to mean “dog” or “wholehearted.”

verses.text: “The black fifth waters you saw raining are the works the Amorites did, the spells of their incantations, the wickedness of their mysteries, and the mixing of their pollution.
Even Israel was defiled by sins in the days of the judges, although they saw many signs from the One who made them.”
“The bright sixth waters you saw are the time when David{a} and Solomon{b} were born.
At that time Zion was built, the sanctuary was dedicated, much blood of the nations that sinned then was shed, and many offerings were made at the dedication of the sanctuary.
There was peace and calm at that time.
Wisdom was heard in the assembly, and the riches of understanding were honored in the congregations.
The holy festivals were kept in blessing and great joy.
The judgment of the rulers was seen to be without deceit, and the righteousness of the Mighty One’s precepts was carried out in truth.
The land was loved by the Lord at that time, and because its inhabitants did not sin, it was glorified above all lands, and the city of Zion ruled over all lands and regions.
These are the bright waters you saw.”

notes.text: “David” (Hebrew *David*) probably means “beloved.”
“Solomon” (Hebrew *Shelomoh*) is related to *shalom*, “peace.”

verses.text: “The black seventh waters you saw are the perversion that came from the plan of Jeroboam{a}, who planned to make two golden calves,
and all the wrongdoing that the kings after him did wickedly.
They are the curse of Jezebel{b} and the worship of idols that Israel practiced at that time,
the withholding of rain, and the famines that happened until women ate the fruit of their own wombs,
and the time of captivity that came on the nine and a half tribes, because they were in many sins.
Shalmaneser{c}, king of Assyria{d}, came and led them away captive.
As for the nations, it would be tiresome to tell how they always practiced ungodliness and wickedness and never did righteousness.
These are the black seventh waters you saw.”

notes.text: “Jeroboam” (Hebrew *Yarovam*) is usually explained as “the people contend” or “may the kinsman increase.”
“Jezebel” (Hebrew *Izevel*) is a Phoenician name, perhaps meaning “where is the prince?”
“Shalmaneser” (Assyrian *Shulmanu-asharedu*) means “Shulmanu is foremost.”
“Assyria” (Hebrew *Ashshur*) is named for its chief city and god, Ashur.

verses.text: “The bright eighth waters you saw are the uprightness and honesty of Hezekiah{a}, king of Judah, and the grace that came upon him.
For Sennacherib{b} was stirred up, so that he would perish, and his rage troubled him, so that he would perish by it, together with the multitude of the nations that were with him.

When King Hezekiah heard what the king of Assyria was planning, which was to come and seize him and destroy his people, the two and a half tribes that remained, and even to overthrow Zion also, Hezekiah trusted in his works and hoped in his righteousness, and he spoke with the Mighty One and said,
‘See, Sennacherib is ready to destroy us, and he will be boastful and proud when he has destroyed Zion.’
The Mighty One heard him, for Hezekiah was wise, and He paid attention to his prayer because he was righteous.
Then the Mighty One gave orders to Ramiel, His angel who speaks with you.
And I went out and destroyed their multitude, the number of whose commanders alone was one hundred eighty-five thousand, and each of them had an equal number under him.

At that time I burned their bodies inside, but I kept their clothes and weapons untouched on the outside, so that the still more wonderful deeds of the Mighty One would appear, and so that His name would be spoken of in all the earth.
So Zion was saved and Jerusalem delivered, and Israel was freed from tribulation.
All who were in the holy land rejoiced, and the name of the Mighty One was glorified, so that it was spoken of everywhere.
These are the bright waters you saw.”

notes.text: “Hezekiah” (Hebrew *Chizqiyyahu*) means “Yahweh strengthens.”
“Sennacherib” (Assyrian *Sin-ahhe-eriba*) means “Sin (the moon god) has replaced the brothers.”

verses.text: “The black ninth waters you saw are all the wickedness in the days of Manasseh{a}, son of Hezekiah.

He did much that was ungodly. He killed the righteous, twisted judgment, shed the blood of the innocent, and violently defiled married women. He overturned the altars, destroyed their offerings, and drove out their priests so that they could not serve in the sanctuary.
He made an image with five faces. Four of them looked toward the four winds, and the fifth, on top of the image, stood as an opponent of the zeal of the Mighty One.
Then wrath went out from the presence of the Mighty One so that Zion would be uprooted, as also happened in your days.
A decree also went out against the two and a half tribes, that they too would be led away captive, as you have now seen.
Manasseh’s ungodliness grew so great that it removed the praise of the Most High from the sanctuary.
For this reason Manasseh was called ‘the ungodly’ at that time, and in the end his dwelling was in the fire.
Though his prayer was heard by the Most High, in the end, when he was thrown into the bronze horse and the bronze horse melted, it served as a sign to him for the hour.
He had not lived perfectly, for he was not worthy. But from then on he would know by whom he would finally be tormented.
For the One who is able to help is also able to torment.”

notes.text: “Manasseh” (Hebrew *Menashsheh*) means “he who makes forget.”

verses.text: “So Manasseh acted ungodly and thought that in his time the Mighty One would not look into these things.
These are the black ninth waters you saw.”
“The bright tenth waters you saw are the pure generations of Josiah{a}, king of Judah, who was the only one at that time who submitted to the Mighty One with all his heart and all his soul.

He cleansed the land of idols and made holy all the vessels that had been defiled. He restored the offerings to the altar and raised the horn of the holy ones. He lifted up the righteous and honored everyone wise in understanding. He brought the priests back to their service and destroyed and removed the magicians, enchanters, and necromancers from the land.
Not only did he put to death the ungodly who were alive, but they also took the bones of the dead out of the tombs and burned them with fire.

He set up the festivals and the Sabbaths in their holiness, and he burned their defiled ones in the fire. The lying prophets who deceived the people he also burned in the fire, and the people who had listened to them while they lived, he threw into the Kidron brook and heaped stones on them.

He was zealous with zeal for the Mighty One with all his soul, and he alone was firm in the law at that time, so that all the days of his life he left no uncircumcised person or anyone who practiced ungodliness in all the land.
So he will receive an eternal reward, and he will be glorified with the Mighty One above many at a later time.
For his sake and for the sake of those like him, the honorable glories of which you were told before were created and prepared. These are the bright waters you saw.”

notes.text: “Josiah” (Hebrew *Yoshiyyahu*) probably means “Yahweh supports.”

verses.text: “The black eleventh waters you saw are the calamity that is now falling on Zion.

Do you think there is no anguish among the angels in the presence of the Mighty One, that Zion was handed over like this, and that the nations boast in their hearts, gather before their idols, and say, ‘She who so often trampled others is trampled down, and she who enslaved others has been enslaved’?
Do you think the Most High rejoices in these things, or that His name is glorified?
But how will it serve His righteous judgment?
After these things, those scattered among the nations will be seized by tribulation, and they will live in shame in every place.

For as long as Zion is handed over and Jerusalem laid waste, idols will prosper in the cities of the nations. The fragrant smoke of the incense of righteousness that comes by the law will be put out in Zion, and in every place in the region of Zion there will be the smoke of ungodliness.
But the king of Babylon, who has now destroyed Zion, will rise up and boast over the people, and he will say great things in his heart before the Most High.
But he too will fall in the end. These are the black waters.”
“The bright twelfth waters you saw are this word.
After these things a time will come when your people fall into distress, so that they all run the risk of perishing together.
Even so, they will be saved, and their enemies will fall before them.
In due time they will have great joy.
At that time, after a short interval, Zion will be rebuilt again, its offerings will be restored, the priests will return to their service, and the nations will come to honor it.
Even so, it will not be fully as it was in the beginning.
But after these things there will be the fall of many nations.
These are the bright waters you saw.”
“The last waters you saw, which were darker than all those before them, those that came after the twelfth and were gathered together, belong to the whole world.
The Most High made a division from the beginning, because He alone knows what will happen.
He foresaw six kinds of the outrages and ungodliness that would be done before Him.
And He foresaw six kinds of the good works of the righteous that would be done before Him, besides those that He Himself will do at the completion of the age.
For this reason there were no black waters mixed with black, and no bright with bright, for it is the end.”
“Now hear the meaning of the last black waters that are to come after the black ones. This is the word.

See, the days are coming. When the time of the age has ripened and the harvest of its evil and good seeds has come, the Mighty One will bring on the earth, its inhabitants, and its rulers a disturbance of spirit and a stupor of heart.
They will hate one another and stir one another up to fight. The lowly will rule over the honored, and those of low rank will be lifted above the famous.
The many will be handed over to the few, those who were nothing will rule over the strong, the poor will have more than the rich, and the ungodly will exalt themselves above the heroic.
The wise will be silent and the foolish will speak. Neither the thinking of people nor the counsel of the mighty will be confirmed then, and the hope of those who hope will not be confirmed.
When what was foretold has come to pass, confusion will fall on everyone. Some will fall in battle and some will perish in anguish,
and some will be destroyed by their own. Then the Most High will call up the nations He prepared beforehand, and they will come and make war on the leaders who are left at that time.
Whoever escapes the war will die in the earthquake, whoever escapes the earthquake will be burned by the fire, and whoever escapes the fire will be destroyed by famine.
Whoever, among the victors and the defeated, escapes all these things I have mentioned will be handed over to My servant, the Messiah.
For all the earth will devour its inhabitants.”
“The holy land will have mercy on its own and protect its inhabitants at that time.
This is the vision you saw, and this is its meaning.
I have come to tell you these things because your prayer has been heard by the Most High.”
“Now hear also about the bright lightning that is to come at the end, after these black waters. This is the word.

After the signs I told you of before have come, when the nations are in turmoil and the time of My Messiah has come, he will summon all the nations. Some of them he will spare, and some he will put to death.
These things will come on the nations that he spares.
Every nation that has not known Israel and has not trampled the seed of Jacob will indeed be spared.
This is because some from every nation will be made subject to your people.
But all who have ruled over you, or have known you, will be given up to the sword.”
“When he has brought low everything in the world and has sat down in peace for the age on the throne of his kingdom, then joy will be revealed and rest will appear.
Then healing will come down like dew, and disease will withdraw. Worry, anguish, and lamentation will pass from among people, and gladness will spread through the whole earth.
No one will die before his time again, and no misfortune will strike suddenly.
Judgments, abusive talk, quarrels, revenge, bloodshed, passions, envy, hatred, and everything like these will go into condemnation when they are removed.
These are the very things that have filled this world with evils, and because of them human life has been greatly troubled.
Wild beasts will come out of the forest and serve people, and asps and dragons will come out of their holes to submit to a little child.
Women will no longer have pain when they give birth, and they will not suffer torment when they bring forth the fruit of the womb.”
“In those days the reapers will not grow tired and the builders will not be worn out, for the work will move ahead quickly by itself, together with those who do it, in great peace.
For that time is the end of what is corruptible and the beginning of what is not corruptible.
So the things that were foretold will belong to it. It is far from evils and near to things that do not die.
This is the bright lightning that came after the last dark waters.”
I answered, “Who can understand Your goodness, Lord? It cannot be grasped.
Who can search out Your compassion, which has no end?
Who can comprehend Your intelligence?
Who can recount the thoughts of Your mind?
Who among those who are born can hope to reach those things, unless it is someone to whom You are merciful and gracious?
If You did not have compassion on humanity, those under Your right hand could not reach those things, but only those counted by name can be called.
But if we who exist know why we have come, and submit to the One who brought us out of Egypt, we will come again and remember the things that have passed, and we will rejoice over what has been.

But if we do not know why we have come, and do not acknowledge the rule of the One who brought us up out of Egypt, we will come again and look for the things of the present, and be grieved with pain over what has happened.”

chapters.heading: Baruch is told to teach the people for forty days

verses.text: He answered me, “Since the meaning of this vision has been explained to you as you asked, hear the word of the Most High, so that you may know what will happen to you after these things.
You will surely depart from this earth, but not to death. You will be kept until the end of the times.

So go up to the top of that mountain, and all the regions of that land will pass before you, together with the shape of the inhabited world, the tops of the mountains, the depths of the valleys, the depths of the seas, and the number of the rivers, so that you may see what you are leaving and where you are going.

This will happen after forty days. So go now, and during these days teach the people as far as you can, so that they may learn and not die at the last time, but may learn so that they live in the last times.”

chapters.heading: Baruch’s address, and his two letters

verses.text: I, Baruch, went there and came to the people. I gathered them together, from the greatest to the least, and said to them,
“Listen, children of Israel. See how many of you remain from the twelve tribes of Israel.
To you and to your fathers the Lord gave a law more excellent than any given to all other peoples.
Because your brothers broke the commands of the Most High, He did not spare the earlier ones, and He gave the later ones also into captivity. He did not leave a remnant of them,
but see, you are here with me.
If you direct your ways rightly, you also will not depart as your brothers departed, but they will come to you.
The One you worship is merciful, the One in whom you hope is gracious, and He is true, so that He will do good and not evil.
Have you not seen here what has happened to Zion?
Or do you perhaps think the place had sinned and was overthrown for that reason? Or that the land had acted foolishly and so was handed over?
Do you not know that because of you who sinned, what did not sin was overthrown, and because of those who did wickedly, what did not act foolishly was handed over to its enemies?”
The whole people answered me, “As far as we can recall the good things the Mighty One has done for us, we recall them, and the things we do not remember He knows in His mercy.
Even so, do this for us, your people: write also to our brothers in Babylon a letter of teaching and a scroll of hope, so that you may strengthen them too before you leave us.
The shepherds of Israel have perished, the lamps that gave light have gone out, and the fountains have held back the streams we used to drink from.
We are left in the darkness, among the trees of the forest, and in the thirst of the wilderness.”
I answered them, “Shepherds, lamps, and fountains come from the law. Though we depart, the law remains.
If you therefore respect the law and give yourselves to wisdom, a lamp will not be missing, a shepherd will not fail, and a fountain will not dry up.
Even so, as you have asked me, I will write to your brothers in Babylon and send it by men. In the same way I will write to the nine and a half tribes and send it by a bird.”
On the twenty-first day of the eighth month ({a}October–November), I, Baruch, came and sat down under the oak, in the shade of its branches. No one was with me, and I was alone.
I wrote these two letters. One I sent by an eagle to the nine and a half tribes, and the other I sent to those in Babylon by three men.
I called the eagle and said these words to it:
“The Most High made you higher than all birds.

Now go, and do not linger anywhere, do not enter a nest, and do not settle on any tree until you have crossed the breadth of the many waters of the river Euphrates{b} and have gone to the people who live there, and drop this letter to them.
Remember that at the time of the flood Noah{c} received an olive branch from a dove when he sent it out from the ark.
The ravens also served Elijah{d}, bringing him food, as they had been commanded.
Solomon, too, in the time of his kingdom, whenever he wished to send or look for anything, commanded a bird to go, and it obeyed him as he commanded.
Now do not let this tire you. Turn neither right nor left, but fly straight, so that you keep the command of the Mighty One, as I have told you.”

notes.text: October–November: The text says the “eighth month” of the Hebrew calendar, which is Marcheshvan.
“Euphrates” (Hebrew *Perat*) is the great river of Mesopotamia, whose name means “fruitful.”
“Noah” (Hebrew *Noach*) is linked in Genesis 5 with “rest” or “comfort.”
“Elijah” (Hebrew *Eliyyahu*) means “my God is Yahweh.”

chapters.heading: The letter to the nine and a half tribes

verses.text: These are the words of the letter that Baruch, son of Neriah, sent to the nine and a half tribes across the river Euphrates, in which these things were written.

Baruch, son of Neriah, says this to the brothers carried into captivity: “Mercy and peace.” My brothers, I keep in mind the love of the One who created us. He loved us from of old and never hated us, but above all He trained us.
I know that all of us, the twelve tribes, are bound by one bond, since we were born from one father.

So I have been all the more careful to leave you the words of this letter before I die, so that you may be comforted about the evils that have come on you, and may also grieve over the evil that has come on your brothers. I also want you to justify His judgment,

which He decreed against you, that you be carried away captive, since what you have suffered is out of proportion to what you have done, so that in the last times you may be found worthy of your fathers.

So if you consider that you have suffered these things for your good, so that in the end you will not be condemned and tormented, then you will receive eternal hope. Above all, you must destroy from your heart the empty error that caused you to leave this place.

If you do this, He will always remember you, He who always promised on our behalf to those more excellent than we are that He will never forget or abandon us, but will gather again, with great mercy, those who were scattered.
Now, my brothers, first learn what happened to Zion: how Nebuchadnezzar{a}, king of Babylon, came up against us.
We sinned against the One who made us and did not keep the commandments He gave us, yet He has not punished us as we deserved.
What happened to you we also suffer in a still greater degree, for it happened to us as well.

notes.text: “Nebuchadnezzar” (Babylonian *Nabu-kudurri-usur*) means “Nabu, protect my heir.”

verses.text: Now, my brothers, I tell you that when the enemy had surrounded the city, the angels of the Most High were sent, and they overthrew the fortifications of the strong wall and destroyed the firm iron corners, which could not be uprooted.
Even so, they hid all the vessels of the sanctuary, so that the enemy could not take possession of them.

When they had done this, they handed over to the enemy the overthrown wall, the plundered house, the burned temple, and the people, who were overcome because they had been given up, so that the enemy could not boast and say, “By force we have been able to lay waste even the house of the Most High in war.”
They have also bound your brothers and led them away to Babylon, and made them live there.
But we have been left here, very few.
This is the tribulation I wrote to you about.
I know that the comfort of the inhabitants of Zion consoles you, since, as long as you knew it was prospering, your comfort was greater than the tribulation you endured in having to leave it.
Now hear the word about comfort.
I was mourning over Zion, and I asked the Most High for mercy, and I said,
“How long will these things last for us? Will these evils come on us always?”

The Mighty One acted according to the abundance of His mercies, and the Most High according to the greatness of His compassion. He revealed the word to me so that I would receive comfort. He showed me visions so that I would not endure anguish again, and He made known to me the mystery of the times and showed me the coming of the hours.
So, my brothers, I have written to you so that you may comfort yourselves in the abundance of your tribulations.

Know that our Maker will surely avenge us on all our enemies for everything they have done to us. The end that the Most High will bring is very near, and His mercy that is coming and the end of His judgment are not far off at all.
We now see the abundance of the nations’ prosperity, though they act ungodly, but they will be like a vapor.
We see the greatness of their power, though they do wickedly, but they will be made like a drop of water.
We see the firmness of their strength, though they resist the Mighty One every hour, but they will be counted as spit.
We consider the glory of their greatness, though they do not keep the statutes of the Most High, but they will pass away like smoke.
We think about the beauty of their grace, though they deal in pollution, but they will fade away like grass that withers.
We consider the strength of their cruelty, though they do not remember its end, but they will be broken like a wave that passes.
We take note of the boasting of their might, though they deny the kindness of God who gave it to them, but they will pass away like a passing cloud.
For the Most High will surely hasten His times, and He will surely bring on His hours.
He will surely judge those who are in His world, and He will visit all things in truth through all their hidden works.
He will surely examine the secret thoughts and everything stored in the inner rooms of all the members of the human body, and He will make it plain before everyone with rebuke.
So let none of these present things rise into your hearts, but above all let us wait expectantly, because what has been promised to us will come.
Let us not now look to the pleasures of the nations in the present, but let us remember what has been promised to us in the end.
For the ends of the times and seasons, and whatever goes with them, will surely pass by together.
The end of the age will then show the great power of its ruler, when all things come to judgment.
So prepare your hearts for what you believed before, so that you do not end up in bondage in both worlds, led away captive here and tormented there.
For in everything that exists now, or has passed, or is to come, neither is the evil fully evil, nor again the good fully good.
All the health of this time is turning into sickness,
all the might of this time is turning into weakness, and all the force of this time is turning into helplessness.
Every energy of youth is turning into old age and decline, and every graceful beauty of this time is turning faded and hateful.
Every proud rule of the present is turning into humiliation and shame,
every praise of the glory of this time is turning into the shame of silence, and every empty splendor and insolence of this time is turning into voiceless ruin.
Every delight and joy of this time is turning to worms and corruption,
every clamor of the pride of this time is turning into dust and stillness.
Every possession of riches in this time is being turned into Sheol alone,
all the plunder of passion in this time is turning into unwilling death, and every passion of the desires of this time is turning into a judgment of torment.
Every scheme and trick of this time is turning into a proof of the truth,
every sweetness of perfumes in this time is turning into judgment and condemnation,
and every love of lying is turning into disgrace through the truth.
Since all these things are done now, does anyone think they will not be avenged? But the end of all things will come to the truth.

See, I have made these things known to you while I am alive. I said it so that you would learn what is excellent, for the Mighty One has commanded me to teach you, and I will set before you some of the commands of His judgment before I die.
Remember that Moses once called heaven and earth to witness against you and said, “If you break the law you will be scattered, but if you keep it you will be kept.”
He also told you other things when you, the twelve tribes, were together in the desert.
After his death you threw them away from you, and for this reason what had been foretold came on you.
Moses told you before these things happened to you, and now they have happened to you, for you abandoned the law.
I also say to you, now that you have suffered, that if you obey what has been said to you, you will receive from the Mighty One whatever has been stored up and kept for you.
Let this letter be a testimony between me and you, so that you remember the commands of the Mighty One, and so that I also have a defense before the One who sent me.
Remember the law and Zion, the holy land and your brothers, and the covenant of your fathers, and do not forget the festivals and the Sabbaths.
Hand on this letter and the traditions of the law to your sons after you, as your fathers handed them on to you.

At all times ask persistently and pray earnestly with your whole heart that the Mighty One may be reconciled to you, and that He may not count the multitude of your sins but remember the uprightness of your fathers.
For if He does not judge us according to the abundance of His mercies, woe to all of us who are born.”
“Know also that in former times, in the generations of old, our fathers had helpers, righteous men and holy prophets.
We were in our own land, and they helped us when we sinned. They interceded for us with the One who made us, because they trusted in their works, and the Mighty One heard their prayer and forgave us.

But now the righteous have been gathered, the prophets have fallen asleep, and we too have gone out from the land. Zion has been taken from us, and now we have nothing except the Mighty One and His law.
So if we direct and set our hearts in order, we will receive everything we lost, and far better things many times over.
What we lost was subject to corruption, and what we will receive will not be corruptible.
I have also written like this to our brothers in Babylon, so that I may bear witness to them as well about these very things.
Let all the things I have mentioned be always before your eyes, because we are still in the spirit and power of our freedom.
Again, the Most High is patient with us here. He has shown us what is to come and has not hidden from us what will happen in the end.

So before judgment claims what is its own and truth what is due to it, let us prepare our souls so that we possess and are not possessed, so that we hope and are not put to shame, and so that we rest with our fathers and are not tormented with our enemies.

For the youth of the world is past, the strength of creation is already spent, and the coming of the times is very near. Indeed, they have gone by. The pitcher is near the cistern, the ship near the port, the course of the journey near the city, and life near its end.
Prepare your souls again, so that when you sail and step off the ship, you may have rest

and not be condemned when you depart. For when the Most High brings all these things to pass, there will be no more a place for repentance, no limit to the times, no duration for the hours, no change of ways, no place for prayer, no sending of petitions, no receiving of knowledge, no giving of love, no place of repentance for the soul, no pleading for offenses, no intercession of the fathers, no prayer of the prophets, and no help of the righteous.
There is the sentence of corruption, the way of fire, and the path that leads to Gehenna.
For this reason there is one law through one, one age, and an end for all who are in it.
Then He will keep safe those He can forgive and at the same time destroy those who are stained with sins.”
When you receive this letter of mine, read it carefully in your congregations.
Think it over, above all on the days of your fasts.
Remember me by means of this letter, as I also remember you in it, always. Farewell.
When I had finished all the words of this letter and had written it carefully to its close, I folded it, sealed it securely, tied it to the neck of the eagle, and let it go and sent it off.

books.name: 4 Baruch
books.sourceNote: Translated from the Greek text of 4 Baruch (the *Paraleipomena Ieremiou*, “Things Omitted from Jeremiah”) as edited by J. Rendel Harris, *The Rest of the Words of Baruch* (London, 1889), which is in the public domain and prints three groups of Greek copies, called a, b and c in its notes, along with readings from the Ethiopic version. Harris’s Greek was read directly; his English rendering and R. H. Charles’s later reference translation (public domain) were consulted only to line up verses, and the English here is new. Where the Greek is damaged or the copies differ in a way that changes the sense, the footnotes say so. Greek *Kyrios* is “the Lord” throughout; where the Bible’s own text would have Yahweh, this book simply says “the Lord,” because the Greek never writes the Hebrew name. **Date and text.** The story is set at the fall of Jerusalem to the Babylonians in 587/586 BC, but it was written much later. Most scholars place the Jewish core shortly after the Romans destroyed Jerusalem in AD 70 and before the Bar Kokhba revolt, perhaps between about AD 100 and 136; Harris himself argued for a date close to AD 136. Some wording, especially the passage in chapter 9 about the Son of God and Jesus Christ, may have been added by a Christian editor or may reflect a Christian rework of the whole. The Greek is preserved in medieval copies, and the book also survives in Ethiopic, Armenian, Slavonic and other translations, which sometimes keep readings the Greek lost. **Numbering.** The chapters here (nine) and the verse counts follow the numbering most commonly used in English study of the book. Harris’s own verse divisions differ in several chapters (his chapters 3 and 8 have far fewer verses, for example), so a verse number here may not match a citation to Harris’s page. **Canon status.** 4 Baruch is not in the Jewish Bible, the Catholic and Orthodox Old Testaments, or the Protestant canon. It is accepted in the wider canon of the Ethiopian Orthodox Tewahedo Church, where it is known as the “Rest of the Words of Baruch.” **About the book.** In 4 Baruch, Jeremiah and his scribe Baruch are in Jerusalem as the Babylonians approach. Jeremiah hides the Temple vessels and keys, and the people are taken to Babylon, while the Ethiopian Abimelech, who had once rescued Jeremiah from a pit, is spared and sent to rest among the figs of Agrippa’s estate, where he sleeps sixty-six years. When Abimelech wakes, an angel leads him back to Jerusalem; Baruch and Jeremiah’s letter bring the exiles home. Jeremiah then calls the people to leave the habits of Babylon; those who refuse build Samaria, and Jeremiah falls into a three-day trance in which he sees the coming of the Son of God. The people stone a stone that has taken his shape, and he is killed after finishing his message. The book aims to comfort Jews after the loss of the Temple and to teach that resurrection and a return from exile follow faithfulness to God, and it later played a part in Christian reading of Jeremiah.

verses.text: When the people of Israel were being carried away captive by the Chaldean king,{a} God spoke to Jeremiah.{b} “Jeremiah, my chosen servant,” he said, “rise up and leave this city, you and Baruch,{c} because I am about to lay it in ruins; those who live in it have heaped up so many sins.”
Your prayers stand in the middle of it like a firm pillar, and like a wall of unbreakable steel running all around it.
So now, get up and go out before the Chaldean army has the city ringed.
Jeremiah answered, “I beg you, Lord,{d} let your servant speak in your presence.”
“Speak, Jeremiah, my chosen one,” the Lord answered.
So Jeremiah said, “Lord Almighty,{e} are you handing your chosen city over to the Chaldeans, so that the king and all his people may boast and say, ‘I have beaten the holy city of God’?
No, my Lord. But if that is what you want, then destroy it with your own hands.”
The Lord said to Jeremiah, “Because you are my chosen one, get up and leave this city, you and Baruch, because I am going to destroy it for the great number of sins of those who live in it.
The king and his army cannot get inside unless I myself open its gates for them.
So get up, go to Baruch, and give him these words.
At midnight,{f} after you have gotten up, climb onto the city walls. I will show you that they cannot enter until I have brought the city down first.”
When the Lord had spoken, he went away from Jeremiah.

notes.text: “Chaldeans” is the Greek form of Hebrew Kasdim, the people who ruled Babylon. The book looks back to the Babylonian conquest of Jerusalem in 587/586 BC (compare 2 Kings 25; Jeremiah 39).
The Hebrew name Yirmeyahu is often explained as “Yahweh lifts up” or “Yahweh throws down”; the meaning is uncertain.
Baruch (Hebrew Barukh) means “blessed.” He is Jeremiah’s scribe in Jeremiah 36 and 45.

The Greek text has *kyrios*, “Lord,” the word the Greek Bible regularly uses for Yahweh. Throughout the book, “the Lord” renders *kyrios*; the Hebrew name Yahweh itself does not occur in this Greek text.
Greek *pantokratōr*, “ruler of all,” which the Greek Bible uses for the Hebrew title Yahweh Sabaoth (“Yahweh of Armies”).
Greek “the sixth hour of the night.” Counting the night hours from about 6 p.m., the sixth hour is about midnight.

verses.text: Jeremiah hurried to tell Baruch everything. The two of them went to the Temple of God; there Jeremiah ripped his robe, covered his head with dust, and walked into the sanctuary of God.{a}
When Baruch saw him with his garments torn and dust on his head, he cried out in a loud voice, “Father Jeremiah, what has happened to you? What dreadful sin has the people committed?”
Each time the people had sinned, Jeremiah would throw dust over his head and plead for them, until their sin was forgiven.
So Baruch asked him, “Father, why are you doing this? What is going on?”
Jeremiah said to him, “Rather, let us tear open our hearts, and not fetch water for the troughs. Let us weep until our tears fill them, because the Lord will show this people no pity.”
Baruch said, “Father Jeremiah, what has happened?”
Jeremiah said, “God is handing the city over to the king of the Chaldeans, to carry the people away captive to Babylon.”
When Baruch heard it, he tore his own robe too. “Father Jeremiah,” he said, “who told you this?”
Jeremiah said to him, “Stay with me a little while, until midnight, so that you can know that this word is true.”
So the two of them remained beside the altar,{b} weeping, with their clothes torn.

notes.text: The Greek says “the sanctuary (*hagiastērion*) of God,” meaning the Temple.
The Greek word is *thysiastērion*, “the place of sacrifice, altar.”

verses.text: When the hour of night came that the Lord had spoken of to Jeremiah, Jeremiah and Baruch went together up onto the city walls.
A trumpet sounded, and angels came out of heaven carrying torches in their hands, and they stood on the walls of the city.
When Jeremiah and Baruch saw the angels, they wept. “Now we know the word is true,” they said.
Then Jeremiah pleaded with the angels: “I ask you not to destroy the city yet, until I have spoken to the Lord.”
The Lord said to the angels, “Do not destroy the city until I have spoken with my chosen servant Jeremiah.”
Jeremiah said, “I beg you, Lord, allow me to speak in your presence.”
The Lord said, “Speak, my chosen Jeremiah.”
Jeremiah said, “Look, Lord, we now know that you are handing the city over to its enemies, and they will carry the people off to Babylon.
What would you have me do with the sacred vessels used in the Temple’s worship?”

The Lord answered, “Take them, give them over to the earth, and say: ‘Listen, earth, to the voice of the one who shaped you, who set you down amid the waters,{a} and who sealed you with seven seals through seven seasons. After all this, you will be given back your adornment.
Keep safe the sacred vessels of the Temple until the beloved ones are gathered.’”
Jeremiah said, “Lord, show me, I pray, what I ought to do for Abimelech the Ethiopian.{b} He has shown great kindness to the people and to your servant Jeremiah.
For he is the one who lifted me out of the muddy pit.{c} I do not want him to see the ruin of the city and its desolation; instead, be merciful to him, so that he is not grieved.”
The Lord said to Jeremiah, “Send him away to the estate of Agrippa{d} by way of the mountain, and I will shelter him until I bring your people back to the city.
And you, Jeremiah, go with your people to Babylon, and stay there preaching the good news to them,{e} until I bring them back to the city.
Baruch must stay here while I speak with him.”
When he had said this, the Lord went up from Jeremiah into heaven.
Then Jeremiah and Baruch went into the sanctuary and took the holy vessels of the service; they handed them over to the earth, just as the Lord had told them.
Right away, the earth swallowed them up.
And the two sat down and wept.

At daybreak Jeremiah sent Abimelech off, saying, “Take a basket, and go along the mountain road to the estate of Agrippa. Bring back a few figs for the sick among the people, because the Lord’s favor rests on you and his glory crowns your head.”
Abimelech went, as he had been told.

notes.text: Greek “in the abundance (or fullness) of the waters.” Ancient writers pictured the earth as a land set in the waters of the sea (compare Psalm 24:2).
“Ethiopian” translates Greek *Aithiops* (Hebrew Kushi, “Cushite”), a man from the upper Nile region south of Egypt. He is the court official of Jeremiah 38:7–13 and 39:15–18.
Greek *lakkos tou borborou*, “the pit of mud”; compare the cistern in Jeremiah 38:6, where Jeremiah sank into the mud.

“Agrippa” is the name the Greek gives to a country property near Jerusalem. It is a Greek or Latin name not otherwise known from Jeremiah’s time, which is one sign that the book was composed long after the events it describes.

The Greek participle *euangelizomenos* means “bringing good news.” It is the verb the New Testament uses for preaching the gospel; here it describes Jeremiah’s message of comfort and return to the exiles.

verses.text: When morning came, the army of the Chaldeans appeared and surrounded the city.
Then the great angel sounded the trumpet and called out, “Come in, you forces of the Chaldeans, for the gate has been opened to you.”
“Let the king come in with his multitude, and let him carry all the people away captive.”

Jeremiah took the Temple keys, went out beyond the city, and hurled them toward the sun,{a} calling out, “Sun, this is my command: take the Temple keys of God and hold on to them until the day the Lord demands them back from you.
For we were not found worthy to guard them, because we proved to be faithless stewards.”
While Jeremiah was still weeping over the people, they were being dragged off to Babylon.{b}

Baruch threw dust on his head and sat down, and he sang this lament:{c} “Why has Jerusalem been laid waste?
Because of the sins of the people we love, it was handed over to enemy hands, because of our sins and the sins of the people.
But let the lawless ones not boast, saying, ‘We had the strength to take God’s city by our own power.’ You could not do it. It was because of our sins that we were handed over.
But our God will have compassion on us and bring us back to our city. You, however, will not live.”
“Happy are our ancestors Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob: they passed out of this world and never saw this city fall.”
When he had said this, Baruch went outside the city, weeping and saying, “I grieve on your account, Jerusalem, because I left you.”
He kept sitting in a burial place, and the angels visited him and made everything clear to him.

notes.text: Addressing the sun, and the earth in chapter 3 above, matches the Bible’s way of calling on creation as a witness (compare Deuteronomy 32:1; Isaiah 1:2).
“Babylon” is the Greek form of Hebrew Bavel, a name sometimes explained as “gate of god” (Akkadian) and linked in Genesis 11:9 to the Hebrew word *balal*, “confuse.”
The Greek word is *thrēnos*, a funeral song or lament, like the Hebrew book of Lamentations.

verses.text: Abimelech took the figs in the scorching heat and came to a tree; he sat down in its shade to rest for a short while.{a}
He leaned his head against the basket of figs and fell asleep. He slept for sixty-six years,{b} and he did not wake from his sleep.
Then, waking from his sleep, he said, “That was sweet sleep, but short; my head still feels heavy, since I have not slept my fill.”
He lifted the cover off the basket of figs and saw that they were still wet, running with a milky sap.

He said, “I would like another little sleep, but my head weighs on me. Still, I fear that if I drift off I will wake late, and my father Jeremiah will think ill of me. He would not have sent me out at first light today unless he needed them quickly.
So I will get up and go on in the heat, and I will reach the place where there is no scorching heat and no daily weariness.”{c}
He got up, took the basket of figs, and lifted it onto his shoulder. He went into Jerusalem, and he did not recognize it, or the house, or the place, or anyone from his own family.
He said, “May the Lord be praised, since a deep daze has fallen on me!
This is not the city! I have lost my way. I came up by the mountain road, and when I woke, my head was so heavy from lack of rest that I wandered off the path.
It will seem remarkable to Jeremiah when I tell him that I have lost my way.”
He went out of the city and looked carefully for the signs of the city, and he said, “This is the city all right, but I have lost my way.”
He went into the city again and looked around, but found no one he knew. He said, “May the Lord be praised, since a deep daze has fallen on me.”
He went out of the city again, and stayed there in distress, not knowing where he should go.
He set the basket down and said, “I will stay seated here until the Lord lifts this daze off me.”
As he was sitting there, he saw an old man coming in from the field. Abimelech said to him, “Look, old man, what city is this?”
He answered him, “It is Jerusalem.”
Abimelech said to him, “Where are Jeremiah the priest and Baruch the reader,{d} and all the people of this city, since I could not find them?”
The old man asked him, “Are you not a native of this city? You mention Jeremiah today, and you ask after him after so long a time?
Jeremiah is in Babylon with the people, who were carried off by King Nebuchadnezzar,{e} and he is there with them to announce good news and instruct them in the word.”

Abimelech heard the old man out, and answered, “If you were not so aged, and if it were not improper to rebuke a man who is older than oneself, I would laugh at you and tell you that you have lost your mind, for claiming that the people have been carried off to Babylon.
Even if the floodgates of heaven had opened on them, it would not yet be time to go to Babylon!
Why, it was only a short time ago that my father Jeremiah sent me to Agrippa’s estate to fetch a few figs, which we meant to give to the sick among the people.
I went and picked them, and on reaching a certain tree in the blazing heat, I sat down for a short rest. I put my head on the basket and dozed off.
When I woke up, I uncovered the basket of figs, thinking that I had slept too long, and I found the figs dripping with milk, just as I had gathered them.
But you say the people were taken captive to Babylon.
But so that you can know, take the figs and look!”
He lifted the cover of the basket for the old man.
When the old man looked at the figs, he said, “My son, you are a righteous man. God did not wish you to witness the city’s desolation, so he sent this daze over you.
For now it has been sixty-six years since the people were taken captive to Babylon.
So that you can learn, my child, that this is true: look out over the field and see that the crops are springing up.{f}
Look also at the figs: it is not their season. Learn from that, and be enlightened.”
Then Abimelech cried out loudly, saying, “Blessed be God, who gives the souls of the righteous rest in every place!”
Then he asked the old man, “What month is this?”
He answered, “Nisan{g} (March–April), the twelfth.”
He took a few of the figs and handed them to the old man, saying, “May God light your path to the Jerusalem above.”

notes.text: The Greek says “the heat” (*kauma*), the midday heat of the Judean hills.
Greek *hexēkonta hex etē*, “sixty-six years”; the same number is repeated in 5:29. Abimelech’s long sleep is the main sign in the book that the exile has begun and that years have passed.
The Greek of this verse is damaged. Harris notes that the manuscripts differ here and that the line is probably corrupt, so the sense given is tentative.
Greek *anagnōstēs*, “reader” (one who reads the Scriptures aloud); here it names Baruch as Jeremiah’s scribe and reader.
“Nebuchadnezzar” is the Greek form of Babylonian *Nabu-kudurri-usur*, “Nabu, protect my heir” (a common spelling in the Bible is Nebuchadrezzar).
The Greek reads “the growth of the crops has appeared” (so Harris); some editors emend this to “has not appeared.” Either way the point is that the figs are out of season.

Greek *Nisan*, the Hebrew first month (March–April). Harris notes that Nisan was never the twelfth month, and suggests that “the twelfth” here means the twelfth day of the first month, the day Ezra left the Ahava river for Jerusalem (Ezra 8:31); he also wonders whether the text once read “Nisan, which is Abib” (Abib is the older Hebrew name of the month, Exodus 13:4). The Ethiopic version has “the twelfth of the month Nisan.”

verses.text: Afterward Abimelech left the city and prayed to the Lord.
And an angel of the Lord appeared, and set him down at the place where Baruch was; he found him sitting in a tomb.
When they saw each other, they embraced and kissed one another.
Baruch looked up and saw the figs, still covered over in the basket.
Then he raised his eyes toward heaven and prayed:

“Lord, you are the God who pays back those who are holy. Prepare yourself, my heart, and be glad and celebrate inside your tent,{a} and tell your house of flesh that your sorrow has turned into joy. For the One who is able is on his way, and he will bring you out of your tent; there is no sin in you.
Come to life again in your dwelling, in my unspoiled faith,{b} and believe that you will live!
Look at this basket of figs: it has been sixty-six years since they were picked, and they have not withered or rotted; they are dripping milk.
So it will be for you, my flesh, if you carry out what the angel of righteousness has told you.
The one who kept the basket of figs safe is the same one who will keep you safe again by his power.”
After saying this, Baruch turned to Abimelech. “Rise, and let us pray that the Lord will teach us how we can get word to Jeremiah in Babylon about the shelter that was given you on your way.”
Baruch prayed, “You are our strength, our God and Lord, the chosen light that has come out of your mouth.
We turn to your goodness and plead with you, whose great Name{c} nobody can know: listen to the voices of your servants, and let understanding enter our hearts.
What do you want us to do? How can we send word to Jeremiah in Babylon?”

While Baruch was still praying, an angel of the Lord appeared and spoke to him. “Baruch, helper of the light, do not worry over how you are to get word to Jeremiah. An eagle will come to you tomorrow, at the hour of light, and you will send it to Jeremiah.

So put this in the letter: ‘Say to the sons of Israel: Anyone who has become a foreigner among you should be kept apart, and let fifteen days go by. After that, I will bring you to your own city, says the Lord.
Whoever is not separated from Babylon, Jeremiah, will not enter the city. I command that they not be taken back again by the Babylonians, says the Lord.’”
When the angel had said this, he left Baruch.
Baruch sent a messenger to the market of the Gentiles, who returned with papyrus and ink, and Baruch wrote a letter that read: “From Baruch, servant of God, to Jeremiah in the Babylonian exile.
Greetings! Rejoice and be glad, because God did not let us leave this body in grief over the city that was laid waste and insulted.
For this reason the Lord had compassion on our tears and remembered the covenant that he made with our fathers Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob.{d}
He sent his angel to me, who told me these words that I am sending to you.

These are the words of the Lord, the God of Israel, who brought us up from the land of Egypt,{e} from the great furnace:{f} ‘You did not keep my laws; your heart grew proud, and you held your necks stiff against me. So in anger and fury I gave you over to the furnace of Babylon.

If you will obey my voice, says the Lord, as it comes through Jeremiah my servant, then I will lead the obedient up out of Babylon. But whoever will not obey will be an outsider to Jerusalem and to Babylon alike.
You will put them to the test with the water of the Jordan:{g} the one who will not obey will be shown up. That is the sign of the great seal.’”

notes.text: “Tent” translates Greek *skēnōma*, “dwelling,” the body, as in 2 Corinthians 5:1 and 2 Peter 1:13; the speaker is preparing his soul for the resurrection of the body he describes next.

Greek *parthenikē pistis*, literally “virginal faith,” meaning a faith not spoiled by any impurity. The manuscripts differ widely in this verse; Harris notes that one of them reads “in your own home, my virginal faith.”
Greek *to mega onoma*, “the great Name”; here it refers to the divine name, which is Yahweh in Hebrew (Exodus 3:14–15). The Greek text does not spell it out.

“Abraham” (Hebrew *Avraham*) means “father of a multitude” (Genesis 17:5); “Isaac” (*Yitskhaq*) means “he laughs” (Genesis 21:6); “Jacob” (*Ya’aqov*) is linked in Genesis 25:26 to “heel” and means “he grasps the heel,” or “he supplants.”
“Egypt” is Greek *Aigyptos*; the Hebrew is *Mitsrayim*, of uncertain meaning.
The “iron furnace” is the Bible’s image for Egypt (Deuteronomy 4:20; 1 Kings 8:51; Jeremiah 11:4).
“Jordan” (Hebrew *Yarden*) means “the descender,” because the river drops steeply from the north to the Dead Sea.

verses.text: Baruch got up and left the tomb, and he saw an eagle sitting outside the tomb.
The eagle answered in a human voice, “Greetings, Baruch, steward of the faith.”
Baruch said to him, “You who speak this way: you are chosen out of all the birds of heaven, because it shows in the look of your eyes. Tell me what you are doing here.”
The eagle replied, “I have been sent so that you can use me to carry any word you wish.”
“Can you take a message to Jeremiah in Babylon?” Baruch asked.
The eagle said to him, “Yes; that is the very reason I was sent.”

Baruch took the letter, together with fifteen figs from Abimelech’s basket, and fastened them around the eagle’s neck. “Hear me, king of the birds,” he said. “Go in peace and good health, and bring back word to me.
Do not be like the raven that Noah sent out,{a} which did not come back to him in the ark. Be like the dove that, after the third time, brought the news to the righteous man.
